Then, several rays of light appeared in the air and slowly condensed into a solid form. A device similar to a walkie-talkie fell from the air to the ground.
"What are you doing?!"
Seeing this.
The bald man hurriedly rushed forward, quickly picked up the "Consciousness Transporter" that had fallen to the ground, and checked it several times with an anxious expression. After confirming that it was not damaged, he muttered.
"Be gentle, don't break it for me."
"This is my great opportunity!"

chapters.title: Chapter 97 (2): The Maze Designer II
chapters.content:
In the cavern outside the train, all the slaves had finished their dinner. But tonight, instead of immediately returning to their sleeping quarters on the train, they were gathered around, watching the commotion.
In the center of the crowd, a slave knelt on the ground, his face a mask of terror. He wasn't bound, but he didn't dare move.
A circle of armed guards maintained order.
Behind the kneeling slave, Li Shiji hefted a police baton. He leaned down, his head close to the man's ear, and whispered.
"Enjoying my iron ore?"
"Karma always comes around; it's just a matter of timing."
"Remember this."
"My name is Li Shiji." 【TN: "Shiji" sounds like "right time" in Chinese, creating wordplay with his previous statement about timing. 】
The next second—
Li Shiji's eyes filled with rage. He swung the baton with more force than he had ever used for mining, bringing it down hard on the kneeling slave's back. He didn't utter a single curse, just clenched his jaw.Like a storm, he rained down blow after blow, not holding back in the slightest.
It was clear he was trying to beat the man to death.
"Uncle Li."
In the crowd of watching slaves, a young man turned to the man beside him. "Look at that guy," he whispered. "He got promoted so easily, and he's just a Tier 3 slave who recently joined the train."
"You've been here since the beginning, old man. You're practically a veteran, and you've got Tier 1 status."
"How come you haven't gotten ahead yet?"
"Have you thought of a new plan?"
"Can you shut the hell up?!"
Uncle Li turned, his face flushed with anger and embarrassment. "Are you some kind of nag? Can you stop pressuring me every day? I'm under a lot of stress too, you know."
"Are you trying to live vicariously through me or something?"
"Well... I can't exactly count on myself, can I? I'm not the reliable type."
"Shut up! I'll think of something!"
"Of course. I've always believed in you, Uncle Li."
...
In the inner circle of the crowd.
Biao stood with his arms crossed, a cigarette dangling from his lips. A smile played on his face as he watched the scene. "Chief Zhu, I guarantee you that kid reported him on purpose."
"No shit."
Lao Zhu's face was grim. "You think I can't see that? The kid's a cunning little bastard. I don't like him."
"Boss Mang seems to like him though."
"Of course, Boss Mang likes him. I don't like the kid, but he's got talent."
Lao Zhu hesitated, then added reluctantly, "That kid can take an incredibly complex rectangular maze and mentally stretch it into a straight line. Can you even do that? I tried for a while, and my head almost exploded. When I closed my eyes, I kept seeing endless lines floating in front of me."
"I almost started hallucinating, but I still couldn't do it."
"I'm just a brute, Chief Zhu. If I had that kind of skill, do you think I would have been a small-time construction foreman?"
"With your brain, that's all you're good for. If the work dried up, you'd be screwed."
"I'm a brute, Chief Zhu."
"So what?"
Biao grinned, his eyes crinkling. "A brute collecting debts is a perfect match. There's no debt I can't collect. Otherwise, you think I could have been the boss back then?"
Lao Zhu snorted in disdain.
"Give it a rest. You were almost killed by that black rat. Don't brag about it. By the way, you were a Level 2 Train Captain before. Do you know of any situation that would require a massive maze capable of trapping a robot?"
"No idea."
Biao shook his head, his face serious. "Is that what Boss Mang wants this kid for?"
"Don't look at me. I don't know. It's not that I'm holding back; it's just that my old train and Boss Mang's operation are completely different things. To say they're worlds apart is an understatement."
"But..."
"I have to give you some advice. Boss Mang didn't tell you to beat the man to death. That kid is going too far. The slave looks like he's about to stop breathing."
"And don't get into a power struggle with this kid. Boss Mang is just using him to build a maze. After that, he'll be useless."
"You're still the second-in-command on this train, Chief Zhu. Don't make things ugly. You'll be the one who loses out."
"I know that."
Lao Zhu sighed. "Of course I'm not stupid enough to get into a pissing contest with him. It's just... It's the first time I've been reported over someone's head, and I'm a little pissed off. He didn't come to me; he went straight to Boss Mang. I don't know what Boss Mang will think. Maybe he'll think I'm oppressing the slaves all day, so they don't dare come to me with their problems."
"Don't worry about it. It was your oversight. You can't solve a problem until it's exposed. Relax."
Lao Zhu said no more, just took a step forward, his voice deep.
"That's enough."
He then looked at the half-dead slave on the ground. "Take him to the train for medical treatment."
"Carriage Chief Zhu."
Seeing Lao Zhu approach, Li Shiji immediately handed over the baton and bowed respectfully.
"Mm."
Lao Zhu took the baton, his facial expressionless. He looked at the crowd of slaves and pointed to the nearby iron mine. "All of you, back to the train to sleep. If you're not tired, you can go over there and keep digging with Duo Ba."
The slaves instinctively turned to look at the hundred-plus goblin slaves still digging in the iron mine. A shiver ran down their spines, and they scrambled for the carriages.
Those goblins...
They were absolute lunatics!
They had witnessed the goblins' madness these past few days. The slaves would go to sleep, and the goblins would still be digging. They would wake up, and the goblins would still be digging, as if they didn't need rest at all.
They were like cold-blooded machines, working around the clock.
Especially that Duo Ba.
He had dominated the daily mining leaderboard for days, completely undefeated.
At first, they had looked forward to the daily mining rankings.
But after the goblins swept the top hundred every single day, they had lost interest. The competition was too intense, so intense it scared them. The goblins were like a bunch of supermen.
Initially...
Many of them were seeing goblins for the first time and were curious. They would try to strike up conversations during breaks.
But after being cursed at several times—"Foolish humans, don't disturb the great goblins' mining!"—no one bothered to approach them anymore.
"That Duo Ba seems to spend his whole life trying to prove his greatness."
As the slaves scrambled for the carriages, Lao Zhu stayed behind, watching Duo Ba dig with relentless determination. He let out a sigh, a touch of something like admiration in his voice.
"To be honest, that guy has serious stamina."
"Yeah," Biao said, nodding. "He's strong."
Then Biao glanced toward the giantess among the short goblins, his expression shifting. "But that woman’s strong, too. Looks like she’s picked a fight with the goblins—determined to see who can dig more."
"I heard she went up to talk to Duo Ba today. Got cursed at."
"She seemed furious. Now, she’s dead set on out-digging them all."

chapters.title: Chapter 99 (1): The Ten Rules of the Stellar
chapters.content:
The bald man cradled the device like a precious treasure and returned to his locomotive. He settled at the control console, fiddling with it lovingly for a few moments before carefully placing it aside.
"Mom," he said.
"When this thing starts blaring and flashing red, crank the train's sound system to maximum!"
"I don't care what I'm doing—sleeping, taking a shit, whatever—wake me up!"
The next moment, a pleasant, mechanical voice echoed through the locomotive.
"Understood."
Every Train Captain could name their Train Auxiliary AI to make receiving commands easier. He had named his "Mom." His actual mother had passed away before the apocalypse, after several rounds of chemotherapy for cancer had failed.
With that settled, the bald man finally relaxed. He leaned back in his chair, gleeful anticipation spreading across his face as he stared at the device on the table, hoping it would start shrieking at any moment so he could claim his practically free reward.
As for not finding a compatible train to descend upon, that was perfectly normal.
The S-rank specialization mission for the "Mechanical Train" was absurd—practically impossible for any normal person to complete. Only a headstrong fool would choose it, even with two chances to select a mission.Completing an S-rank specialization mission required massive investments of time, energy, and resources.
In the apocalypse, no one would do something so foolish, to pour everything into a nearly impossible task.
But...
He wasn't worried. This world was short on many things, but headstrong people weren't one of them. He was confident that before long, some stubborn Train Captain would choose that S-rank mission, and he would be there with a savage grin to deliver a painful and despairing blow!
He would teach them a lesson in reality!
"Thirty Mofei Stones..."
The bald man gazed at the 3D model of his train on the control console screen, biting his finger as he frowned. "How should I spend them? A couple for the 'Tripod-Mounted Heavy Machine Gun,' maybe? Using Mofei Stones on green-grade accessories is the most cost-effective—just two stones for one advanced effect."
"No, no, a Level 5 'Tripod-Mounted Heavy Machine Gun' alone is useless. The heavy machine gun bullet production line would need two more."
"What a headache..."
"I've never been so spoiled for choice. It's torture trying to decide."
"Mom, any suggestions?"
"I suggest you wait until you have the thirty Mofei Stones in hand before considering this problem," the Train Auxiliary AI's voice came through the speakers.
"Alright, that's enough from you, Mom."
...
The next day.
Chen Mang woke from sleep, stretched with a long yawn, then looked out the window at the already-gathered slaves. A satisfied smile spread across his face. He had slept well.
The train had successfully reached Level 3.
And he had found a way to complete the S-rank specialization mission.
He was in an excellent mood.
He glanced at the train's panel. Including the iron ore the slaves had brought back yesterday, the train now had 60,000 units of iron ore.
His task for today was to craft and upgrade all accessories available for a Level 3 train.
In a word: splurge.
The two iron mines were almost depleted. The Resource Detection Radar showed just over 30,000 units of mineable iron ore remaining. They should finish by noon.
The Resource Detection Radar also revealed another high-level rare resource mine five thousand meters further down.
A Level 3 Crimson Heart Ore mine.
Estimated mineable quantity: 1,800 units of Level 3 Crimson Heart Ore.
Although he couldn't use this resource yet and didn't know which accessory required it, he still planned to excavate it after finishing the two iron mines.
The main reason was that the quantity was so small.
Only 1,800 units.
With so many slaves, they could dig it out in an hour or two. He might as well get it done, then head to other iron mines in the afternoon. The Ironridge Wasteland had plenty of underground iron mines—enough for him to dig for a long time!
With that decided, he pulled his gaze from the window and said casually to the door, "Come in."
Soon.
A young woman carrying a tray carefully pushed the door open, placed the tray on the control console, and said in a low voice, "Boss Mang, this is the breakfast Vice-Captain Zhu had me prepare for you. From now on, I'll be delivering your breakfast, lunch, and dinner."
"Mm."
Chen Mang glanced at the woman and said casually, "You can go."
A few days ago, he had Lao Zhu select ten women to handle cleaning the train, plus one specifically to clean his locomotive. This was the woman Lao Zhu had chosen. She was responsible for his daily meals and cleaning the locomotive at regular intervals.
She was quite good-looking.
Though she wore no makeup, her skin was tender. It was just that her clothes, though washed many times, still looked worn and didn't make a good impression.
He had tried trading iron ore for wood on the Train Radio yesterday, but...
On the Ironridge Wasteland, there were only two ways to get wood. The first was to go to the Mohe Hills and chop down trees. There were numerous lumberyards there. That area was part of the Ironridge Wasteland, not another region—just a place name.
But the terrain in that area was too rugged for a train to enter easily, making logging difficult and costly.
The second method was to find the occasional few trees growing alone or in small clusters on the Ironridge Wasteland. Chopping them down would yield a hundred or two hundred units of wood.
Although not much, it was enough.
After all, Level 1 and 2 trains didn't require much wood. For those small needs, chopping down a few trees on the Ironridge Wasteland was usually sufficient.
His demand was relatively large.
After all, the Custom Clothing Production Line would consume considerable wood to produce two sets of clothes for over 1,000 people. His idea was to make two sets of clothes for each slave and guard.
The colors of the clothes for Tier 1 slaves, Tier 2 slaves, and so on would be different.
This would clearly define the classes. He would also add a Stellar train arm patch to the clothes to make it more uniform and official.
The Train Radio didn't have that much wood available.
He would head toward the Mohe Hills later, digging up the underground iron mines along the way, and drive to the Mohe Hills.
After breakfast, Chen Mang had Li Shiji, who had been waiting outside the door, come in. He lay back in his chair, lit a cigarette, and frowned as he looked at the blueprint Li Shiji handed him.
To be honest.
He wasn't nearsighted, but looking at this blueprint made him feel like he had astigmatism.
The blueprint only showed a huge cube outlined with dotted and solid lines. Inside the cube were several marks like "1," "2," "3," and numerous dotted lines.
In the bottom right corner of the blueprint was a corresponding legend.
"1": Refrigerator.
"2": Mirror.
"3": Speaker.
"4": Taunts.
A minute later.
He put down the blueprint and looked at Li Shiji, who stood before him with a somewhat anxious expression. "Relax. I can understand the refrigerators and mirrors on your blueprint. What do you mean by 'taunts'?"
"Boss Mang, it's like this."
Li Shiji took a deep breath and began explaining. "Doesn't the robot you want to trap have superhuman intelligence? Since it has superhuman intelligence, it must have some human emotions."
"And among human emotions, there are many negative ones we can exploit."
"For example, suspicion."
"When this robot faces a fork with three paths, we can mark on the wall that the left side is a dead end, then actually make the left refrigerator a dead end—with no other refrigerators inside, a dead end that can be identified immediately."
"After a few times, this robot will start doubting itself when it sees these signs."
"And mockery."
"We can also write taunting slogans on the walls, like ‘I made this maze with my eyes closed—why are you acting like it's a Herculean task?’ to affect the robot's state of mind. When people are agitated, they often lose rational judgment. If that robot has human emotions, it will be affected."
"Even if the robot has no human emotions, it's just a few meaningless words on the wall. It doesn't affect anything. It's all pros and no cons."
"..."
Chen Mang silently looked down at the maze sketch in his hand again. He suddenly felt that this was somewhat absurd.
At first, he had thought the S-rank specialization mission for the Mechanical Train was almost impossible.
But when he remembered he had a Level 10 refrigerator, he felt it wasn't impossible.
And after hearing Li Shiji's idea today, he felt that the half-hour time limit might be a bit short...
A moment later.
He looked up at Li Shiji again. "In a few days, I'll build you a new carriage and 100 refrigerators. You need to build the maze from this sketch in that carriage."
"If you have any other ideas in the next few days, you can add them in."
"No problem, Boss Mang."
Chen Mang watched Li Shiji's retreating, his eyes narrowing slightly. Although he felt this maze sketch was already perfect, it was just theory on paper. After the maze was built, he would find a few slaves to test it and see how long it took them to get out.
Then he shook his head.
He looked at the train's panel, preparing to start crafting the accessories available for a Level 3 train.

chapters.title: Chapter 99 (2): The Ten Rules of the Stellar
chapters.content:
Outside the train, a group of slaves had gathered. Lao Zhu stood below the carriage, holding a draft and looking at Boss Mang's handwriting
Outside the train, a group of slaves had gathered.
Lao Zhu stood below the carriage, holding a draft and looking at Boss Mang's handwriting on it. He looked up at the slaves, his voice amplified by the train's sound system.
"The following ten rules must be followed by all members of the Stellar. Violators will be punished."
"1: Raping or molesting any female or male, goblin, or any other creature that joins the train in the future is punishable by death."
"2: Robbing others of their iron ore, food, etc., will result in ten strikes with a rod and a one-tier demotion in status."
"3: In a fight, whoever strikes first will receive ten strikes with a rod and a one-tier demotion in status."
"4: Causing trouble or inciting rebellion is punishable by death."
"5: Taking another's life without authorization is punishable by death."
"6: Hoarding iron ore, copper ore, or other resources will result in ten strikes with a rod and a one-tier demotion in status.""7: Hoarding weapons, Train Tokens, or other items during an external mission is punishable by death."
"8: Leaking any confidential information about the train to the outside world is punishable by death."
"9: Attempting to escape is punishable by death."
"10: Strictly obey and execute any orders from Train Captain Mang. Disobedience is punishable by death."
After reading the ten rules of the Stellar issued by Boss Mang, Lao Zhu put away the draft, his face expressionless as he looked at all the slaves. "You've heard the rules. Now, start mining."
Then he handed the draft to a woman beside him.
"Make four copies. Post one in each slave carriage."
"Understood."
With these ten rules—or rather laws—the Stellar finally became somewhat more official. In the lawless and chaotic world of the apocalypse, a few rules, rather than being a constraint, provided a sense of security.
"This is great."
Biao watched everything with a happy smile, his eyes full of satisfaction. He had truly watched the Stellar grow from a single carriage to its current scale of eleven carriages and over a thousand slaves.
And the Stellar was already a Level 3 train.
"By the way."
Lao Zhu stopped Biao, who was about to go on patrol. "Boss Mang is planning a major reform for the train soon. He's already told me. We'll need two more teams of guards. You're in charge of one team, and we'll need a second and third."
"Each team will have ten people, including the captain."
"You're a bit short-handed now. After all, with over a thousand slaves, there's no shortage of things to do every day."
"Boss Mang wants you to pick some candidates from the slaves."
"Hmm..."
Biao frowned and thought for a long time, then looked at the muscular woman among the slaves in the distance and hesitated. "Can a woman be a guard?"
"You mean that one?"
"She's not a bad choice. Find a few more candidates. If Boss Mang says no, we'll have someone to replace her."
"Alright."
—--
"Uncle Li, would anyone rape a goblin?"
In the crowd of slaves heading toward the mine, a young man walked beside Uncle Li, his pickaxe slung over his shoulder. He looked at the goblins also heading toward the iron mine and shrugged.
"But it's quite something."
"I never thought the first time I'd see a law against raping men would be in the apocalypse."
"It feels a bit absurd."
"..."
Uncle Li's eyes narrowed slightly. He didn't speak. He seemed to have thought of a new plan. The most important information in these ten rules was the demotion in status!
Currently, there were only three statuses on the train.
Tier 1 slave, Tier 2 slave, and Tier 3 slave.
The guards had no status distinction.
That Li Shiji, who had gotten ahead with his professional knowledge, also had Tier 1 slave status. Boss Mang couldn't possibly make Tier 1 slaves the highest status, nor could he fail to distinguish the guards' status.
From the information revealed, he vaguely guessed that Boss Mang was very likely to carry out a major reform of the train, and the core of the reform was the status system—clearly defining everyone's status at a certain level.
This also meant that as long as he found the right opportunity, he could move up in this reform.
"Uncle Li, what are you spacing out about?"
Seeing that Uncle Li hadn't answered, the young man leaned in curiously.
"..."
Uncle Li shot the young man an irritated look. "I've already thought of a new plan. Just be patient."
He'd only bothered talking to the young man in the first place because he saw potential and was considering making him a confidant once he moved up.
Now...
He was starting to wonder if he'd made a mistake. The kid was getting on his nerves.
"Great."
The young man nodded, satisfied, and gave him a thumbs-up. "Go for it, Uncle Li. I knew you were the best."
...
Inside the Stellar.
Having dealt with all the trivial matters, Chen Mang sat alone in the control car. He glanced at his 60,000 units of iron ore and began a major construction spree.
First, the four mandatory accessories.
Mechanical Nano-Spiders, Combat Training Virtual Space, Internal Space Stabilizer, Soldier Exoskeleton Production Line.
He spent 4,000 units of iron ore to craft them all.
The Mechanical Nano-Spiders took the form of a fist-sized mother spider, taking up very little space. It was made entirely of steel and looked like an exquisite, handcrafted model.
It was linked to the Train Auxiliary AI.
The AI would detect the extent of any damage to the accessories and then control the Mechanical Nano-Spiders to produce enough nano-mechanical spiders for repairs.
He spent 50,000 units of iron ore to upgrade it straight to Level 10.
Yellow-grade accessories were more expensive to upgrade; each level cost an additional 1,000 units of iron ore.
The accessory's upgrade effect was that each level allowed it to repair higher-level accessories.
For example, a Level 3 Mechanical Nano-Spiders could only produce spiders capable of repairing Level 3 damaged accessories, while a Level 10 one could repair Level 10 damaged accessories.
At the same time, he gained two Advanced Effects.
[Mechanical Nano-Spiders Level 5 Advanced Effect]:
Increases repair speed.
[Mechanical Nano-Spiders Level 10 Advanced Effect]:
Can produce a larger number of nano-spiders simultaneously.
Both Advanced Effects were quite practical.
The first reduced the time needed for repairs, and the second allowed for simultaneous repair of multiple damaged accessories.
While these effects might not seem significant during downtime—a little extra time hardly mattered—they would be crucial in the middle of battle.
Producing nano-spiders consumed iron ore.
Chen Mang looked at the control console screen, at the 62% integrity of the No. 4 Living Quarters, the 78% integrity of the Cola Production Line, and so on. "Repair all damaged accessories on the train to 100% integrity."
"Understood."
The AI's crisp, mechanical voice soon sounded in the control car. "Total cost: 3,800 units of iron ore. Proceed with repairs?"
"Proceed."
The next moment, the steel spider he had placed on the control console lifted its abdomen slightly. Countless, minuscule nano-mechanical spiders poured out of its birth canal—a black tide that squeezed through the cracks in the control car door.
Normal spiderlings were already tiny, almost cute.
These nano-mechanical spiders were about one-twentieth the size of a normal spiderling.
About three minutes later, Chen Mang looked at the screen on the control console again. It now showed that all the accessories on his train had been repaired to full integrity. He raised an eyebrow. This accessory was quite useful.
Most importantly, it saved money.
Replacing all those damaged accessories would have cost tens of thousands of iron ore. The repair only cost 3,800 units.
The grade, level, and extent of damage of an accessory all affected the number of nano-spiders needed and, thus, the amount of iron ore consumed.
The accessory was small.
He decided to just leave it on the table next to the control console as a decoration. It looked quite nice.
He glanced down and saw the "Immediate Self-Destruct" and "Immediate Ejection" buttons on the console. The self-destruct button came with a plastic cover to prevent accidental activation. The ejection button, which had been bare before, now also had a cover.
This was a new option he had found in the "Personalized Customization" menu after the train reached Level 3.
He could add a plastic cover with a fingerprint lock to any button on the control console for 100 units of iron ore.
There was no reason not to install it. It just didn't have the secondary confirmation on the screen like the self-destruct button.
Chen Mang then turned his attention to the Combat Training Virtual Space accessory. He had placed it in the No. 5 Guard Carriage. He stood up and walked out of the control car, heading to the No. 5 carriage to experience it for himself.
Biao and the others were outside, supervising the slaves' work; they weren't in the carriage.
Only Ji Chuchu and a few other minor celebrities were there, chatting and laughing. When they saw Chen Mang enter, their smiles quickly vanished, and they stood in a line, their voices small and fearful. "Boss Mang."
"Mm."
Chen Mang nodded without looking at them, his eyes narrowing as he focused on the machine before him. It was a device similar to a spa capsule, with a leather sofa inside and a glass lid on top.
When a person lies down inside, several wires with suction cups would attach to their scalp, projecting their consciousness into a virtual space.
The capsule would also fill with a nutrient solution to maintain the user's physical health.
After studying it for a moment, he stripped off his clothes and lay down naked in the Combat Training Virtual Space. As the nutrient solution filled the capsule, his consciousness was projected into another space.

chapters.title: Chapter 111 - 111: Twelve Scrolls of Military Documents, Each Scroll Bears My Name.
chapters.content:
"However..."
Uncle Li turned to look at the young man rolling around on the bed behind him, his lips slightly parted but no words came out. He couldn't find a way to refute. After a long while, he muttered in a daze.
"But how dare you intercept Lord Mang?"
"Because I thought that compiling daily data for so many people must be an extremely troublesome task. Uncle Li, you happen to be proficient in this, and the train is just short of such a person. Of course, I had to recommend myself."
"You..."
"What about me?"
"This process isn't right! Success can't be this simple!"
Uncle Li felt as if his values were being shattered, finding it hard to accept for a moment: "If you had the ability to recommend yourself, why were you only earning a few thousand a month before?"
He had always believed.
Talent is like the shit in your belly; only when a tip peeks out from behind can others see that you have talent. Otherwise, even if your belly is full of shit, no one can tell.
So his approach had always been to showcase his talent.
But this young man had told him a more straightforward and crude method.
Throw it in someone else's face.
"Me?"
The young man lying on the bed spoke somewhat irritably: "Uncle Li, I'm just a young man from a no-name town with no skills. What can I recommend myself for? And I just recommended you, not me. It's you who have the skills, not me."
"But..."
"Well, in the end, it was my plan that succeeded, so I have some credit. Let me make it clear first, I don't understand any of this, so you'll need to be patient when you start teaching me."
"Alright."
After a long while, Uncle Li nodded heavily, took a deep breath, and turned to look out the window, his eyes filled with pride. Even his back straightened a bit.
No matter what.
The plan had finally succeeded, and he had finally become a middle manager of the Stellar Train. Now was his time to shine!
At this moment—
The door of Carriage 6 for high-level talents was pushed open, and Li Shiji walked in holding two steaming Roujiamo. Seeing Uncle Li and the young man, he was momentarily stunned, then suddenly laughed.
"Looks like your plan succeeded?"
"Huh?"
Uncle Li's body froze in place, his eyes filled with confusion as he looked at Li Shiji.
"What huh? I was lying behind you eating last time when you were discussing how to suppress the Slave rebellion. From what I gathered, you've been planning this for a long time, but kept failing. I didn't expect your plan to suddenly succeed now. Well done."
"Why were you lying down eating?"
"Digging ore all day makes my back ache. Can't a man eat lying down?"
The young man sitting next to Uncle Li stood up, his eyes filled with pride as he smiled: "Uncle Li and I are responsible for the daily data compilation and verification of the residents' Iron Ore and Stellar Coupons. We're both treated as Level 3 high-level talents."
"That's a good job."
Li Shiji sighed deeply, his eyes filled with envy: "This job can be done continuously. Unlike me, after finishing the maze, I don't know what to do next. Lord Mang hasn't given me any new tasks either, making me feel a bit guilty even eating steamed buns now."
"Before you came, this carriage was just me, quite lonely. Now I finally have someone to chat with."
"Want some Roujiamo? I just heated them."
"Well..."
Uncle Li hesitated for a moment before looking toward Carriage 5 behind Li Shiji and asking: "You came from Carriage 5? Train Conductor Zhu just told me Ji Chuchu is in Carriage 5 and not to enter it casually."
"Oh, that."
Li Shiji waved his hand: "Right now, only Ji Chuchu lives in Carriage 5. Lao Zhu set up a bed curtain for her. Passing by is no big deal, just don't casually lift the curtain and crawl in."
"I just heated two Roujiamo, here you go. Consider it a welcome treat. I'll heat a few more later."
"Heh"
"This is much better than bread slices. I've been eating a dozen a day these days, so satisfying!"
"Oh right, it's been a while since you had a smoke, huh?"
Li Shiji smiled, pulling out a pack of cigarettes from his pocket and tossing it to the two: "Lord Mang just rewarded me with 100 Stellar Coupons. I bought two packs of cigarettes for 4 Stellar Coupons. Here's a pack for you to smoke."
"Aren't you saving up to buy a refrigerator?"
Uncle Li took the pack of cigarettes with both hands and handed it to the young man beside him: "Many people are planning to save the Stellar Coupons they earn to buy a refrigerator."
"That's not as comfortable as living in this carriage. The store inside has a lot of good stuff."
Li Shiji suddenly thought of something, stood up, and walked over to the two: "Train Conductor Zhu put the store in a refrigerator. That refrigerator is in Carriage 11. I'll take you to see it. I'll pay for whatever you buy."
"We're all treated as Level 3 high-level talents, earning two Stellar Coupons a day."
"It's enough."
"Let's go, come with me to see. It's a good time now since everyone's working, the store is less crowded, and we can take our time looking."
Inside the Stellar Train.
Sitting at the control panel, Chen Mang was looking at the robot in front of him and... a loose iron box.
Yes.
That drone had dropped a box, and when the four sides opened, this robot crawled out. He took the box with him when he left. Though so far, he hadn't found anything special about it.
It's not a special item.
And the box can't be reassembled; it's just loose. But since it's something from an S-Rank Job Change Quest, he decided to collect it and stuff it in the refrigerator. There's a Level 10 refrigerator in his train room.
It's chilling some cola.
And other miscellaneous things he's collected, which might come in handy someday.
As for this robot...
Special Item: Life Robot.
Item Effect: Can serve as the body of a 'Train Auxiliary AI' and perform light physical tasks.
The robot's exterior is smooth blue steel, painted, with no exposed wires or armor. There are no interfaces for heavy weaponry; it's just a life robot with minimal combat capabilities.
It can be an assistant.
"Can you enter?"
"Yes."
The train soon echoed with the mechanical electronic voice of the AI. Then, a wire extended from the control panel screen towards the robot. Soon, the robot stood up, facing Chen Mang.
"..."
Chen Mang frowned slightly, tilting his head to look at the screen beside him: "Can you still control those accessories now?"
"Yes."
The robot's speaker emitted a slightly muffled mechanical electronic voice: "I'm a Level 10 AI, with higher computational power and intelligence. The robot only occupies a part of my consciousness. Most of my consciousness remains in the Train Auxiliary AI, and my powerful computational power allows me to multitask."
"Currently, activating all train accessories would only consume 37% of my total computational power."
"If I could eat."
"I could even leisurely crack a few melon seeds."
Chen Mang looked at the robot in front of him, pausing for a moment: "I'll give you a name."
"Okay."
"Let's call you Xiao Ai."
"Okay, Master. You can command Xiao Ai anytime."
This robot is just a side dish in this harvest, not even a snack. The real appetizers are the special item and two blueprints he got from that Level 4 train.
All special items have no grade or level; most are small auxiliary items for individual use.
Like the special item in his hand.
Special Item: Salted Fish Hairpin.
Item Effect: While wearing this hairpin, you can breathe underwater for ten minutes.
It looks like a salted fish hairpin, clipped onto the head. He tried it on, looked in the mirror, and immediately took it off, placing it in a drawer.
Wearing it makes one look a bit silly.
An item that might be useful at certain times.
Then he looked at the two blueprints.
The first blueprint is a green-grade accessory "Nitrogen Tailjet," and the second is a yellow-grade accessory blueprint "Bunny Cloud."
"Well, well"
Chen Mang looked at the second yellow-grade vehicle accessory blueprint, a flash of surprise in his eyes. This time, he really hit the jackpot.
Last time he went to the Kunlun Mountains, a train left an extremely deep impression on him. That train had cloud wheels and could fly in the air. He was still a Level 2 train then, and that scene left him in awe.
He had wondered when his Stellar Train could also fly in the sky.
He didn't expect it to be so soon!
"Bunny Cloud" is a special type of wheel, cloud-shaped, allowing the train to fly in the sky. However, it's temporarily unusable. Only when the train's maximum speed reaches 650 km/h can a train equipped with Bunny Cloud wheels fly in the sky.
Even if he upgrades "Bunny Cloud" to Level 10 now, he still can't reach that speed limit.
Normally.
Level 4 or 5 trains, even Level 6 trains, can't reach that base speed limit.
To achieve that speed, some speed-enhancing accessories are needed, like the green-grade accessory "Nitrogen Tailjet," which increases train speed.
Presumably, this Level 4 train also started collecting speed-enhancing accessories after obtaining the "Bunny Cloud" blueprint, preparing to reach that speed limit and fly the train in the air.
Unfortunately...
It was cut short halfway, poor kid.
After organizing all the loot from this train, he looked at the resource units on the train panel.
430,000 units of Iron Ore, 750,000 units of Copper Ore, 224,000 units of Wood.
120,000 units of Spider Silk, 180,000 units of Crimson Heartstone, 1,158 units of Corpse Meat.
He glanced at the conditions for upgrading to Level 4 train.
Upgrade Conditions: Need to have 18 carriages, four essential vehicle accessories fully crafted, consume 10,000 units of Level 2 Iron Ore, and the total level of all accessories in the train must exceed 80.
After crafting three ordinary carriages, he finally met the 18-carriage requirement.
Thus, all conditions for upgrading to Level 4 train were met. As for the condition that's quite challenging for other trains, "total accessory levels exceeding 80," for him... when he was a Level 2 train, he already surpassed that number.
As for now.
After consuming 100,000 units of Iron Ore.
The next moment—
A panel appeared before him.
Your train has upgraded to Level 4.
More craftable accessories will be unlocked, and you have successfully transitioned to a Mechanical Train with S-Rank potential.
On the train panel, a new section called "Reputation Points" appeared. His current Reputation Points are 30.
The detailed record shows that the regional announcement of "Iron Ridge Wasteland" increased his Reputation Points by 10, and the regional announcement of "Shahe Plain" increased it by another 20, totaling 30 Reputation Points.
And at the moment of successful upgrade!
The "Train Radio" finally fully joined the Shahe Plain. From this moment on, he could no longer return to the Iron Ridge Wasteland, and the abandoned Goblin Train at the bottom of the "Doomsday Abyss" would forever remain there.
Until one day, the Goblin Train, covered in dust and spiderwebs, long forgotten, suddenly welcomes its owner.
This is Doba's train.
Upon learning that this Goblin Train was crafted by Doba alone, groping in absolute darkness to find a pickaxe and then Iron Ore, bit by bit, spending who knows how much time, he couldn't bear to feed this abandoned Goblin Train to the "Geothermal Furnace."
It wouldn't give him much Iron Ore.
Better to leave it there.
Perhaps...
One day, he will return there and tell Doba.
"Now you are the Goblin King."
He doesn't know if he can achieve such a monumental task as helping Doba rebuild the Goblin civilization, but Doba's sincere, admiring, and fervent gaze made him somewhat unable to meet it directly. If, one day in the future, he can truly accomplish this, then this abandoned Goblin Train, lying dormant at the bottom of the Doomsday Abyss, will silently record everything like a cosmic historian.
At least leave a memento.
Suddenly, the "Train Radio" emitted a series of beeps. Many people were chatting in the radio, and the chat room's top-right corner showed a total of 289 trains in this chat room.
This number is about the same as in the Iron Ridge Wasteland.
Wait, it should be much less than the Iron Ridge Wasteland, since only Level 2 trains can craft a Train Radio, and there are still many Level 1 trains in the Iron Ridge Wasteland, as well as some Level 2 trains that haven't crafted a Train Radio.
"No way..."
Chen Mang looked at the chat records in the chat room, his mouth twitching slightly.
Why are there twelve scrolls of military documents, each scroll bearing my name again?
He had thought that the Train Radio in the Shahe Plain would be discussing something else, but it turns out they're still talking about him, no different from the Train Radio in the Iron Ridge Wasteland.
Everyone in the chat room is discussing the "Stellar Train" that completed the S-Rank Job Change Quest.
The regional announcement of "Shahe Plain" leaked his train's name, and now everyone knows that a train called the Stellar successfully completed this S-Rank Job Change Quest.

chapters.title: Chapter 112 - 112: "Supermodel Effect Quantity Leaderboard"
chapters.content:
At that moment—
A single comment shattered the discussion atmosphere in the Train Radio.
Broken Defense Train: "Quick, check the leaderboard! The Stellar Train has successfully upgraded to a Level 4 Train and officially entered the green zone. Holy shit, he's topped the chart!!!"
Ten Steps One Kill Train: "What chart? Even if he completed an S-Rank Job Change Quest, that just means he has high potential. How could he directly top the chart?"
Cosmos Train: "That guy's definitely mistaken, but... the Stellar Train is indeed outrageous. A score of 6,524? That's no joke. Normally, a Train just upgraded to Level 4 wouldn't have that kind of score. Even many Level 5 Trains don't have that high a score!"
Only Love One Train: "A score of 6,524 is genuinely insane. He's already ranked 34th on the Shahe Plain Power Value Regional Leaderboard. This guy just upgraded to Level 4. Did he stuff all the Survivors from the white zone into his Train? How can he even sustain that? If he can't find ore in two days, all the Slaves will starve to death."
Broken Defense Train: "You're looking at the wrong leaderboard! I'm not talking about that one. I'm talking about the Supermodel Effect Quantity Leaderboard. He's topped that one! Go check it out!"
Cosmos Train: "Just checked. He's really number one. My only thought is... can I add a question mark?"
Ten Steps One Kill Train: "?"
Only Love One Train: "?"
"Ah..."
Chen Mang helplessly looked at the information flooding the Train Radio. He just wanted to quietly develop his Train. He really didn't need everyone constantly watching him. His original score was 5,412. After upgrading to Level 4, his Train's base score became 1,000.
He also obtained a new red-tier Vehicle Component, the Ground Burst Missile, and upgraded some miscellaneous components in the Geothermal Furnace. He also picked up a new batch of Survivors.
Then, his Train's score jumped to... 6,542.
That does seem a bit high.
He glanced at the Shahe Plain Regional Leaderboard, where the Stellar Train was ranked 34th, sandwiched between a bunch of Level 5 Trains. The highest-ranked Level 4 Train had a score of 4,500, while most other Level 4 Trains were around 3,800.
And—
In the Iron Ridge Wasteland, there was only one leaderboard: the Regional Power Value Leaderboard. But in the Shahe Plain, there were several leaderboards, such as—
Supermodel Effect Quantity Leaderboard
1st Place: Stellar Train, S-Rank Potential Level 4 Mechanical Train, 57 Supermodel Effects.
2nd Place: Wife Hunter Train, S-Rank Potential Level 6 Flesh Train, 28 Supermodel Effects.
3rd Place: Kill a Bloody Path Train, A-Rank Potential Level 6 Flesh Train, 26 Supermodel Effects.
4th Place: World Weary Train, A-Rank Potential Level 5 Mechanical Train, 24 Supermodel Effects.
This was the first time Chen Mang had seen this leaderboard. If it was solely based on the number of Supermodel Effects, then yes, no one could compete with him. After all, he effectively had an infinite supply of Murphy Stones. How could anyone challenge that?
There was no contest.
And the most important thing—
He had discovered a few days ago that Supermodel Effects marked as "None" were still counted in the score and the total number of Supermodel Effects.
At this moment—
A data nerd had already emerged in the Train Radio.
Broken Defense Train: "Let me break it down for you. Yellow-tier Components can be upgraded to Level 5 at most. A Level 3 Train has 7 craftable yellow-tier Components, a Level 4 Train has 3, and Level 5 and 6 Trains each have 2. Only purple-tier Components can be upgraded to Level 10, and even Level 6 Trains don't have craftable purple-tier Components."
"In other words, a normal Level 6 Train, if it crafts all its yellow-tier Components, can obtain a total of 14 Supermodel Effects."
"If you manage to get a few yellow-tier Blueprints or some Murphy Stones, you can have even more Supermodel Effects."
"For example, the previous top-ranked Wife Hunter Train has a whopping 28 Supermodel Effects."
"But—"
"The Stellar Train is only a Level 4 Train, and it just upgraded to Level 4. It hasn't even had time to craft its Level 4 Components, meaning it can only craft 7 yellow-tier Components at most, resulting in a maximum of 7 Supermodel Effects."
"As everyone knows, Murphy Stones can break level restrictions, and the most cost-effective way to use Murphy Stones for Supermodel Effects is to apply them to green-tier Components. Two Murphy Stones can give you one Supermodel Effect."
"And the Stellar Train has a staggering 57 Supermodel Effects, which is 50 above the normal value."
"That means—"
"He either has an extra 50 yellow-tier Component Blueprints or has consumed 100 Murphy Stones."
"You decide which one sounds more realistic."
Cosmos Train: "? Can I say both conclusions sound equally unrealistic? Are yellow-tier Component Blueprints and Murphy Stones as common as cabbages? Since when did the numbers get so high?"
Broken Defense Train: "Maybe he went through a lot of Fortuitous Encounter maps and cleared them all."
Azure Dragon Train: "Let me chime in. There are no Fortuitous Encounter maps in the white zone."
"They're really sensitive to data..."
Chen Mang let out a long, helpless sigh. These people were incredibly serious about digging up information about others' Trains. Unfortunately, their logical deductions were correct, but... the answers were all wrong.
100 Murphy Stones?
That was just insulting.
If resources weren't a limitation, he could give you 9,999 Supermodel Effects in minutes.
However—
His gaze fell on the World Weary Train, ranked 4th on the Supermodel Effect Quantity Leaderboard. It was an A-Rank Potential Level 5 Mechanical Train. Among the top ten on this leaderboard, only two were Mechanical Trains.
One was him, and the other was the World Weary Train.
The other eight were all Flesh Trains.
After all, Flesh Trains, which constantly hunt monsters, have a higher chance of dropping Murphy Stones compared to others. It's not like you can mine ore and suddenly find a Murphy Stone. What really interested him about the World Weary Train wasn't just that it was one of the two Mechanical Trains in the top ten.
It was because it was... an A-Rank Potential.
He remembered the A-Rank difficulty Job Change Quest for Mechanical Trains very clearly. It required training the AI to develop human emotions and then falling in love with it. This guy was a true hardcore player.
He had to admire someone willing to put their life in someone else's hands.
What if they break up one day?
If the AI presses the Immediate Self-Destruct button, it'll be hilarious. After completing this Job Change Quest, the AI gains full control over the Train, equivalent to the Train Conductor's authority.
But—
The effort wasn't without reward. Being able to rank above a bunch of Level 6 Trains as a Level 5 Train showed that the rewards were quite substantial.
Mechanical Trains and Flesh Trains were just different types of Trains. The only difference was that Mechanical Trains were more sci-fi, while Flesh Trains looked more terrifying, even more monstrous than some monsters.
Flesh Trains don't need to mine ore or rely on Slaves.
Upgrading the Train and its Components requires monster flesh. As long as you keep killing monsters, you can keep upgrading. The Train can function normally with just one person, as long as you don't mind the loneliness.
Mechanical Trains can't do that. A single Train Conductor can't operate it alone; you need a whole team.
In terms of mortality rates—
Mechanical Trains are far lower than Flesh Trains. Mechanical Trains can avoid danger; just stay away from the scary monsters. But Flesh Trains can't avoid it. If you avoid it this time, will you avoid it next time? If you keep avoiding it, how will your Train ever upgrade?
Because of this—
All Flesh Trains in the Shahe Plain only stop there during rest periods. The rest of the time, they're charging through the monster-infested regions of the Kunlun Mountains.
The more bosses you kill—
The more Murphy Stones and yellow-tier Component Blueprints you'll drop, naturally ranking higher on the Supermodel Effect Leaderboard.
Mechanical Trains and Flesh Trains actually get along quite well.
After all, Flesh Trains don't need ore or Slaves, so there's basically no conflict of interest with Mechanical Trains, except for the occasional muttered insults about Flesh Trains being a bunch of lunatics.
After watching the Train Radio for a while, Chen Mang turned his attention away. He didn't pay too much attention and had no intention of joining the conversation. His current goal was to quietly develop.
To survive.
And to live a little better.
And at that moment—
Someone privately messaged him.
Azure Dragon Train: "Hello, I'm the one who yelled 'Mom, I can't tell!' in your Train today. I went to an Underwater Labyrinth Fortuitous Encounter and chose an S-Rank difficulty maze task. Fortunately, I ended up in your Train. Of course, the task failed."
"But that's not important. I found a new Fortuitous Encounter. Would you be interested in exploring it with me?"
"..."
Chen Mang's expression turned slightly strange as he looked at the private message. He now realized that the consciousness in that robot was actually a real person's consciousness. This guy had taken on an S-Rank difficulty maze task from somewhere and ended up in his Train?
What's a Fortuitous Encounter?
Hmm... how to explain it? They're hidden maps that often have tasks. Clearing them gives you a lot of rewards. I've actually known about this Fortuitous Encounter for over a month, but I never found the right person to team up with. You're the best candidate.
How so?
That day, was it you driving the Train on the nearly 90-degree cliff face in the Kunlun Mountains?
Was that you flying in the air?
Yes, it was me. That Fortuitous Encounter map is called the Tower of Heaven. Only your Train can go up there. No one else can.
But you can fly, can't you?
...I can only fly up to 3,000 meters. That map is at 5,000 meters. You can tow my Train up there. I'll provide the coordinates, and you provide the means. If it's a cooperative task inside, we'll split the rewards 50-50. If it's individual tasks, we'll each rely on our own skills.
On the Shahe Plain—
The Bald Man sitting in the Azure Dragon Train's control room sighed with emotion. He really hadn't expected it to be that guy. When he heard that the Stellar Train had completed an S-Rank Job Change Quest and entered the Shahe Plain, he knew it was the same Train.
If it were in different regions, it might not be the same person.
But in these neighboring regions, how could it not be the same guy?
That guy...
He had secretly calculated that the Spider Leg Component needed to be upgraded to at least Level 13 to traverse cliff faces like that. Where on earth did he get so many Murphy Stones?
And he knew more than those people in the Train Radio.
This guy had upgraded at least a hundred Refrigerators to Level 5 or 10. The number of Murphy Stones he'd consumed far exceeded what that data nerd had guessed.
Right!
He suddenly slapped his forehead. The other guy must be on high alert right now, especially since his S-Rank task failed because of the Stellar Train. With so many Murphy Stones in hand, he must suspect that he's planning something.
But he really didn't have any such intentions.
His only joy was exploring Fortuitous Encounters and unlocking hidden maps.
The rewards were one thing, but more importantly, it gave him a rare sense of happiness in this godforsaken world. He'd found the Tower of Heaven Fortuitous Encounter Map a long time ago but had never been able to reach it. Now that he'd finally caught the Stellar Train, he didn't want to miss the chance to see what was up there.
Just as he was about to say something more to dispel the other guy's suspicions—
He quickly received a reply.
Stellar Train: "Sure, but it'll have to be in half a month."
"Huh..."
Now it was his turn to be stunned. He agreed just like that? He was a Level 5 Train. Wasn't this guy afraid? Either he was incredibly bold or just plain stupid...
Then—
He remembered the half-hour of torment in the other guy's Train and the first impression he'd formed of this Train Conductor he'd never met.
The guy really wasn't afraid of him.
He was just... tough.
Now, it seemed like he was the one who should be worried about being double-crossed.
After replying and settling on a time, Chen Mang stopped paying attention to the Train Radio.
He was indeed curious about this Fortuitous Encounter Map. He'd never seen one in the white zone. He was also curious about the special places in the Iron Ridge Wasteland, like the Doomsday Abyss, but that seemed more like a unique location rather than a Fortuitous Encounter Map.
But he wasn't going now.
His Train had just upgraded to Level 4, and there were many things he hadn't crafted yet. His Armor was already Level 6. By the time he got the Ground Burst Missile to Level 6, he wanted to see...
Who would dare mess with him!
He was even eager to test the power of the Ground Burst Missile.
Of course, before that, he needed to upgrade the few craftable Components from Level 3 to Level 10. Half a month shoul
d be enough to build a half-maxed Level 4 Train. Then he could go out and explore.
With so much copper ore piled up in the Stellar Train, he needed to find an opportunity to test its firepower and see how it performed.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 113 - 113: "The patient has a hangnail on the second finger of their right hand."
chapters.content:
"Central Air Conditioning," "Permanent Shock Absorption," "Medical Bay."
These three yellow-grade Vehicle Components were all optional parts for a Level 3 Train, and he had already crafted them all back in the Iron Ridge Wasteland. However, he hadn't upgraded them at the time due to a lack of Iron Ore.
Upgrading yellow-grade Vehicle Components from Level 1 to Level 10 generally required 45,000 units of Iron Ore, which was significantly more expensive than white-grade components. White-grade components often only needed 4,400 units of Iron Ore to upgrade from Level 1 to Level 10.
After consuming 45,000 units of Iron Ore.
The yellow-grade component "Central Air Conditioning" was quickly upgraded to Level 10 and gained two Supermodel Effects!-
"Central Air Conditioning Level 5 Supermodel Effect": Reduces energy consumption by half.
"Central Air Conditioning Level 10 Supermodel Effect": When operating the fresh air system, if toxic gases or extremely poor air quality are detected outside, it will immediately stop air intake. This effect requires the "Oxygen Generator" to be upgraded to Level 10 and obtain its corresponding Supermodel Effect, as well as fully upgrading the Train Auxiliary AI.
The Central Air Conditioning comes with a fresh air system that can effectively improve the air quality inside the Train.
Upgrading had no additional effects.
It basically functioned within the normal temperature range of a standard air conditioner, unable to directly heat up to over a hundred degrees or cool down to negative two hundred degrees Celsius. However, in extremely cold or hot environments, it could still maintain a normal temperature range inside the Train.
The only downside was that energy consumption would increase significantly.
This was where the Level 5 Supermodel Effect came into play, which was a decent universal effect.
The Level 10 Supermodel Effect only came into play in specific environments and was mostly unused. But when it was needed, it played a critical role. The Level 10 Supermodel Effect of the "Oxygen Generator" was to analyze the surrounding air quality in real-time and synchronize the report to the Train Auxiliary AI.
The weather was getting colder.
Winter was approaching, and by then, Trains that hadn't been upgraded to Level 3 and couldn't craft the "Central Air Conditioning" component would likely struggle, and many people might freeze to death.
The Train Conductor naturally had ways to stay warm, as the highest treatment on a Train was always prioritized for the Conductor. However, many Slaves would likely freeze to death, and even if they didn't, frostbite would significantly reduce their work efficiency.
Residents on his Train didn't have to worry about this.
Inside the Train, there was air conditioning, and outside, they had clothes with the "Temperature Lock" effect. This effect was a Supermodel Effect obtained by upgrading the "Clothing Customization Production Line" to Level 5. Most people couldn't upgrade this component to Level 5, as even if they had Murphy Stones, they wouldn't want to spend them on this component. Moreover, only Level 4 Trains or higher had a chance to obtain Murphy Stones, as they didn't appear in lower-level areas.
Additionally—
Residents on his Train also had "Bread Slices" and "Mineral Water," which had Supermodel Effects that, when consumed long-term, could enhance physical fitness and reduce the likelihood of falling ill.
It could be said.
The living conditions of the residents on his Train were almost superior to those on all other Trains in the Iron Ridge Wasteland and Shahe Plain.
At least, under the daily high-pressure workload, no resident had died from exhaustion or serious illness so far, which was enough to prove that the Train was doing an excellent job in this regard.
In the apocalypse, what more could one ask for with such an environment?
Chen Mang then turned his attention to the yellow-grade component "Permanent Shock Absorption." The effect of this component was to significantly reduce the impact force when the Train was subjected to a violent collision, thereby protecting the lifeforms inside the Train.
A very useful component.
At least when he was driving deep underground and collided with that Level 4 Train, he didn't feel much impact. At the time, the "Permanent Shock Absorption" was only Level 1. If he hadn't had this component, colliding with another Train at such a high speed would have been unbearable.
After consuming 45,000 units of Iron Ore, he upgraded this component to Level 10.
With each upgrade, the effect of reducing impact force was enhanced. After reaching Level 10, the impact force from a violent collision was much smaller, and it gained two Supermodel Effects.
"Permanent Shock Absorption Level 5 Supermodel Effect": None.
"Permanent Shock Absorption Level 10 Supermodel Effect": None.
Both Supermodel Effects were "None," but he still upgraded it to Level 10, not for the Supermodel Effects, but for the upgrade effects themselves.
He then spent another 45,000 units of Iron Ore to upgrade the "Medical Bay" to Level 10. Although he already had a Level 10 "Simple First-Aid Kit," which could treat external injuries and even regenerate severed limbs, he wanted to see if the yellow-grade component would have stronger effects after being upgraded to Level 10.
Upgrading had no additional effects.
It was the same as before.
But.
The two Supermodel Effects it gained could almost be described as "insane."
"Medical Bay Level 5 Supermodel Effect": Can regenerate severed limbs.
"Medical Bay Level 10 Supermodel Effect": Humans have never truly had any incurable diseases. It can treat any disease, including so-called cancer. Treating different diseases requires consuming different units of Iron Ore. The more severe the illness, the more resources are needed. Additionally, replacing any mechanical organs in the Medical Bay will cause no discomfort.
The Level 5 Supermodel Effect overlapped with the Level 10 Supermodel Effect of the "Simple First-Aid Kit."
However, the "Simple First-Aid Kit" was a one-time use, while this one could be used permanently.
Moreover, using the "Simple First-Aid Kit" to suture a severed limb required a professional. It didn't have to be a professional surgeon, but if the suturing went wrong, they could just take it off and try again. Suturing dozens of times would eventually get it right.
The only downside was that the whole process was quite painful.
The likelihood of dying from the pain was low.
But passing out from the pain was still possible.
With the "Medical Bay," there was no need to worry about this. For limb regeneration, all you had to do was place the severed limb and the patient into the Medical Bay, close the lid, and after a minute, open it to find the limb fully regenerated. The entire process was completely painless and incredibly easy.
Of course.
For the same limb regeneration, the "Medical Bay" consumed more resources than the "Simple First-Aid Kit."
The Level 10 Supermodel Effect of the "Medical Bay," if placed in peacetime, would be a technological product that would shock all of humanity. At least in the world before the apocalypse, nearly 90% of diseases were untreatable, including common colds.
New diseases were still being discovered occasionally.
It was like a game that occasionally produced bugs. With nearly ten billion people, it was completely understandable and normal for some strange things to pop up now and then.
"Hmm."
Chen Mang walked to Carriage 2 and placed the Medical Bay inside a Refrigerator in this carriage. After upgrading the Refrigerator to Level 10, it significantly increased the space utilization of each carriage. After all, adding a new carriage wasn't a simple task, as the Armor for the carriage had to be installed, and Armor wasn't cheap.
He stood there, looking at the Medical Bay, which was similar to the "Combat Training Virtual Space" in appearance but more technologically advanced. It was entirely white, and he remained silent, lost in thought.
He didn't seem to have any physical issues or diseases.
But after some consideration, he still took off his clothes and lay inside.
As he lay in the bay, the lid quickly rose from both sides and slowly closed. At the same time, a white, viscous liquid began to overflow from the bottom of the Medical Bay, soon enveloping his entire body. A small screen appeared on the inside of the lid.
"Detected the following issues with the body: Lung integrity 78%, Heart integrity 89%, Limb integrity 99%, Genital integrity 87%, Liver integrity..."
"To target a specific organ for repair, please tap the corresponding organ on the screen, and the repair cost will be displayed."
"If repairing all, it will consume 43,000 units of Iron Ore."
"So expensive?!"
Chen Mang's first thought was that the price was absurd. He hadn't been injured, wasn't sick, and didn't even have a cold. He was just getting a full-body checkup, and after the checkup, he was told he needed to consume 43,000 units of Iron Ore?
This felt strangely familiar.
How much Iron Ore would it cost to treat a terminal illness?
And—
In the world before the apocalypse, when he went to the hospital for a checkup, the data he received included specific disease names, with a string of data that seemed extremely professional. This "Medical Bay" simply rated each organ's integrity?
It sounded strange, as if it were repairing Train components.
He could accept that other organs weren't at 100% integrity, but why were his limbs at 99%?
"My limbs are fine. I have no injuries."
He voiced his confusion.
The screen quickly displayed another line of text.
"The patient has a hangnail on the second finger of their right hand."
"..."
"Repair all."
In the next moment—
The white, viscous liquid began to flow rapidly from the bottom, covering his face and nostrils. He initially held his breath, but soon realized that the white, viscous liquid didn't interfere with his breathing at all.
One minute later.
The white, viscous liquid quickly receded, and Chen Mang climbed out of the Medical Bay. He walked to a full-length mirror nearby and examined himself, his eyes filled with disbelief.
The person in the mirror—
Was he really that handsome?
He rarely used the word "handsome" to describe himself. He always believed that for men, appearance wasn't a high-priority compliment.
But this time, he truly felt handsome. The person in the mirror had a completely different aura and energy compared to before.
He had never felt so light and comfortable in his body. This feeling—
It was like a factory reset.
He looked at his right hand and noticed that even the hangnail had been completely repaired. He glanced down and saw that nothing had grown larger.
It seemed the "Medical Bay" could only repair and not alter the original body. But that was fine—he was already more than sufficient. Any larger, and he'd have clearance issues in tunnels.
The 43,000 units of Iron Ore were well spent!
After putting on his set of High-Precision Clothes, he now felt like he could easily live another hundred years. If he continued using the Medical Bay, he might even live to three or four hundred.
After all, human death was largely caused by the irreversible decay of organs.
But now.
That "irreversible" had become "reversible"!
"Not bad."
Chen Mang, quite satisfied, took another look at himself in the mirror before heading back to the Train cabin. He decided not to make this component available to the residents for now—it was too expensive, and the Train couldn't afford it at the moment. The "Simple First-Aid Kit" would suffice.
Thus—
All craftable components for the Level 3 Train had been completed, except for the "Storage Box." He didn't need it for now, as there were already 100 Level 10 Refrigerators on the Train, providing more than enough storage.
"..."
In Carriage 5, the Advanced Talent Carriage, Ji Chuchu sat in her seat, looking out at the bustling scene outside. Train Conductor Zhu and others were at the entrance of Carriage 4, the Advanced Talent Carriage, busy moving Bread Slices to distribute as the residents' food for the day.
Lord Mang hadn't sought her out in a long time.
The minor celebrities who used to chat with her for company didn't have the authority to enter this carriage, leaving her with no one to talk to.
Ji Chuchu's expression gradually grew distant as her thoughts wandered. The Train had arrived at the Shahe Plain, and she wondered if Lord Mang still remembered what she had told him—that her best friend Yan Yao was hiding in a safe house in a villa in Sand River City.
Her position on the Train was limited by her circumstances.
Thanks to Lord Mang's current fondness for her, she didn't have to sell herself like the minor celebrities. But... how long would this favor last? She knew men better than she knew herself. She made a living off this—once the novelty wore off, it was easy for them to grow bored.
The only way to secure her position on the Train.
Was Yan Yao.
Her best friend was slightly more beautiful than her, still a virgin, and a celebrity with high capital. Even if Yan Yao couldn't rise to the top, Lord Mang would undoubtedly favor her more.
Then.
She could use Yan Yao to secure her own position on the Train. Moreover, Yan Yao didn't know anything—someone would have to teach her, and no one was more suitable than Ji Chuchu herself.
After a long while, she snapped out of her thoughts.
She looked down at a tube of lipstick in her hand. In the apocalypse, cosmetics were rare and precious. She had just bought this lipstick with Stellar Coupons at the store. She didn't know when Lord Mang would seek her out or when he would pass by this carriage. All she could do was maintain a perfect appearance so that the moment Lord Mang saw her, her beauty could provide him with some emotional value.
That was enough.
Outside the Stellar's Train cabin.
Lao Zhu, panting heavily, let out a long breath before wiping the sweat from his forehead. He leaned against the Train and looked at Biao Zi, who had come to fetch water. He pulled out a cigarette, stuck it in his mouth, and continued to breathe heavily.
"Working hard, Biao Zi? Saving up for a Train Token?"
"Hey, Biao Zi."
"How about naming it the 'Biao Zi' when you get it? I'll be your deputy conductor. I think following you has more potential."
