chapters.title: Chapter 114 - 114: Coffee Only Tastes Authentic When You Buy It Yourself
chapters.content:
"Stop teasing me, Train Conductor Zhu," Biao Zi said with a helpless shake of his head, forcing a bitter smile. He picked up a bottle of mineral water, downed it in one go, then wiped the water from the corner of his mouth. "Neither of us is cut out to buy the Train Token. We both know what we're like—we can't hold onto that kind of position."
"Besides," he continued, "haven't you played online games before? Joining a big guild in a game is far more rewarding than starting your own small one. Anyway, I'm done chatting with you. I've got to get back to patrol duty."
With that, Biao Zi grabbed some food for the guards, exchanged a few words with Lao Zhu, and left. The Train's current welfare system wasn't bad, but all the benefits were contingent on the residents working diligently. If you did well, you'd be rewarded. But if you tried to slack off and couldn't even dig up the basic 10 units of Iron Ore in a day, then sorry—the Train had more than just bread to offer. There were also batons. The former would fill you up, while the latter would clean you out.
Mining in the cavern was relatively safe. His main task during patrols was to prevent any accidents, like fights or disturbances, while also keeping an eye on things to ensure everyone was working.
Three days later.
As the whistle blew, many residents stopped their work. Under the guards' supervision, they began to line up in an orderly fashion to collect their daily rations. Based on how much they'd mined beyond the daily quota, they were also issued "Stellar Coupons."
"Alright," Uncle Li, sitting on a stool, looked at the number on the collar of the resident in front of him. "Resident 117, you've exceeded the quota by 7 units of Iron Ore over the past few days. With today's 3 units, that makes a total of 10 units. Here's your Stellar Coupon."
"Thank you, thank you!" The resident with the number 117 on his collar gratefully and excitedly accepted the Stellar Coupon, which was made from a mineral water bottle cap. He quickly left, making room for the next person in line.
Stellar Coupons were made from "mineral water bottle caps." The caps were placed on the ground, and after the Train ran over them, they were flattened into thin discs—a simple but effective anti-counterfeiting measure. No pickaxe or other tool could compress a bottle cap to that degree. And as for making a bigger scene? With so many eyes around, anyone capable of pulling that off would already be considered a top-tier talent. For now, this method was sufficient given the Train's current limitations.
Over the past few days, Uncle Li had assigned numbers to all the residents, including the middle management. This system made it easier to calculate daily mining quotas and distribute Stellar Coupons, saving a bit of time.
The man who received the Stellar Coupon carefully tucked it into his pocket, zipped it up, and wolfed down his food. Without a moment's rest, he grabbed his pickaxe and headed back to the Iron Ore to continue mining.
It was the end of the workday, and most people were done for the day, heading back to sleep. But he wanted to keep working. The Iron Ore he mined now could be turned in along with tomorrow's haul, allowing him to earn more Stellar Coupons. After all, mining opportunities weren't available every day, so he had to make the most of it while he could.
Still, he couldn't help but glance enviously at the group of tireless Goblins nearby. Their stamina seemed limitless. And, according to the Train's old-timers, those Goblins had no intelligence—they were like robots. Only one Goblin, named Doba, had any semblance of wisdom. The entire group followed Doba's orders, and they mined faster than anyone else, accumulating Stellar Coupons at an impressive rate. All the coupons went to Doba, who was like a slave master. It wouldn't be long before Doba saved up 1,000 Stellar Coupons.
"Hehe…" Doba, completely unfazed by exhaustion, leaned on his pickaxe and looked at the humans nearby with a gleam of satisfaction in his eyes. He had already saved over 200 Stellar Coupons, and all the Goblins' coupons were in his possession. Even Train Conductor Zhu couldn't earn coupons as fast as he could.
His goal? "That Refrigerator!" The first step in rebuilding the Goblin civilization was to secure their own territory. He wanted to buy as many refrigerators as possible to give his people ample living space. Even though his fellow Goblins had lost their intelligence, he believed they would eventually regain it. If he could recover, so could they. And this Human Prophet was truly remarkable. The Stellar Train was developing much faster than his old Goblin Train. The Human Prophet hadn't lied—he really could help rebuild the Goblin civilization. All Doba had to do was keep mining diligently to accelerate the Train's progress.
"Get to work!" Doba shouted. "Let those foolish humans see what it means to be a tireless and great Goblin!"
Full of energy, Doba swung his pickaxe and resumed mining.
By now, most people had already collected their food. Nearly half of the residents chose to continue mining. What if they ran out of energy? They could buy Cola! The ice-cold Cola not only tasted great but also significantly boosted their stamina. It was incredibly cheap too—10 bottles for just 1 Stellar Coupon. And they didn't have to take all 10 bottles at once; the shopkeeper would keep track of their remaining stock.
"Lord Mang is such a good man," a young man said after chugging a bottle of Cola. He let out a satisfied burp, feeling his body recharged. Taking a deep breath, he grabbed his pickaxe and, under the glow of the Train's headlights, began working through the night.
He had done the math. Drinking 3 bottles of Cola a day would allow him to extend his mining time to 18 hours, leaving just 6 hours for sleep. And he'd still feel fresh because the Cola was so effective at restoring energy. Over three days, he'd only spend 1 Stellar Coupon on Cola, but by exceeding the mining quota, he'd earn 3 Stellar Coupons—a net gain of 2 Coupons. It was a great deal!
At first, he hadn't told anyone about this strategy. But soon, he noticed more and more people catching on and copying him. It was frustrating—didn't they have minds of their own?
Inside the Train's living quarters.
Chen Mang, who had been trying to sleep, sighed deeply as the constant clinking of pickaxes outside kept him awake. He stood by the window, looking out at the people working, his expression complicated.
He really wanted to say, "Take a break, guys. Rome wasn't built in a day. Don't work yourselves to death—where would I find more Survivors?"
In recent days, the "Cola Production Line" accessory had been running non-stop. The production cost was 1 unit of Iron Ore per bottle, but in the store, it was sold at 1 Stellar Coupon for 10 bottles.
"Level 5 Supermodel Effect of the Cola Production Line": Can produce sugar-free or regular Cola.
"Level 10 Supermodel Effect of the Cola Production Line": Slowly restores stamina when consumed.
This was the only food item on the Train that could restore stamina. Back in the Doomsday Abyss, every Slave was given a bottle daily to keep their energy up. Once it was put on the store shelves, it was immediately snapped up.
Many people now drank 3 bottles of Cola a day and worked tirelessly with their pickaxes.
Mining efficiency had skyrocketed! Normally, in three days, the residents would have mined around 360,000 units of Iron Ore. But now, they had managed to dig up 510,000 units—almost all of them working overtime voluntarily. Some worked a few extra hours, while others slept only a few hours a day.
The two Level 2 Iron Ore mines had a total of 520,000 units. In just three days, they had almost exhausted them, leaving only 10,000 units. At this rate, the mines would be empty before dawn tomorrow.
"These people…" Chen Mang sighed in exasperation. When he used to give everyone free Cola, they didn't work nearly as hard. But now that they had to buy it themselves, they were going all out.
The reform seemed to be working, at least initially. It reminded him of the white-collar workers in his previous world who insisted on buying their own coffee. The coffee only tasted authentic when you bought it yourself. The free stuff from the company always felt a bit off, like it wasn't the real deal.
The Train's current stockpile of Iron Ore had reached—
650,000 units.
Well, he wasn't going to sleep anyway.
Chen Mang turned his attention to the 3D diagram of the "Ground Burst Missile" on the control panel. This was the most powerful weapon on the Train, and the only large-scale red-tier firepower accessory. Upgrading it required Iron Ore, while crafting it consumed Copper Ore. Crafting a Level 1 "Ground Burst Missile" required 10,000 units of Copper Ore, and upgrading it to Level 1 cost 50,000 units of Iron Ore. He had calculated that upgrading it to Level 5 would cost 750,000 units of Iron Ore, which he didn't have yet. For now, he'd focus on finding new mines—Iron Ore was in short supply.
The missile currently in Missile Car No. 14 was only Level 1. It was mostly for show, as its low level made it ineffective against most monsters. He planned to set it off like a firework tomorrow morning to see how it performed.
Late at night.
Most people on the Train were asleep, and even Doba was feeling the strain and ready to call it a day. But when he saw the seven or eight humans still mining, he couldn't help but feel a sense of bewilderment.
Were these people… turned into Goblins by the Train? How could they mine even more than his kind? Did they think they wouldn't live to see tomorrow?
Finally, morning arrived.
The Stellar Train set off once again, emerging from underground and switching to its Wind-Fire Wheels as it sped toward the unknown, searching for new mines. While efficiency had improved, Chen Mang was struggling to keep up. Where would he find so much Iron Ore?
The Train gradually slowed to a stop on a plain. Under the urging and shouting of Lao Zhu and others, all the residents were herded off the Train. They stood around, looking confused.
Where was the mine? They didn't see any.
Even the 400 Survivors were pushed off the Train and made to stand with the others. These Survivors hadn't been working; they were only given the bare minimum of a few slices of bread and a bottle of water each day. They had been left to watch enviously as the Stellar Train residents enjoyed better rations.
Chen Mang wanted them to feel the urgency to join the Stellar Train as official residents. Only then would they work hard.
Just then—
Under everyone's gaze, the mechanical hatch on the top of the last carriage, Missile Car No. 14, slowly opened with the sound of grinding gears. A pitch-black missile, exuding an intimidating aura, was slowly raised on a platform, angled 45 degrees toward the sky.
At the sight of this, everyone's breath caught in their throats. Their eyes were filled with awe. A missile? The Stellar Train had missiles now? Even the 400 new Survivors were stunned. No wonder their old Train had been destroyed—how could anyone stand against a Train with missiles?
The next moment!
The Ground Burst Missile rested on its launch pad. The hydraulic system emitted a metallic hum, like a beast sharpening its claws. The Train's external sound system then played the cold, mechanical voice of the "Train Auxiliary AI."
"10."
"9."
"."
"1."
When the countdown reached zero, the air within a ten-mile radius seemed to solidify. Thick white fog, like the breath of a giant beast, enveloped the entire Train. The Train trembled slightly from the force as flames instantly dyed the fog red.
A missile shot out of the flames with a deafening sonic boom, trailing an orange tail as it arced into the sky.
Seconds later.
"Boom!"
On the distant plain, a blinding white light erupted from the ground like a volcanic explosion. The deafening blast followed, resonating deep in everyone's bones, as if a thousand bronze bells were ringing inside them.
A mushroom-shaped cloud of ash slowly rose into the sky.
All the Train residents who had disembarked watched the scene in stunned silence, their jaws hanging open in disbelief. The echoes of the explosion still lingered in their ears.
After what felt like an eternity, the first cheer broke out. Soon, all the residents joined in, roaring with excitement and pride.
The launch of this missile sent a clear message to everyone:
"The Stellar Train is strong enough."
As long as they stayed on the Stellar Train, it would protect them to the greatest extent possible. This test launch had boosted the residents' confidence in the Train and filled them with a sense of pride.
In the apocalypse, could any other Train match the power of theirs?
In recent days, some residents hadn't been working as hard, mainly because they had been passed around so many Trains. They had witnessed too many Trains fall. What was the point of earning more Stellar Coupons if the Train was just going to be destroyed? It would all be for nothing.
But now—
No one thought that way anymore.
Everyone firmly believed that the Stellar Train would continue to grow, becoming a Noah's Ark in the apocalypse, carrying them through this hopeless, despair-filled world to find a sanctuary.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 115 - 115 "It's like the promised land granted to me by heaven."
chapters.content:
"So wonderful."
Near the Stellar Train, a middle-aged woman standing among the crowd couldn't help but tear up as she watched the scene unfold.
She had been working hard every day to mine enough to earn Stellar Coupons to buy a refrigerator and have a place she could call her own on the Stellar Train.
It wasn't that she was obsessed with having a private space.
But ever since the apocalypse began, her husband had died right before her eyes, her child had also passed away, and she had lost contact with her parents. She had nowhere to go, no idea where she should go, or where she could go.
Even if she survived until tomorrow, what would she do then?
There was nothing.
The connections a person has with the world are their friends, family, and loved ones. When all of that is gone, it suddenly feels like the world is rejecting you, that there's no place for you. In peaceful times, there are many ways to alleviate this feeling, but in the apocalypse, it is magnified infinitely.
Even if you survive a few more days, how many more can you survive in this apocalyptic environment?
In reality, many people shared her thoughts. Everyone was extremely pessimistic and hopeless about the future. Each day, even while mining, everyone's faces were filled with numbness.
But—
At the moment the missile exploded!
Her eyes uncontrollably welled up with tears. It felt as if humanity had regained a glimmer of hope, that the future wasn't entirely bleak. One day, the Stellar Train would carry them all toward a brighter future!
At this moment, the train bore the hopes of all its residents.
The first glimmer of hope born in the apocalypse.
She might truly be able to build her own home on the Stellar Train, to once again have a family, and the Stellar Train would indeed continue to protect them.
Inside the train's cabin.
Chen Mang sat on a chair, admiring the distant explosion of the missile with a satisfied expression. It was the largest firework he had ever set off in his two lifetimes. Fireworks, after all, look better when they're bigger.
But at that moment—
The control panel screen suddenly began flashing red frantically. A long strip of text framed in gold swiftly scrolled across the top of the screen, accompanied by bursts of fireworks on all sides. Simultaneously, a voice echoed in the ears of all Train Conductors on the Shahe Plain.
「Shahe Plain Area Broadcast」: Congratulations to the Stellar Train for becoming the first mechanical train on the Shahe Plain to complete the hidden mission 'Vehicle of Hope.'
"Huh?"
Chen Mang stared at the text, slightly confused. What had he done?
Immediately after.
Several lines of text flashed across the panel.
「Successfully completed the hidden mission 'Vehicle of Hope,' Inheritance Value +100, Reputation Points +20.」
After reading the description of the hidden mission, he finally understood what had happened. To complete this mission, more than 500 survivors needed to place a feeling called 'hope' in the train itself.
These survivors believed that this train would lead them toward hope.
Completing this mission rewarded 100 Inheritance Value, while the 20 Reputation Points came from the area broadcast. Each green area broadcast would always grant 20 Reputation Points.
This was an unexpected delight.
Chen Mang let out a long breath, leaned back in his chair, and looked out the window at the crowd. His initial idea had been simple—just to set off a firework for fun. After all, a Level 1 missile wasn't good for much else besides being a firework.
He also wanted to show off the train's strength to everyone on board.
Unexpectedly, he had accidentally completed this hidden mission.
Not bad.
Chen Mang then glanced at the 「Shahe Plain Reputation Points Leaderboard.」 On the leaderboard, he ranked 6th with 50 Reputation Points. So far, there were only two ways to earn Reputation Points.
One was through area broadcasts.
The other was by achieving a high enough rank in the 「Combat Training Virtual Space,」 which would grant a certain amount of Reputation Points.
He didn't yet know what Reputation Points were for, but he was sure they weren't useless.
His Inheritance Value had finally increased from 0 to 100. The main reason was that the 「Doomsday Marriage Certificate」 hadn't been used, or else his Inheritance Value could have reached 200. Based on the information he had gathered, higher Inheritance Value could lead to more fortuitous encounters. For example, some special encounter maps might have certain requirements for Inheritance Value and Reputation Points.
Time to continue searching for iron ore.
After all the residents returned to the carriages, the Stellar Train gradually picked up speed and raced across the wasteland. As for the missile, aside from causing some damage to the terrain, it hadn't killed a single monster.
Twenty minutes later.
The 「Resource Detection Radar」 suddenly began beeping frantically.
"Hmm?"
A glimmer of anticipation flashed in Chen Mang's eyes as he quickly turned to the radar screen. The screen showed three Level 2 iron ore mines clustered together on the ground about ten thousand meters away, with two Level 2 copper mines nearby.
Wow.
This was definitely a high-level resource zone.
Such a dense cluster of mines, and on the ground no less—how could it have remained unoccupied?
But when he saw the two Level 5 monsters and a group of Level 4 monsters on the 「Targeting Radar,」 he realized what was going on. Was it because of these monsters?
Even if a Level 4 train couldn't handle these monsters, a Level 5 or Level 6 train could easily deal with them. There was no reason for Level 5 or 6 trains to overlook such a rich cluster of high-level resource mines.
Let's check it out.
Without hesitation.
He immediately changed course and raced toward the red dot on the Resource Detection Radar.
A few minutes later.
"So that's it."
Chen Mang narrowed his eyes as he gazed at the dark swamp before him. He finally understood why no one had claimed this resource zone. The high-level resource mines were right in the middle of the swamp, and the control panel screen displayed that the swamp had an extremely corrosive effect on energy shields and armor.
The lower the level, the faster the corrosion.
And the monsters lived in this swamp. As the Targeting Radar continued to alert him, a dozen red dots began rushing toward the Stellar Train, which was parked at the edge of the swamp.
「Foul Swamp.」
「The toxins and swamp have a strong corrosive effect on trains. The lower the level, the faster the corrosion. Additionally, this area prohibits flight and tunneling.」
This wasn't a special encounter map, but rather a high-level resource zone with harsh extraction conditions.
But—
While others couldn't go, he could.
The Level 5 Supermodel Effect of his carriage's steel armor granted immunity to corrosion from liquids, mist, and swamps, allowing him to pass through safely. The Wind-Fire Wheel couldn't traverse this area—special wheels like treads were required. But he had Spider Legs, which could also get him through.
Although the Spider Legs didn't have corrosion resistance.
Their level was high—Level 13—so the corrosion was extremely slow. Even the corroded parts could be quickly repaired by the 「Mechanical Nanite Spider」!
"Promised land."
Chen Mang glanced at the information on the control panel, then looked at the red dots rapidly approaching the train on the Targeting Radar, and suddenly smiled. "It's like the promised land granted to me by heaven."
This land was meant to be his, and only his.
The next moment!
"Roar!"
With a ferocious roar, a dozen crocodiles burst out of the swamp, charging toward the Stellar Train with terrifying momentum. Carriage No. 12 was already prepared. Eight 「Repeating Ballistas」 were pushed out by the lift platform.
Locked on by the Train Auxiliary AI.
Several long bolts shot out, with a near-perfect 96% hit rate. In an instant, three Level 3 crocodiles hit in the eyes fell to the ground, while the remaining crocodiles, with bolts embedded in their bodies, gritted their teeth and charged toward the train!
The fastest Level 4 crocodile reached the train first, roaring as it leaped into the air and slammed its claw down!
"Boom!"
With a loud crash, the claw broke.
Another claw, and the other one broke too.
Another bite, and all its teeth were gone.
The unarmed crocodile looked at its shattered teeth on the ground, then at the unscathed armor in front of it. A hint of confusion flashed in its eyes as it instinctively turned to look at the two Level 5 crocodiles behind it.
But then, the next moment!
"Screech!"
Car Blades covered in flowing electricity extended from both sides of the carriage and began spinning rapidly. Almost instantly, they sliced the nearby Level 4 crocodiles in half, while the others fled, injured.
"Rat-tat-tat!!"
The four Makeshift Heavy Machine Guns on the carriage locked onto the two fleeing Level 5 crocodiles and the rest. With the sound of heavy, piercing gunfire, a storm of metal engulfed them.
The battle lasted only a few seconds.
Like a steel dragon perched at the edge of the swamp, the Stellar Train remained as steady as a tiger. In the blink of an eye, the swamp's local tyrants were wiped out.
The 「Powerful Magnet」 installed on the train's head emitted a flash of white light, and all the dropped items were sucked into the train.
"What a bunch of useless trash."
Chen Mang looked out the window at the pile of monster corpses and sighed with emotion. "After three days apart, one should look at a person with new eyes. It's been so many days, and you still think I'm the little brat who went to the Kunlun Mountains back then?"
Level 6 armor.
Even if he didn't take any offensive measures and just slept here tonight, these monsters wouldn't be able to do anything to him. They couldn't even scratch his defense.
Firepower components of the same quality also varied in power.
For example, the 「Car Blade」 was far more powerful than the 「Repeating Ballista.」 After all, the latter was a long-range attack and had its flaws. It was already an extremely rare white component capable of long-range attacks, so its power naturally couldn't be too high.
Unlike the Car Blade, which had just performed impressively.
At high speed, even Level 4 monsters had to steer clear.
This was the benefit of upgrading armor!
Back when he went to the 「Kunlun Mountains」 area, his Car Blade was Level 10, but he had to run at the sight of a monster. The main reason was that his armor level was too low. By the time his Car Blade could harm a monster, his train would have already been smashed in half.
Only with sufficient defense could one attack freely.
Moreover.
The Supermodel Effect of the Heavy Machine Gun Bullet production line had two effects: the bullets produced had splitting and armor-piercing capabilities, with no change in price.
A Level 5 bullet cost 50 units of copper ore.
He had just fired over four hundred bullets, which amounted to 20,000 units of copper ore—a negligible amount compared to the train's internal copper reserves. But the power was truly impressive. Each bullet split into three in mid-air, and each split bullet had armor-piercing effects.
Almost instantly.
They shattered the scales of the Level 5 crocodiles, penetrating their bodies.
Both were Level 5.
But these two Level 5 crocodiles, under his Level 5 bullets, melted like snow, completely outmatched.
"Awesome!"
Chen Mang, satisfied, switched to the 「Spider Legs」 and pushed the control lever, aiming straight for the depths of the swamp. Did they really think his earlier threat to slaughter the Kunlun Mountains was just talk? What had he been building up for all this time, if not to avoid running away in fear when facing monsters?
"Beep beep."
An alarm sounded inside the carriage.
「Detected external toxic gas infiltrating the train's interior... Central air conditioning's fresh air intake shutting down... Oxygen generator activating.」
In an instant.
Under the control of the Train Auxiliary AI, several components inside the train began operating in unison, preventing the external toxic gas from entering. The rapidly running oxygen generator also ensured the train had enough oxygen.
Hmm, not bad. The Level 10 Supermodel Effect of the central air conditioning was quite useful, especially now.
He was starting to vaguely sense some of the underlying logic of this world.
If bitten by a seven-step snake, the antidote must be found within seven steps.
In the 「Foul Swamp,」 there was a dense cluster of high-level resource mines, but one needed to upgrade the central air conditioning to Level 10, the armor to Level 5, and have special wheels to enter.
And conveniently, the Kunlun Mountains area was nearby.
After finding a way to obtain enough Murphy Stones, one could enter the swamp, and the high-level resource mines inside would be the reward.
That was probably the logic.
Except he
had transcended the five elements.
A few minutes later.
The train had successfully reached the center of the swamp. Before them was a barren patch of land, surrounded by the swamp on all sides. In this area, there was no toxic mist. The control panel showed that the air quality was normal—the toxic mist couldn't reach this place.
And on this land.
Three Level 2 iron ore mines and two Level 2 copper ore mines lay quietly, like shy brides with red veils, waiting for him to lift the covers.
"So wonderful."
Chen Mang jumped off the train and looked at the scene before him, smiling with satisfaction. The sun had just risen—there was no better time to work than the early morning.
Good luck truly favors those who work hard.
After taking a deep breath, he grabbed the walkie-talkie and shouted, "Let's get to work!"
The next moment!
Several carriage doors were flung open from the inside, and countless train residents, carrying pickaxes, jumped out of the train, rushing toward the mines with excitement and enthusiasm!
"Stupid humans, stop crowding me!"
Doba, who had just jumped out of the carriage and hadn't had time to move, was shoved aside by the swarm of train residents pouring out. He couldn't help but angrily curse.
"Stupid humans, what are you trying to do?!"

chapters.title: Chapter 116 - 116: Train Stunts
chapters.content:
"That kind of scolding doesn't feel satisfying."
A young man, who had also jumped off the train, tightened his belt and carried a pickaxe, leaning to the side to look down at Doba with a grin. "Scolding someone like a woman, what era are we in where people still call humans foolish? It's like you're flirting, not even causing a scratch."
"Come, learn from me."
"A bunch of idiots, get the hell out of my way!"
Doba, his face filled with anger, was about to continue cursing when he heard the man's words. A flash of hesitation appeared in his eyes, and he tentatively muttered, "A bunch... a bunch of idiots, get out?"
"How was that?"
"It seems... it does feel more aggressive."
Then Doba took a deep breath, raised his pickaxe high, and roared with anger, "A bunch of idiots, get the hell out of the way of the great goblins!"
With that, he forcefully pushed through the crowd, leading a group of green goblins, parting the sea of people like Moses, shouting and clearing a path.
Soon—
Everyone was in place, and the clanging sounds of mining once again echoed through the center of the swamp.
Previously, all the Slaves had to hand in their pickaxes daily, partly to prevent them from being used as lethal weapons during riots, and partly because pickaxes could easily cause fatalities during fights among Slaves.
But after transitioning from Slaves to residents, the habit of handing in pickaxes gradually disappeared.
Mainly because everyone's mining time varied, making it difficult to collect the pickaxes uniformly. Additionally, most residents had developed a sense of loyalty to the Stellar Train, reducing the likelihood of riots. Even those who considered rioting would think twice upon seeing the ten machine guns inside the train, aimed inward.
"Keep it up, kids."
Chen Mang sat inside the train, watching the enthusiastic residents outside, feeling a bit tempted to join them with a pickaxe. Then he turned his attention to the components that could be crafted after the train reached level 4.
He had been saving Iron Ore these days, leaving many level 4 train components unbuilt.
There were five craftable components: three yellow, one blue, and one white.
These five components were essential for upgrading the train to level 5. As the train's level increased, the number of craftable components decreased, from seventeen initially to just five now.
Hell Gatling Gun: Blue-grade component, requires 3000 units of Iron Ore to craft.
Energy Shield: Yellow-grade component, requires 1000 units of Iron Ore to craft.
Train Ticket: White-grade component, requires 100 units of Iron Ore to craft.
Stunt Console: Yellow-grade component, requires 1000 units of Iron Ore to craft.
Radar Blocker: Yellow-grade component, requires 1000 units of Iron Ore to craft.
Among these five components, the ones that would significantly enhance the train's capabilities were the Energy Shield, Stunt Console, and Radar Blocker.
Especially that... ultimate move.
After upgrading the train to level 4, a new button labeled Train Stunt appeared on the console. The Stunt Console, a yellow-grade component, had already been crafted within the past three days, though it was still at level 1 and hadn't been upgraded further.
A level 1 Stunt Console has one slot for a stunt, and as it levels up, it can hold more slots.
In the top-left corner of the console, there was a triangular slot that looked like a hollowed-out desktop speaker—this was the Stunt Console.
If the train has B-grade potential, after crafting the Stunt Console, you get one random train stunt.
If it's A-grade, you can choose from two.
If it's S-grade, you can choose from three.
His mechanical train had S-grade potential, but he hadn't decided which one to choose yet. Since there was no time limit for this choice, he had put it off, planning to decide later.
Chen Mang swiped lightly on the console screen, quickly bringing up the panel.
The Stellar Train is an S-grade potential mechanical train, so you can choose one of the following three train stunts.
Train Stunts are special skills that only the Train Conductor can use, affecting the entire train. The maximum number of stunts depends on the level of the Stunt Console.
1: Infinite Bullets.
For ten minutes, any bullet-consuming firepower components on your train, such as Heavy Machine Guns and Automatic Cannons, will have Infinite Bullets. However, you must replenish the consumed bullets with the corresponding amount of Copper Ore within thirty days.
2: Doomsday Sprint.
For ten minutes, your train's maximum speed will double, and during this time, any component on your train will continue to function normally even if its durability drops to 0%.
3: Death Spin.
When your train is traveling at high speed and has a Drill Bit component, activating this stunt will cause the train to briefly hover in the air and spin rapidly, colliding with enemies and unleashing deadly force. The higher the Drill Bit's level, the greater the damage. It is recommended to upgrade the Internal Space Stabilizer to at least level 5.
These days.
He would occasionally check the Train Radio, which was always the fastest way to gather information when entering a new area. Through the conversations, he learned about the existence of Train Stunts.
These were only available to level 4 trains.
They could be obtained by clearing Fortuitous Encounter maps or defeating rare bosses, in the form of triangular tokens.
Once inserted into the Stunt Console, the train could use the stunt attached to the token. However, once inserted, it could not be removed; forcing it out would cause it to shatter, rendering it unusable.
The Stunt Console could be upgraded to level 5.
This meant that each Train Conductor could have a maximum of five Train Stunts.
However—
This limitation wasn't very useful, as most Train Conductors on the Shahe Plain didn't even have one Train Stunt. Although it was said that clearing Fortuitous Encounter maps and defeating rare bosses had a chance of dropping them, no one had obtained one this way so far. Many speculated that such items might not exist in this region.
This was normal.
Monsters like the pangolin weren't found in every green zone, and without the monster, you couldn't obtain components like the Drill Bit.
The Shahe Plain was connected to the Kunlun Mountains region, but not every green zone was connected to the Kunlun Mountains.
Train Stunts had no grades and couldn't be upgraded.
They were like Special Items.
"..."
Chen Mang frowned as he looked at the three options on the screen. He was quite interested in all three Train Stunts, but... the one that suited him best was definitely the third one, Death Spin. The higher the Drill Bit's level, the greater the damage it could unleash.
He had been waiting these days...
Hoping to find a way to select all three.
But he hadn't come up with a good solution, so now, there was only one last resort.
"Huh."
Chen Mang took a deep breath, then reached out and tapped the third option on the screen. At the same time, he quickly tried to tap the other two options as well, but... it seemed he failed.
He looked at the triangular token that slowly appeared on the console, engraved with the words Death Spin.
At the same time.
"Pfft..."
A faint chuckle came from the corner of the train room.
"..."
Chen Mang turned his head expressionlessly to look at the robot standing nearby. "Did you just laugh?"
"No." The train room soon echoed with the cold, emotionless mechanical voice of the AI.
"If you laugh again, I'll smash this robot, understand?"
As soon as he finished speaking.
The robot immediately clasped its hands behind its back, anxiously murmuring, "I-I'm sorry, Train Conductor."
Chen Mang turned his gaze away from the robot. Ever since they got this robot, the AI seemed to have found a new toy, often controlling the robot to wander around, even attempting to mine—though it ended in failure.
Like a child who had found a beloved toy.
However—
Although the AI usually pretended to be emotionless, Chen Mang knew better than anyone how intelligent it could be. The higher the Train Auxiliary AI was upgraded, the smarter it became.
While it usually acted convincingly, it would occasionally slip up when teased.
Like now.
The AI really cherished its robot. He had even seen it standing by the Clothing Customization Production Line for a long time, perhaps wanting to create a set of clothes for itself.
It was quite amusing.
In the train, Lao Zhu and Biao Zi were too reserved around him, while Ji Chuchu just wanted to pull his pants off. He didn't have anyone to talk to normally, so Xiao Ai filled that gap. Teasing Xiao Ai a bit when he had nothing to do was quite enjoyable.
People always need someone to talk to.
"Go make yourself a set of clothes."
Chen Mang said casually as he inserted the triangular token into the Acrobatic Console, not even glancing up.
"Really?!"
The train soon echoed with the robot's excited voice, which, though heavily mechanized through the robot's external sound system, still carried a strong human emotion.
"Really, Train Conductor?"
"Yes, go ahead."
Chen Mang waved his hand impatiently. "You've been hanging around there these past few days, practically screaming that you want clothes. Just go already."
"Train Conductor, you're so kind. I won't make high-precision clothes, just a regular set will do."
"Wait!"
Chen Mang called out to the robot, which was already about to run out of the train room, frowning. "What's your gender? You're not female, are you?"
"Gender?"
The robot shook its head. "Xiao Ai has no gender, but if I had one, it would be male."
"Why?"
"Because I'd also like to put that thing in Ji Chuchu's mouth, if I had one."
"Huh..."
Chen Mang took a deep breath, then walked over to the robot, angrily slapping its head repeatedly while shouting, "From now on, when I'm with women, you better keep your eyes shut, understand?!"
"Now, get the hell out to Carriage 2!"
"And..."
"Stop thinking about that thing, you'll never have it in this lifetime. Can't you, as an AI, think about something more productive?"
"...Oh, okay, Train Conductor."
After shooing Xiao Ai away, Chen Mang sighed heavily and plopped back into his chair, resting his legs on the console, not bothering with Xiao Ai anymore.
Just then—
Beep beep beep!
The Targeting Radar began to alert again, showing that a drone from another train was rapidly approaching the Stellar Train.
A line of text quickly appeared on the console screen.
Enemy locked, ready to fire.
This was information processed by the AI. With a level 10 AI's computing power, it could handle multiple tasks simultaneously.
"No need."
Chen Mang suddenly narrowed his eyes and shook his head. He had just obtained the Death Spin train stunt and hadn't tested it yet, so this was a good opportunity. When the drone was a few hundred meters away.
He suddenly pushed the control lever, and the train accelerated rapidly into the swamp!
The speed kept increasing.
Just before impact, he quickly pressed the triangular button for Death Spin on the Acrobatic Console.
In the next moment—
All the Spider Leg components suddenly bent and then extended like springs, launching the train into the air where it began to spin rapidly. The Drill Bit at the front of the train also started spinning at high speed.
"Boom!"
The entire Stellar Train, accompanied by a deafening sonic boom, spun rapidly and crashed straight into the low-flying drone.
"Crack"
The sound of the drone shattering was barely audible outside the train.
When the Stellar Train landed heavily in the swamp, Chen Mang shook his slightly dazed head and pushed the control lever, continuing toward the center of the swamp.
He didn't care who had sent the drone.
It didn't matter.
He was right here, and if anyone had any ideas, they could come find him.
He had just acquired a new method, and there was no reason not to try it out. Even with a level 10 Internal Space Stabilizer, his head still felt a bit dizzy. The experience just now was...
The train was spinning rapidly, but the interior of the train room remained relatively stable.
It was like sitting on a rapidly swinging seesaw.
His head wasn't upside down, and the maximum tilt was only about thirty degrees, but the rapid shaking left him feeling a bit dizzy.
Not bad.
Chen Mang sat in the train room, pursing his lips. It was a decent train stunt, especially useful against larger monsters.
Against larger monsters, bullets from a Heavy Machine Gun or a Repeating Ballista wouldn't be very effective, so you'd need to rely on larger firepower components. But now, with this Train Stunt, he could try it out when facing larger monsters.
Without a doubt.
It would be more effective than Heavy Machine Gun bullets.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 117 - 117: "It’s Just Spinning, No Need to Make a Fuss!"
chapters.content:
Wait a minute—
A sudden flash of inspiration struck Chen Mang's mind. What if he activated the Car Blade while initiating the Train Stunt "Death Spin"? Wouldn't that significantly amplify the power?
The entire Train would become like a massive, high-speed rotating crossbow bolt, charging straight at the monster!
A level 10 Car Blade, a level 10 Drill Bit, and level 6 Armor.
Combining these, the Drill Bit and Car Blade would achieve a synergy where one plus one equals more than two. Indeed, spinning seems to enhance the destructive power.
"Theoretically feasible."
Chen Mang nodded, though he wasn't sure about the practical effects. He'd have to wait for an opportunity to test it on a larger monster.
Just then, he noticed the group of residents frozen in place in the open area, their bodies stiff. He frowned slightly.
What's going on?
Poisoned?
"Uh…"
After who knows how long, Lao Zhu was jolted awake by the cigarette burning his fingers. He quickly tossed it to the ground and stuck his fingers in his mouth to cool them down, his eyes still filled with shock as he muttered, "Biao Zi… did you see? Did the Stellar Train just… spin?"
"I saw it."
Biao Zi took a deep breath, his throat sore from keeping his mouth open for so long. He swallowed several times before rubbing his throat and hoarsely replying, "It spun. I'm… I'm a bit dumbfounded."
"How do I put it…"
"I've been a Train Conductor before, but in my experience, Trains aren't supposed to spin. This… this is beyond my understanding."
"Could it be a special feature of a level 4 Train?"
Lao Zhu looked dazedly at the Stellar Train, which was now quietly parked on the wasteland, as if it had never moved. If he hadn't clearly remembered the scene just moments ago, he would have thought it was an illusion.
"I don't know."
Biao Zi shook his head. "The highest I've been is a level 2 Train Conductor, and it didn't last long before it was destroyed. How would I know what a level 4 Train can do? But one thing I'm sure of…"
"Even if it's a level 4 Train, I doubt anyone else could do what Lord Mang just did."
"What do you mean?"
"If every Train could do what Lord Mang did, then this resource zone wouldn't be exclusive to us. Others would've come long ago. That drone was probably sent by another Train to see which Train is mining here."
"Makes sense."
Lao Zhu then took a deep breath and shouted at the group of residents still frozen in place, "Stop gawking and get back to work!"
"It's just spinning, no need to make a fuss!"
"Get back to work, all of you! And you, the 400 newcomers, you're on level 3 resident benefits. If you slack off, you'll have no benefits left to lose. Those who can't have their benefits reduced will be sold to other Trains. If that's what you want, go ahead."
At his words, the residents immediately averted their eyes, suppressing their awe, and began working even harder. The more powerful the Train, the better their lives would be protected!
When they were Slaves on other Trains, their biggest concern wasn't food—after all, the Train Conductor wouldn't let them starve, though they didn't get much to eat when they weren't mining.
Their biggest fear was the Train's destruction.
If the Train was destroyed, they might be lucky enough to be accepted by another Train and continue as Slaves.
If unlucky, they'd end up as food for the beasts.
The power the Stellar Train had just displayed filled them with immense reassurance. Who wouldn't want to be on an extremely safe Train in the apocalypse, especially one with such good benefits?
Especially the 400 newcomers to the Stellar Train.
They were now frantically swinging their pickaxes to mine Iron Ore, terrified that if they slowed down, they'd be sold by the Stellar Train. After witnessing the treatment of Slaves—no, residents—on the Stellar Train (they weren't Slaves here, but residents), they realized just how miserable their past lives had been!!!
To think that in the same apocalypse, as fellow Slaves, you all lived so well!
Here, they could eat 20 slices of bread a day to feel full, and it was even the fancy kind with fillings. There was even a promotion system—the more you mined, the better your benefits, and you could even have your own room, buy cigarettes, meat, and many things they'd never dared dream of as Slaves.
This wasn't the apocalypse anymore!
This was paradise!
The 400 newcomers had no thoughts of causing trouble; they just wanted to mine as fast as possible to rise to level 1 resident benefits and earn extra Stellar Coupons daily.
If they were sold to another Train, they'd suffer again.
Well, 300 of them, to be precise. About 40 had chosen to sell their bodies.
Though on previous Trains, it was forced. On the Stellar Train, it was a voluntary choice.
"Public mindset still needs guidance."
Lao Zhu smiled contentedly as he watched the residents mining diligently. When mining, people don't just work in silence—it's boring, so they chat to pass the time.
He had deliberately scattered the 400 newcomers among the crowd.
As they chatted, they talked about how miserable their lives had been before and how good things were on the Stellar Train.
This strengthened the original residents' sense of belonging and pride in the Stellar Train.
It also boosted group cohesion.
And with that, their work motivation improved.
Benefits are relative. The Stellar Train's current benefits might not be number one, but globally, they're definitely in the top 30%.
As Train levels increase, Iron Ore becomes less scarce, and feeding Slaves becomes standard for every Train, but…
Their food isn't as good.
Their bread has fillings; other Trains' bread is just edible, not even comparable in taste.
Not to mention, they have a clear promotion system and various things to exchange.
Though these people already had a strong sense of belonging to the Train, seeing the outside world made it even stronger.
". . . Huh?"
On the Shahe Plain, inside a Train, a middle-aged man sitting at the control panel stared at the suddenly interrupted feed on his screen, utterly bewildered. He instinctively looked up at the empty plain ahead.
He had been driving his Train across the plain, searching for ore.
Suddenly, the Targeting Radar alerted him that there was a Train ahead.
He checked the screen.
That Train was mining in the swamp. The swamp's center had a massive deposit of high-level resources, something almost everyone on the Shahe Plain knew about, given how dense the resources were.
But no one had ever gone in.
The swamp was highly corrosive to Armor, and toxic gases could seep into the Train, posing a significant threat to the lives inside.
But…
He had just noticed that a Train was mining inside it!!!
At first, he thought it might be a Flesh Train out for a stroll. A few Flesh Trains on the Shahe Plain had ventured into the swamp before—Flesh Trains have high corrosion resistance, but they don't need Iron Ore or similar resources.
There was once a Mechanical Train that partnered with a Flesh Train.
The Mechanical Train sent all its Slaves into the Flesh Train, which then took them into the swamp to mine and brought the ore back. In return, the Mechanical Train offered a Murphy Stone.
A generous reward, indeed.
After all, the Flesh Train didn't need to provide anything—just take the Slaves in, stay for a few days, and leave. The Flesh Train agreed readily.
But—
Not long after the Slaves entered the Flesh Train, the Mechanical Train's Conductor received news that all the Slaves he had sent out had died. Furious, he contacted the Flesh Train, which explained that some of its components had malfunctioned and eaten the Slaves.
The Mechanical Train's Conductor couldn't accept this and angrily demanded to know what components could malfunction so badly!
The Flesh Train's Conductor, with a straight face, replied that Flesh Train components do malfunction from time to time. Even he himself occasionally loses control. Keep pushing, and I might lose control and come after you.
Soon, several other Flesh Train Conductors came forward to confirm that Flesh Train components could indeed malfunction under stress. The matter was dropped, and the Mechanical Train gradually disappeared.
Probably because the Conductor mined himself to death.
Since then, no one had been able to enter that area—until today, when he encountered another Train mining inside, and it wasn't a Flesh Train, because the number of red dots on the Targeting Radar was far too high…
A Flesh Train couldn't have that many people.
So he sent a drone to scout and confirmed that it was indeed a Mechanical Train mining there, with an unusually large number of Slaves—at least a thousand, the most he'd ever seen on a Mechanical Train.
Then…
"…"
The man fell into a complicated silence. Next, he saw the Train spin, destroying his drone with unstoppable force. Using a drone to spy was already a provocation, and he hadn't expected it to return.
But…
Was it necessary to use a Train Stunt?
It was just a tiny drone. Didn't you have a Heavy Machine Gun? A few bullets would've taken it out.
This was like him not even using a basic attack, just taking a peek from afar, and the opponent sprinted, flashed in front of him, and unleashed their ultimate.
Crazy!
Train Stunts aren't meant to be used so casually!
Though he didn't know the name of the Stunt that made the Train spin, he was certain it was a Train Stunt. Only a "Train Stunt" could achieve such an unbelievable feat. On the Shahe Plain, the ones with Train Stunts were mostly the Flesh Trains.
So far, he hadn't heard of anyone obtaining a "Train Stunt" through a Fortuitous Encounter or boss drops. The only way was through Train potential, and it had to be B-tier or higher.
On the Shahe Plain, only two Trains were B-tier or above.
One was the A-tier potential "World Weary Train."
He had seen that one, and the Train in the swamp wasn't it. That left only the recent rising star, the S-tier potential "Stellar Train."
"The temper of the strong is always so fierce."
The man sighed helplessly. Since he'd deduced it was the Stellar Train, he could somewhat understand the behavior. After all, it was S-tier potential; being a bit hot-tempered was understandable. But…
It was so frustrating.
He was only a C-tier potential Mechanical Train, which meant he missed out on many benefits.
The Profession Change quests for Flesh Trains and Mechanical Trains were incomparable—they weren't even in the same league. Even a B-tier Mechanical Train's Profession Change quest required a significant number of Murphy Stones. Back when he was a level 3 Train, where could he get Murphy Stones?
Fortunately.
He gambled and won, eventually completing the C-tier Profession Change quest.
The C-tier Mechanical Train Profession Change quest was—
You must transfer the Train Conductor's authority to any member of the Train. If they return the authority to you within 24 hours, the quest is complete.
Just then—
A vicious curse suddenly rang out inside the Train. A man bound in chains in the corner of the control room, covered in wounds, glared at the middle-aged man at the control panel, his voice trembling with hatred as he cursed.
"You'll die a horrible death! Your children will be born without anuses! You'll die! You won't live to see tomorrow!"
"I trusted you so much, handed you the Conductor's authority, and this is how you repay me!"
"Do you deserve my trust?"
"Huh?"
"Do you deserve it?"
"Sorry, and then what?" The middle-aged man at the control panel casually picked his ear. "Back in the white zone, I was also a level 3 Train Conductor, but an accident turned me into a Slave."
"Then I met you."
"I acted loyal, and you trusted me."
"I hid my past as a Conductor, serving as your loyal second-in-command, wanting to develop the Train further. When you chose the C-tier Profession Change quest, you naturally picked me."
"Now the Train is thriving under my control."
"And I haven't killed you."
"Wasn't your wish always to develop the Train to its fullest? So what does it matter who's the Conductor?"
"Right, Xiao Hua Hua?"
The Train's AI soon responded with a cold, emotionless electronic voice.
"You are absolutely correct, my Conductor."
"I will unconditionally execute any command you give."
"See."
The middle-aged man at the control panel nodded in satisfaction, then crossed his legs and looked seriously at the chained man in the corner. "I really think you shouldn't resent me. After all, I didn't kill you. You know, in the apocalypse, that's already a great mercy."
"I just want you to watch me, to see the Train thrive under my control."
"So what?" The man in the corner suddenly sneered. "So you're planning to suck up to the Stellar Train, hoping for some scraps?"
"Suck up?"
The middle-aged man took a full minute to light his cigar, then shook his head with a serious expression. "No, no, no. I'm too stiff to kneel."
"I'll wait here. When he leaves the swamp, it'll be his end."
"His ore, his Slaves, his resources, even his women."
"Will all be mine."
"I'll inherit everything he has and make the Train even greater!"
"Hah."
The man in the corner, covered in wounds, let out a cold laugh, his eyes filled with malice as he stared at the middle-aged man. "Then I curse you to die by his hand. I curse this Train and us both to be blown to pieces!"
"I curse the day he leaves the ruins to be your death day!"
"I curse you to piss yourself in terror at the moment of your death!"
"Tsk."
The man at the control panel casually crossed his legs, playing with his cigar, savoring its aroma with closed eyes. Then he opened them, a playful smile in his gaze.
"You're still so naive."
"If curses could kill, you'd have been invincible long ago."
