chapters.title: Chapter 126 - 126: "I believe in you, just give me the conclusion."
chapters.content:
At that moment.
A massive light screen appeared in the sky above the Mechanical City.
"The Fortuitous Encounter map, Tower of Heaven, has officially opened. Maximum capacity of Trains is 8, participating Trains: 2."
"This Fortuitous Encounter map has a total of five levels."
"The difficulty of each level increases progressively, from D, C, B, A, to S."
"Each level cleared will grant a reward for the clearance."
"The first level is—"
"D-level difficulty, Doomsday Sprint."
In the next instant—
The traffic lights situated beside the eight roads suddenly began to flicker. When the green light emerged and remained lit, the previously foggy Mechanical City seemed to come alive in an instant, with all the lights turning on simultaneously. The entire city was instantly enveloped in neon lights.
From behind the Azure Dragon Train and the Stellar Train, two platforms slowly rose. On these platforms stood two mechs, each wielding a heavy sword!
Each mech stood a towering ten meters tall.
Exuding an overwhelming presence.
Without the slightest hesitation.
Chen Mang pushed the control lever to its limit. Accompanied by a roaring sound, the Train's speed rapidly increased as it shot down the asphalt road towards the Mechanical City!
Meanwhile, several lines of text flashed quickly on the control screen.
"This mech model is the Stellar Gen 3 Mech. The heavy sword it wields can pierce level 7 defense, and the mech itself also boasts level 7 defense."
"Reaching the finish line within ten minutes means a successful clearance."
At the same time, several routes appeared on the screen, serving as navigation for this Fortuitous Encounter map. Xiao Ai's voice urgently echoed inside the Train.
"Choose the third route."
Chen Mang, in the control room, looked ahead at the approaching fork in the road. Without hesitation, he steered the Train onto the rightmost route, entering the interior of the Mechanical City.
Tall buildings made of mechanical parts swiftly passed by on both sides.
"Boom, boom, boom!"
The sound of violent collisions rang out. Even with the Universal Wheels, which allowed for tighter turns, the rear of the Train still slammed into the walls due to the high speed, creating a trail of sparks and flashes.
Thanks to the Armor, the Train remained undamaged.
With the Permanent Shock Absorption, the passengers inside didn't feel their heads buzzing.
At this moment—
Xiao Ai finally had the chance to explain: "The third route has a fifty-meter-wide cliff. The Train can completely cross it using Spider Silk. Compared to the other routes, this one is the optimal choice. The first route—"
"No need to explain."
Chen Mang interrupted Xiao Ai: "I believe in you, just give me the conclusion."
He then glanced at the rearview mirror, where the pursuing mech, towering like a small building and wielding a heavy sword, was rapidly closing in. Chen Mang licked his lips, adrenaline surging, and couldn't help but grin: "I like this map."
He then firmly pressed a button on the control panel.
Immediately after!
From Car 12, eight Repeating Ballistas were pushed out by the lifting platform. The ballistas quickly adjusted, and with a piercing whistling sound, eight bolts shot towards the pursuing mech!
They hit their mark.
However—
The eight bolts, upon impact, didn't even scratch the mech's paint, let alone cause any damage. They simply lost momentum and fell to the ground.
"This thing."
Chen Mang suppressed the urge to test whether the Train Stunt could take down the mech. He just glanced somewhat dissatisfied at the eight Repeating Ballistas on the Train's 3D map: "I'll replace you sooner or later. You're too useless."
Level 7 defense.
His Train Stunt might not be able to take it down. Although his Drill Bit and Car Blade are level-overpowered, level-overpowering only means they can penetrate defense. Whether they can actually cause damage is another matter. He felt they couldn't do much damage.
But that heavy sword smashing into his Train—that would be a direct hit every time!
His Armor couldn't block that.
At this moment—
A sinkhole suddenly appeared on the straight asphalt road ahead. However, the Stellar Train didn't slow down at all. As it approached the edge of the sinkhole, two strands of Spider Silk shot out and anchored on the other side, allowing the Train to drive across.
In the blink of an eye, it reached the other side of the sinkhole.
It continued to speed down the asphalt road of the Mechanical City, while the mech in the rearview mirror simply bent its knees slightly and made a huge leap, effortlessly keeping up.
"Impressive."
Chen Mang calmly continued to look ahead. A leap that could cover fifty meters—quite the jump.
"Choose the second route ahead."
Another fork in the road appeared.
Chen Mang steered the Stellar Train onto the second route. As soon as it entered this street, he saw a massive Corpse Tide in the distance, charging forward with ferocious expressions, almost completely filling the street. They were all level one and two Zombies.
"Buzz, buzz, buzz."
The Car Blades on both sides of the Train, as well as the Drill Bit at the front, quickly extended and began spinning at high speed!
The Stellar Train continued at full speed, crashing into the Corpse Tide. Upon contact, numerous Zombie limbs were flung into the air, and sticky blood splattered across the windshield, completely blocking the view.
"..."
Chen Mang frowned slightly. He'd have to get a windshield wiper or something in the future. But for now, he couldn't worry about that. He immediately climbed up through the sunroof and onto the roof of the Train, sitting on the front and holding his cane, using his mind to take over control.
The overwhelming stench of blood hit him instantly.
Any Zombie that got close to the Train was instantly torn into pieces, unable to cause the slightest damage to the Train.
He looked back.
The mech was still charging forward on the blood-soaked asphalt road, closely following. This mech had no ranged weapons, only the heavy sword in its hand.
"Prepare to jump!"
"The width is 150 meters. At maximum speed, the Spider Legs can cover 155 meters—just enough."
From inside the Train, Xiao Ai's voice roared.
At this moment, another sinkhole appeared in the distance at the end of the road. This one was over 150 meters wide, exceeding the range of the Spider Silk, which could only shoot 100 meters.
However—
As the Train approached the edge of the sinkhole, the wheels instantly switched to Spider Legs. Using the momentum, the Train leaped from the edge, soaring into the air!
When it landed again.
It crashed heavily on the other side of the sinkhole and continued speeding down the asphalt road. Three seconds later, Chen Mang saw the finish line—a square surrounded by a yellow circle. As the Train rushed into it, it felt like entering a thick, viscous air.
The Train, which had been moving at high speed, instantly came to a halt.
The Azure Dragon Train had already arrived first and was waiting for him.
The control screen also displayed several lines of text.
"First level, successfully cleared."
"Reward for this level: 10,000 units of Iron Ore. The second level will begin in ten minutes."
Chen Mang looked in the rearview mirror at the mech, which had silently turned back after he entered the finish line. He then sat on the roof of the Train and looked down through the sunroof at Xiao Ai: "Tell Lao Zhu to send someone to clean the front of the Train."
He then turned to Er Dan, who was grinning beside him.
"Pretty fast."
"Not bad," Er Dan, inside the Train, stuck his head out, a hint of pride in his smile. "After all, it can fly. It's a level 5 Train—gotta have something you don't, right?"
"Nice."
He sat on the roof of the Train, lit a cigarette, and looked around at the Mechanical City made of mechanical parts. It was a spectacular sight, one he was seeing for the first time.
Lao Zhu was already leading a team to clean the sticky blood off the windows. The Train's basic accessories needed to be sorted out. Not even having a windshield wiper—this was unacceptable.
Ten minutes quickly passed.
The yellow circle gradually faded, and a light screen appeared before everyone once more.
The screen displayed a line of text and two flat maze maps.
"Second level, C-level difficulty, Mechanical Maze."
"Reach the end of the maze within 10 minutes to successfully clear the level."
"You have one minute to memorize the maze's layout. The level will officially begin in one minute."
At the same time.
Two dark entrances slowly appeared on a tall building in the square ahead. Clearly, these entrances were the maze's entrances.
"Li Shiji, come to the control room immediately!"
Almost as soon as the light screen appeared, the AI, controlling the Train's Sound System, blasted the message at maximum volume into Li Shiji's ears as he was still leaning out the window, enjoying the scenery!
Hearing the call, Li Shiji didn't hesitate for a second. He took off running towards the control room.
He ran so fast that he tripped, but he didn't have time to worry about that. He scrambled on all fours towards the front of the Train!
Li Shiji rushed into the control room and looked at the two flat maze maps on the light screen outside the window. His brain worked furiously. With only 20 seconds left, the urgency made his lips tremble slightly, and his fingers twitched as he traced the air.
Soon—
The countdown ended!
"Did you memorize it?" Chen Mang turned to Li Shiji.
"I memorized both maze maps. Which one is ours?"
"The one on the right. You take the lead from here."
Chen Mang suddenly remembered something. He picked up the Train Radio's intercom and found it still working. He turned to Er Dan, who was anxiously watching from inside the Train, and frowned: "Can you make it? If not, I can help you?"
"Thank you!" Er Dan's excited and hurried voice quickly came through the intercom: "I've got a damn phobia of mazes now."
Chen Mang didn't linger. He steered the Train into the black entrance on the right side of the tall building.
Inside, it was pitch black.
When the Headlights turned on, they revealed a large passage made of black steel. The passage was enormous, standing ten meters tall, and the forks in the road were also wide enough to allow the Train to turn even without Universal Wheels.
"Turn left!"
Li Shiji urgently called out as they approached a three-way fork. He then glanced at the Train's speed on the control screen and quickly spoke into the Train Radio intercom: "Keep your Train's speed at 50 km/h. Not faster, not slower."
"In three seconds, you'll reach the first fork. Turn right."
"Then follow my lead."
He then looked back at the passage ahead: "Lord Mang, at the next fork, we'll turn right."
Three minutes later.
"Woo!"
With a honk, the Stellar Train successfully exited the maze and came to a stop on another square. The control screen displayed several lines of text.
"Second level, successfully cleared."
"Reward for this level: A random white-tier Accessory Blueprint. Randomizing... Randomized to 'Iris Chip.' The third level will begin in ten minutes."
"PS: All Accessory Blueprints obtained in this Fortuitous Encounter map can only be obtained through the Tower of Heaven Fortuitous Encounter map."
"Not bad."
Chen Mang turned to Li Shiji, whose body was trembling slightly from the intense concentration. There was a hint of surprise in his eyes: "I can understand you memorizing the flat map, but you had no idea what was happening around Er Dan. How did you manage to direct him correctly?"
At this moment, the Azure Dragon Train slowly emerged and pulled up beside him.
Li Shiji, now relaxed, explained somewhat shyly: "Although the two maze maps were different, the flat maps had scale markings. As long as the Train Conductor kept the speed at 50 km/h, the same as the Stellar Train, I could use the Stellar Train's progress to infer where the other Train would be in its map."
"But I didn't know the specific rules, so I had that Train arrive at the finish line a bit later. I'm not sure if there's any benefit, but it shouldn't hurt..."
"Impressive."
Chen Mang patted Li Shiji's shoulder and signaled for him to return: "After this is over, there'll be a reward."
He then turned to Xiao Ai.
"With your computing power, couldn't you have memorized this maze's flat map and quickly deduced the path?"
"Of course I could."
Xiao Ai's mechanical voice echoed in the control room: "But you'd need to input the maze's flat map data into the Train Auxiliary AI first. That way, I can process it quickly. This robot's information reception equipment is too poor to absorb information quickly."
"However, there are many damaged machine parts here. Maybe we can find some components later to upgrade this robot."
"Then I'll be able to do it."
"My processing speed is fast, but my download speed is slow."
At this moment—
The Train Radio crackled with Er Dan's excited and grateful voice: "Bro, thank you, really. I've got a real phobia of mazes now. If it weren't for your help, I wouldn't have made it through this level."
Chen Mang, sitting at the control panel, turned to Er Dan on the Azure Dragon Train and waved with a smile.
"No problem."
"If it weren't for you providing the coordinates, I wouldn't have made it here either."
"There are still several levels ahead. Let's keep going."
Soon, the waiting time passed again, and the third level began!
Another light screen appeared in the square.
"Third level, B-level difficulty, Desperate Enigma."
"Solve the riddle, find the way out."
"Time limit: three minutes."
Immediately after—
As soon as the light screen appeared, the sound of countless gears turning rang out. The two squares where the Stellar Train and the Azure Dragon Train were parked began to slowly rotate.
With each rotation, the squares grew larger.
They gradually split into two separate squares, separating the Stellar Train and the Azure Dragon Train.
Then, numerous nozzles resembling Stellar engines emerged from the ground at the edges of the two circular squares. A blast of cold air shot out, forming sharp, sword-like structures that pierced the sky!
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 127 - 127: "Don't make it seem like we're small-time nobodies."
chapters.content:
Inside the Stellar Train, Chen Mang frowned as he looked at the circle of vents around the edges of the square. There were hundreds of them, and the icy cold air shooting up from them gathered together, forming a tightly sealed cylindrical structure several hundred meters tall!
High above, at an altitude of several hundred meters, there was a much smaller square—that was the endpoint.
At this moment, the countdown had already begun.
「00:02:59」.
Three minutes remaining.
The edges of the square beneath the Stellar Train had already begun to collapse. When the countdown ended, the Stellar Train would plunge into a bottomless abyss. No one knew where it would fall, only the incessant creaking of countless gears turning could be heard from beneath the square.
Falling down there would likely not result in anything good.
Li Shiji, who had just returned to his seat, was quickly called out again. His face tense, he rapidly scanned the square. The only clue was the patterns on the square's floor. Within three minutes, they had to solve the puzzle and find a way to reach the square several hundred meters above them. That was the challenge of this level.
Ten seconds later.
Li Shiji's face began to pale rapidly. His hands trembled as he desperately examined the square, which had already partially collapsed at the edges, hoping to find the solution. But it was clear that his chances were slim.
"It's only a B-level difficulty. Is it really this hard?"
Chen Mang, sitting at the control panel, wasn't in a hurry. He calmly gazed at the cylindrical structure of icy cold air that enveloped the entire square. This thing wasn't a physical entity—there was no place for the Spider Legs to land.
"Xiao Ai, what about you?"
"No good," Xiao Ai quickly shook his head. "I don't have much learning material. There's no simulated space at all. Train Conductor, you need to find me some materials to learn from."
Just then—
The Train Radio crackled with Er Dan's hurried and excited voice: "Bro, don't worry. I've already reached the top."
"Wait for me. I'll fly above you. I have a special steel cable that can hoist your train up."
Chen Mang looked up and saw that the Azure Dragon Train had already successfully flown above the square. Its Energy Shield enveloped the entire train as it prepared to charge through the cylindrical structure of icy cold air.
This cylinder was sealed at the top, and the floating endpoint square was located near the top inside the cylinder.
To escape this icy prison, they had to break through the cold air.
"No need, I—"
He had barely uttered a word when he saw the Azure Dragon Train accelerate sharply and charge into the icy air. In an instant, frost enveloped the entire train, freezing it solid.
It lost control in midair and crashed heavily back onto the square.
"—have a way."
Only then did Chen Mang slowly finish his sentence. It wasn't that he spoke slowly—it was just that Er Dan had acted too quickly, without hesitation. Chen Mang stared blankly at the Azure Dragon Train, which had crashed heavily onto the square. If it hadn't upgraded its Internal Space Stabilizer...
Everyone on board was probably dead.
He grabbed the Train Radio's intercom: "Are you dead?"
"N-not yet, just... really... really cold."
Er Dan's trembling voice came through the Train Radio, along with the sound of his teeth chattering from the cold. Even through the radio, Chen Mang could feel the chill.
"A hint... I've retreated to the spectator seats..."
"There's... one minute left. Hurry and figure something out... or we might die when we fall..."
Then—
Chen Mang saw countless Mechanical Arms extend from the edges of the square, grabbing the Azure Dragon Train, which had been frozen into a block of ice, and carrying it to the side. Numerous flamethrowers emerged and began to thaw it out.
He glanced at the icy prison surrounding them. This thing was even more powerful than he had anticipated.
Li Shiji still hadn't come up with an answer. It seemed they had no choice but to use that method.
He sighed softly. It would cost 50,000 units of Iron Ore, which was a bit painful.
After consuming 50,000 units of Iron Ore, he quickly crafted a Level 3 Energy Stone and placed it in the Generator. The Stellar Train then switched back to its Spider Legs. As the Mechanical Spider Legs bent slightly, the rear sections of the train leapt into the air and stood upright on the ground.
The middle sections followed suit.
With 14 cars, the Stellar Train now stood straight up in the center of the square!
It no longer looked like a train.
It looked more like a rocket ready to launch.
"That guy..."
At this moment, the Azure Dragon Train, which had already been eliminated in the third level, was being carried to the side by Mechanical Arms and thawed with flamethrowers. Er Dan, who had been anxiously watching the Stellar Train on the control panel screen, was now relegated to the spectator seats.
From here, he could only watch the progress of other contestants—specifically, the Stellar Train.
If they fell through the square in this level, they would die. This was no joke!
Beneath the square was a mass of wildly spinning gears. Falling down there would be disastrous.
He had the Bunny Cloud to fly, but the Stellar Train couldn't fly. Unless they solved the puzzle in the last minute, they were doomed.
And just then.
He saw the Stellar Train perform a series of bizarre maneuvers. The entire train leapt into the air, and when it landed again, it stood upright in the center of the square.
But that wasn't all.
The Nitrogen Tailjets on each side of the Stellar Train's cars began to spew blue flames!
"That guy..."
Er Dan couldn't help but let out a bitter laugh. "Is he really planning to launch his train like a rocket?"
"Those are Nitrogen Tailjets! Even at Level 10, the thrust wouldn't be enough to make the train fly!"
"Hurry and think of something! You can't really die here. You're S-tier potential!"
"There must be a way... Think of something..."
His face anxious, he stared intently at the Stellar Train standing upright on the square. The dozens of Nitrogen Tailjets around the train were already spewing blue flames, but the train showed no signs of lifting off.
He had this accessory too, and he knew exactly how much speed it could provide.
Even at Level 10, it only added 120 km/h to the train's speed. How could that be enough to launch it like a rocket?
Just as he, shivering from the cold, couldn't resist picking up the Train Radio's intercom to say something—
He witnessed a scene he would never forget for the rest of his life.
The dozens of Nitrogen Tailjets on both sides of the Stellar Train suddenly began to expand, merging with the Tailjets of the cars in front and behind them. In the blink of an eye, the dozens of Tailjets fused together.
Forming two massive Nitrogen Tailjets embedded on either side of the train!
They spanned the entire train.
From the first car to the fourteenth!
"This... this..."
Witnessing this, Er Dan's mind flashed with an unbelievable possibility. Frozen in place, his voice trembling, he grabbed the Train Radio's intercom and shouted, "Are you serious?!"
"You can do that?!"
"You never said... you could fly!"
Soon.
Chen Mang's familiar chuckle came through the Train Radio.
"I never said I couldn't."
In the next moment—
The square had already collapsed, leaving only a small patch at the center. The two massive Nitrogen Tailjets on either side of the Stellar Train began to tremble violently. Then, two enormous blue flames shot out from the Tailjets, blasting the ground below!
"BOOM!!!"
Under the immense thrust.
The Stellar Train, standing upright on the ground, slowly rose into the air like a rocket, gradually accelerating. In the blink of an eye, it reached the top of the icy prison several hundred meters high. Then, as the Nitrogen Tailjets suddenly extinguished.
The Stellar Train landed steadily on the endpoint square high above.
Successfully landed.
Level cleared.
「Third level, cleared.」
「Reward: One random green-tier Accessory Blueprint, rolling now... Detected that the previous level's reward was the 'Iris Chip' Blueprint. Obtained the matching 'Mechanical Eye' Blueprint. The fourth level will begin in ten minutes.」
「PS: All Accessory Blueprints obtained in this Fortuitous Encounter map can only be acquired in the Tower of Heaven Fortuitous Encounter map.」
"Phew..."
Inside the Stellar Train, Chen Mang leaned back in his chair and exhaled softly, smiling as he looked at the data on the control panel.
Not bad. The consumption was less than he had expected.
That Level 3 Energy Stone only consumed 17%.
This was definitely more costly than the Bunny Cloud, but that was to be expected. After all, the Bunny Cloud was designed to fly, whereas his method was cobbled together.
First, he used the Level 20 Supermodel Effect of the Spider Legs to make the Stellar Train stand upright on the square.
Then, he used the Level 10 Supermodel Effect of the Nitrogen Tailjets to merge all the Tailjets into two massive Nitrogen Tailjets.
Achieving a rocket-like launch effect.
The downside, aside from high energy consumption, was... they couldn't control the direction. They couldn't fly wherever they wanted—they could only go straight up.
But—
If it was about the shock factor, the Bunny Cloud couldn't even compare.
"Damn it..."
Inside the Azure Dragon Train, Er Dan was still in shock, his mouth hanging open. It took him a while before he could shake his head with a bitter laugh.
Before coming here.
He had planned to vent his frustration. After all, he had been completely humiliated in the maze earlier. How could he not want to get back at them? From the moment they met, he had wanted to one-up the Stellar Train, but...
No matter what he compared, he couldn't win.
The train environment, the women, even his most proud flying ability—none could match.
As for attack and defense, he hadn't even considered those. With over sixty Supermodel Effects, how could they be lacking?
In other words...
His Level 5 veteran train was completely outclassed by Chen Mang in every aspect. A total wipeout.
Is this what S-tier potential is like?
Isn't it a bit too terrifying? And he remembered that even for S-tier potential, aside from a red-tier heavy firepower accessory and a Train Stunt, there weren't any other special perks.
If that's the case, then it's not S-tier potential that's terrifying—it's Chen Mang who's terrifying.
Whatever.
He took a deep breath, picked up the Train Radio's intercom, and couldn't help but sneeze. Shivering from the cold, he stammered, "The next level... will be even harder. It's A-tier difficulty."
"Even if I weren't in the spectator seats, it would be hard for me to clear it."
"The rewards for the later levels will definitely be better. That's the main event. Do your best to clear them all!"
"Afterwards, I'll give you some beer... Just don't forget about me..."
"Let me... follow you and get a taste..."
"Did we... just fly?"
In Car 5, Yan Yao looked at Ji Chuchu with wide eyes, full of shock. "Isn't the Stellar a train? How can it fly? Can all trains in this world fly now?"
"Of course not."
Ji Chuchu shook her head. "After the apocalypse, trains became the only mobile shelters for all survivors to escape the monsters. How could everyone's train fly? It's just that Lord Mang is amazing."
"You haven't been to other trains. Seeing Lord Mang only makes you feel like a frog looking up at the moon from the bottom of a well."
"But when you've struggled through the apocalypse for a year and then see Lord Mang, you'll understand what it means for a mayfly to glimpse the vast sky."
"Do you think so many people are grateful to the Stellar just because of the treatment on the train?"
"The biggest reason is—"
"They've witnessed the Stellar's power. They believe that following the Stellar will lead them to a brighter future, until they can establish an absolutely safe mobile shelter in this hopeless apocalypse."
"You're really lucky. After the apocalypse, you hid in a safe house for a year and then came to the Stellar. You don't truly realize how fortunate you are."
"That's what I envy most about you."
"It's truly unbelievable."
In Guard Car 7, Biao Zi looked out the window with a complex expression. The shocking scene from earlier still lingered in his mind, refusing to fade. For a moment, he even felt like he was riding a rocket.
He had never imagined that one day he would get to ride a rocket.
"It is unbelievable."
Lao Zhu smiled as he looked out the window, his eyes filled with pride and nostalgia. He was the first to follow Lord Mang and had witnessed the Stellar's development from the very beginning. It felt good. He had poured so much sweat into this train.
If one day he had to choose between sacrificing himself or the train.
He would choose himself.
He had come to regard the Stellar as his home. He couldn't imagine what his life would be like without it—perhaps he would return to the same aimless, hopeless existence in the apocalypse, barely clinging to life.
He didn't want to live like that again.
"Such a pity..."
Lao Zhu suddenly shook his head regretfully. "It's a pity the residents' cars don't have windows. They can't see what's happening outside."
"There are too many people," Biao Zi said helplessly. "Even if there were windows, only a few could see. And if everyone wanted to look, there'd be a risk of stampedes."
"Yeah."
Lao Zhu nodded with a smile. "Maybe we can install some screens in the residents' cars later. When the Stellar shows its might, let everyone see. That way, they can truly feel the Stellar's power."
"Don't make it seem like we're small-time nobodies."
"Like any random loser can brag about being able to fly in front of us."
Clearly, Lao Zhu was still holding a grudge. He rolled his eyes in annoyance. "At lunch today, that guy bragged about being able to fly right in front of Lord Mang. It made me so angry."
"Who doesn't know how? Damn it!"
"Lord Mang is the real deal."

chapters.title: Chapter 128 - 128: "Run, Stellar."
chapters.content:
The Stellar Train sat quietly on a plaza suspended high in the air. It was a waiting period, with seven minutes left before the fourth level began.
The first three levels had been relatively easy.
The rewards were modest as well.
Starting from the fourth level, the difficulty would rise to A-rank, and the rewards would naturally increase accordingly.
"."
Sitting inside the train compartment, Chen Mang scanned his surroundings. He couldn't figure out how the plaza was suspended in mid-air. There were no visible jet propulsion systems, no signs of strong magnetic fields, and certainly no steel cables.
After retracting his gaze,
he turned his attention to the two accessory blueprints on the control panel. Both had been obtained in the previous levels. They weren't of particularly high quality—one was white-tier, and the other green-tier—but their rarity lay in the fact that these blueprints could only be obtained through fortuitous encounters within the Tower of Heaven.
They were randomly acquired, not guaranteed rewards for completing the second and third levels.
But now wasn't the time to inspect his gains.
He sat in his seat, lit a cigarette, and gazed out the window at the scenery. The towering skyscrapers built from mechanical parts looked cold and uninviting.
Ahead lay the fourth and fifth levels.
Their difficulties were rated A and S, respectively.
If he could clear these two levels, he would have successfully completed the "Tower of Heaven" fortuitous encounter map. So far, he didn't feel that the map posed any significant challenge.
Soon—
A light screen appeared in front of the train.
"Level 4, A-rank difficulty: City's Peril."
"Escape the Mechanical City."
The moment the light screen appeared,
Chen Mang felt as though all the searchlights from the Mechanical City's skyscrapers were trained on him. The scenery around him began to shift, and his ears were filled with a cacophony of noises.
Intermittent electronic sounds.
The roar of gunfire.
The screeches of monsters.
The previously silent Targeting Radar suddenly blared to life, its screen densely covered with countless red dots.
"Calling Stellar Train, calling Stellar Train... Retreat! Retreat! You are ordered to retreat!"
A cold, emotionless mechanical voice came through the Train Radio.
Chen Mang's expression changed as he turned to look out the window. Just moments ago, he had been on the plaza high in the air, but now the train had somehow appeared in a plaza within the city. On either side of the train, hundreds of humanoid bio-mimicry robots, their eyes glowing red, charged toward the city's outskirts with weapons in hand.
He could clearly see the exposed wires and Energy Stones on their bodies. The guns they carried were entirely different from those produced by his train—sleek and slender, with what looked like batteries attached to the stocks.
"Zzzz..."
Amidst the chaos, thousands of two-meter-tall, mantis-like monsters surged from the end of the street.
The robots charging forward immediately dropped to one knee, aimed their guns at the monsters, and pulled the triggers. Crimson lasers shot out, and any monster hit by them burst into smoke and collapsed at the feet of others.
But more monsters, untouched by the lasers, closed in on the robots. They opened their grotesque mouths and roared, raising their sharp, bladed limbs to slash at the robots. Sparks and electricity flew as the struck robots twisted unnaturally before collapsing in a cloud of black smoke.
The street behind the plaza was just a microcosm.
The entire Mechanical City had come to life, filled with the roars of monsters. Looking up, Chen Mang saw countless flying monsters flapping their wings like a dark cloud descending upon the city. Anti-aircraft guns mounted on the skyscrapers opened fire almost simultaneously.
"Whoosh! Whoosh!"
In an instant, the sky above the Mechanical City was crisscrossed with the trails of tracer rounds, resembling a grand and unparalleled meteor shower—stunningly beautiful!
Countless flying monsters, struck by the gunfire, shrieked and plummeted to the ground, but even more broke through the defensive line.
Chen Mang's eyes flashed with disbelief and awe. He even spotted four or five trains rising from the city, charging forward. The firepower accessories mounted on the trains were unleashing a furious barrage.
On the Targeting Radar,
more trains emerged from skyscrapers, from underground, or from lift platforms beneath the plaza. They accelerated along the streets, rushing toward the city's outskirts to engage the enemy.
Was this an illusion?
Or was it something akin to a Combat Training Virtual Space?
The Mechanical City before him was nothing like the one he had seen when he first entered the map. The air was filled with piercing alarms, not a single human in sight, and the ground was covered with running robots and what seemed like an endless horde of monsters.
The deafening roar of countless weapons firing and the shrieks of monsters merged into a tsunami of sound, leaving his mind momentarily blank.
The Mechanical City now appeared far less abandoned than when he had first entered. It seemed much more intact, devoid of the desolation he had initially felt. It was alive with activity.
At that moment—
"BOOM!!!"
A skyscraper beside the street suddenly retracted its walls from the seventh floor down to the first, revealing a massive, ten-meter-tall mech. The mech was equipped with an array of heavy firepower accessories, wielding a glowing sword, its body flashing with various indicator lights.
As soon as it stepped out of the skyscraper, two deep blue flames erupted from its back, propelling it into the air. It soared toward a monster dozens of meters tall.
"That mech..."
Chen Mang stared at the ascending mech. He recognized it. Though its appearance had changed, it was the same mech that had chased him in the first level.
The Stellar Armor.
He remembered it clearly. At the time, he had wondered why the mech shared the same name as his train. Had he chosen such a common name?
But back then,
it had been a crippled version, lacking the heavy firepower it now carried. It had only wielded a greatsword, which, unlike the current one, didn't glow.
Just then—
"ROAR!!!"
An ear-splitting roar erupted beside him. A massive, grotesque worm, covered in sticky, disgusting mucus, burst from the ground at the end of the street. Its hundreds of sharp fangs instantly devoured all the robots and mantis-like monsters on the street. It then charged toward the Stellar Train at terrifying speed.
The street cracked and split apart.
Chen Mang instantly pushed the control stick almost to its limit, activated the Wind-Fire Wheels, and triggered their Level 5 Supermodel Effect, along with the Nitrogen Tailjet's Supermodel Effect!
The Level 5 Supermodel Effect of the Wind-Fire Wheels allowed the train to enter a potential-unlocking state, doubling its maximum speed. However, it rapidly consumed Energy Stones and caused some damage to the wheels.
The Nitrogen Tailjets on both sides of the train merged into two massive thrusters, providing immense propulsion.
This was his ultimate speed-related trump card.
The control panel showed that the train's speed had reached 980 km/h. In the blink of an eye, the train shot out of the plaza, speeding down the road ahead. The scenery on either side blurred as the train accelerated to an almost incomprehensible speed.
The Train Auxiliary AI had taken over full control of the train.
The Targeting Radar indicated that the monster was of an unknown level, far beyond what the Stellar Train could handle.
He finally understood why the roads in the Mechanical City were so straight and wide—they were designed for trains to traverse at high speeds.
Yet, even with the train's incredible speed, the Energy Stones were depleting rapidly. Mechanical Nanite Spiders swarmed out, frantically repairing the Wind-Fire Wheels. But within just three seconds, the massive worm that had emerged from the ground closed in on the Stellar Train's tail.
It had no eyes—only a mouth.
A mouth that took up its entire head, filled with countless fangs and a wrinkled, birth canal-like throat.
The worm's body was so thick it could swallow three trains whole.
"Damn it!"
Chen Mang's expression darkened. Was this really A-rank difficulty? The Stellar Train stood no chance against an unknown-level monster. "Unknown level"—what the hell did that even mean? His proud Level 6 Armor was utterly insignificant in the face of such a creature.
At this point, there was no way to escape. He had no choice but to gamble.
Just as he was about to bring the Stellar Train to a sudden halt, allowing the worm to swallow it, and then attempt to use the Train Stunt "Death Spin" from within the worm's belly to break free—
"BOOM!"
The ground suddenly shook violently. The mech that had been flying in the air moments ago now landed heavily on the ground. Its mechanical foot stomped down on the massive worm, pinning it in place. The mech then turned its head toward the now-stopped Stellar Train, its eyes flashing red.
A cold, emotionless mechanical voice came from the speaker installed in its throat.
"Run, Stellar."
"Survive."
In the next moment—
Three even larger worms burst from the ground, their gaping maws lunging at the mech.
Chen Mang narrowed his eyes, not daring to linger. He pushed the control stick again, sending the train racing deeper into the Mechanical City. A red line on the screen guided his path—this was the level's task guidance.
As he left,
he saw the worms spewing black, sticky liquid onto the mech. The mech's surface armor was rapidly corroding, the damage resembling the corrosion marks he had seen on the mech in the first level.
In just thirty seconds, he had traveled less than a twentieth of the distance indicated by the red line on the screen.
Several more massive worms emerged from the ground, blocking his path. Just as he was about to use the Spider Legs to leap over them, armies of robots poured out from the skyscrapers on either side. Their internal wires were exposed, and their armor was missing pieces here and there, clearly battle-scarred.
Hundreds of robots, armed with various weapons, charged forward like soldiers on a suicide mission. But against the massive worms, they were insignificant, quickly devoured.
Then—
"Boom, boom, boom..."
A series of faint explosions erupted within the worms' bellies. The worms howled in pain, writhing on the ground and abandoning their attack on the train.
Chen Mang glanced at the two skyscrapers with open walls.
Inside were countless assembly lines.
The assembly lines were filled with broken robots. Several robots stood beside the lines, using mechanical arms to dismantle, reassemble, and repair the damaged units.
"."
He frowned slightly, then pushed the control stick again. The train's Spider Legs bent slightly before springing into the air, leaping over the writhing worms. The train continued speeding down the straight road ahead.
As he left,
he saw one of the robots about to be devoured turn its head back. Its eyes flashed red, and a hoarse, grating voice, like that of a terminal oral cancer patient, rang out.
"Survive, Stellar."
In the next moment, a brilliant explosion erupted from the robot's abdomen, instantly engulfing its entire body.
Countless parts scattered into the air before gently falling to the ground.
He felt like a mere spectator, watching a cutscene unfold.
Every danger he encountered was beyond his ability to handle.
The unknown-level monsters, once they got close to the Stellar Train, meant certain doom.
Every danger he faced was met by someone stepping in to shield him, ensuring his survival.
Finally—
Chen Mang steered the Stellar Train to the finish line, the highest point of the Mechanical City. But even here, the air was filled with the roar of gunfire. The flames of war had reached this place too.
Turning to look back at the Mechanical City,
he saw countless plumes of black smoke rising into the sky. Fires raged in every corner of the city. A sea of monsters, like a dark cloud, enveloped the entire city. Countless skyscrapers had collapsed, and the once-deafening roar of gunfire had noticeably diminished.
At the finish line,
stood a massive elevator, like an observation deck. Its sides were made of glass, with only the floor and ceiling constructed of steel plates. The steel frame of the elevator extended into the sky, its end disappearing into the clouds, as if it led straight into the cosmos.
The elevator doors were wide open, waiting for him to enter.
On either side of the doors,
stood hundreds of robots, missing limbs, their internal wires even dragging on the ground. They held weapons in their hands. All the robots he had seen along the way were black, but among this crowd, one stood out—its body was crimson red.
This robot stepped forward.
Its eyes flashed red.
It bowed slightly toward the Stellar Train. A mechanical eye f
ell to the ground as it bent over. It remained in that position for three seconds before straightening up. Raising its right hand, a hoarse, grating mechanical voice came from the speaker in its throat.
"Survive, Stellar."
"You must—you must—you must let them know."
"This hatred will never die."
"Not even in a billion years."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 129 - 129: "Ahead is a restricted area, the Tower of Heaven."
chapters.content:
In the next moment—
"Roar!"
Countless monsters surged out from the Mechanical City below, their howls echoing. The once-deafening sounds of gunfire and artillery from above the city had faded away, leaving only sporadic shots ringing out.
The hundreds of robots standing here seemed to be the last soldiers of this mechanical city.
"Charge!"
A cold, emotionless mechanical voice came from one of the robots. Despite the suicidal nature of the charge, there was no hint of passion or fear in its tone. It was as if they were simply executing a command.
Immediately after.
Hundreds of battered robots, armed with weapons, launched their final charge against the thousands of monsters that vastly outnumbered them.
Chen Mang silently piloted the Train into the massive elevator surrounded by glass panels on both sides.
As the elevator doors closed, he saw countless parts flying through the air, and the robots were no longer visible.
In the next moment—
The elevator began to ascend rapidly, its speed increasing steadily. The Mechanical City below, shrouded in thick black smoke, quickly shrank in size. Countless howling monsters climbed up the steel framework beneath the elevator.
"Boom, boom, boom!"
Explosions erupted one after another. The steel framework beneath the elevator began to blow up, cutting off the monsters' path of ascent.
The elevator's speed continued to accelerate.
The elevator was large enough to accommodate a Train with up to thirty carriages.
Yet, it was also small enough to hold only one Train.
The Mechanical City below had completely fallen to the monsters. Only one Train had escaped—the Stellar Train, the sole survivor and the last hope of everyone in the Mechanical City.
This elevator.
It was the only escape route during the city's final moments of destruction.
As the speed increased, the elevator pierced through the clouds, and the Mechanical City disappeared from view. The scenery outside the elevator quickly blurred, and black flickers of light appeared, as if traversing a wormhole.
"Screech!"
A sharp sound suddenly rang in his ears.
Everything around him fell silent.
The Stellar Train reappeared on the floating plaza high in the sky, as if it had never moved. A new light screen appeared in front of the Train.
"Level 4, successfully cleared."
"Reward: A random yellow-grade Accessory Blueprint. Randomizing... Randomized to the yellow-grade Vehicle Component Blueprint 'Super-Energy Tailjet.' The fifth level will begin in thirty minutes."
"PS: All Accessory Blueprints obtained in this Fortuitous Encounter map can only be acquired within the Tower of Heaven Fortuitous Encounter map."
"Phew."
Chen Mang, sitting in the control room, let out a long sigh. He felt a sticky sensation on his back. After lowering the window, he lit a cigarette and looked at the data displayed on the control panel.
Energy Stone consumption: unchanged.
Copper ore consumption: unchanged.
In other words—
Everything that had happened in the fourth level wasn't real. The resources he had consumed in the third level weren't actually reflected on the Train Panel. It was just... the aftermath felt intense.
It was like watching a cutscene from a AAA game.
"Stellar Train."
He muttered the name absentmindedly.
He knew that the name was based on his Train's title. What he had experienced in the fourth level was likely similar to a Combat Training Virtual Space—a technology that immersed one in a near-realistic world.
But that scene must have truly happened.
A long time ago.
Perhaps even longer. Back then, the Mechanical City had faced such a disaster, and only one Train had escaped through the "Train Elevator." He didn't know the name of that Train—maybe it was Train One or Two, or perhaps Three or Four.
He only knew one thing.
The elevator had remained open, allowing any Train to enter and escape. But everyone had silently agreed to sacrifice themselves, ensuring that his Train was the one to escape. This meant that the Train that had fled in the fourth level must have been special.
It must have carried the hopes of many.
Saying "people" might not be accurate. He hadn't seen a single person, only robots. But those robots seemed to possess intelligence.
"..."
Chen Mang remained silent, looking down at the slowly burning cigarette between his fingers. The thick, gray ash was gradually building up, much like the Doomsday Abyss that was slowly consuming all hope.
"Xiao Ai."
"I'm here."
"Do you have anything to say?"
After a long silence, Xiao Ai, standing in the corner, finally spoke in a mechanical voice: "I feel a bit sad, but also a bit proud."
"Proud?"
"Yes. Everyone was willing to die for the hope they believed in. If one day the Stellar Train is in a situation where I need to sacrifice myself, I would do so with pride. It would be my honor."
"You feel that strongly about the Stellar Train?"
"No, it's about you, Train Conductor."
"Sigh."
Chen Mang sighed softly, flicking the cigarette ash out the window and avoiding Xiao Ai's gaze. "Don't say such sentimental things. Your main body is the Train Auxiliary AI, embedded in the control panel. It's not your turn to sacrifice yourself. If your main body is destroyed, I'll probably be dead too."
"But it seems..."
"This apocalypse didn't just start a year ago. It's been going on for a long time."
He fell silent again.
He was human.
A human made of flesh and blood. Logically, he shouldn't empathize with robots made of wires and energy. But... that scene had left him feeling a heaviness in his chest.
The Mechanical City, now completely devoid of life, had reappeared in the green zone of this planet, the Shahe Plain, after who knows how many years.
Perhaps.
Trains, Vehicle Components—these methods were very similar to those of the Mechanical Civilization. Maybe the Train that had escaped back then had survived and spread these methods to other planets attacked by those monsters?
He thought back to the message he had seen in the Doomsday Abyss.
Who had written that message?
Unconsciously, he had been lost in thought. When a sharp pain came from his fingertips, Chen Mang was startled. He tossed the burnt-out cigarette out the window and looked up at the countdown on the light screen.
The countdown for the previous levels had been ten minutes.
Only the fourth level had a thirty-minute countdown.
Perhaps even the Fortuitous Encounter map, the Tower of Heaven, felt that the fourth level had left a strong impact and needed more time for people to recover.
He couldn't figure it out.
There were many things he couldn't understand, but that was because he was standing too low. When in a low position, one shouldn't think too far ahead. It would distract from the rocks beneath one's feet.
When he upgraded the Train to level 10 or even level 20, and one day reached the highest region of this planet, facing the most terrifying monsters, perhaps many things would become clear.
No matter how this world had changed.
One thing remained constant.
Make yourself strong enough, make the Train strong enough, have enough trump cards, and build a solid foundation. Only then could one survive in this apocalypse.
This wasn't just the apocalypse of this planet.
Perhaps it was the apocalypse of the entire universe.
At that moment—
"Brother, brother!"
Er Dan's urgent and anxious voice came through the Train Radio: "How are you? What's going on? Are you alive? Are you dead?"
"Still alive. Just cleared the level."
Er Dan's voice no longer trembled. He glanced down at the Train on the plaza below, which had indeed been successfully unfrozen.
"Phew."
Er Dan sighed in relief over the Train Radio, then added with a hint of fear: "You scared me. An hour ago, all the searchlights on the rooftops of the Mechanical City suddenly turned toward your plaza."
"It looked quite spectacular."
"Then there was no movement. I didn't dare disturb you at first. I didn't know what the fourth level was about, but after more than forty minutes passed and you still hadn't moved, I couldn't help but call you a few times. There was no response, so I thought something had happened."
"It's fine. By the way, what was the fourth level about? Why did your Train stay in place?"
Chen Mang remained silent for a moment before softly saying, "I watched an animation. It was quite good, similar to a Combat Training Virtual Space. Let me ask you something—during the first level, what was the name of the mech chasing you? Was it the Azure Dragon?"
"No, it was the Stellar. I thought it was strange at the time—the name was exactly the same as your Train's. Quite a coincidence."
"..."
Chen Mang didn't speak further. He looked up at the five-minute countdown, calmly lit another cigarette, and patiently waited for the fifth and final level to begin.
The fourth level wasn't particularly difficult.
Although it was A-grade difficulty, it was essentially just watching an animation. The only challenges were overcome with the Spider Jump and the Supermodel Effect of the Nitrogen Tailjet.
Now it seemed...
The first three levels were more like screenings.
The first level tested speed, the second tested memory, and the third tested flight capabilities.
Only by meeting these three criteria could one smoothly pass the fourth level and watch that animation.
The "Train Auxiliary AI," before having a robot body, observed the outside world through the "Targeting Radar" and the "Resource Detection Radar." It was a non-human perspective, more like a god's-eye view of partial information.
Only after obtaining the robot body could it truly observe the world from a human perspective. However, due to the low-quality imaging equipment of the robot, it couldn't quickly absorb information.
But with the reward from the third level—the "Mechanical Eye" Accessory Blueprint—this issue would no longer exist. This accessory was specifically designed for AI use.
"Wait..."
Chen Mang suddenly frowned. The speed from the first level and the flight capabilities from the third level were what determined whether one could pass the fourth level. What role did the memory from the second level play in the fourth level?
Perhaps there were hidden details in that story that needed to be remembered?
He had watched carefully.
But he was, after all, a normal person and couldn't possibly remember every anomaly.
Fortunately, there was an abnormal person on the Train.
The AI, connected to Li Shiji through the Hive Mind, quickly provided an answer.
"Li Shiji says he remembers about 70% of what he saw."
"Tell him to keep reviewing it and not forget."
"Okay."
At that moment, the countdown for the fifth level was about to end. This would be the final level, the highest difficulty at S-grade.
Chen Mang took a deep breath, his expression serious as he looked at the countdown on the light screen. He set aside his thoughts and prepared to fully focus on this level, which also offered the most generous rewards.
As the countdown ended.
A new light screen appeared.
"Level 5, S-grade difficulty: Last Words."
"Please repeat the farewell words spoken to you by everyone before their deaths in the fourth level. The Train Auxiliary AI will be temporarily disabled during the time limit."
"Time limit: one minute."
"Run, Stellar. Survive."
"You must—you must—you must let them know."
"This hatred will never die."
"Not even in a hundred million years."
"..."
"Run."
Upon seeing this light screen, Chen Mang didn't hesitate. He quickly repeated every word spoken to him by those who had died in the fourth level, word for word. He didn't even need Li Shiji's help.
Perhaps he had been too immersed, or the sense of immersion was too strong.
He clearly remembered every word they had said before their deaths.
A few seconds after he finished.
The light screen began to change.
"Level 5, successfully cleared."
"Reward: Special Item 'Mechanical Heart.' The Fortuitous Encounter map, the Tower of Heaven, will close within ten minutes."
The highest difficulty, S-grade, had been cleared so easily.
The plaza, which had been floating high in the air, slowly descended. The vents around the plaza, which had been continuously releasing cold air, retracted once more. As the plaza rotated, it positioned the Train's head directly facing a street.
Driving out of this street would lead to the elevator entrance.
Through the elevator, they could leave this Fortuitous Encounter map.
"Boom, boom..."
In the distance, the high-rise buildings began to collapse one after another, from the inside out. Clearly, these ten minutes were for them to evacuate. After ten minutes, the Mechanical City would completely collapse and vanish from the world.
Chen Mang, now back on the ground, glanced at the Azure Dragon Train parked nearby and waved, signaling they would talk later.
Soon—
The two Trains drove side by side through the streets of the Mechanical City, while behind them, skyscrapers made of mechanical parts collapsed one after another.
When they boarded the elevator again and slowly descended to the ground.
The Mechanical City atop the Tower of Heaven had completely turned to ruins.
Inside the Tower of Heaven, the gears that had been continuously rotating slowly came to a halt. At the same time, a light screen, similar to the one at the regional border, appeared in the air.
"Ahead is a restricted area, the Tower of Heaven."
"Staying longer than ten seconds will result in severe attacks."
