chapters.title: Chapter 142 - 142: When You Hold a Hammer, Everything Looks Like a Nail.
chapters.content:
Er Dan, who had fled in panic almost immediately, finally stopped to catch his breath after running all the way to the Shahe Plain.
Those two enormous worm monsters.
Their level was clearly high, and his Train was no match for them.
His guess was correct. This was indeed a Fortuitous Encounter map, but it was a Fortuitous Encounter map for the Flesh Train.
"How could it be a Fortuitous Encounter map for the Flesh Train?"
Only after ensuring his safety did Er Dan begin to recall everything that had just happened, his face filled with confusion. He had seen Fortuitous Encounter maps exclusive to the Flesh Train before, but those maps were completely inaccessible to Mechanical Trains.
The entrance he had just seen was clearly drilled by a Drill Bit.
It was undoubtedly created by a Mechanical Train.
Based on this, he had thought it was a Fortuitous Encounter map for a Mechanical Train. After all, why would a Mechanical Train go to such lengths to enter a Flesh Train's Fortuitous Encounter map?
Wait...
His expression gradually turned strange. His level 3 Drill Bit would have had no effect on that fleshy wall. At least a level 10 Drill Bit would be needed. But on the Shahe Plain, the only one who could possess a level 10 Drill Bit was probably that guy.
Could it be that this hole was created by that guy?
The more he thought about it, the more likely it seemed.
"Phew..."
Er Dan wiped the cold sweat from his forehead, relieved that he hadn't contacted that guy. If he had rushed over excitedly, only to find that the so-called Fortuitous Encounter map was the hole he had just drilled, his face would have turned black instantly.
That guy, really.
Was it necessary to upgrade the Drill Bit to level 10?
But it had to be said, that guy leveled up incredibly fast. Earlier, on the Sandy River Plains Regional Leaderboard, he saw that guy had reached level 5, and his ranking had jumped from 34th to 12th.
At this rate, it wouldn't be long before he topped the leaderboard.
It was truly absurd. A level 5 Train's ranking was higher than his level 6 Train's. It made him feel utterly humiliated.
"Forget it!"
Er Dan shook off his thoughts and turned his attention to the information on the control panel screen. The green zone called the Ice and Snow World, which was located beyond the Kunlun Mountains, was currently experiencing a blizzard. It was said that after an avalanche on a high mountain, a massive arm had been revealed at the summit.
He decided to go and investigate.
Not every Train could fly. To meet the conditions for flight, it wasn't enough to just have the Bunny Cloud accessory. Many other acceleration components were also required.
And that arm was located at an altitude of 2000 meters.
Aside from him, few people could get close enough to investigate.
"Let's go!"
After taking a deep breath, Er Dan steered his Train back into the Kunlun Mountains area, preparing to pass through it and reach the green zone of the Ice and Snow World. As for the yellow zone beyond the Kunlun Mountains, he had no intention of going there yet. He planned to wait until Chen Mang reached level 6 and then go with him. It would be safer that way.
Maybe they could get a Mecha Blueprint.
It had been so long, and he hadn't come across a single Mecha Blueprint. Were they really that hard to find?
"Hmm..."
Inside the Goblin Tomb, Chen Mang stared at the blueprint in his hand for a long time before looking up at Biao Zi. "So you're saying this Mecha Blueprint was dug out of the ground?"
"Yeah."
Biao Zi nodded seriously. "Not only did we dig up this Mecha Blueprint, but we also found a Train Token, some discarded pickaxes, scattered Iron Ore, Copper Ore, wood, and even Spider Silk. There were also remains that clearly belonged to a Goblin."
"All sorts of random stuff. You can dig up anything."
"Alright, I get it. You can go now."
Back inside the Train.
Chen Mang looked at the three blueprints in his hand. One was a Mecha Blueprint, and the other two were Vehicle Component Blueprints, both green in quality but already damaged. The experiment he had wanted to conduct for a long time had finally yielded a conclusion.
Blueprints could indeed be damaged.
They looked like they had been damaged for a long time, completely faded. However, the Mecha Blueprint in his hand was still intact.
Green Quality Mecha Blueprint——
"Executioner Generation Two."
"Close-quarters burst-type Mecha."
"All firepower configurations removed, with defense and speed maximized."
"External Armor and built-in giant axe are level 4, with a maximum speed of 140 km/h. Equipped with a level 2 Energy Stone, it can fight at full capacity for 100 hours. Detailed Mecha attributes as follows..."
"Requires the pilot's Physical Fitness Index to exceed 13.5. At 14.0 or above, it can unleash its full power."
"No requirements for mental strength."
"Construction cost: 18,000 units of Crimson Heartstone."
"..."
Chen Mang sighed deeply as he looked at the Mecha Blueprint in his hand. He stepped out of the Train, lit three cigarettes, and stuck them into the ground. Looking up at the sky, he murmured, "Heaven, you really are watching over me."
He had just been wondering where to find a Mecha Blueprint, and now he had stumbled upon one.
Mechas couldn't be upgraded.
To get a stronger Mecha, you had to create one using a Mecha Blueprint.
According to the information from Xiao Ai, only Zhang Da Mei on the entire Stellar Train could use this Mecha. Everyone else's Physical Fitness Index fell short. He immediately instructed Xiao Ai to call Zhang Da Mei over.
Before leaving, he stuck three more cigarettes into the ground as a farewell to the Ziyun.
Then, after consuming 18,000 units of Crimson Heartstone, he created the first Mecha for the Stellar Train.
Chen Mang stood beside the Train and tossed a suitcase-like object into the air. It quickly unfolded and expanded, and by the time it landed on the ground, it had transformed into a heavy Mecha, four meters tall.
Not very tall, just four meters.
Smaller than the Mecha he had seen in the Mechanical City, but standing before a human, it still exuded a sense of immense weight.
The overlapping steel composite armor on its chest, with bolts the size of an adult's fist along the edges, and the crimson lines on the armor, resembled molten lava veins on a giant's skin.
The shoulders extended outward with rhino-like armor.
The cockpit was located in the abdomen. The pilot would sit there, controlling the Mecha with joysticks and mental commands. The cockpit was also equipped with various components.
Such as...
"Mini AI," "Mini Oxygen Machine," and so on.
The cockpit's observation window was shielded behind layers of protective grating. The pilot could observe the enemy with the naked eye or use the hidden cameras on the Mecha to view the surroundings on the cockpit's screen.
In its hand was an exaggerated giant axe, with a handle nearly four meters long.
"Whoa."
Chen Mang stood there, staring at the Mecha. Unable to resist, he walked up to it and pressed a hidden red button on its knee. The cockpit in the abdomen slowly descended to the ground.
He opened the cockpit door and climbed in.
The next moment.
Several cables from the back of the seat attached to his neck with suction cups, and the seat contracted inward, firmly securing his body. At the same time, silicone-like molds around the cockpit enveloped his hands and feet.
Simultaneously.
The cockpit's screen began flashing red.
"Warning, warning!"
"The pilot's Physical Fitness Index does not meet the requirements. Forced operation may result in injury."
Ignoring the warning.
Chen Mang glanced at the message. There weren't many buttons in the cockpit. When the four silicone molds fully enveloped his limbs, he felt as if he had become one with the Mecha.
He tried to raise his left arm.
As he lifted his left arm in the cockpit, the Mecha's left arm slowly rose as well.
But...
Chen Mang clenched his teeth, exerting all his strength to lift his left arm. At that moment, all he could think was, "Heavy... so heavy."
But perseverance pays off!
After a few seconds, he managed to raise his left arm into the air, though his back was already drenched in sweat.
"Phew!"
"Not bad."
Chen Mang smiled with satisfaction as he manipulated the Mecha to raise its arm. Then, he prepared to use the left arm to grab the giant axe held by the right arm. He gripped the axe with the left arm and released it with the right.
But the next moment—
"Boom."
The weight of the axe caused the Mecha to stagger and kneel on the ground.
Earlier, the axe had been stuck in the ground, so it didn't feel heavy. But when the Mecha tried to lift it, the weight became apparent.
"So... so cool!"
At that moment.
Zhang Da Mei, who had just arrived, stood frozen, staring at the scene before her. The Mecha knelt on one knee, the axe handle planted in the ground, its head raised toward the sky, like a general returning triumphantly to report to his emperor.
Then.
She saw Lord Mang step out of the Mecha's cockpit, one hand behind his back, calmly walking to the side with a cane.
"Lord... Lord Mang?"
Zhang Da Mei's eyes flashed with astonishment. She had been wondering who the pilot of this Mecha would be. Maybe Biao Ge? But it turned out to be Lord Mang. She had never fought with Lord Mang before, but she had heard from Biao Ge that he was incredibly skilled in life-and-death battles. Now she could see it was true!
"Hmm."
Chen Mang, with one hand behind his back, looked at Zhang Da Mei calmly. "This Mecha is yours from now on. Go and figure out how to operate it. There's a beginner's tutorial inside. It shouldn't be too difficult."
"Go."
Without lingering, he calmly walked back into the Train and headed to carriage number 2. Without even taking off his clothes, he lay down in the Medical Pod.
"Full treatment, quickly."
"It hurts."
He didn't know if it was a bone fracture or a pulled muscle, but it didn't matter. All he knew was that it hurt—excruciatingly.
What kind of crappy Mecha was this?
Did Mecha pilots really need such a high Physical Fitness Index?
It was probably partly because this Mecha was built using Zhang Da Mei's Individual Exoskeleton Armor as its frame, which didn't quite match him. The construction cost for this thing was much cheaper than Train Armor.
Both had level 4 defense.
This Mecha only cost 18,000 units of Crimson Heartstone.
Building one was enough. There was no point in making another, as no one else could use it.
Soon—
After consuming 11,000 units of Iron Ore, Chen Mang jumped out of the Medical Pod and strode back to the Train. He grabbed a few Roujiamo on the way and stuffed them into his mouth. He needed to eat more. His Physical Fitness Index was too low. Every little bit helped.
Back in the Train, he lay down in the Combat Training Virtual Space. He needed to practice more.
Otherwise, he might not even be able to operate a Mecha in the future.
Beside the Train.
Zhang Da Mei sat in the cockpit, her eyes filled with excitement as she controlled the Mecha, dashing across the wasteland. Occasionally, she performed jumps and slashing movements.
"Die!!!"
Caught up in the moment, Zhang Da Mei roared as she hurled the giant axe into the air. Then, with a powerful leap, the Mecha's nitrogen thrusters ignited, propelling it upward to catch the axe mid-air. Gripping the handle with both hands.
She swung the axe in a full circle, like a Noxian guillotine, bringing it down with immense force onto a dry branch on the ground.
"Boom!"
A deafening crash echoed, and a cloud of dust erupted.
As the dust settled, the Mecha knelt on one knee, the axe handle planted firmly in the ground, its head tilted upward. The mechanical eyes in its sockets glowed faintly with a crimson light.
The jet-black surface of the Mecha, adorned with crimson lines, added a touch of血腥 to its appearance.
"So cool!"
Inside the cockpit, Zhang Da Mei couldn't help but grin from ear to ear. Lord Mang's move was indeed cool. She decided that from now on, this would be her MVP celebration pose. Every time she completed a mission and returned triumphantly, she would kneel before Lord Mang like this!
A bloodied general returning victorious!
"..."
Standing nearby, Biao Zi watched the scene with a mix of admiration and envy. "You have to admit, she really has a talent for combat. This is the first Mecha on the Stellar Train, and it's just given to her. It's hard not to be jealous."
All the Train Residents were mining.
Even those who usually worked as butchers, shop clerks, or cleaners were now wielding pickaxes, digging in the open space nearby. The ground was full of buried treasures.
No one was idle. Everyone was put to work.
They only had 48 hours. Every able body was utilized.
"That Mecha requires a Physical Fitness Index of at least 13.5 to operate, and 14.0 to fully unleash its power. Even if it were given to you, could you even pilot it?"
Lao Zhu scoffed. He didn't have to work. His job was to distribute all the resources evenly during these 48 hours—things like cola, bread, water, and so on.
He was also responsible for keeping an eye out for any unknown dangers and ensuring that no Train Residents were pocketing any contraband. Especially after the first resident turned in a Train Token, there was bound to be a second.
When you hold a hammer, everything looks like a nail.
The Train Token itself was useless.
But stuffing it in your pocket showed intent. Sooner or later, it would lead to trouble.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 143 - 143: "Are You Familiar with This Place? Are There Any Level 4 Mines Here?"
chapters.content:
"Alright."
Lao Zhu patted Biao Zi's shoulder and sighed, "Let's get to work. I have to go now. Lord Mang said we can only stay here for 48 hours, so let's put in more effort."
"Go ahead."
Biao Zi glanced at Zhang Da Mei, who had already started hacking at the ground with an axe, searching for anything buried beneath. He sighed softly and silently vowed that once these few days were over, he would go back and eat 40 bread slices every day!
He would force them down if he had to!
Ten slices of bread only yielded one unit of iron ore, and one roujiamo required one unit of iron ore.
Then, combined with the Combat Training Virtual Space, he would strive to quickly raise his Physical Fitness Index to 13.5. He also wanted to pilot a mech as soon as possible.
But—
It had to be said that the long-term consumption of those bread slices barely increased his overall physical fitness. It had been over ten days since he obtained the Iris Chip, and he had been mining on the northernmost mountain of the Shahe Plain for ten days.
Yet his Physical Fitness Index had only risen from 12.1 to 12.2.
It wasn't that there was no improvement, but it was minimal.
At this rate, how long would it take for him to raise his Physical Fitness Index to 13.5? Moreover, only one decimal place was shown, and the rest was hidden. He didn't even know if he had gone from 12.19 to 12.2 or from 12.10 to 12.2.
"Only..."
Biao Zi clenched his teeth slightly and looked enviously at Zhang Da Mei, who was operating a mech in the distance. He could only eat more bread slices—100 of them, damn it!
He didn't even know if eating so many would be useful.
After all, in the apocalypse, individual strength was always insignificant. Even if his Physical Fitness Index reached 20.0, a single burst from a heavy machine gun would turn him into a mist of blood. Hadn't he seen how tough Zhang Da Mei's body was? Yet she was still taken down by a single burst from his Gatling Gun in the arena.
No matter how high your Physical Fitness Index was, if you encountered a Level 2 monster unarmed, it would be useless.
Only after your Physical Fitness Index was high enough would you have the chance to use heavy individual weapons that required a certain level of physical fitness, such as... mechs.
"..."
Chen Mang called Lao Zhu over and gave him a few instructions. Then he recorded the coordinates of this place on the control panel screen and slowly pushed the control lever, steering the Train deeper into the black fog.
As the Train departed, the visibility in the mine instantly decreased. Only a few dozen flashlights provided a much weaker light source. When the Train Residents saw the Train leave, they all put down their work, their faces filled with panic, and couldn't help but ask:
"Where did Lord Mang go?"
"Biao Ge, where did Lord Mang go? Will he come back?"
"Did something happen?"
The initial excitement on their faces had completely vanished, replaced by anxiety and unease.
At first, everyone was excited because of the free cola these past few days and the abundance of mines to dig, which meant they could earn more Stellar Coupons. There was also the sense of security from these Level 3 mines that could make the Train stronger, as well as the thrill of arriving at an unknown location.
But as the Stellar Train departed, all these emotions turned into unease.
None of them knew where this was.
A place without a moon or sky, just utter darkness. When they looked up, they could only see a void-like blackness. When the Stellar Train was still here, they felt a sense of security. But once it left, everyone panicked.
What if some monster appeared? They would be left to die, with no idea where to escape.
"Quiet."
Biao Zi held a loudspeaker and looked at the crowd with a cold expression. "Pay attention to the notice Director Ai sent in the top left corner. Lord Mang has gone deeper to continue the exploration. There won't be any monsters in this space, and everyone's safety is guaranteed."
"Even if there is danger, we will stand in front, and Lord Mang will come back."
"Continue mining as you were, just like before."
"Only Level 3 mines at most..."
In the desolate and dark space, Chen Mang stared at the Resource Detection Radar on the control panel screen and murmured. Although those two Level 3 Iron Mines were already perfect, they weren't the Level 3 "Crimson Heartstone" mine deep beneath the Iron Ridge Wasteland.
That Level 3 mine had a very low ore content and was exhausted in just over an hour, yielding 180,000 units of Crimson Heartstone.
These two Level 3 Iron Mines had an extremely high ore content, with millions of units of iron ore, enough to keep them mining for 48 hours.
He had been gone for ten minutes now.
Along the way, the Resource Detection Radar kept beeping incessantly. There were Level 1 and Level 2 mines everywhere, and Level 3 mines appeared occasionally, but he had yet to encounter a Level 4 mine.
"Doba."
"Are you familiar with this place? Are there any Level 4 mines here?"
He turned his head to look at Doba. He hadn't brought anyone else, only Doba, as Doba was somewhat of a guide here.
"Not really."
Doba shook his head seriously. "My memory is a bit hazy. I didn't witness the fall of the Goblin civilization. I didn't live that long—I died before I could see that moment."
"Much of my memory is lost, with only a small portion preserved."
"I only remember that from some point onward, every time I died, I would appear in this space. There were many scattered items buried beneath the ground. I dug up a Train Token and a pickaxe and started building a Goblin Train."
"I don't know how big this place is."
"I don't know if there are any Level 4 mines here. I've never encountered one."
Chen Mang nodded and didn't say anything more, though he furrowed his brows slightly and continued driving deeper into the darkness. By now, he was already far from Biao Zi and the others, and they had lost contact. However, if anything happened and someone died, it would be displayed on the Train Crew roster, making it easier for him to return immediately.
It seemed that the highest-level mines in this space might only be Level 3?
Just then—
"Hmm?"
In the distance, he spotted a Train wreck with seven carriages. The carriages were severely damaged and abandoned. He immediately stopped the Stellar Train in front of it and, along with Doba and Xiao Ai, jumped off to take a closer look.
The carriages were empty.
There was nothing inside the Train, no wreckage, no scattered resources, no food—just complete emptiness. As they got closer, they could smell an intense, rotting odor.
It seemed that this Train wasn't very high-level, probably around a Level 2 or Level 3 Train.
The only unusual thing was...
The wheels of this Train weren't Wind-Fire Wheels or Spider Legs, but Goblin remains. Under each carriage, there were four Goblin skeletons. Despite the passage of time, the dozens of Goblin skeletons still stood there, using their shoulders to carry the Train.
It looked somewhat like a ghost bride's sedan.
"What... what is this?"
Doba stared at the scene in front of him, momentarily stunned. Then, a memory deep in his mind suddenly resurfaced, and he roared in anger, his face twisted with rage. "Those bastards! They actually did it in the end!"
"What's going on?"
Chen Mang frowned slightly and looked at this strange, scrapped Goblin Train. "Do you recognize this special type of wheel? It's not made from Goblin Merchants, is it?"
This was the first time he had seen "humanoid" wheels. Although he knew there were many special types of wheels, such as "Spider Legs," using Goblins as wheels seemed excessively bizarre. He had once considered using Goblin Merchants as wheels, as their carrying capacity and foot strength were impressive, and they had great endurance.
But it was just a fleeting thought. After all, while Goblin Merchants were fast when traveling light, they could only reach speeds of 150 km/h, which was much slower compared to other wheels.
The only possible advantage was lower energy consumption—ten slices of bread and a bottle of cola per 100 kilometers.
"No."
Doba took a deep breath, his eyes red and his body tense as he spoke in a trembling voice. "These are wheels made from Black Market Merchants."
"Before I died, I remember the Goblin Think Tank proposed an idea to use Black Market Merchants as wheels to build a Train. That way, the Train could have the same random teleportation ability as Black Market Merchants, allowing it to infiltrate enemy lines and become a ghost Train that no one could detect."
"But—"
"When Black Market Merchants carry heavy objects and teleport randomly, the heavy objects aren't teleported with them—only the Black Market Merchants themselves are teleported. The only solution was to fuse the Black Market Merchants with the Train, which was an extremely cruel process."
"Especially since each Black Market Merchant teleports randomly, making it impossible to have all of them teleport to the same point. There were also many other challenges to overcome, and almost all Goblins opposed using such a cruel plan on their own people."
"Particularly the Black Market Merchants—each one was a blessed individual of the Goblin race. This went against our ancestral teachings!"
"So the plan was shelved."
"I never thought that after I died, they managed to overcome all the challenges and built this Train with Black Market Merchants as its wheels. Unlike us, Black Market Merchants aren't naturally strong. Carrying such a heavy Train on their shoulders must have been excruciating, leaving them half-dead, and relying on other means to stay alive. It's even more cruel than the enemy!"
"..."
Chen Mang's eyes flickered with shock as he looked at the scrapped Goblin Train in front of him. Although it was somewhat inhumane, he had to admit that the concept was perfect—a Train that could teleport randomly would indeed become a ghost Train, casting a terrifying shadow over its enemies.
But...
In battles of that scale, how would they replenish ammunition? What if they teleported into the middle of the enemy's forces? There were many obvious issues, including how to control all the Goblin Merchants to teleport to the same point. He couldn't figure out how to solve that problem.
Indeed, once a war starts, all sorts of "idea kings" emerge.
He sighed softly, admitting that humans were the same. Once a war began, all kinds of "idea kings" would come up with crazy schemes, and all sorts of black technology would be thrown into the mix.
"Train Conductor."
Doba, his eyes red, looked at Chen Mang. "I want to bury my fellow clansmen here. They've sacrificed too much."
"Go ahead, bury them."
Chen Mang watched as Doba began digging a hole, then glanced at the Goblin Train. He had no intention of using the Geothermal Furnace to consume this scrapped Train. A Level 2 or Level 3 Goblin Train wouldn't yield much iron ore even if consumed.
Moreover, Doba was already crying his eyes out.
If he went ahead and consumed the Train right in front of the deceased's family, it would be like digging up a grave and grinding the bones to ashes in front of the bereaved.
It would make leading this team much harder in the future.
The Goblin remains had been there for who knows how long. Doba only had to lightly tap them with a pickaxe, and the skeletons crumbled to the ground. However, the arm bones were completely fused with the Train and couldn't be removed—they had to be pried out forcibly.
"..."
Chen Mang leaned on his cane, unconsciously rubbing the smooth red gem at its tip. He gazed into the dark depths of the distance, lost in thought, and remained silent.
Soon.
Doba had thrown all the Goblin remains into the pit and built a small mound over it. Then, with red eyes, he walked up to Chen Mang, lowered his head, and said hoarsely, "It's a pity. If they had met you, sir, their fate might not have been so tragic."
"Yeah."
Chen Mang nodded without saying much. He simply took Doba and Xiao Ai back to the Train and continued exploring further into the darkness.
Thirty minutes later.
"Boom!"
The Stellar Train slammed heavily into a wall. The high-speed rotating Drill Bit pressed against the wall, attempting to break through. But after a full five minutes, the wall showed no signs of damage.
Inside the Train, Chen Mang stared at the wall made of dirt. He had reached the edge of this space—a towering wall. Even when he flew up to 5,500 meters, he still couldn't get past it.
The same was true underground.
His Drill Bit had already been upgraded to Level 50. Even the walls of the Flesh Map could be forcibly drilled through.
But this wall seemed utterly impervious.
This was the end.
He slowly retracted the Drill Bit and decided not to continue trying. At this rate, even if he upgraded the Drill Bit to Level 100, he probably still wouldn't be able to break through this wall. He realized he had developed a bad habit.
In the past, when he encountered impassable walls, such as regional barriers, he would usually just go around or give up.
But after getting the Level 50 Drill Bit, whenever he saw something, he wanted to try drilling into it.
What if it worked?
"Let's head back."
Chen Mang shook his head and turned his attention away from the wall. This was clearly the boundary of the map. Trying to break through from the inside wasn't just difficult—even if he succeeded, it probably wouldn't lead to anything good...
On the way back, he didn't take the same route but instead followed the edge of the wall.
An hour later.
The Stellar Train returned to Biao Zi and the others. As the Headlights lit up, visibility was restored.
The Train Residents, who had been on edge the entire time, finally breathed a sigh of relief.
Along the way, apart from that scrapped Goblin Train, they hadn't seen any other Goblin Trains, though they did spot many scattered Goblin remains on the ground.

chapters.title: Chapter 144 - 144
chapters.content:
"Lord Mang, the mission failed."
It wasn't a complete body. Scattered hand bones, leg bones, and skulls were strewn across the area, most of them buried underground, with only sharp corners protruding.
He had originally guessed that the space of the "Goblin Tomb" might be circular.
Unexpectedly, it was square.
He had walked along the edge of the wall and returned to the starting point. The length and width were consistent, the angles were all right angles—a standard square. As for the ground, after drilling down 6,000 meters, he encountered another wall lying horizontally, marking the edge of the map.
The Stellar Train could only fly up to 5,500 meters. Barring any accidents, the height should also be exactly 6,000 meters.
The entire Goblin Tomb was such a place. The area wasn't too large, as if it were a space independent of the planet. There was no sun, no light, no clouds, and no weather changes, but it wasn't lacking in oxygen.
Returning to the coordinates, Chen Mang leaned back in his chair, deep in thought, not speaking.
He hadn't found any Level 4 Iron Ore. The highest was only Level 3. There was no need to change locations; this place was sufficient. All he needed to do now was wait patiently here for over 40 hours.
He glanced at the Train Radio.
No one had been chatting for a long time. Ever since entering this area, he had completely lost contact with the outside world.
After stretching lazily, he once again headed toward the "Combat Training Virtual Space" nearby.
He would train a bit to enhance his Physical Fitness Index.
A man had to be tough, after all.
Soon—
Forty-eight hours passed.
The moment the countdown ended, a massive portal over thirty meters tall appeared in front of the Stellar Train. The center of the portal resembled the Milky Way, appearing both deep and incredibly beautiful.
All the Train Residents had already boarded and were in a state of waiting.
The moment the portal appeared, the Stellar Train drove into it.
After passing through the portal, the Stellar Train reappeared on the Shahe Plain. As the portal closed, the sky was filled with stars, and the surroundings were quite peaceful. The past two days felt like a fleeting dream.
If it weren't for the large amount of Iron Ore loaded onto the Train, they might have thought it was all just a dream.
"It's really good."
Chen Mang looked at the 4.9 million units of Iron Ore on the Train Panel and couldn't help but smile slightly. The Goblin Tomb not only had Iron Ore and Copper Ore but also a lumberyard. He hadn't chosen the Copper Ore, as Iron Ore was still a higher priority.
However, there were only these three types of resources—nothing like the rare "Crimson Heartstone."
It's a pity that one could only enter once a month.
If only he could go in one more time.
Wait—
He looked at the "Token of Civilization" in the control panel drawer. As long as he completed another trip to the Goblin Ruins and finished an S-level mission, wouldn't he be able to obtain another Token of Civilization and enter again?
He naturally couldn't go in himself.
But he could have another Train go in.
Without hesitation, he immediately had Xiao Ai call Biao Zi to the Train room.
At this moment, all the residents had already fallen asleep. Even with unlimited cola provided, working continuously for 48 hours was a significant toll on both the mind and body. At this point, even if the sky were to fall, all they wanted was to sleep.
A person's core desires are essentially three things:
Hunger, sleep, and lust.
Among them, hunger is the most important, while lust is the weakest. Only when one is full can they think of lust.
Only Biao Zi and Lao Zhu, who had taken turns sleeping on schedule, didn't feel too tired at the moment.
Standing in front of the Train room, Biao Zi nervously recalled everything he had done these past days. After confirming that he hadn't made any mistakes, a sudden thought crossed his mind—was it because of the time he risked his life exploring the cave and caverns?
Was Lord Mang going to reward him?
Although he hadn't achieved any major feats that time, his courage was evident, and his loyalty to the Train had been perfectly demonstrated.
Thinking of this, the nervousness on Biao Zi's face instantly dissipated, replaced by excitement and anticipation as he pushed open the door to the Train room and looked at Lord Mang sitting in the chair.
"Lord Mang, you called for me?"
"Yes."
Lord Mang tossed a token-like object into his arms. Biao Zi instinctively caught it and, upon closer inspection, realized it was a "Train Token." A look of confusion and bewilderment flashed in his eyes.
What did this mean?
Immediately after, Lord Mang's voice rang in his ears again.
"Take this and build a Train. You'll be the Train Conductor."
As soon as the words fell, Biao Zi instantly snapped awake. His legs went weak, and he immediately knelt on the ground, his eyes red and his voice choked with tears as he shouted, "Lord Mang, I've never had any disloyal thoughts toward you or the Train! I've never thought of going independent!"
"There must be some villain spreading rumors about me behind my back!"
"Lord Mang, you can have someone interrogate me—I'm truly loyal!"
"..."
Chen Mang gave Biao Zi a look of exasperation and said impatiently, "Get up. What's with a grown man crying like a woman?"
"I'm not asking you to go independent."
"This is a green zone. Trying to go independent with just a Train Token—you'd die without even knowing how."
"Also, take this card. I have a mission for you. Later, I'll take you to the 'Goblin Ruins' Fortuitous Encounter map. Insert this card into the control panel, and you'll gain access to this Fortuitous Encounter map."
"Once inside, you'll encounter five tasks of different difficulty levels."
"The hardest task is the S-level mission. The reward is a Token of Civilization. The requirement is to have the Train shelter 50 Goblins. Later, go find Doba and have him bring 60 Goblins to squeeze into your Train."
"After completing that S-level mission, return to the Stellar Train."
"You're the only one among all the Train Residents who's been a Train Conductor before. You're definitely the most suitable candidate. Understand? Any questions?"
"Well, uh..."
Only now did Biao Zi fully understand. He wiped the tears from the corners of his eyes with his sleeve and cautiously asked in a low voice, "Lord Mang, when I come back, can I still be the captain of the Guardian team?"
"Of course. As long as you don't die in there, it's still yours."
"No problem! I'll complete the mission!"
"Go."
After leaving the Goblin Ruins map, Chen Mang activated the Token of Civilization. Exiting the Goblin Tomb, they were still in the same location. The entrance to the "Goblin Ruins" Fortuitous Encounter map was the low hill behind them.
Soon, a brand-new Level 1 Train was built. It was extremely simple, consisting of only one locomotive and two carriages. Each carriage was packed with 30 Goblins, all sound asleep, including Doba, who was in a daze.
Goblins weren't machines. Digging continuously for 48 hours—even an iron man would collapse.
"Whew..."
Biao Zi sat in the control panel chair, using his mind to control this Level 1 Train. For some reason, he felt restless, especially with the Stellar Train still behind him. The discomfort was overwhelming.
Without further delay, he inserted the card into the control panel. Soon, the small hill in front of him split open, revealing a passage wide enough for the Train to enter. He pushed the control lever hard, driving the Train into the passage.
"Let's hope this works."
Chen Mang looked at the "Goblin Ruins" map that had opened again and turned his gaze to the stack of Train Tokens in the nearby drawer. Over the past 48 hours, besides mining Iron Ore, they had also dug up a lot from the ground.
But the only intact blueprint they found was that "Mecha Blueprint."
They had also dug up quite a few blueprints, but they were all in a scrapped state, along with some other miscellaneous junk. He hadn't thrown any of it away, instead collecting it all. Who knows, maybe one day they'd find parts that could repair the blueprints.
After all, they had plenty of Refrigerators.
As long as it wasn't absolute garbage, he kept it all. It might come in handy someday.
However, they had dug up quite a few Train Tokens. Combined with the ones he already had, there were now 14 Train Tokens on the Train.
Not bad.
If only these things could be combined into one, he would probably have an Exquisite Train Token by now.
If Biao Zi returned successfully, these 14 Train Tokens could be exchanged for 14 Tokens of Civilization. That way, he could basically guarantee that he could stay in the "Goblin Tomb" all day, mining to his heart's content!
Thirty minutes later.
The "Goblin Ruins" Fortuitous Encounter map slowly opened again. The Train built by Biao Zi slowly emerged and parked beside him. Soon, Biao Zi jumped off the Train and knelt on the ground, his face filled with guilt.
"Lord Mang, the mission failed."
"Failed?"
Chen Mang frowned and stepped down, looking at Biao Zi in confusion. "Didn't I give you 60 Goblins? How could you fail?"
"The S-level mission reward was already completed and couldn't be chosen again."
"Only the A-level to D-level missions were available."
"I see."
Chen Mang paused for a moment but didn't seem too disappointed. He helped Biao Zi up and patted his shoulder casually. "It's fine. This was just an attempt. If it failed, it failed."
"Take these Goblins back."
"Uh..."
Seeing that Lord Mang wasn't blaming him too much, Biao Zi carefully handed over an Accessory Blueprint. "The C-level mission couldn't be chosen either, so only the A, B, and D-level missions were available."
"I thought that even if the S-level reward couldn't be chosen, since we were already here, we shouldn't return empty-handed."
"The A and B-level missions were too difficult—I wasn't confident. So I chose the D-level mission."
"Although the reward is the lowest."
"I figured something is better than nothing. At least we could minimize the loss."
"..."
Chen Mang looked down at the white-grade Accessory Blueprint in his hand, silent for a long time. Finally, he looked up at Biao Zi, patted his shoulder again, and said softly, "Biao Zi..."
"You've done so much for the Stellar Train. You really don't have to go this far..."
"It's what I should do."
"You've worked hard. Go rest."
"Yes!"
After Biao Zi left, Chen Mang looked at the white-grade Accessory Blueprint in his hand and sighed helplessly. Biao Zi's logic wasn't wrong. Since the mission failed, why return empty-handed?
Might as well salvage something.
But...
Was Biao Zi being too harsh on himself?
If it were him, he definitely wouldn't go to such lengths for a white-grade Accessory Blueprint. At the very least, it would have to be another Token of Civilization or something similar to make him consider it.
Accessory Name: Redheart Nut Production Line
All the accessories obtained in this map were exclusive to Goblin Trains. The "Redheart Nut" was a snack that Goblins loved. He hadn't seen it before, but after producing it, he could give some to Doba and the others as snacks. He wasn't sure if the Supermodel Effect would enhance physical fitness.
However, Biao Zi's actions reminded him of something.
He called for Li Shiji and handed him another Train Token.
"You, go in and complete the B-level mission reward."
Ten minutes later.
He looked at the Train with only a locomotive and nodded in satisfaction. If he remembered correctly, the B-level mission reward involved watching a cutscene of the Goblins' demise, memorizing some information from it, and answering four out of five questions correctly to pass.
This kind of task was right up Li Shiji's alley—professional expertise at its finest.
Exchanging a Train Token for a "yellow-grade" Vehicle Component was worth it.
As for the A-level mission reward, he decided to skip it. The difficulty aside, it required 30 days to complete, and he didn't have that much time to spare here.
Thirty minutes later.
Li Shiji successfully emerged from the Goblin Ruins and handed him a yellow-grade Accessory Blueprint.
Everything went smoothly.
According to Li Shiji, the S-level and D-level missions had already been completed and couldn't be chosen again.
"Good."
Chen Mang looked at the yellow-grade Accessory Blueprint in his hand and smiled. He then controlled the Stellar Train to absorb the two nearby Trains.
Although both were Fortuitous Encounter maps, the "Tower of Heaven" and the "Goblin Ruins" were different.
The Tower of Heaven was a challenge-based map. After exiting, the map became a restricted area. On the other hand, the "Goblin Ruins" could be entered repeatedly as long as you had the coordinates and the key.
However, once a mission of any difficulty was completed, subsequent Trains couldn't choose that mission again. For example, his S-level mission, Biao Zi's D-level mission, and Li Shiji's B-level mission.
As for the original owner of this key card, that person was likely the first to enter this Fortuitous Encounter map. Er Dan had told him that the first person to enter a Fortuitous Encounter map received special treatment. Even if that person completed one of the five missions, that mission wouldn't disappear.
The yellow-grade Accessory Blueprint in his hand was also an exclusive accessory for Goblin Trains. It could only be obtained in places like the Goblin Ruins, making it quite rare.
Goblin Ticket
The effect is equivalent to a Train Ticket.
The difference is that a Train Ticket has a range limit—it can only be used to teleport back to the Train if you're within 10,000 meters of it. However, the Goblin Ticket is different—no matter where you are, you can teleport back to the Train.
But it's only for Goblins.
Humans can't use it.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 145 - 145: "Doomsday Cannon"
chapters.content:
Chen Mang spent 49,400 units of Iron Ore to directly upgrade the "Red Heart Nut Production Line" and the "Goblin Ticket," two exclusive accessories for the Goblin Train, both to level 10. Each of them gained two Supermodel Effects.
-
"Red Heart Nut Production Line Level 5 Supermodel Effect": Nuts are automatically shelled when produced.
"Red Heart Nut Production Line Level 10 Supermodel Effect": When consumed by males, it slightly enhances sexual performance; when consumed by females, it slightly reduces menstrual cramps.
"Goblin Ticket Level 5 Supermodel Effect": If teleportation fails, the user's first-person perspective from the last minute before death is transmitted back to the Train.
"Goblin Ticket Level 10 Supermodel Effect": None.
-
"Hmm."
Chen Mang walked to the 4th Living Carriage, casually picked up a freshly produced nut, and examined it in his palm. It resembled a macadamia nut, red in color, and looked quite appetizing. He immediately tossed one into his mouth.
The taste wasn't bad.
Crisp, sweet, with a hint of dragon fruit in the creamy flavor.
He had never eaten this type of nut before, but he had to admit it tasted good. The production cost was also cheap—one unit of Iron Ore could produce ten nuts, the same price as a slice of bread. It made for a decent snack.
He grabbed another handful of nuts and placed them on a nearby plate, then carried the plate toward the Train's control room.
The sound of the night wind howling faintly seeped through the gaps between the carriages.
The wind was strong tonight.
But then again, were there female Goblins in that batch? He hadn't noticed. And do Goblins even have menstrual cycles?
"Biao Zi?"
In the 7th Guard Carriage, Lao Zhu looked at Biao Zi, whose face seemed slightly off, and asked with concern, "What's wrong? Are you injured or something? You look terrible."
"It's nothing."
Biao Zi took a deep breath and shook his head. After a moment of silence, he rasped, "I'm just tired, feeling a bit unwell."
"If you're tired, get some rest. It's the second team's turn to keep watch tonight."
"Alright."
"You look like something terrible happened to you."
"It's fine."
In the Train's control room.
Chen Mang looked at the several messages from the "Azure Dragon Train" on the Train Radio. He had been completely out of contact while in the Goblin Tomb and only now had the time to respond.
"I was out of touch for the past few days. What's up?"
The next moment—
Er Dan's urgent voice rang out in the control room.
"Bro, you finally replied!"
"Big trouble!"
"I've found something huge! I'm in the middle of a desperate escape—do not come to the 'Ice and Snow World' area. The people here are practically wiped out!!!"
"I'm trying to save as many as I can. I'm the only one who can fly."
"No time to explain too much. There's an incredibly terrifying boss that was sealed in the mountains. The recent snowstorm caused a landslide, and its arm was exposed. I went to take a look and accidentally released it."
"This boss is slaughtering every Train in this area. I'm rushing to save people now. Damn it, this can't be bad karma, right? I didn't know it would be so easy to release that thing!"
"..."
Chen Mang stared blankly at the control panel screen. The "Ice and Snow World" area was a green zone located west of the Kunlun Mountains region. He hadn't expected this guy to have run that far.
But...
Although his words were rushed and vague, it was clear that he had caused a major disaster by accidentally releasing a huge boss.
Chen Mang's expression turned slightly odd as he fell silent.
Could someone really be that careless?
A boss sealed inside a mountain—unless you topple the entire mountain, it should be hard to release it. Still, he quickly replied.
"What level is the monster? I might be able to give it a try."
"You can't get in! This area has been sealed off!"
Well.
He had been eager to test his "Death Spin," composed of a level 50 Drill Bit and level 50 Car Blade, but now he had no chance. He then turned his attention to the four new accessories that became available after the Train reached level 5.
-
"Doomsday Cannon": Blue-grade accessory, requires 5,000 units of Iron Ore to craft.
"Dust-Free Glass": Yellow-grade accessory, requires 1,000 units of Iron Ore to craft.
"Space Gate": Yellow-grade accessory, requires 1,000 units of Iron Ore to craft.
"Spray Nozzle": White-grade accessory, requires 100 units of Iron Ore to craft.
-
These four accessories were the ones that became available after the Train reached level 5.
There wasn't much to say.
After consuming 96,500 units of Iron Ore, he crafted the latter three accessories and upgraded them all to level 10.
"Spray Nozzle."
A Living-series accessory, upgrading it had no special effects. Each Spray Nozzle was connected to the water tank and could create a public bathroom in the Refrigerator, divided into male and female sections.
Previously, washing up on the Train involved pouring Mineral Water into a basin and sitting in it to clean oneself. Now, bathing had become much more convenient.
-
"Spray Nozzle Level 5 Supermodel Effect": Comes with strong detergent.
"Spray Nozzle Level 10 Supermodel Effect": None.
-
The built-in strong detergent could effectively and quickly remove dirt from the body.
As for the "Dust-Free Glass," a yellow-grade accessory, it applied a transparent film to the glass that didn't obstruct vision but prevented any dust or bloodstains from sticking to it.
This ensured that the next time the Train charged into a Corpse Tide, the front windshield wouldn't be smeared with sticky blood, and it would also handle heavy rainstorms well.
-
"Dust-Free Glass Level 5 Supermodel Effect": Can toggle between one-way glass or not.
"Dust-Free Glass Level 10 Supermodel Effect": Can filter light, ensuring that the light entering the Train doesn't harm the human body.
-
One-way glass meant that when activated, he could see through the glass, but people outside couldn't see him.
Of course.
It could also be set so that he couldn't see outside, but people outside could see him.
However, the latter would rarely be useful.
The former, on the other hand, was quite practical and could be used in many situations.
For example, when interacting with other Trains, or... when taking Ji Chuchu out for some excitement.
Lastly, the "Space Gate" accessory was worth mentioning.
Its effect was similar to a level 10 Refrigerator.
He had always been curious about one thing: he had a level 10 Refrigerator, which greatly improved the Train's space utilization. What about other Trains? As Train levels increased and populations grew, carriages would inevitably become insufficient.
Hundreds of carriages might sound impressive, but the cost of crafting Armor and firepower to cover hundreds of carriages would skyrocket.
Now, a solution had arrived.
This "Space Gate" would do the trick.
Chen Mang walked to the second carriage. The level 10 Space Gate he had just crafted was embedded in the wall of the second carriage. It looked like an ordinary wooden door, but upon pushing it open, the space behind it was vast.
It was a square space, 1,000 meters in length and width.
At level 1, it was 100 meters in length and width. After upgrading to level 10, it became 1,000 meters.
This was a yellow-grade accessory, meaning that even without Murphy Stone, one could still have a space of 500 meters in length and width.
The ground in this space was covered with grass that just reached the shoes.
Looking around, it was a sea of green, with clouds floating in the sky and even a sun. Around the space, a circle of pine trees was planted, making it look like a paradise, starkly out of place in the apocalypse.
"Not bad."
Chen Mang smiled as he looked at the scene before him. The green grass on the ground was a result of the "Space Gate's" level 5 Supermodel Effect. As for the white clouds, the sun, and the circle of trees, they were all projected using the "Holographic Projection."
They weren't real.
But they looked indistinguishable from the real thing.
Looking up at the sky from within the space, the clouds seemed extremely far away, and there was no sense of oppression, even though the height of the space was only 50 meters.
If he placed the Refrigerators inside.
A high-end, luxurious residential community would be complete.
When the first Train Resident exchanged for a Refrigerator, he would place it inside this space. A community in such a living environment would be incredibly tempting, boosting work motivation even further.
-
"Space Gate Level 5 Supermodel Effect": After consuming Iron Ore, the space can be modified, such as adding grass or flowers.
"Space Gate Level 10 Supermodel Effect": Can be disassembled and relocated anywhere on the Train.
-
The area was much larger than a level 10 Refrigerator, but there was one thing it couldn't match: the Refrigerator could be taken out of the Train, while this couldn't.
Each had its strengths.
After finishing all this.
Chen Mang checked the amount of Iron Ore, took out 3.2 million units, and upgraded the Armor of all 15 carriages, including the Train's head, to level 7.
With level 7 Armor, even venturing into yellow zones wouldn't be too daunting.
He still had 1.55 million units of Iron Ore left.
After a moment of thought, he spent 950,000 units of Iron Ore to craft a "Doomsday Cannon" on each of the first ten carriages, all upgraded to level 10!
Currently, against bosses, he had the Train Stunt "Death Spin" and "Ground Burst Missiles," but the former had a cooldown, and the latter was too costly.
For weaker monsters, he had Heavy Machine Guns, Car Blades, Drill Bits, and the Eighteen-Barrel Cherry Blossom Fall Rocket, though he hadn't had the chance to use the rocket yet.
For intimidating firepower, he had the "Repeating Ballista."
This white-grade accessory was too useless. He was planning to dismantle all the Repeating Ballistas when he needed a new carriage, freeing up space.
He had solutions for both strong and weak enemies.
But for those in the middle, he had nothing. The "Doomsday Cannon" perfectly filled that gap.
Chen Mang stepped off the Train and stood on the Shahe Plain, looking at the Stellar Train parked on the plain.
Fifteen carriages in total.
Each carriage was covered in thick, black Armor. If you struck it with a pickaxe, you'd hear a dull echo.
On the outside of the carriages were mounted four Makeshift Heavy Machine Guns, ten Doomsday Cannons, and one "Hell Gatling Gun."
The Doomsday Cannon had the largest caliber.
It was more than three times that of the Hell Gatling Gun and far exceeded that of the Heavy Machine Gun. It also had eighteen barrels, resembling a Gatling Gun, with an extremely fast rate of fire. A single burst would be hard for any carbon-based life form to withstand.
Both the "Hell Gatling Gun" and the "Doomsday Cannon" were blue-grade accessories.
The Hell Gatling Gun was unlocked when the Train reached level 4. He had only crafted one and didn't upgrade it, as it was merely a transitional firepower accessory not worth wasting resources on.
But the "Doomsday Cannon" was different.
As a blue-grade accessory, it had sixteen more barrels than the Hell Gatling Gun, and its power was naturally far greater.
Most importantly.
Its level 5 Supermodel Effect was a 50% reduction in consumption. This effect, while unremarkable on other accessories, was exceptional on a firepower accessory.
At level 10, the consumption was halved again.
Two consecutive halvings.
"Level 1 Ammo": 5 units of Copper Ore to craft one round.
"Level 2 Ammo": 10 units of Copper Ore to craft one round.
"Level 3 Ammo": 20 units of Copper Ore to craft one round.
"Level 4 Ammo": 50 units of Copper Ore to craft one round.
"Level 6 Ammo": 100 units of Copper Ore to craft one round.
"Level 7 Ammo": 200 units of Copper Ore to craft one round.
The price of a level 6 round, originally 100 units of Copper Ore, became 25 units after two halvings.
This was much cheaper than Heavy Machine Gun bullets.
A level 6 Heavy Machine Gun bullet cost 100 units of Copper Ore.
The price was much lower.
But the power was greater, making the cost-performance ratio almost maximized!
"Pretty good."
Chen Mang looked at the ten "Doomsday Cannons" on the Stellar Train with satisfaction. The Stellar Train currently had 850,000 units of Copper Ore, enough to buy nearly 100,000 level 6 rounds.
100,000 rounds.
That could carpet-bomb an area.
That's a cannon, not a machine gun! The rounds explode!
"Whew!"
He let out a long breath, feeling a wave of security wash over him. In the apocalypse, having a Train with such a configuration was pure luxury. The issue of ammo consumption, which had been troubling him, was now resolved.
"Consumption halved."
This effect on a firepower accessory was nothing short of a divine skill!
If only Supermodel Effects could be chosen.
He'd set all firepower accessories from level 1 to 50 to have the "consumption halved" effect, and he could practically walk anywhere, setting off fireworks wherever he went.
Chen Mang glanced at his Iron Ore balance.
Only 600,000 units left.
Two days of hard mining, and he had spent it all in a matter of minutes.
At that moment—
Someone sent him a private message.
-
"A-grade Potential Level 5 Train, World Weary Train": "Friend, can we meet and talk? Someone asked me to connect you with someone who wants to meet you."
-
"World Weary Train?"
Chen Mang frowned slightly. He had some impression of this Train—it was the Train with the highest potential on the Shahe Plain, aside from his own.
Without much thought, he sent back three dots.
-
"Don't rush to reject."
"In the apocalypse, everyone has the chance to encounter opportunities that could skyrocket them to success, but that's unsustainable."
"All A-grade Potential Flesh Trains on the Shahe Plain were nurtured by them."
