chapters.title: Chapter 154 - 154: "How the Hell Can a Logistics Guy Handle a Mech?"
chapters.content:
Though it might sound perplexing, a logistics personnel had acquired the second mech of the Stellar Train.
And it was the "Leech" mech.
But upon closer thought, it made sense—Li Shiji was the only one on the entire Stellar Train whose mental strength exceeded 14.5.
"Sigh."
Biao Zi remained silent for a long time before letting out a soft sigh. "I'm not upset, just feeling a bit inferior. Zhang Da Mei and Li Shiji, they've both been blessed by the heavens with talent. Why don't I have that kind of gift?"
"How the hell can a logistics guy handle a mech?"
Just then—
Li Shiji, who had been standing nearby, walked over.
"Biao Ge."
Li Shiji looked at Biao Zi with a serious expression. "Lord Mang has granted me the use of the second mech on the Stellar Train, the 'Leech.' It's an honor, but as you both know, I'm just a logistics guy. It's hard for me to fully utilize the mech's potential."
"Didn't I just apply for access to the Combat Training Virtual Space?"
"I've created a map inside that can boost mental strength. Biao Ge, why don't you come take a look with me?"
Biao Zi was slightly taken aback, a hint of embarrassment flashing in his eyes. "Uh, Li Shiji, I was just..."
"Let's go."
Lao Zhu chuckled, wrapping an arm around Biao Zi's shoulder. "This guy often talks nonsense. Don't mind him. Show us that map you made."
Biao Zi, Lao Zhu, and Li Shiji entered the Combat Training Virtual Space and appeared in a plaza.
In front of them was a white room.
In the center, a light screen floated.
Mental Strength Enhancement Training Map.
Creator: Li Shiji.
"Here's the thing."
Li Shiji stood still and explained to Lao Zhu and Biao Zi. "The Combat Training Virtual Space allows the physical enhancements gained here to manifest in the real world. Mental strength can be trained here and improved externally."
"I've created a simple challenge."
"My initial estimate is that if you can clear it four or five times, you should be able to increase your mental strength by 0.8."
"That much?" Lao Zhu's eyes flickered with surprise.
"Yeah. Let's start with the first level."
"Mental strength is reflected in multiple aspects and dimensions. Sensitivity to color, or color perception, can effectively boost mental strength to a certain extent."
In the next moment—
Four green squares appeared on the light screen, three of which were dark green, and one was emerald green.
A 30-second countdown appeared on the screen.
"The rule is simple. You just need to select the square that's a different color before the timer runs out."
"That easy?"
Biao Zi frowned slightly, focused his mind, and quickly selected the emerald green square. The first level was cleared, and they moved on to the second level.
"The second level is a bit more challenging."
As soon as Li Shiji finished speaking, eighty-one black squares appeared on the screen, along with a 3-second countdown.
Three seconds later.
Failed.
"..."
Biao Zi turned to Li Shiji with a blank expression. "Are those eighty-one black squares really not identical?"
"Of course not."
Li Shiji brought up the second level again and pointed to the center black square. "This one is slightly lighter. It's quite obvious, right? Like throwing a red date into a glass of water."
"Let me try again!"
Thirty minutes later.
Biao Zi rubbed his reddened eyes and gave Li Shiji a thumbs-up. "Bro, you're amazing!"
"But thanks for making me realize I'm not cut out for this."
"Uh..."
Li Shiji awkwardly chuckled. "There are nine levels in total, and the difficulty increases gradually. Biao Ge, you didn't even pass the second level... If it's useful, I can design more maps to help enhance mental strength."
"And I've noticed that many of the pre-made maps in this Combat Training Virtual Space have limitations. I've also looked at the history of the maps you've created—they have some limitations too."
"I used to be a game designer."
"I think I can help design better maps to improve physical fitness and mental strength. This way, Lord Mang's vision of a mech squad can be realized sooner."
"..."
"..."
Biao Zi and Lao Zhu exchanged glances, both seeing the same thought in each other's eyes—this kid is a damn genius.
"We need to tell Lord Mang about this."
"Yeah, we should." For the first time, Biao Zi looked at Li Shiji with admiration. "Even though I can't use your map, I have two guys in my team with decent initial mental strength, like Shan Mao Zi. I'll have them come train with you."
"In the future, they'll handle long-range fire support, and I'll charge in front."
"I'm still better suited to being a warrior."
"You're impressive!"
At this moment.
He finally felt genuine respect for this young man, Li Shiji. He was no match for him.
"Really? If I rebel, will you join me?"
"Haha." Biao Zi forced a smile.
"Just a bad joke to lighten the mood..." Li Shiji awkwardly chuckled.
"Let's go."
Lao Zhu shook his head, laughing as he left the Combat Training Virtual Space. "The last time I heard a joke that bad was from Lord Mang."
At dusk.
The Stellar Train rested on the plains. Many Train Residents had stepped out of the train, lying on the nearby grass, breathing in the fresh air and enjoying the brief tranquility. The occasional monsters that appeared were swiftly dealt with by Zhang Da Mei and her second team.
Instead of being frightened, the Train Residents gathered together, laughing and commenting on the monsters in the distance.
"That monster's not impressive."
"Not as good as the nearly 100-meter-tall Zombie from earlier."
"True. When I saw that 100-meter Zombie, I was filled with despair. Who knew a single missile from the train would take it down instantly?"
"I heard it was a Level 7 monster!"
"According to Lao Zhu, Level 7 monsters are incredibly strong. That giant spider we encountered in the Iron Ridge Wasteland was only Level 3. The monsters in this area are Level 6."
Before encountering the Zombie King.
Chen Mang had installed many display screens inside the train carriages and refrigerators, connected to the generators and mechanical eyes, allowing the Train Residents to see the outside world through the screens.
The nearly 100-meter-tall Zombie had left a deep impression on everyone.
And Lao Zhu occasionally gave the residents some political lessons.
Mainly about the changes in the post-apocalyptic world, the hierarchy of train monsters, and most importantly, the strength of the Stellar Train and Lord Mang's abilities, as well as the tragic state of other trains.
"This is nice."
The young man who had been following Uncle Li lay on the grass, looking at the twenty or so children following a few women in the distance. He rested his hands behind his head, feeling the gentle breeze as he murmured, "For a moment, it felt like I wasn't in the apocalypse, but camping in a park."
"Somehow."
"I never liked kids before, but seeing these children, I suddenly felt a sense of peace, like seeing hope. It feels like the Stellar Train can continue on forever."
"Of course, it could also be the apocalypse that made these kids so mature."
"Especially the look in those boys' eyes. They don't seem like kids—more like adults tempered by the apocalypse."
"Hey, Uncle Li, why aren't you saying anything?"
"..."
Uncle Li, also lying on the grass, remained silent for a moment before hoarsely replying, "Stop worrying about those kids. Worry about yourself."
"I saw today that the Space Gate has a vast area inside, with a lot of grassland."
"It's clearly more suitable for farming and raising livestock than the Breeding Carriage."
"I'm worried we might be out of a job soon."
"Hmm..."
The young man, who had been enjoying the moment, fell silent. "Uncle Li... that's a real possibility. What should we do?"
"How the hell should I know? I'm trying to figure it out!"
"Alright, I'll think with you, Uncle Li."
"Can you even think of anything?"
"I can't, but I'll at least have the right attitude."
"Say... Train Conductor Zhu is looking for teachers for those kids. Do you think I could be a teacher?"
"That's hard to fake, isn't it?"
"I've actually been a teacher before."
"You graduated with a degree in civil engineering, spent a few years in prison, and then switched to accounting. Where does teaching fit into that?"
"I ran an accounting training class."
"That counts as teaching?"
"Teaching and imparting knowledge—doesn't that count as teaching?"
"Well... Uncle Li, why don't you give it a try?"
"Try? I'll try!"
Uncle Li gritted his teeth, got up from the ground, brushed the dirt off his pants, and headed straight for the train. "I'll go talk to Train Conductor Zhu. I think this position could be a long-term one!"
"And when these kids grow up and become the backbone of the Stellar Train, my status will rise with them!"
"After all, it's all about raising something."
"Raising kids is way more prestigious than raising pigs!"
"You? A teacher?"
Lao Zhu glanced at Uncle Li and immediately shook his head. "No way. If you become a teacher, who's going to manage the Breeding Carriage?"
"Focus on raising your pigs."
"Stop thinking about these things."
"Uncle Li, why are you back?"
"Just keep lying down."
Uncle Li lay back on the ground with a blank expression. "Raising pigs is fine. Raising kids is just a headache."
"Rejected?"
"Shut your mouth, thanks."
"Oh."
"Biao Ge... let me try again."
Inside the Combat Training Virtual Space, Shan Mao Zi lowered his head in shame. "I'll try a few more times. I'm sure I can clear it."
"..."
Biao Zi remained silent. Shan Mao Zi had just cleared the second level in thirteen minutes. Each time they restarted, the level changed completely, meaning Shan Mao Zi had talent—at least more than him.
He couldn't even scan all eighty-one squares in three seconds, let alone find the one that was almost indistinguishable from the others.
He just patted Shan Mao Zi's shoulder and said softly, "Stay here and train."
"When your mental strength exceeds 14.5, I'll go to Lord Mang and request a 'Leech' mech for you."
Then his figure disappeared, heading to another virtual space.
In the entire train, only Li Shiji's mental strength exceeded 14.5—his was an astonishing 26.8. The second highest was the third team captain.
His mental strength was 13.9.
There were three reasons he became the third team captain.
He's ruthless.
His marksmanship is sharp.
His physical fitness is strong.
Though none of these individually made him the strongest on the train, he was well-rounded, excelling in all three areas.
Appearing in another virtual space, Biao Zi looked at the words Biohazard on the light screen, took a deep breath, and adjusted his body to its peak condition.
This was something Lord Mang had brought back.
Normal clear: increases physical fitness by 0.2 each time, up to three times.
Extreme clear: increases difficulty, increases physical fitness by 0.5 each time, up to three times, with actual death.
His goal was simple.
Clear the normal mode three times, then the extreme mode three times.
In the next moment—
The words Biohazard exploded into countless light particles, and the previously white virtual space rapidly transformed. When everything settled, he found himself in an elevator that was steadily ascending.
The elevator's lights were dim and flickering.
The button for the 31st floor was lit, and the elevator had reached the 7th floor.
On the elevator's surface, a line of crimson text slowly appeared.
Biohazard, Normal Mission.
Reach the 31st floor and escape the building via the steel cable on the rooftop.
Just then!
"Thud!"
Something heavy seemed to have fallen from high up in the elevator shaft, landing on top of the elevator. The elevator immediately stopped, stuck on the 7th floor.
Before Biao Zi could react.
The steel plate above the elevator was pried open, and a Zombie covered in blood, with exposed muscles, crawled onto the elevator's frame, sticking its head inside and roaring at him.
The intense stench of blood and rot instantly filled the elevator.
Blood and saliva mixed into a thick, sticky liquid, dripping onto the elevator floor.
"..."
Biao Zi's breath almost stopped. It was all too real, and without any warning, he was thrust into the scenario, which was a significant psychological shock. He quickly scanned the elevator.
Picking up a steel pipe from the elevator, he immediately thrust it at the Zombie above!
But it was useless.
This was clearly a high-level Zombie, completely ignoring his attacks, frantically tearing into the elevator's roof, trying to force its way inside.
"Bang, bang!"
Biao Zi, now anxious, began kicking the elevator door, trying to escape.
But it was too late.
"Thud!"
The Zombie successfully forced its way into the elevator, opening its massive, fang-filled mouth and swallowing Biao Zi's upper body whole.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 155 - 155: 1v28.
chapters.content:
"Crack."
A crisp sound rang out, as if someone was eating a crunchy shark.
Biao Zi's upper body was severed at the waist.
Dead beyond dead.
"No!!!"
Inside the train, Chen Mang looked at the screen with a pained expression, watching the scene of Biao Zi's death. He trembled as he lit a cigarette, bringing it to his lips. His eyes reddened, and he spoke hoarsely, "Xiao Ai... do you know..."
"The first time I really looked at Biao Zi, he carefully reported to me that he was the elected captain of the thugs. Back then..."
"Train Conductor."
Xiao Ai, standing beside him, spoke in a mechanical voice, "This is just a normal mission in 'Biohazard.' There's no real death. Biao Zi isn't dead."
"..."
Chen Mang, still caught up in his emotions, glanced at Xiao Ai with slight dissatisfaction. "You don't seem very intelligent yet. Next time something like this happens, I hope you'll choose to stay silent."
"Received."
Chen Mang leaned back in his chair with renewed enthusiasm, propping his feet on the table as he watched the screen showing Biao Zi's successful clearance of the mission.
Earlier, Lao Zhu had come to talk to him about Li Shiji.
He was very interested.
He hadn't expected Li Shiji to have such a use. He immediately promised Li Shiji a great reward if he performed well.
Then, with great interest, he began to watch the map designed by Li Shiji and others in the Combat Training Virtual Space. Coincidentally, he also saw Biao Zi heading into the Biohazard mission.
Although it was in third-person view, the immersion was still strong.
This was far more thrilling than any apocalypse movie.
However, even the normal Biohazard mission was this difficult at the start. He calculated that if you didn't escape the elevator within the first twenty seconds, it was a guaranteed death.
The monster in the elevator shaft was practically invincible; there was no way to kill it.
The only solution was to kick open the elevator door and escape quickly.
And you couldn't bring any weapons in—you could only pick up weapons that might exist in the map, like the steel pipe in the elevator.
The overall difficulty wasn't low.
If one could successfully make it to the 31st floor, an increase of 0.2 in the Physical Fitness Index seemed a bit too little.
Finally—
After dying three times in a row, Biao Zi managed to kick open the elevator door right at the start of the fourth attempt.
The elevator door was stuck between the 7th and 8th floors.
Biao Zi first looked down at the 7th floor, then peeked up at the 8th floor. Seeing no zombies outside, he hesitated for a few seconds before jumping up and climbing through the door to the 8th-floor platform.
But just then!
"Crash!!"
With the sound of the steel cables falling, the entire elevator suddenly plummeted. Before Biao Zi could climb out, he was once again severed at the waist, his eyes filled with despair and pain.
"Hmm..."
Chen Mang frowned slightly as he leaned back in his chair. This seemed a lot like that movie "Final Destination." Just a little too slow, and it meant death. How many times would one have to die to reach the top?
The pain was still 100% real.
He could see that Biao Zi hadn't immediately re-entered the mission. Instead, he was lying on the floor of the white space, his body twitching—clearly in considerable pain.
But soon, Biao Zi got up and charged back in!
This time, he climbed out of the elevator shaft at the fastest speed possible, reaching the 8th floor.
As soon as Biao Zi climbed out, the elevator behind him began to fall.
But before he could even catch his breath—
"Roar!!"
Dozens of zombies emerged from the corridors on both sides of the elevator shaft. Just as Chen Mang was about to see how Biao Zi would handle this, Biao Zi didn't hesitate for a second. He turned and jumped back into the elevator shaft.
He fell heavily to the bottom, severely injured but not dead.
Fortunately, the zombie in the elevator shaft was there to finish him off.
Again, one more try.
This time, Biao Zi chose to go to the 7th floor. After climbing out, he was safe. Biao Zi was clever—he chose to take the fire escape. Just as he opened the fire escape door, dozens of zombies rushed out.
Again.
This time, Biao Zi decided to search the offices on the 7th floor for a suitable weapon. During his search, he noticed a hanging basket outside the window, used for cleaning the building's exterior glass. At the moment, no one was on it.
Biao Zi's eyes lit up. He picked up the fire axe he had just found and jumped onto the basket, seemingly hatching a brilliant plan.
As soon as he stood on it, the rope holding the basket snapped.
Dead.
Again.
This time, Biao Zi grabbed the fire axe on the 7th floor and, without trying any shortcuts, charged straight into the fire escape to fight.
1v28.
A bloody battle ensued. The score was 3/1, then 5/1, 8/1, 11/1—gradually improving.
After a full hour, when the sky had completely darkened, the score finally reached 28/0. On the screen, Biao Zi, drenched in blood and staggering, climbed up the fire escape to the 12th floor, only to find the fire escape blocked. He had to detour to another fire escape on the same floor.
As he opened the door to the 12th floor, he saw over a hundred zombies turn their heads in unison, roaring as they charged toward him.
Biao Zi's body finally gave out, and he collapsed to his knees. Before the zombies could reach him, he raised the axe and struck himself, clearly trying to lessen the pain. But he must have hesitated—he didn't kill himself.
But it didn't matter. The charging zombies delivered the final blow, though it meant he suffered a bit more pain.
As the screen flashed, Chen Mang noticed a set of armor and... a healing spray on the table.
"Hmm..."
Chen Mang sighed as he watched Biao Zi charge back into the map on the screen. The guy never stopped. From dying at the start to now flowing through the mission like water, it was truly a sight to behold.
This map was really hard. Even the "normal mission" was this difficult. Could anyone actually clear the extreme version?
The extreme version would not only be harder, but it also only allowed one life.
If you died in the map, it meant real brain death in the outside world.
"Train Conductor."
Xiao Ai, who had been standing beside him watching the entire time, spoke up. "Biao Zi's movements are becoming more precise. Every strike is just right, and he instinctively protects his vital areas. When he needs to engage in close combat, he can quickly judge whether the exchange of injuries is worth it."
"Biao Zi's combat experience is improving rapidly."
"If he can really clear it three times..."
"It'll be like a complete transformation."
"That's true."
Chen Mang nodded in deep agreement. He shifted his gaze to the three-dimensional train diagram on the screen. His "Swarm Platform," the component that controlled drones, had already been upgraded to level 10, but its two supermodel effects were still empty.
In addition—
The "Vehicle-Mounted Zombie Perception Blocker," a green-tier component, had also been upgraded to level 10 using 45,000 units of Iron Ore.
The effect of reaching level 10 was that it could make the train immune to the perception of level 10 zombies.
Considering the effect, the Iron Ore spent was quite cost-effective.
However—
Most of the time, it was useless. After all, he wasn't afraid of Corpse Tides. Even if they were detected, it didn't matter. Unless he encountered level 80 or 90 zombies that he couldn't defeat, this component would be very useful.
It was worth mentioning that crafting this component required the "Handheld Zombie Perception Blocker," a special item.
He still had two of these special items.
He used one and had one left.
If he hadn't traded it in the Iron Ridge Wasteland, he would have had three.
The handheld version could only block the perception of level 1 zombies, making it practically useless except during the early stages. Many times, it could save your life, but the vehicle-mounted version had much more utility.
He still had 12 Murphy Stones.
The harvest over the past few days had been quite substantial. He planned to take a day off to process these gains.
He glanced at his train panel's resource balance.
He had 525,000 units of Copper Ore and 470,000 units of Iron Ore.
"Bring Doba and the Black Market Merchant here."
"Received."
"Great Human Prophet."
Doba and the Black Market Merchant stood solemnly in the train compartment, bowing to Chen Mang.
Chen Mang picked up a few Redheart Nuts from the plate beside him and handed them to the two with a smile. "I heard these are your favorite snacks. Later, Xiao Ai will take you to the production car to get some more. You can enjoy them as snacks."
In his train compartment, he kept a plate filled with Redheart Nuts. Whenever it was almost empty, Xiao Fang would refill it.
It wasn't that he needed them.
He just genuinely liked the taste of these nuts. They made for a great snack—crunchy and satisfying.
"This..."
Doba and the Black Market Merchant froze as they took the Redheart Nuts. Their eyes reddened, and they trembled as they put the nuts into their mouths. Tears streamed down their faces as they spoke, their voices shaking.
"This... this is the taste of home."
"It's been so long since I've seen Redheart Nuts. I never thought I'd get to taste them again in my lifetime."
"Hmm."
Chen Mang wasn't too surprised by their reaction. If he had tasted something unique from his previous world, he would have felt the same way. These two goblins were essentially displaced on this planet.
This world originally had no such thing as goblins.
But this wasn't why he had called them here. He pulled out ten "Goblin Tickets" and handed them to Doba.
"These are Goblin Tickets. No matter where you are, as long as you crush the ticket, you can return to the Stellar Train."
"Give them to him."
"Have him randomly teleport, then crush the ticket to return. There's no specific mission, but it'd be great if he could gather some information."
"Like what he sees in other regions, what kind of monsters are there, and so on..."
"Wait."
Chen Mang paused for a moment, then crafted a Mechanical Eye and a level 2 Energy Stone. He also used a Mechanical Heart to create something resembling a black box, connecting the two to form a head-mounted camera.
"Tie this to his head. The main task is to bring back various pieces of information."
"Understood?"
"Understood."
Doba nodded solemnly.
"Alright, you can go now."
Chen Mang waved his hand.
The price of a Goblin Ticket was slightly higher than that of a Train Ticket. A Train Ticket cost 100 units of Iron Ore, while a Goblin Ticket cost 500 units.
He didn't directly speak to the Black Market Merchant.
This goblin didn't seem very bright. When Er Dan was on the train, this guy had come over and repeated the same lines he had said when he first met Chen Mang—word for word, as if it were a pre-programmed script.
It was better to let Doba handle the arrangements.
Among these goblins, Doba seemed the most intelligent.
So when Doba had first met him and claimed to be the smartest among the goblins, he wasn't lying. He was a good kid who never lied.
"Do this, then this... and finally this... got it?"
Doba stuffed the ten Goblin Tickets into the Black Market Merchant's arms, then fixed the camera to his chest. He also stuffed a handful of Redheart Nuts into the merchant's pocket before giving his final instructions.
"You can randomly teleport up to ten times a day, right?"
"This time, use all ten teleports. When you're out of energy, crush one of the Goblin Tickets and return."
"Got it?"
"Got it."
The Black Market Merchant's mouth was stuffed with Redheart Nuts, too precious to chew, so he held them in his mouth like a squirrel, mumbling, "I'm off, King Doba."
"Go, and may you return victorious, bringing glory to the goblin race!"
Doba placed his hands solemnly on the Black Market Merchant's shoulders, his expression devout and solemn, like a king knighting a general.
In the next moment—
A flash of white light enveloped the Black Market Merchant, and he vanished without a trace.
"What a great tool for exploration."
Chen Mang looked at the control panel screen. The Black Market Merchant was no longer on the train, and his location was unknown. The only way to tell if he was still alive was through the Train Crew panel. It was unclear if he was still in the Shahe Plain region.
Up to this point, his understanding of this world was limited to just four regions: "Shahe Plain," "Kunlun Mountains," "Ice and Snow World," and "Iron Ridge Wasteland." He knew nothing about other regions.
But with the Black Market Merchant, he could learn about events in other regions. Even if he couldn't go there himself, it would give him a clearer understanding of the world. It was unclear whether the Black Market Merchant could teleport to any region or if he was limited to random teleportation within a single region.
Testing it out would provide the answers.
By tomorrow morning, when the Goblin Merchant returned, the camera he carried would reveal a lot of information.
As everyone knew, in any strategic game, the importance of exploration was paramount.
"..."
Chen Mang glanced at the mineral resources on the train panel. With a bit more Iron Ore, he could prepare to upgrade the train to level 6 and head to the yellow region.
Originally, he had planned to leave the Shahe Plain and visit the "Underwater Labyrinth" fortuitous map to obtain more Murphy Stones.
But now, it seemed he wouldn't have the chance for a while.
He had asked Er Dan about it.
To navigate underwater, he needed the "Deep Sea Shield," a blue-tier vehicle component. Although it wasn't a high-tier item, it was extremely rare.
It could only be obtained by defeating the "Green Dragon" monster.

chapters.title: Chapter 156 - 156: "Wait, Where Did That Flamethrower Come From?"
chapters.content:
The Green Dragon wasn't too difficult to kill.
It was only Level 5.
But the problem was that this monster didn't have a fixed territory and kept wandering around. Not long ago, it appeared in the Kunlun Mountains area. At that time, Chen Mang had just entered the Kunlun Mountains for the first time, and the Level 5 Train flying in the sky was none other than Er Dan, who had gone there to hunt the Green Dragon.
There was only one of them.
Once Er Dan killed it, that was it.
The chances of encountering another Green Dragon were about as likely as finding Iron Ore falling from the sky.
"Whatever."
Chen Mang shook his head with a hint of regret, silently comforting himself in his mind. It was just some Murphy Stones—not particularly valuable or important!
Not worth coveting!
Since the "Deep Sea Maze" Fortuitous Encounter map was off the table, after stockpiling some more Iron Ore, he would directly upgrade to a Level 6 Train and prepare to head to the yellow zone known as the "Zombie Basin."
He had already claimed most of the Fortuitous Encounters on the Shahe Plain, and even the ones in the Ice and Snow World zone had been taken by him.
The only exception was the Kunlun Mountains Fortuitous Encounter, which was exclusive to the Flesh Train. Otherwise, it too would have fallen into his grasp.
As night fell.
All Train Residents had already entered their slumber, except for the Guards on night duty, including Chen Mang, who had also drifted off to sleep.
The AI was controlling the Stellar Train as it sped across the Shahe Plain, searching for Iron Ore.
Dawn broke.
Chen Mang, having risen from his sleep, freshened up briefly before looking out the window. There, he saw an open-air Level 2 Iron Ore deposit. Many Train Residents had already started mining, while he turned his attention to the Train Log.
After three hours of travel last night, they had come across this open-air Level 2 Iron Ore deposit.
Along the way, they had encountered three Level 2 Ore deposits and one Level 2 Copper Ore deposit, but those Mines were already occupied by other Trains. Following the program he had set, the AI didn't stop but continued to search for unclaimed Mines.
They had also run over a few insignificant monsters on the way.
Nothing else of note happened.
Chen Mang leaned back in his chair and closed the Train Log. Last night had been largely uneventful.
He then looked at the upgrade conditions for the Train to reach Level 6.
-
Upgrade Conditions: All four essential Vehicle Components must be crafted, 40,000 units of Level 2 Iron Ore must be consumed, all Accessory Levels within the Train must exceed Level 120, and a Level 6 monster must be killed.
-
The upgrade conditions were mostly unchanged, except for the increased Iron Ore requirement—now needing 400,000 units.
There was also the added condition of killing a Level 6 monster.
As far as he knew.
Many purely development-focused Train Conductors focused solely on growth, fleeing at the sight of slightly stronger monsters. This condition essentially forced all Train Conductors aiming to upgrade to Level 6 to confront a Level 6 monster.
For those Level 5 Trains that had rapidly upgraded without building a solid foundation, this task would likely stall them for a long time.
But for him, this condition was already fulfilled.
To be honest.
He couldn't recall ever actively hunting a Level 5 monster. The ones he had killed were mostly incidental—like when he launched a missile into the Kunlun Mountains area and accidentally took out a few Level 5 monsters.
Then there was Shan Mao Zi and his girlfriend's wedding.
His initial idea was that, as a Level 4 Train at the time, he needed to invite three Trains of the same level to attend. Coincidentally, the Ziyun had also arrived at the Shahe Plain, so it could count as one of the guests since they had some prior interaction and familiarity.
Unfortunately, the Ziyun had fallen in the Kunlun Mountains area.
With that, his list of three guests was left incomplete.
If he upgraded to a Level 6 Train, the Azure Dragon could attend the wedding. He would just need to find two more Level 6 Trains to secure the 500 Inheritance Points.
Chen Mang had just mentioned this to Er Dan, briefly explaining that he was planning a wedding and wanted to invite him, along with two Level 6 Trains.
Er Dan quickly replied.
"Two Level 6 Trains? I have two friends on the Shahe Plain who are Level 6 Trains. Would they work?"
"You have that many friends?"
"Not exactly close friends. We've never met in real life, but we've chatted on the Train Radio. I think once they see your Stellar Train, they won't have any ulterior motives. They seemed decent when we talked."
"Alright, I'll give you the specific date later."
"Got it."
Another matter settled.
Chen Mang stretched and turned to the screen to check on Biao Zi's progress. Biao Zi had been training in the Combat Training Virtual Space all night, and it seemed like he was doing well—already reaching the 29th floor.
"Not bad."
A hint of surprise flashed in his eyes as he leaned back in his chair, tossing a Redheart Nut into his mouth. The last time he checked, Biao Zi was stuck on the 12th floor. Now, he was already on the 29th.
He was close to clearing the 31st floor.
On the screen, Biao Zi was fully equipped, wearing armor, a motorcycle helmet, a steel sword at his waist, a flamethrower in his hands, and a large fuel tank on his back.
He also had a rifle slung over his shoulder.
Currently, Biao Zi was on the 29th floor of an office building, using the flamethrower to slaughter the Zombies charging at him. Though he still bore some injuries, they weren't as severe as last night. His demeanor had changed, his eyes now colder and more resolute.
"Wait, where did that flamethrower come from?"
Chen Mang quickly scrolled through the historical records and soon found that during the 14th floor, Biao Zi had grabbed a fire hose from the seventh floor and cleared the Zombies in the fire escape. Instead of heading upward as he had done before, Biao Zi went downward.
He methodically cleared the sixth and first floors, finding the flamethrower and motorcycle helmet before continuing his ascent up the fire escape. On the 12th floor, he obtained the armor and a healing spray.
When the screen switched back.
Biao Zi had already reached the 31st-floor rooftop. After removing all his weapons and equipment, he let out a few fierce roars of triumph before walking to the edge of the rooftop where a zip line was set up.
He tightly gripped the short pole on the zip line, kicked off with his feet, and swiftly swung toward the rooftop of a shorter building.
Then—
The screen began to zoom out.
Biao Zi's figure on the zip line between the two tall buildings gradually shrank, and the perspective shifted from third-person to a bird's-eye view. The city was teeming with Zombies, even scaling the sides of countless skyscrapers like ivy.
As the view zoomed out to the clouds, the Zombies in the city appeared as mere black dots.
Finally, the screen exploded with four large characters:
"Mission Accomplished."
"Not easy."
Chen Mang sighed with emotion as he watched Biao Zi, who was now in the white space, overwhelmed with joy. Clearing it once would make subsequent attempts much easier, and this "Biohazard" map was more impressive than he had imagined.
-
It tested many things.
Like timing, choices in desperate situations, the awareness to descend, and life-and-death melee combat.
And so on.
Even someone who had never killed a chicken would undergo a dramatic transformation in demeanor after clearing this map once—developing a certain fierceness.
"..."
Chen Mang frowned slightly, pondering a question. By browsing the historical records, he could see many strategies for clearing the map. So far, Biao Zi was the only one on the Train who knew these strategies. He was considering whether to compile and share these strategies with others.
Doing so would boost the overall combat strength of the Guard team by about ten percent.
But it would be unfair to Biao Zi, as it would mean giving away the strategies he had painstakingly discovered through countless deaths, for others to easily learn.
Moreover.
The map was designed to significantly cultivate one's abilities. If all the strategies were handed out, it would diminish the opportunity for growth.
At that moment—
Xiao Ai suddenly spoke up, "Train Conductor, the Black Market Merchant has returned. I've organized the footage he collected. Would you like to view it now?"
"Go ahead."
Soon.
The screen displayed the footage the Black Market Merchant had collected last night.
There was a lot of footage.
For example.
In a derelict Mechanical City, it was overrun by Zombies. These Zombies even seemed to possess intelligence, as they were actively repairing the city, with Zombie Guards and Zombie Soldiers manning heavy artillery on the city walls.
In a freezing canyon, a battered robot crouched on the ground, welding a completely wrecked Train.
A Train stopped and traded with the Black Market Merchant. This Train had over forty carriages, resembling a mechanical dragon traversing the wasteland. Its Train Conductor was a burly man with a scarred face and a menacing expression, who had stared thoughtfully at the Black Market Merchant's chest camera for a long time.
Who knows what wild conspiracy theories were running through his mind—perhaps he thought the Black Market Merchant was some high-dimensional civilization's spy or something equally absurd.
There was also a deserted forest where the Black Market Merchant had been swinging on a tree branch in the night before being startled by a sudden snake and teleporting away.
And a gathering of roughly thousands of humans on a sea-surrounded island, where they had built numerous wooden huts and tents. Occasionally, Trains could be seen emerging from the sea around the island.
And so on.
Chen Mang exhaled slowly, lit a cigarette, leaned back in his chair, and closed his eyes. His understanding of this world had deepened with these images. The world was more complex than he had imagined.
Or rather.
More diverse.
For instance, the "Mechanical City" was designed to help human civilization better control Trains for survival. If there was a Mechanical Civilization, it would likely be friendly toward humans. But the Mechanical Zombie King was clearly creating even more terrifying monsters.
Perhaps these monsters were meant to fight other monsters?
Using poison to counter poison, magic to fight magic.
But one thing was undeniable—the Black Market Merchant was truly free, going wherever he pleased. Without him, it would have taken Chen Mang much longer to see these scenes.
After a while, he spoke.
"Call them over."
Soon.
Doba and the Black Market Merchant arrived in the Train's interior.
"Well done."
Chen Mang looked at the Black Market Merchant with a serious expression. "Go rest for now. Keep doing this—I want more of this information. Do you have a name?"
"I forgot."
The Black Market Merchant shook his head, a hint of confusion in his eyes. "I had one, but I can't remember."
"Alright, I'll give you a name. From now on, you'll be called Mundo."
"Okay."
"Go on."
A new day had begun.
All Train Residents had started their daily tasks.
Everyone was contributing in their respective roles, including the teachers. Three women, who had been teachers before the apocalypse, were now responsible for teaching the children theoretical knowledge. Once they grew older, they would begin practical training.
Currently, everyone on the Train was in a role that suited them best.
And today—
Something significant happened for the Train Residents.
The first "Refrigerator" had found its buyer. The price of a Refrigerator was a staggering 1,000 Stellar Coupons. Currently, no one on the Train had that many Stellar Coupons except for one person—Doba.
All Train Residents had gathered near Carriage 11 to watch the commotion.
Lord Mang had created a "Space Gate" in Carriage 11. Inside, the space was vast, with clouds and a sun in the sky, and an endless expanse of grassland on the ground. Trees surrounded the perimeter, making it look like a utopia.
On the grassland sat an open Refrigerator.
Inside the Refrigerator, Doba and over a hundred Goblins were decorating the space with various household items they had purchased.
Doba had made himself a small stool to serve as his throne.
He had also bought many rugs to cover the entire floor of the Refrigerator, allowing the Goblins to sleep on the ground at night. Since Goblins were short, the space was more than enough.
It was roomier than being in the Train.
Most importantly.
This territory belonged to the Goblins, giving them a stronger sense of home.
Doba stood resolutely at the Refrigerator's entrance, gazing out at the vast grassland. He planned to buy two more Refrigerators, ensuring his people could sleep even more comfortably!
Meanwhile, in Guard Carriage 7, Biao Zi looked at his physical stats—12.4—and grinned with satisfaction.
Finally!
After an entire night, he had finally cleared the map!
Currently, he was the only one on the Train to have succeeded. This morning, his team was on duty. He planned to share the clearing strategies with everyone after his shift. Initially, he had considered sharing them only with his team.
But then he thought, strengthening the other teams would strengthen the Stellar Train.
Holding back might earn Lord Mang's disapproval, so he decided to share with everyone, earning some goodwill. In the future, the other two team leaders might remember him when they had something good to offer.
You give to receive.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 157 - 157: "The Doomsday Wedding."
chapters.content:
Time moved to the evening of the following day.
On this night, all residents were busy, though not with mining, but with preparing tables, chairs, and the like. Tomorrow at noon, Lord Mang would host a wedding for Shan Mao Zi and his girlfriend Mei Jia!
Everyone was excited.
Though they weren't the main characters of the wedding and didn't know the couple, the juxtaposition of "doomsday" and "wedding" was inherently jarring.
Doomsday represented despair, symbolizing the fall of life.
While a wedding represented hope, symbolizing the birth of life.
A doomsday wedding.
For those who had struggled to survive in the doomsday for over a year, they were eagerly anticipating this wedding. It would allow them to momentarily forget the apocalypse and immerse themselves in the celebration.
Inside the Stellar Train.
Over the past two days, they had mined a total of 210,000 units of Iron Ore. Combined with their existing reserves, they now had 670,000 units of Iron Ore.
Chen Mang had already spent 400,000 units of Iron Ore to upgrade the Stellar Train to level 6.
Soon—
A line of text appeared on the train's control console screen.
-
"Your train has been upgraded to level 6."
"More craftable accessories will be unlocked."
-
"Level 6 train."
Chen Mang silently gazed at the screen. Months ago, when he first crossed over, he had obtained his first train. After months of development, the train had finally reached level 6.
Every time the train leveled up, it gained a special function.
He wasn't sure if this happened at every level or just the early ones.
The function unlocked at level 5 was "Mecha Crafting," which enhanced the combat capabilities of the Train Crew. After reaching level 6, a new button appeared on the control console.
「?」
However, this button was just a question mark, with no other information provided.
He wasn't in a hurry. He would ask Er Dan about this situation tomorrow during the wedding. Train radio channels rarely had level 6 trains speaking up, and no one had discussed this scenario.
The number of level 6 trains was already small.
Now, the big event was tomorrow's wedding for Shan Mao Zi and Mei Jia. This would earn him another 500 Inheritance Points, adding to the 100 he hadn't spent yet, totaling 600 Inheritance Points. This should allow him to buy quite a few good things from the Black Market Merchant.
Actually, he had been somewhat tempted by the "White-tier Accessory Blueprint" that cost only 10 Inheritance Points.
White-tier items might not be very useful for other trains, but in his hands, they could be maximized!
With just a small amount of Iron Ore, he could gain many Supermodel Effects. Even life-related accessories could have miraculous effects in certain situations, like a level 10 Refrigerator.
But he was afraid that if he spent a little now, he might miss out on something valuable worth 600 Inheritance Points later, so he had been saving up. After the wedding tomorrow, he could start spending.
Chen Mang looked at the conditions for a Golden Wedding.
-
Golden Wedding.
Requires a wedding to be held in the presence of 1,000 witnesses, with three trains of the same level attending the banquet. Food and drinks must be prepared for all attendees, along with basic items such as wedding dresses, red carpets, artificial flowers, and fireworks.
Successfully hosting a Golden Wedding will grant the train 500 Inheritance Points and 20 Reputation Points.
-
The population requirement was met, and Er Dan had arranged for the three trains of the same level. He had the food and drinks, with the alcohol being a gift from Er Dan. He had used the Mechanical Heart to create artificial flowers. These inanimate objects could still be crafted by the Mechanical Heart, of course... Iron flowers, which looked no different from artificial flowers and were even more three-dimensional.
The Iron Ore consumption was minimal.
For the wedding dress and suit, he had spent 1,000 units of wood to create high-precision outfits for the couple.
As for fireworks.
He had prepared a level 1 missile.
Level 1 missiles were cheap and could serve as a deterrent at the start of the banquet. Later, they could be used as fireworks, which would look good. He had prepared everything.
Although the two trains were friends of Er Dan.
He didn't know them personally.
The wedding needed to be held on the plains. If those two trains attacked his Train Residents at the start of the wedding, it wouldn't be a good situation. So, it was necessary to show his fangs from the beginning and intimidate the other side.
If they dared to attack him.
They should think twice about whether they could leave alive.
Lao Zhu had already taken care of the wedding arrangements, so there was nothing for him to worry about. He just needed to wake up naturally.
The night was already deep.
Lao Zhu, holding a walkie-talkie, looked out at the wedding venue being constructed outside the train, continuously shouting.
"That board is fucking crooked!"
"Hurry up with the trusses! We don't have starry skies, so just lay out some artificial flowers."
"And those four ground burst balls next to the red carpet. Tomorrow, you'll be in charge of watching this spot. The moment the couple walks past, detonate them, got it?"
He wasn't very knowledgeable about wedding decorations.
But as a second-in-command, he often dealt with venue arrangements, as there was a lot of profit involved. Through exposure, he had picked up some knowledge about wedding decorations, and he could manage well enough, with no major issues.
He was also the host for tomorrow.
"Uh..."
At this moment, Shan Mao Zi, standing beside him, whispered sheepishly, "Train Conductor Zhu, there's really no need to go to such lengths. My status on the train isn't that high, is it?"
"This is Lord Mang's intention."
Lao Zhu patted Shan Mao Zi's shoulder and smiled. "Just accept it. Even before the doomsday, many people didn't have weddings as grand as yours. You two are the first couple to marry on the Stellar Train, so it's a good omen."
"But since you're getting married, you can't go to the Red House anymore."
Upon hearing this, Shan Mao Zi's face instantly turned anxious, and he hurriedly said, "Train Conductor Zhu, you can't just say things like that! I've never been there. If you don't believe me, ask Biao Ge. He can vouch for me. I've never been there!"
"Mei Jia, you have to believe me. I really haven't been there!"
The Red House was a Refrigerator in the Stellar Train's Resident car where meat-selling residents gathered to receive clients.
A red cloth hung outside the Refrigerator, serving as a signboard.
Residents jokingly called it the Red House.
Blushing, Mei Jia leaned on Shan Mao Zi's shoulder, her eyes filled with quiet anticipation for tomorrow's wedding. She pinched Shan Mao Zi's lower back and whispered, "It's okay if you went. I don't mind."
"Ouch!"
Shan Mao Zi sucked in a sharp breath from the pain, then his voice rose in anxiety, "Train Conductor Zhu, where's Biao Ge? I need him to vouch for me. I really haven't been there!"
"What do you mean it's okay if I went? I've never been there!"
"Alright, alright."
Lao Zhu chuckled and patted Shan Mao Zi's shoulder again, looking helplessly at Mei Jia. "He really hasn't been there. I was just teasing him. He spends most of his time training. Don't bring this up with him in the future."
"I just saw he was a bit nervous and wanted to lighten the mood."
"Your task for tonight is to rest well and be in top form for tomorrow's wedding. There will be other trains coming to the banquet, so make sure to present yourselves well in front of outsiders."
"Uh..."
Shan Mao Zi hesitated for a moment before asking softly, "What about the 'Bowing to the Elders' part of the ceremony?"
"Bow to the Stellar Train when the time comes."
"Okay."
After this little episode, the couple seemed less nervous and walked back into the train. Only faint voices carried by the night breeze reached Lao Zhu's ears.
"Mei Jia, I really haven't been there, honestly."
"I believe you."
"You really believe me?"
"Yeah, the first time we met on the Stellar Train, you were quick. Usually, if it's been a while, it's fast."
"Damn it, you might as well not believe me!"
"Whatever... I'll buy some nuts tomorrow night."
Standing where he was, Lao Zhu looked at the couple's retreating figures with emotion. It was so nice. Seeing such a scene in the doomsday was rare. For these two, the doomsday had become a paradise.
Not only had their ALS been cured, but they also had a wedding arranged for them, and Lord Mang had even assigned them a wedding suite.
Well.
Where else could they have enjoyed such treatment before the doomsday?
The next day—
The Azure Dragon Train met up with the other two level 6 trains on the Shahe Plain, preparing to attend the wedding together.
The three Train Conductors stood on the plain, discussing.
"Remember."
Er Dan looked seriously at the other two Train Conductors. "I was the only one originally invited to this wedding. I only agreed to introduce you two because we've gotten along well."
"Once we're there, speak less and listen more. Just be spectators."
"And absolutely don't make any suspicious moves. Don't let a gun fall out of your coat while clapping, and then tell me it's reasonable for a Train Conductor to carry a gun."
"Got it?"
"Got it." The Train Conductor of the "Only Love One Train" slapped his chest solemnly. "You know me. In my life values, there are only three types of people."
"Ants, comrades, and seniors."
"When facing seniors, I'm extremely well-behaved. The Stellar Train is definitely a senior, so I won't provoke him."
Then he suddenly laughed sheepishly.
"Uh... If I lick up to him like you do, will he give me some benefits too?"
"That's what I was thinking." The Train Conductor of the "Ten Steps to Kill One Train" also said excitedly. "He has so many Supermodel Effects, so he must have a lot of Murphy Stones, right? Maybe he'll casually toss a Murphy Stone to us or something."
"..."
Er Dan gave them a sidelong glance. "I don't even want to comment on the names of your trains. Hey, I've always wanted to know, do you two fight over who owns 'One'?"
"And Murphy Stones? Dream on!"
"You're just going to see the world and get a free meal. Whether you can connect with Chen Mang afterward depends on your skills. But looking at your wretched appearances, it's probably not happening. Like beggars."
"But..."
Er Dan licked his lips and looked at them with emotion. "The reason I brought you two to the wedding is that, like me, you're cautious and won't cause trouble."
The two looked at each other, both seeing the smile in each other's eyes.
"I became a level 6 Train Conductor thanks to one excellent quality: being cautious enough."
"Same here."
"Alright, get on your trains and let's go."
The sun hung high in the sky.
It was noon.
"..."
Chen Mang looked at the control console screen. When the three trains were still over 10,000 meters away, he detected them. He immediately turned to Xiao Ai and ordered, "Tell everyone to get ready. The missile and Sakura Blossom Rocket Launcher can be raised."
"The mechas should also move around."
"Get everything moving."
"Yes."
Then he walked to the mirror and looked at his outfit for the day. He had crafted a new set of clothes for himself. The weather was getting cold, and although his previous clothes had good Temperature Lock, they still let in some wind.
The top was an orange sweater, and the bottom was just ordinary pants.
A very casual outfit.
"Hmm..."
"How did that saying go? Ttod? Or Ctod?"
"Whatever, I can't remember. It's all a mess."
"Huh?"
The Train Conductor of the "Only Love One Train" twitched his mouth as he looked at the Targeting Radar, which showed over a thousand red dots ahead. This guy! He knew this train must have a lot of Slaves!
After all, it was the top-ranked train on the Shahe Plain in all three rankings.
The "Power Value Ranking," "Supermodel Effect Quantity Ranking," and "Reputation Points Ranking." The Stellar Train was undoubtedly first in all three, and the gap with the second place was significant.
Especially the gap in the Supermodel Effect Quantity Ranking with second place.
He now strongly suspected that even if they went to the yellow zone, it would still be first. Even the Flesh Train couldn't get that many Murphy Stones.
Where on earth did he get them from!
Soon—
He saw a train resembling a mechanical dragon parked on the wasteland not far away. Around the train, over a thousand Slaves were busily and excitedly preparing the banquet.
Although Er Dan had told him that the Stellar Train treated its Slaves well.
But this was too good...
At least he had never seen his own Slaves smiling while working.
"Wait..."
The man suddenly froze, looking at the missile, Rocket Launcher, Heavy Machine Gun, and Doomsday Cannon that had emerged from the Stellar Train, all aimed at his train.
"Don't mess with me, buddy. I'm here for the wedding, not a funeral."
"This is making me nervous..."
But soon.
The weapons turned away again, clearly without malicious intent. The man sighed in relief and slowly reduced the train's speed, parking it about a hundred meters away from the Stellar Train.
Then he jumped down, bringing his trusted aides and subordinates, and walked toward the young man standing in front of the Stellar Train with a broad smile.
The man held a cane, so he must be Chen Mang.
He seemed quite approachable.
No airs. He had thought they would have to wait outside for a while.
Strange. The Train Conductor ranked first in all three rankings was actually this approachable?
"Welcome from afar."
Chen Mang looked at Er Dan and the two men beside him, smiling. "These two must be Er Dan's friends, right?"
"Food and drinks are plentiful today."
"Why not let the ot
hers from your trains come down and join the fun?"
"Better not..."
Er Dan said helplessly. "Last time, after just a brief interaction, I felt they were looking at me differently. If they stay longer this time, I think they might defect."
"It's not about the treatment being bad, but about comparison."
"Actually, I treat them quite well, but it's nothing compared to you."
