chapters.title: Chapter 162 - 162: The Accessory Blueprint?
chapters.content:
"."
With the Mechanical Eye, Chen Mang could clearly observe the scene outside the Train. It wasn't a three-dimensional image or a Radar display, but rather a direct, visible picture, like a television screen.
Chen Mang looked at the Green Dragon quietly perched on top of the Train, his expression gradually turning strange.
This guy can't swim?
Your home is in the depths of the sea, yet you can't swim? No wonder you can't return home.
So, when this Green Dragon kept looking back at the Azure Dragon Train, it wasn't actually a provocation but a genuine attempt to guide the Train to help it return home. However, Er Dan mistook it for a challenge.
Flying and then glancing back—isn't that clearly looking down on others?
"But..."
Chen Mang frowned slightly, still puzzled. According to Er Dan, the Green Dragon was a creature that roamed various regions. In the Kunlun Mountains area, Er Dan had only seen the Green Dragon once before; it had never come to the Kunlun Mountains before.
But since the Green Dragon's home is in the Underwater Labyrinth, it should have been wandering around this area all along.
Wait!
Chen Mang's lips twitched slightly. He roughly understood the situation. The panel stated that this monster had long been dead, with only a damaged soul controlling its decayed body, allowing it to continuously revive.
So, most likely, every time this Green Dragon died, it tried to fly back home.
But the revival locations weren't fixed.
It kept reviving in random places. This planet was much larger than the one from his previous world, which meant it was highly possible that even a year after the apocalypse began, it had never reached the Shahe Plain.
The distance was too great.
And it was easily killed along the way.
Finally—
After enduring countless hardships, after an unknown number of obstacles, it finally flew to the Kunlun Mountains area more than a year after the apocalypse began, ready to start its journey home. But then, the Azure Dragon Train, having somehow gotten wind of it, attacked fiercely, sending it away again!
Revived once more in some remote corner.
This time, it was relatively lucky, reviving not too far from the Kunlun Mountains area. It didn't take long, and by sheer luck, it encountered him, finally embarking on a successful journey.
Had it been anyone else.
This poor Green Dragon might have had to start its journey home all over again.
The lakebed.
The light was dim. The Train's head provided a strong contribution, while Xiao Ai piloted the Stellar Train toward the coordinates provided by Er Dan. After entering the water, the Green Dragon showed no reaction.
Clearly.
Without the coordinates provided by Er Dan, he would have had to search the lakebed for a long time to find the Fortuitous Encounter map of the "Underwater Labyrinth."
Chen Mang sat in his chair, quickly jotting down a brief summary of everything that had just happened.
This was another story worth recording in the textbooks.
Under his keen insight, he once again led the Stellar Train to success.
After about ten minutes.
The Stellar Train finally reached the lakebed. Directly in front of the Train, a grand, golden palace sat in the center of the lakebed, exuding a heavy, historical sense of decay.
At the palace entrance was a straight road.
At the end of the road was a massive circular archway, large enough for a Train twice the size to pass through effortlessly. Markings on the ground guided the way, and above the palace entrance floated several white glowing characters.
"Underwater Labyrinth."
It looked somewhat like a regional border, though not as vast.
"Is this the Underwater Labyrinth..."
Chen Mang observed everything before him with curiosity, slowly guiding the Train onto the road and driving it into the palace. As the Train approached the archway, it automatically opened, much like Ji Chuchu had willingly parted her legs the night before.
Upon entering the palace.
The first sight was a massive square with an extremely high ceiling, easily over ten meters tall.
From the outside, the palace was large, but the ceiling was definitely not over ten meters tall. Clearly, some sort of space-folding technology was at work here, similar to the "Space Gate."
Moreover, there wasn't a single drop of water inside the palace.
It was quite dry, with ample oxygen.
Immediately after—
A line of text appeared on the Train's control panel screen.
"Please disembark, Train Conductor, and choose your maze difficulty."
"..."
Chen Mang opened a drawer, taking out the long-unused Special Item, the "Salted Fish Hairpin," and placed it on his head. He then slipped the "Individual Exoskeleton Armor" under his clothes and carried a cane and the Soaring Dragon Assault Rifle loaded with level 6 bullets in his arms before jumping off the Train.
Strange.
This was the first Fortuitous Encounter map he had encountered that required the Train Conductor to disembark.
He didn't feel safe without bringing extra equipment.
There was still a level 5 boss lying on the Train's head. Although it seemed extremely docile and non-aggressive for now, who knew what might happen later? If it attacked him, he'd be done for.
Even the "Salted Fish Hairpin," a Special Item he had always found embarrassing, had its use. It allowed him to breathe underwater for ten minutes, with a 24-hour cooldown. Although the palace had oxygen, they were still at the bottom of a lake, so it was good to have it just in case.
"Phew..."
The palace was enormous. Inside, his Stellar Train seemed rather insignificant, and he himself appeared even more so.
Standing beside the Train, Chen Mang glanced up at the Green Dragon perched on the roof, placing his index finger on the rifle's trigger, ready to react at a moment's notice.
He also wore white gloves.
Another Special Item that temporarily enhanced his physical abilities. He even wore the Badge he had thought was useless.
The next moment—
At the center of the palace, five massive light screens suddenly appeared, with an even larger screen above them.
-
"Welcome, Conductor of the Stellar Train. The Underwater Labyrinth is located in the green zone of the Shahe Plain."
"For Trains in the green zone, the Underwater Labyrinth is not an easily accessible place, yet there are always Train Conductors who manage to set foot here through various means."
"Human civilization is like a centipede—dead but not stiff."
"Perhaps one day in the future, the planet you inhabit will face destruction."
"But I believe that the shattered human civilization will turn into countless stars, seeking out habitable planets in the depths of the universe."
"Please choose your maze difficulty."
"Once you make your choice, it cannot be changed."
-
"..."
Chen Mang looked at the panel expressionlessly. Could they not have phrased that better? "Dead but not stiff"?
But...
He didn't dwell on it for now, instead focusing on the five difficulty levels of the maze.
-
S-level difficulty maze: Your consciousness will descend into a robot body and appear on a randomly selected Train. The Conductor of that Train will meticulously design a static maze for you. If you reach the endpoint within half an hour, you will have successfully passed.
PS: The Accessories and armed personnel on that Train cannot attack you, nor can you attack any Accessories or personnel on that armed Train. The "Train Auxiliary AI" from your Train will inhabit the robot, granting you extraordinary thinking abilities. The robot has the running speed of an adult male, and the Train's carriages are limited to a maximum of 18.
Reward: 30 Murphy Stones.
-
A-level difficulty maze: You will fall asleep and enter 99 layers of dreams. If you regain consciousness within 24 hours, you will have successfully passed.
B-level difficulty maze.
C-level difficulty maze.
D-level difficulty maze.-
Chen Mang's attention was mainly on the S-level difficulty maze. This S-level maze hadn't disappeared. This was the task Er Dan had chosen last time, but unfortunately, he had failed.
"What a pity."
He shook his head regretfully. If only he had been the first to enter. Based on his experience at the "Goblin Ruins," as the first to enter, completing a task once wouldn't make it disappear.
He could complete it again, and only then would it disappear.
Effectively allowing him to complete it twice.
Wait, perhaps there were other restrictions preventing him from completing it twice. Otherwise, during the "Goblin Ruins," there should have been a task that disappeared after completion. After all, the owner of the Goblin Ruins key could have completed a task they had already passed again.
Without hesitation.
He immediately chose the S-level task, only glancing briefly at the other four difficulty levels.
Just like Er Dan had that day, he was quite confident.
This task.
Li Shiji couldn't help him with this; he could only rely on himself and the AI. He wasn't particularly skilled with mazes, but he knew other Trains well. He didn't believe anyone could design a maze on a Train as complex as his.
If there was such a genius.
He would admit defeat.
But the Train's space was limited. Without a "Space Gate," the space was essentially fixed. A level 3 Train had no space-related Accessories. How complex a maze could be designed?
Even Li Shiji, without a level 10 Refrigerator, could you ask him to design a maze?
Even a skilled housewife can't cook without rice.
After he successfully made his choice, the five light screens above the palace slowly dissipated, merging into one.
-
"The Conductor of the Stellar Train has successfully chosen the S-level difficulty maze."
"Searching for a corresponding Train... Search failed. No available Train for descent."
"Issuing the one-time Special Item 'Consciousness Transmitter.'"
"When a Train suitable for descent is found, the 'Consciousness Transmitter' will emit a piercing alarm and flash red. Press the button on the Consciousness Transmitter within one hour, and your consciousness will be transmitted into the robot body, officially starting the S-level difficulty maze."
-
The light screen slowly shattered, forming a walkie-talkie made of lines in the air.
As the lines solidified, the walkie-talkie materialized.
Landing in Chen Mang's hand.
"30 Murphy Stones, not bad."
Chen Mang smiled, weighing the walkie-talkie in his hand. This was a perfect way to leave the Shahe Plain without any regrets. Now, he just had to wait for someone to show up. When someone chose the S-level Mechanical Train Profession Change task, he would appear on their Train, just like Er Dan had.
Success would earn him 30 Murphy Stones.
That was a hefty sum.
He had only gotten 10 Murphy Stones from killing the "Level 7 Mechanical Zombie King." This S-level task was essentially free 30 Murphy Stones for any Train Conductor who could reach here.
This opportunity was significant.
The Underwater Labyrinth might be unique to this area, but there were likely similar Fortuitous Encounter maps in other regions with comparable tasks.
Now, it was just a matter of waiting.
This couldn't be rushed.
He tossed the walkie-talkie into the Train cabin and looked at the Green Dragon perched on the Train's head, about to say something, when he noticed that its body had begun to rapidly decay.
No blood.
The quickly decaying flesh turned into powder, floating in the air.
Then, the Green Dragon staggered to its feet on the Train's head and fell heavily to the center of the palace. In less than half a minute, the entire Green Dragon had turned into powder, scattering in the air.
At the same time—
The square began to tremble slightly, and a dark hole appeared at the center, revealing stone steps.
Dim oil lamps hung on the walls.
The hole wasn't too large.
People could enter, but Armor and Trains couldn't.
Below this hole was likely the generous reward for sending the Green Dragon home in the "Apocalypse Fortuitous Encounter, Hellish Green Dragon" task.
"..."
Chen Mang strode back to the Train, instructing Xiao Ai.
"Send a team down to check it out."
He then turned his gaze back to the line of text on the control panel, his eyes narrowing slightly as his thoughts began to race.
-
"...Before death, it swallowed the 'Deep Sea Shield' Accessory Blueprint, making killing the Hellish Green Dragon the only way to obtain the Deep Sea Shield."
-
The Accessory Blueprint?
This sentence carried a lot of information, leading to many possible connections.
Before death, the timeline was likely before the apocalypse on this planet. It seemed similar to Doba, belonging to another planet that had also faced the extinction of its civilization in the apocalypse.
But this Green Dragon, before death, had put up a strong resistance and swallowed the 'Deep Sea Shield' Accessory Blueprint?
He quickly shook his head.
Dismissing these thoughts for now. How the apocalypse came about could be pondered later. Right now, he was more concerned about what rewards he could reap.
Biao Zi wore the "Mechanical Eye" on his chest. Within the Radar's range, everything Biao Zi saw could be transmitted to the Train's control panel screen.
Chen Mang leaned back in his chair, watching the screen like a first-person tomb exploration game. The passage was long, with nothing but stone steps.
Even the oil lamps weren't real oil lamps.
Upon closer inspection, they were electric bulbs shaped like oil lamps, with some clever designs to make the light flicker like an oil lamp.
"Lord Mang."
Biao Zi's voice came from the Train cabin. "I... I think I see a dragon."
"..."
Chen Mang didn't speak because he saw it too. At the bottom of the stone steps was a massive square with a huge dragon skeleton.
This place...
Seemed somewhat similar to the Goblin Tomb!

chapters.title: Chapter 163 - 163: "Dead... Dead?"
chapters.content:
The dragon's skeleton was much larger than that of the Green Dragon. In comparison, the Green Dragon seemed like a mere hatchling.
Pitifully delicate.
After briefly reporting the situation, Biao Zi, holding a high-powered flashlight, slowly ventured deeper, his eyes filled with both excitement and caution as he scanned the surroundings.
The square before him had nothing but the skeletal remains of a dragon.
The high-powered flashlight in his hand was given to him by Lord Mang. It was embedded with a Level 1 Energy Stone, making its brightness and duration far surpass those flashlights scavenged from the City Ruins.
Another chance to earn merit...
The next moment—
The dragon's skeleton suddenly began to tremble, and countless particles of dust fell from its bones. The patterns on the walls around the square began to glow with an eerie red light. In the blink of an eye.
The once skeletal dragon had regained its flesh.
Completely green.
A larger Green Dragon.
"ROAR!!!"
A deafening roar echoed throughout the square.
At the same time, the gate behind them slammed shut, completely blocking the way back.
Biao Zi's expression changed slightly as he quickly turned to look at the now completely sealed passage. There was no going back.
At that moment, a message from Director Ai quickly appeared on his Iris Chip.
「Detected Level 5 Monster: Undead Green Dragon.」
「The space below has been sealed. The Train Conductor is trying to find a way to provide support. Please hold on.」
This message appeared simultaneously before all members of the Guardian Team One.
"It's over!"
A team member who usually had low presence almost instantly became overwhelmed with despair. He pressed his back tightly against the square wall, his voice trembling with a sob.
"Biao Ge, it's over. We're done!"
It was a Level 5 Monster.
For the Train, a Level 5 Monster could be easily dealt with, hardly worth a second glance. But for them, a Level 5 Monster was something that could completely wipe them out.
"All of you, calm the fuck down!"
Biao Zi, unable to communicate through Director Ai at this moment, knew he needed to boost morale first. He roared towards the Level 5 Undead Green Dragon that was flexing its body in front of them.
"It's just a measly Level 5 Monster. Our rifles are loaded with Level 6 bullets!"
"Everyone, listen to my command. I'll—"
Before he could finish, the panicked team member, realizing that tearing up his Train Ticket was useless, succumbed to complete despair. He aimed his rifle at the Undead Green Dragon and pulled the trigger. The dull sound of gunfire echoed in the confined space as bullets accurately hit the monster's body.
However...
The monster's body was too large, with a length of nearly seven to eight meters. Sensing the attack, it wrapped its wings around itself. Although the Level 6 bullets successfully penetrated its defenses and entered its body.
They didn't cause significant damage. Instead, they enraged the Undead Green Dragon, making it even more ferocious. It roared and flapped its wings, charging towards the team member who had fired.
"BOOM!!!"
Its claws instantly pierced through the team member's chest, pinning him firmly against the wall.
"Shoot its eyes!!"
Biao Zi, seeing this, shouted angrily at the team member: "Xiao Mao, shoot!"
Then he charged towards the Green Dragon.
"Everyone, climb onto the Green Dragon. Try to insert knives and bullets into its weak spots. Don't give it space to charge!"
"Where..." The team member, tightly pinned against the wall by the Green Dragon's claws, felt his life force rapidly diminishing. His eyes filled with despair and unwillingness as he threw his rifle aside: "Where the hell are there any more bullets..."
He then pulled out a Train Blade Fragment from his chest and, with all his strength, stabbed it into the Green Dragon's eye as it prepared to devour him.
Squelch!
The Level 50 Train Blade Fragment easily pierced through.
The pain from hitting a weak spot drove the Green Dragon into a frenzy. It bit off the team member's entire upper body and swallowed it before flying to the top of the square, thrashing violently.
The intense pain from its body made the Green Dragon even more berserk.
Biao Zi had already climbed to the Green Dragon's neck, tightly gripping a scale to secure himself. With his other hand, he held a Train Blade Fragment, relentlessly chiseling away.
He had faced countless more perilous situations in the Combat Training Virtual Space's "Biohazard" map.
Although death wasn't possible in the map.
The extensive experience with death still allowed him to remain calm in the face of real danger.
This spot was the Green Dragon's blind spot!
At that moment—
Muffled gunshots suddenly came from within the Green Dragon's body, followed by an agonized wail. The Green Dragon then fell like a leaf, crashing heavily to the ground. After struggling for a few moments, it suddenly stopped moving.
"Dead... Dead?"
Biao Zi, still perched on the Green Dragon's neck, stood up in a daze. How did it die?
He grabbed his rifle, jumped off the Green Dragon, and walked to its head. After firing a burst into its eye, he reloaded while surveying the scene. It was indeed dead—completely dead.
But...
Guardian Team One had suffered its first loss today.
Xiao Mao was dead.
Xiao Mao was too scared. If only he had listened calmly...
"Wait!"
Biao Zi's expression suddenly changed as he looked at the team members climbing off the Green Dragon. His voice slightly urgent: "Where's Shan Mao Zi?"
There were only seven people in front of him, eight including himself!
Where was Shan Mao Zi?
In the chaos earlier, he hadn't carefully checked everyone's positions. Could it be that Shan Mao Zi hadn't climbed onto the Green Dragon and had been swallowed by it?
At that moment!
"Here... here I am."
Shan Mao Zi, covered in mucus and blood, struggled out from the Green Dragon's tail. His hair looked like it hadn't been washed in days, sticking together in clumps. Trembling, he stood up and raised his rifle, grinning at Biao Zi.
"I followed the Green Dragon's rear, made an opening deep inside, and crawled into its womb. I fired a few bursts there."
"Biao Ge, you said to attack the weak spots. I thought this was weak enough."
"..."
Biao Zi was momentarily stunned, then quickly realized what had happened. He strode over and hugged Shan Mao Zi tightly, grinning: "Damn, brother! You just made a huge contribution. No wonder the Green Dragon suddenly died."
"But..." Shan Mao Zi glanced at the half-corpse in the corner, his voice tinged with sadness: "Mao Zi is dead."
"BOOM"
At that moment, the gate sealing the passage slowly opened. Zhang Da Mei, who had been waiting outside with Team Two, immediately strode over to Biao Zi. Seeing the motionless Green Dragon corpse, her eyes flashed with disbelief: "Dead... Dead?"
"You killed a Level 5 Monster without any mechs?"
Biao Zi didn't respond to Zhang Da Mei immediately. Instead, he patted Shan Mao Zi's shoulder and said softly.
"He's gone. Let it be."
"Mao Zi was always timid. Living in this apocalypse was too painful for him. Perhaps death is a release for him."
Then he examined Shan Mao Zi's twisted body.
"Seriously injured?"
"Not too bad. The monster kept squeezing me inside, probably fractured a bit."
As they spoke.
The fallen Green Dragon gradually turned to dust and disappeared from the square, leaving behind an Accessory Blueprint and a chip.
The square was also beginning to collapse.
Biao Zi quickly picked up the items on the ground and helped Shan Mao Zi up. He looked at Zhang Da Mei and the others: "Let's talk back on the Train. This place is about to collapse. Let's get out of here."
"..."
Inside the Stellar Train, Chen Mang sat calmly in his chair, watching the scene on the screen. He had just witnessed the entire event from Biao Zi's first-person perspective. An unexpected Level 5 Monster had appeared, and the space below the square had been sealed.
The Train couldn't provide support.
Biao Zi and the others had to fend for themselves.
"Level 5 Monster..."
After a long while, Chen Mang's murmur echoed in the car. He had thought perhaps the entire Guardian Team One would be wiped out in the square below. But unexpectedly... they had won.
Theoretically.
Even a newly adult boy, armed with a Level 6 weapon, had a chance to kill a Level 5 Monster.
After all, if it could penetrate the defenses, there was a chance to kill it.
But that was only theoretical. The actual probability was much, much lower.
In real combat, many issues could arise. Biao Zi and the others had almost no defensive means. A single hit could kill them. Yet, they had managed to take down the Level 5 Monster with only one casualty. It could almost be called a miracle.
"This Level 5 Monster wasn't very strong."
Xiao Ai's voice came from the Train car: "Its attack methods were very limited, and it even had blind spots. If it were one of those Level 5 Monsters from the Kunlun Mountains, Biao Zi and the others wouldn't have survived."
"Because it had just revived, a single claw strike only disemboweled. A normal Level 5 Monster would have turned them into a bloody mist instantly."
"Still, it's impressive," Chen Mang said softly.
At that moment—
Several lines of text appeared on the control screen.
-
「You have successfully sent the Green Dragon back to its homeland, fulfilling its wish to return to its roots.」
「The skeleton deep in the cave is the Green Dragon's true body.」
「Long ago, the Green Dragon's soul was imprisoned here. Each time it revived, it would inhabit a different Green Dragon's body. Only by killing the Green Dragon's soul could it truly find salvation.」
「A damaged soul controlled a decaying body.」
「People often think that living is hope, but sometimes only death can bring true salvation.」
「It may attack you, but that is not its true desire.」
「Thank you.」
「The blue-grade Deep Sea Shield Accessory Blueprint, as the Green Dragon found salvation, has disintegrated. There are multiple ways to obtain it, not just by killing the Green Dragon.」
「The Stellar Train's Reputation Points +100.」
-
"..."
Chen Mang remained silent. At that moment, Biao Zi had already brought over the rewards from the battle.
There was an Accessory Blueprint and a chip.
A blue-grade Accessory Blueprint for the "Deep Sea Shield."
And
A map chip, "Dragon Castle."
Like "Biohazard," it required the Combat Training Virtual Space and had both normal and extreme mission options. Completing it could improve one's Physical Fitness Index.
The rewards were decent.
He already had the "Deep Sea Shield" accessory, so this blueprint was temporarily useless. It could only be sold later.
"Xiao Ai."
"Take Shan Mao Zi to the Medical Pod for treatment."
"Train Conductor, Shan Mao Zi has already been treated with the Simple First Aid Kit."
"Huh?"
Chen Mang frowned slightly: "The Simple First Aid Kit's Level 10 Supermodel Effect can only suture severed limbs. Shan Mao Zi had fractures. How was he treated?"
"He used a Train Blade Fragment to cut off the fractured part, then sutured it. Under the Simple First Aid Kit's Level 10 Supermodel Effect, the displaced bones automatically realigned."
"..."
Chen Mang's eyelids twitched, but he didn't say anything more. He simply piloted the Train out of the Underwater Labyrinth, swiftly navigating through the lake. As the Train broke the surface, its wheels instantly transformed into Bunny Clouds, speeding away into the distance.
"Three isn't enough. Bring three more."
Inside Guard Car 7.
Biao Zi lit three cigarettes and stuffed them into Shan Mao Zi's mouth: "They have pain-relieving effects. Feeling better now?"
"Much... much better."
Shan Mao Zi, wrapped in bandages, lay on the bed, his body occasionally twitching. His face was pale, and beads of sweat the size of soybeans dotted his forehead. The fractures had all healed, but the pain... it was excruciating.
Luckily, the cigarettes helped ease the pain a bit. Otherwise, he would have passed out from the agony long ago.
"Shan Mao."
Mei Jia, her eyes red, knelt by Shan Mao Zi's bed, using a hot towel to wipe the sweat from his forehead. She tightly held his hand, her lips slightly parting, but ultimately, she said nothing.
"It's okay."
Shan Mao Zi, lying on the bed, grinned and patted Mei Jia's head: "All my injuries have healed. It's just a bit of pain. By this afternoon, I'll be fine."
"You go back to your room. This is a place for men. It's not suitable for a woman to stay here. Go on."
Mei Jia, her eyes still red, nodded and got up, heading towards the Refrigerator.
At that moment—
Chen Mang, accompanied by Xiao Ai, walked through several cars to Guard Car 7. He sat on the bed opposite Shan Mao Zi and asked softly: "How are you now?"
Seeing Lord Mang, Shan Mao Zi immediately struggled to sit up, leaning against the wall, looking somewhat nervous.
"The injuries are all healed. Ready for duty at any time."
"Next time you're seriously injured, use the Medical Pod. It doesn't take much Iron Ore. The Stellar Train can afford to treat its guards."
"Hmm..." Shan Mao Zi wanted to explain something, but after seeing Biao Zi's look, he swallowed his words and simply nodded weakly.
"Alright."
Chen Mang didn't stay long. He stood up and looked at Biao Zi.
"There's a new map in the Combat Training Virtual Space. Quickly take Team One through all the normal missions to boost your Physical Fitness Index as much as possible."
"If you were all piloting mechs this time."
"It wouldn't have been so rough."

chapters.title: Chapter 164 - 164: "Ahead lies the yellow zone, the Zombie Basin."
chapters.content:
"And..."
"Regarding the guard who died, go and explain the process to Lao Zhu. It will be included in the training manual."
"Yes."
With that, Chen Mang didn't linger any longer and immediately left the car.
The Stellar Train was heading towards the Kunlun Mountains region, preparing to enter the yellow zone, the Zombie Basin once again.
"Train Conductor Zhu, what does Lord Mang mean?"
"..."
Lao Zhu glanced at Biao Zi before lowering his voice, "Appropriately embellish it. Tell me the details later, and I'll make some adjustments."
"Does Mao Zi have any relatives on the train?"
"No."
"Er Dan."
Inside the Stellar Train, Chen Mang was piloting the train high in the sky, speeding towards the Kunlun Mountains region. He picked up the train radio's intercom, "Wait for me in the Kunlun Mountains region. I'll be there soon. The matter is handled, and we can proceed."
"No problem," Er Dan's voice quickly came through the intercom.
At that moment—
"Hmm?"
The Targeting Radar showed a Level 4 train below being chased by a group of mantis-like monsters. The mantises were noticeably faster, and there were even two Level 5 mantis monsters. The train didn't seem to have any effective countermeasures.
It was in dire straits.
Without much thought, Chen Mang immediately maneuvered the train above the Level 4 train. The Doomsday Cannon quickly locked onto the two Level 5 mantis monsters, firing nearly a hundred rounds.
"Boom! Boom! Boom!"
The explosions echoed across the plain, instantly turning the two Level 5 monsters into bloody mist.
Many of the lower-level mantis monsters nearby were also affected, some dead, others injured.
Since he had encountered it.
He might as well save them.
Chen Mang didn't dwell on it, casually glancing at the grateful messages sent by the other train through the train radio before continuing to pilot the train away. The train behind slowly came to a halt, and a group of thugs jumped out to kill the remaining mantis-like monsters.
At that moment—
Xiao Ai, standing nearby, suddenly spoke up, "Train Conductor, Zhang Da Mei says that among the thugs on that train below, two men are his brothers."
"Brothers?"
Chen Mang raised an eyebrow and turned the train around, heading back the same way.
"Did he recognize me as a fellow townsman?"
On the Shahe Plain, inside a Level 4 train, a man was still shaken as he looked at the forced private message on the train radio, his eyes filled with relief and lingering fear.
He had thought he was going to die here.
Unexpectedly, he had been given a second chance at life.
A big shot had passed by and casually saved his life.
Through the chat box of the forced private message, he learned that the other party was the "Stellar Train," the big shot from the Iron Ridge Wasteland. Even in the advanced regions, it remained a top-tier train, leading all three rankings.
He too had come from the Iron Ridge Wasteland.
Was that why the big shot had been willing to save him?
But he had been completely unknown in the Iron Ridge Wasteland. How had this guy recognized him?
At that moment—
He suddenly noticed that the Stellar Train had flown back from the horizon and slowly landed in front of his train. As soon as it stopped, the door of a middle car was flung open.
A mecha jumped out.
It began slaughtering the remaining mantis-like monsters around.
Wait, a mecha...?
Could Level 6 trains already produce mechas?
In the blink of an eye, the remaining monsters around the train were all killed. The mecha seemed to be saying something, and then... then his two idiot thugs actually ran over, each hugging one of the mecha's legs, and started crying?
What kind of scene was this?
The man sitting in the train cabin was utterly bewildered. Although he didn't know what was happening, he didn't dare to make any sudden moves, just cautiously waiting.
Soon.
A message came through his train radio.
"I want these two thugs of yours. Name your price."
Now he understood.
There must be relatives of these two idiots on the Stellar Train. Could it be the sister they kept talking about? He glanced at the ten exaggeratedly large-caliber cannons on the Stellar Train, his mouth twitching slightly.
"The fact that the big shot was willing to help is already a great favor. If the big shot wants them, just take them."
Before he could say more.
The two big idiots had already followed the woman back onto the Stellar Train. In the list of train members, the names of these two thugs quickly disappeared, and then the train took off again into the sky, leaving not a trace of clouds behind.
"Phew..."
The man looked on with mixed emotions as the Stellar Train flew away. Although he often cursed these two big idiots, especially when they came back carrying treadmills during resource collection, now that they were really gone, he felt somewhat empty inside.
It felt like...
The two big yellow dogs he had raised had been taken away by someone else.
Inside the Stellar Train.
Chen Mang looked at the physical data of the two tall men on the control screen. Xiao Ai had already gone to install the "Iris Chips" in them. Their Physical Fitness Indexes were incredibly high.
Zhang Da Mei's Physical Fitness Index was 18.2.
Already the highest on the Stellar Train.
But...
Zhang Da Mei's older brother, Zhang Yi, had a Physical Fitness Index of 22.8.
The second brother, Zhang Er, had a Physical Fitness Index of 21.9.
One higher than the other.
This was just ridiculous. This was supposed to be the apocalypse. Could this planet have been some low-martial arts world before the apocalypse, with some kind of bloodline inheritance?
Were the children born with some tyrannosaurus bloodline, giving them such exaggerated physical abilities?
If it weren't for the information he had gathered, indicating that this planet had been a modern world with technological progress similar to his previous world before the apocalypse, he might have believed the low-martial arts world theory.
Quite impressive.
Now he had two more mecha pilots.
However, with their Physical Fitness Indexes, piloting the green-tier mecha "Executioner" was like using a sledgehammer to crack a nut. To fully utilize the "Executioner" mecha's power, a Physical Fitness Index of over 14.0 was required. These two were almost double that!
But it didn't matter.
The "Zombie Basin" was a yellow-tier region, so there would definitely be higher-grade ores and higher-grade mecha blueprints.
Soon.
He met up with the Azure Dragon Train, which had been waiting for him. The two trains flew side by side in the sky, speeding towards the "Zombie Basin" region!
Several hours later.
A massive light barrier appeared ahead, marking the boundary between regions. On the light barrier were four large characters:
"Zombie Basin."
On the control screen, two lines of text slowly appeared:
-
"Ahead lies the yellow zone, the Zombie Basin."
"Up to Level 9 monsters may exist. Current train level: 6. Danger level: high. Please proceed with caution."
-
As the train passed through the light barrier, it meant the Stellar Train had officially entered the yellow zone, the Zombie Basin.
It was already late in the day, nearing dusk.
"Let's rest here."
The two quickly agreed.
The first night, it was better to rest at the edge. They could move out at dawn. After all, the yellow zone had Level 9 monsters.
A Level 9 boss would be a formidable opponent for both the Stellar and the Azure Dragon.
But fortunately.
Both had one thing in common: they could fly. Since it was the Zombie Basin, the main monsters should be zombies, and zombies couldn't fly. As long as they weren't attacked by other trains, it wouldn't be too dangerous.
Inside the Stellar Train.
Chen Mang looked at the Resource Detection Radar and the Targeting Radar.
On the Targeting Radar, there were many red dots, mostly in the form of Corpse Tides, all quite far away and unlikely to reach him anytime soon. The highest-level zombies in those Corpse Tides were Level 6.
Even if they came, they wouldn't pose much of a threat to the train.
As for the Resource Detection Radar, it showed two Level 2 Iron Ores within range, both open-pit mines, but currently occupied by Corpse Tides.
These Corpse Tides were no match for the Stellar Train.
But since it was the first night, he didn't want to stir up trouble. He'd deal with it in the morning.
He looked at the "Vehicle-Mounted Zombie Perception Blocker" accessory on the screen. This accessory had long been upgraded to Level 10, but it had never been useful until now. In this region, it would be of great use.
Even a Level 9 zombie wouldn't be able to sense him.
He could mine in peace.
Tonight, he would sleep first.
"Zhang Da Mei!"
In Guard Car 7, Biao Zi angrily pointed at Zhang Da Mei's nose and shouted, "Are you going too far? Your Team Two already has a mecha. What exactly are you trying to do?"
"Team One just lost a member."
"These two must join Team One!"
"What are you talking about, Biao Ge?" Zhang Da Mei firmly shielded her two brothers behind her, fearlessly meeting Biao Zi's gaze. "Biao Ge, I respect you as a senior, but they are my brothers."
"My own brothers."
"Both logically and emotionally, there's no problem with them joining Team Two, right?"
"Team Three doesn't have a mecha either," the captain of Team Three, a rather handsome young man, chimed in from the corner, his team members gathering around him. "We must also get one for Team Three."
In an instant.
The car descended into chaos.
All three guard teams were vying for ownership of the two newcomers.
Everyone understood.
These two were destined to pilot mechas, and with such high Physical Fitness Indexes, their addition would significantly reduce casualties during missions and boost the team's combat power. Everyone wanted them.
Although no one resorted to violence, the argument grew increasingly heated.
"Enough!"
Zhang Da Mei shouted, then placed her hands on her hips. "The three team captains will fight in the virtual space. The winner gets them!"
Biao Zi and the Team Three captain exchanged glances, then continued to argue loudly.
No one brought up fighting in the virtual space to decide ownership again.
If they could settle it by arguing, why fight?
"Uh..."
Zhang Er, standing behind Zhang Da Mei, carefully stuffed a steaming bun filled with meat sauce into his mouth, chewing with relish before reluctantly swallowing. He leaned over to Zhang Yi and whispered, "Big brother, are we really this popular?"
"They seem to really welcome us."
"I don't know," Zhang Yi replied, his face serious and cold, as he also stuffed a steaming Roujiamo into his mouth. He whispered back, "Act serious. It makes us look tough."
"Remember what Father told us? In a new environment, if you seem too easygoing, you'll always get bullied."
"Right, right, I almost forgot."
Zhang Er immediately put on a serious face, but then grabbed another Roujiamo from the plate beside him and stuffed it into his mouth. The imposing aura he had just mustered instantly weakened, and he couldn't help but chuckle softly.
"Big brother, this Roujiamo is so delicious. It's so oily and fragrant. It's been a long time since I've eaten something this good."
"Lord Mang is so kind. We just joined the car, haven't done anything yet, and he gave us a whole plate of Roujiamo to eat."
"Now we can finally eat our fill."
Zhang Yi, who had been maintaining a serious expression, couldn't help but nod in agreement. He grabbed another Roujiamo and stuffed it into his mouth. "So this is the kind of life Xiao San has been living."
"It's too comfortable!"
"Second brother, remember this time, when we go out to collect resources, we can't bring back treadmills anymore."
"Don't worry, big brother. This time I'll definitely behave."
At that moment—
"Forget it!"
Biao Zi took a deep breath and shouted to stop the escalating argument. He looked at the other two captains. "Tomorrow morning, I'll go see Lord Mang and let him decide the allocation."
"Is that okay?"
Zhang Da Mei and the Team Three captain exchanged glances, then nodded in unison. "If Lord Mang arranges it, there's no problem."
"Let's eat first. The buns will get cold."
With that.
Everyone in Guard Car 7 turned their attention to the plate of buns on the table, ready to start dinner. However... what they saw was an empty plate.
Only some oil stains remained, proving that the plate hadn't always been empty.
"Where are the buns?"
Biao Zi looked at the empty plate in confusion. He was sure he had asked a Team One member to bring a plate of Roujiamo.
Soon.
His gaze shifted to the two men standing by the plate, taller and broader than Zhang Da Mei. They were now wiping the oil from their mouths with their sleeves, clearly...
"Did you two eat all of them?"
Biao Zi's eyes widened in disbelief. "That was food for thirty people! You two ate it all? Do you have Level 10 refrigerators in your stomachs?"
"Uh..." Zhang Er poked Zhang Yi's stomach cautiously. "What does a Level 10 refrigerator mean?"
"No idea."
Zhang Yi quietly moved behind Zhang Da Mei and whispered, "But I think we ate the wrong thing. That food wasn't meant for us."
"Are we in trouble then?"
"Seems like it."
Zhang Da Mei, who had been so confident and assertive in the argument, now had a hint of embarrassment in her eyes. She waved her hand, pretending to be calm. "It's fine. Tonight, I'll cover the meal for everyone."
"Whatever they ate is on me!"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 165 - 165: "Everyone Has the Right to Die."
chapters.content:
"No need."
After taking a deep breath, Biao Zi looked seriously at the two burly men. "Are you full?"
"Uh, I could be."
"Are you full or not?"
"About sixty to seventy percent."
"Shan Mao Zi," Biao Zi turned to Shan Mao Zi. "Go heat up some more buns. Today, we'll make sure these two brothers eat their fill, and it's all on me."
Guard Car No. 7.
Everyone gathered around, staring at the two burly men in the center. The buns, which weren't particularly small, looked like tiny snacks in their hands as they devoured them one after another, clearly enjoying themselves.
"Thirty-one."
"Thirty-two."
Every time Zhang Yi and Zhang Er ate a bun, the crowd would count in unison.
Finally, when they reached thirty-six,
Zhang Yi patted his round belly and looked at the crowd with some embarrassment. "Thank you, everyone. You're all so kind. It's been a long time since I've eaten this much."
"Same here," Zhang Er said with a satisfied grin.
"..."
Biao Zi looked at the two with a complicated expression, counting on his fingers. "Including the ninety buns from earlier, you've eaten a total of one hundred and twenty-six buns. That means the two of you consume one hundred and twenty-six units of iron ore every day."
"This Train has so many people."
"Your daily food consumption alone accounts for almost one-twentieth of the Train's total daily food consumption."
"Are you two even human?"
"That other Train was only a Level 4 Train. Could it really have supported you two?"
"We never ate our fill there," Zhang Yi said sheepishly. "This is the first time we've been full. We ate a bit more this time because we were so hungry. Normally, we don't need this much. Thirty buns a day would be enough."
"Or we can eat bread slices. We used to eat bread slices before. We know they're much cheaper than buns."
"We can go scavenging for supplies. We're not useless. We're really strong. We can move anything you ask us to!"
"Right, right," Zhang Er nodded repeatedly. "If you don't believe me, I can show you."
"No need for that," Biao Zi waved his hand, his expression still complicated as he looked at the two. Director Ai had already sent him their Physical Fitness Index data. Otherwise, he wouldn't have been so eager. He had to have at least one of them!
They were born melee mecha pilots!
The next day, just as the sky began to lighten.
After finishing his morning routine, Chen Mang sat at the control panel, reviewing the Train Log. Nothing had happened the previous night. Under the Vehicle-Mounted Zombie Perception Blocker, not a single Zombie had approached the Stellar Train.
The Azure Dragon Train remained quietly parked nearby.
Time to set off.
First, mining.
The Stellar Train slowly started moving, beginning its exploration of the area. The Azure Dragon Train quickly followed suit.
The overall structure of this area was a basin.
The surrounding terrain was higher, while the center was a low-lying plain. However, due to the vastness of the area, driving didn't feel particularly steep.
Only ten minutes had passed.
They encountered a dense cluster of resource mines.
There was one Level 3 Iron Ore mine and three Level 2 Iron Ore mines.
As expected of a yellow zone. They had just entered and already found a Level 3 Iron Ore mine. Without further ado, since these were surface mines, both Trains slowly parked nearby, and all the Slaves jumped out to begin the day's work.
The only difference was.
The residents from the Stellar Train excitedly rushed down with their pickaxes.
While the Slaves from the Azure Dragon Train were driven down under the whips of the Thugs.
"Mang Ge."
On the plain.
Er Dan stood on higher ground, looking at the Slaves already busy in the mines. He turned to Chen Mang standing beside him, somewhat embarrassed. "Um... Brother, can I tag along with you for a meal? The yellow zone is a bit too dangerous. I'm a little scared on my own."
"You can take the Level 3 Iron Ore mine. I'll just take the Level 2 one."
"Alright," Chen Mang smiled without saying much, then turned to Biao Zi, who was jogging over. After listening quietly, he paused for a moment before speaking softly. "Both of them will join your First Squad."
"This..." Biao Zi was slightly stunned, clearly not expecting this outcome. He had thought the best-case scenario would be getting one of them, but now he had both. His face lit up with excitement as he grinned widely. "Understood, Lord Mang!"
"..."
Chen Mang watched Biao Zi's retreating figure with a faint smile. He had his own considerations. Biao Zi had been with him the longest and was the most loyal and capable among the Guardians. With the rise of Zhang Da Mei and the Third Squad Leader, Biao Zi's authority among the Guardians had been waning.
It was time to strengthen Biao Zi.
Plus, the First Squad had recently lost a member. He was most comfortable using the First Squad, so giving both of them to the squad was the best decision for him.
Later, he'd build two more mechas and send them to the First Squad.
"Mechas are such good things," Er Dan said enviously, standing beside him. "I still don't have a single Mecha Blueprint. I don't even know where to get one. But even if I had a blueprint, it'd be useless. I don't have any Crimson Heartstone either."
"In the Shahe Plain, I haven't seen any resource mines like that."
"Hopefully, there's some in the Zombie Basin."
"This is Lord Mang's order."
Brimming with joy, Biao Zi cheerfully tossed two suitcases in front of Zhang Yi and Zhang Er. "From now on, you're members of the First Squad. Go down and familiarize yourselves with how to pilot a mecha."
"Ahem."
"If you have any questions, you can also ask your sister for advice."
Then he turned to the remaining members of the First Squad. "The rest of you, follow me to the Combat Training Virtual Space. Let's aim to complete all the normal missions of 'Biohazard' today. And Shan Mao Zi, you focus on the map Li Shiji designed for mental training."
"Now, let's go!"
Since Lord Mang had spoken, Zhang Da Mei and the Third Squad Leader didn't say anything, though they couldn't help but feel jealous as they glanced at the two mechas. Who wouldn't want their squad to be stronger?
Inside the Combat Training Virtual Space.
Biao Zi took a deep breath, looking at the four large characters of "Biohazard," his arms trembling slightly. He had already completed all three normal missions of the "Biohazard" map, which had increased his Physical Fitness Index by 0.6.
His Physical Fitness Index was now 12.8.
Only 0.7 away from the minimum requirement of 13.5 to pilot the "Executioner" mecha.
If he could just clear the extreme mission of Biohazard, it would be enough.
The extreme mission's difficulty would be higher.
And it could kill you—only one life allowed.
But...
"Confirm selection of extreme mission."
Soon, a light screen appeared in front of him.
-
"Choosing the extreme mission means death in the map results in brain death in the real world."
"In the extreme mission, Zombies are faster and stronger. Everything else is the same as the normal mission map."
"Please confirm your selection."
-
"Confirm!"
In the next moment—
The light screen dissolved into countless points of light, and the surrounding white space transformed into a familiar elevator. The elevator was rapidly ascending. He had been here countless times before.
Picking up a steel pipe from the elevator, Biao Zi stood still, silently counting down in his heart.
Then—
"Boom!"
A loud crash echoed as the elevator suddenly stopped between the seventh and eighth floors. Without hesitation, Biao Zi kicked open the elevator door, wedged the steel pipe into the gap, and pried it open before rolling into the seventh floor.
Quickly and efficiently, he found a fire axe in the seventh-floor office, kicked open the fire escape door, let out a roar, and charged into the horde of Zombies.
His adrenaline was surging rapidly.
He had experienced this many times before.
But this time, the adrenaline rush was the fastest. If every previous attempt had been a rehearsal, with a chance to try again if he failed, this was the real deal. If he died here, he was truly dead. Not even the heavens could save him!
Ten minutes later.
Standing in the fire escape, Biao Zi glanced around, not seeing a single Zombie still breathing. He grinned, running his blood-stained right hand through his hair, slicking it back, and spat out a mouthful of blood-tinged phlegm.
Then he strode down the fire escape, heading for the lower floors.
The goal was to reach the rooftop, but there were many weapons downstairs that would help him get there more easily.
He wasn't like Zhang Da Mei's three siblings, or Li Shiji, or even the Third Squad Leader. These people had incredible talent, as if they were born strong. He had nothing. He used to be just an ordinary foreman in a guerrilla team.
Just an average guy trying to get by.
Ordinary to the core.
If he wanted to get stronger, the only way was to push himself harder than anyone else!
Places others didn't dare to go, Biao Zi dared. Things others didn't dare to do, Biao Zi did.
"..."
Inside the Stellar Train, Chen Mang frowned, leaning back in his chair as he watched the screen showing Biao Zi, who was already staggering. He remained silent for a long time, his eyes never leaving Biao Zi.
"Train Conductor," Xiao Ai's voice was mechanical and cold. "If you're worried Biao Zi might die in the map, why didn't you stop him before he made his choice?"
Chen Mang didn't respond immediately. After a long while, he finally spoke softly. "Everyone has the right to die."
"You can't stop them."
On the screen, Biao Zi had reached the 17th floor, but it seemed he was at his limit. There was still a long way to the 31st-floor rooftop. He couldn't make it. Even if they forcibly pulled Biao Zi out of the Combat Training Virtual Space now, it would result in brain death.
If Biao Zi died, who would take his place?
Chen Mang silently pondered the follow-up arrangements, but he couldn't bring himself to decide on a definite successor. He was waiting, waiting for a miracle. He still wanted Biao Zi to remain as the First Squad Leader.
This was his trusted aide. Others just didn't feel right.
Just then—
On the screen, Biao Zi suddenly shakily pulled out a syringe from his pocket and stabbed it into his arm. Immediately, he seemed to regain his strength, charging into the Zombie horde and beginning a bloody massacre.
"Hmm?"
Chen Mang raised an eyebrow, partly relieved that Biao Zi had found a way to break through the crisis, and partly curious about where that syringe had come from. He remembered Biao Zi had already used one on the 12th floor.
"Biao Zi didn't use it on the 12th floor. He just pretended to."
"He's lying to me? He knows I'm watching?"
"No... he's lying to his own brain, making it think he injected it when he actually didn't." Xiao Ai sounded amazed. "At the time, I thought he was just being stingy. Now it seems he really managed to deceive himself."
"Humans are incredible. They can even deceive their own brains."
"AI can't do that."
"...Is that even possible?"
Chen Mang's expression was odd as he closed his eyes and poked his arm with his finger, trying to trick his brain into thinking he had injected himself. But perhaps his brain was too smart—the deception failed.
"That won't work," Xiao Ai shook his head. "I roughly understand the logic. It requires an extremely strong sense of belief and the ability to momentarily shift your perspective to the third person. Don't focus on the syringe. Use the pain to trick your brain into thinking the injection happened. Yeah, that's about it."
With the boost from the syringe.
Biao Zi quickly regained his vigor.
Half an hour later.
Biao Zi, his eyes filled with bloodlust and ferocity, realized the surroundings had gradually transformed back into the familiar white space. He had cleared the mission.
A white light screen appeared before him.
-
"Congratulations on becoming the first member of the Stellar Train to clear the extreme difficulty of the 'Biohazard' map."
"Pioneers are always worthy of reward."
"You have gained an additional 1.0 increase to your Physical Fitness Index."
-
Seeing the light screen, Biao Zi was momentarily stunned. Then, unable to hold on any longer, he collapsed to his knees, but his face broke into an ecstatic grin.
It had to be him!
Big Biao Zi!
Clearing the "Extreme Mission" already increased his Physical Fitness Index by 0.5, and now he got an additional 1.0. His Physical Fitness Index had jumped to—
14.3!
This number already exceeded the minimum requirement to perfectly pilot the "Executioner" mecha!
"Zhang Da Mei, you're no match for me now!"
Perhaps it was the confidence from successfully completing the extreme mission, but Biao Zi's demeanor now carried an unprecedented level of self-assurance. It was the confidence born from surviving a seemingly hopeless situation.
Though he wasn't as naturally talented as Zhang Da Mei, he was quickly catching up!
After a brief rest on the ground, he dove back in.
He wanted to seize the moment and use the remaining two attempts to clear the extreme mission, then go to Lord Mang to request a mecha.
With Zhang Yi and Zhang Er added to the mix.
The First Squad would have three mechas!
As the saying goes, good things often come in pairs.
In the Combat Training Virtual Space, the Third Squad Leader's mental strength had also reached 14.0, which was enough to pilot the "Leech" mecha.
The overall strength of the Stellar Train.
Was visibly increasing.
All the Train Crew members, like strands of DNA, intertwined and gradually formed a single rope, rapidly ascending.
