chapters.title: Chapter 170 - 170 "Did Uncle Know Kung Fu Before the Apocalypse?"
chapters.content:
"Huff... huff..."
Sitting in the cockpit of the Executioner mech, Biao Zi gazed at the scene before him, his breathing gradually becoming more rapid. Despite having faced numerous life-and-death situations, he couldn't help but feel a layer of cold sweat forming uncontrollably on his back.
He was scared.
This place practically had the word "danger" written all over it.
But...
Biao Zi took a deep breath, suppressing the chaotic thoughts in his mind, and was the first to step into the exposed elevator shaft in front of him. The rest of the team followed closely behind.
The elevator shaft was spacious, easily accommodating three mechs and eight team members.
It could even fit an entire Train car.
He turned to look at Zhang Yi and Zhang Er in the two mechs behind him. As newcomers, they probably hadn't been to such a dangerous place on their previous Train. He needed to reassure them beforehand.
Otherwise, when danger struck, they might panic, not only risking their own lives but also disrupting the team's offensive rhythm.
However—
Just as he was about to offer some words of comfort, he saw through the gaps in the mechs that these two were... eating roujiamo?!
They brought roujiamo into the mechs?!
Moreover, they didn't look the least bit scared. Instead, they were eagerly inspecting their surroundings while enjoying their roujiamo with relish.
"..."
Biao Zi expressionlessly withdrew his gaze, swallowing the words he was about to say. Well, Zhang Da Mei had once told him that although her two brothers were incredibly strong, they were a bit... simple-minded.
Now it seemed that was indeed the case.
He just hoped they wouldn't wet their pants when danger came.
The Stellar Train was different from other Trains. As its Guardians, they would inevitably venture into more dangerous places. Unlike the Guardians of other Trains, this was their mission.
Other Trains didn't have the capability to go to such places.
Once everyone had entered the elevator, Biao Zi pressed the red button on the control panel. The elevator immediately began its rapid descent.
Unlike elevators in office buildings, this one had no numbers or floor selections on its control panel. It seemed this elevator would only stop at one place, leaving no room for choices.
Information from Director Ai kept coming through the Iris Chip in front of him.
「70 meters to the first monster.」
「50 meters.」
「20 meters.」
The updates from Director Ai slightly eased his tension. With Director Ai here, it was like having a full map hack—he could know the locations of all enemies.
The next moment—
The elevator suddenly stopped descending, and the doors slowly opened. Biao Zi, already in the lead, roared and swung his axe forward the moment the doors opened, smashing an oncoming monster into pulp!
What greeted his eyes was a pristine white corridor. The ceiling was embedded with two rows of brightly glowing Incandescent Lamps and numerous cameras, as well as... heavy machine guns in the corners, similar to the Internal Fire Control System on the Train.
The walls were covered in dried blood, turning the once spotless corridor into a scene of horror.
Biao Zi stepped out of the elevator and crouched down to inspect the unknown monster he had just smashed. It looked like... a monkey?
Information from Director Ai quickly came through the Iris Chip again.
「No data on this monster in the database. Based on the combat footage, its strength is slightly below a Level 2 monster.」
「Turn left at the end of the corridor. There are seven red dots in the laboratory. Be careful.」
"..."
A glint of killing intent flashed in Biao Zi's eyes. He hefted the axe in his mech's hands and continued deeper into the corridor. The corridor was a staggering ten meters high and ten meters wide, easily accommodating his mech.
It was the tallest corridor he had ever seen.
Was it really necessary to design a laboratory corridor in a military base this tall?
Just then, he suddenly thought of something and turned around. Sure enough, Zhang Yi behind him had opened the refrigerator in his arms and was about to stuff the monster he had just killed into it.
Biao Zi immediately said coldly, "Don't pack that. I'll tell you what to pack."
"Oh."
Zhang Yi awkwardly retracted his mech's right hand, letting the monster's corpse fall freely to the ground before closing the refrigerator and strapping it back onto his back. He felt a bit regretful, though.
With so much space in the refrigerator, it was a shame not to fill it.
And that monster corpse could have been useful.
The Train had several Zombies in it, and the monster corpse could have been used to feed them. As he learned more about the Stellar Train these days, his admiration for Lord Mang grew.
The Zombies that struck fear into countless Trains—Lord Mang had actually captured a few alive and kept them on the Train.
As teaching materials for the children.
Lord Mang was truly impressive.
Zhang Yi then quickly caught up with Biao Zi, gripping his axe with both hands, ready to attack at any moment!
Biao Zi walked to the end of the corridor. There were no forks ahead, only a left turn.
After turning left.
On the left side of the corridor was a laboratory. The wall had a large glass window, smeared with dried blood. Inside the laboratory were various instruments he didn't recognize.
A dozen or so monkeys were sleeping inside.
Hearing the commotion, they immediately bared their teeth and pounced on the glass, letting out fierce roars and pounding on the glass.
But it was clear.
The glass was of high quality and had excellent soundproofing.
「Lord Mang's order: Take all the instruments from the laboratory.」
"..."
After glancing at Lord Mang's command on the Iris Chip, Biao Zi took a step back, took a deep breath, and swung his giant axe with full force, smashing it into the glass.
The glass shattered instantly.
The dozen or so monkeys, baring their teeth, charged out at incredible speed!
Zhang Yi and Zhang Er, standing behind, immediately rushed forward!
The axes swung relentlessly, and any hit meant instant death, with no injuries.
Meanwhile, the other team members aimed their Gatling Guns at the monsters and opened fire. Hundreds of bullets instantly enveloped both the mechs and the monsters.
In the blink of an eye, the area was cleared.
The bullets were only Level 3, unable to penetrate the mechs' armor, but they were deadly accurate against these monsters.
The "Surge Gatling" was an energy weapon.
Energy weapons had many advantages, such as being almost silent, requiring less ammunition, and having much lower recoil and weight compared to gunpowder weapons.
But the biggest advantage was that their "Surge Gatling" was Level 10, each embedded with a Level 3 Energy Stone. This meant they could fire bullets ranging from Level 1 to Level 6, allowing them to choose freely.
Against high-level monsters, they could use high-level bullets; against low-level monsters, low-level bullets.
Resource consumption was minimal.
Unlike the "Soaring Dragon Assault Rifle," which, if loaded entirely with Level 6 bullets, would waste resources when facing Level 3 monsters.
Energy weapons had almost no drawbacks.
The only downside was that Energy Stones were made from Iron Ore, and Iron Ore was the most crucial material for Train upgrades—and it was scarce.
The battle ended quickly.
Biao Zi glanced back at the two, somewhat concerned, and reminded them, "These experimental instruments are very delicate. Be careful when packing them, and pay attention to Director Ai's instructions. Don't be careless."
But soon, he realized his worry was unnecessary.
The mech's hands were large, making it difficult to perform precise actions. For tasks like threading a needle, the "Fourth Hand" needed to be activated.
The mech's mechanical arm had four hands, usually stacked together.
For delicate tasks, the outer three hands could be retracted like peeling an onion, revealing a soft mechanical hand roughly the size of a human hand, allowing one to perform tasks like threading a needle without leaving the mech.
However.
Being a mechanical arm, it wasn't as flexible as using one's own hand.
He had practiced for a long time to barely master the third hand, and he still couldn't fully control the fourth hand. Yet, these two big, seemingly simple-minded guys were skillfully using the fourth hand, flawlessly packing all the instruments into the refrigerator on their shoulders.
The entire process was smooth and perfect, like a robot.
"..."
Biao Zi looked at this scene expressionlessly, remaining silent for a long time. He couldn't accept it—why were these two simpletons better at controlling the mech than he was? And these two were really experienced at collecting supplies!
Most importantly, they loved it!
These two didn't care whether the things they collected were useful or not, or whether they could use them themselves. Even if it was garbage, as long as they could stuff it into their refrigerator, they were happy.
That kind of genuine happiness.
Was it because their minds were simple, thinking less, that they could control the mech better?
He suddenly felt a deep sense of loss.
Despite all his hard work and effort, when faced with these natural talents, he couldn't compare. He took a deep breath, gritted his teeth, and secretly vowed that after this mission.
He would go back and conquer the extreme mission on the "Dragon Fortress" map!
He would also train in the map designed by Li Shiji to improve mental strength!
If talent couldn't be matched, then effort would have to make up for it.
All his life, he had believed in one thing: hard work pays off. Luck wouldn't betray anyone willing to put in the effort.
Keep it up!
Big Biao Zi, you can do it!
Just then—
Another message from Director Ai came through the Iris Chip.
「What are you getting fired up about?」
「Stop daydreaming and keep moving.」
"Ah? Oh..."
Biao Zi, feeling a bit embarrassed, quickly cut off his wandering thoughts. He had forgotten they were still in the Hive Mind. By now, all the instruments in the laboratory had been collected, and he had just stepped out into the corridor.
Another message from Director Ai came through the Iris Chip.
「320 red dots are rapidly approaching your location in the underground base. Estimated arrival in 78 seconds.」
「Prepare for battle.」
「Lord Mang's order: Bring back some monster corpses.」
"..."
Biao Zi immediately calmed down, holding his giant axe and standing ready, staring at the empty end of the corridor. The countdown from Director Ai echoed in his ears. When it reached one.
Piercing roars erupted from the end of the corridor.
Countless monsters appeared at the end, rushing toward them along the ground, walls, and ceiling!
"Open fire!"
Biao Zi roared, leading the charge with his axe!
The scene in the underground military base was projected onto the screen in Guard Car No. 7. The remaining members of the second team, who had stayed in the car, were watching the battle footage of the first team.
Meanwhile, the third team had gone to the Resident cars to maintain order.
Some of the 1,900 new Survivors who had joined the Train were causing trouble, and the third team was sent to suppress them.
In the classroom.
Teacher Qiu led the students in watching the live battle footage on the classroom screen.
"See that?" Teacher Qiu looked at the nervous children. "The reason you can live comfortably on the Stellar, with food and clothing, is because someone is out there fighting for you, carrying the burden for you."
"When you grow up, you can join them too."
Just then—
A monster, having navigated through the hail of bullets, broke through the mech line, its mouth wide open, revealing sharp teeth as it leaped into the air, charging toward a team member at the back of the formation!
"Ah!"
The children in the classroom couldn't help but cover their mouths in fear, some even too scared to watch.
But the next moment.
The team member, unable to turn his gun in time, leaned back sharply, his body almost touching the ground like an arch, dodging the monster's attack. Then he quickly stood up, pulled out a Train Blade Fragment from his chest, and plunged it into the monster's chest as it fell to the ground.
The entire sequence was fluid.
As if he had practiced it a thousand times.
"Wow!!"
The classroom erupted in cheers and excitement.
"That uncle is so cool!"
"Did Uncle know kung fu before the apocalypse?"
"..."
Teacher Qiu looked at the team member on the screen, her tense heart finally easing a bit as she saw him kill the monster. Her eyes sparkled with admiration. "That uncle is called Zhang Qi, a veteran member of the first team. He's very skilled."
She knew the names of all the team members—Train Conductor Zhu had told her.
It's just...
She hadn't known Zhang Qi was this good before.
"Damn."
"Scared the hell out of me."
Zhang Qi, pulling the Train Blade Fragment from the monster's body, couldn't help but curse under his breath.
Luckily, he had been training hard with Biao Ge in the Combat Training Virtual Space, or he might have been done for here.
But there was no time to dwell on it.
He quickly refocused, aiming his Gatling Gun at the endless stream of monsters charging down the corridor, and opened fire again!
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 171 - 171: "Detonation after 10 seconds."
chapters.content:
Although there were many monsters, their levels were not high.
Soon—
The battle ended.
Biao Zi looked at the pile of monster corpses in the corridor ahead, then turned to the team members behind him and said in a deep voice, "Report casualties."
"No injuries."
"No injuries."
"None."
Not a single person was injured. It was just that the corridor was a bit spacious. If the corridor had been smaller, the firepower net woven by the eight "Tidal Gatling Guns" would have been impenetrable as long as the Energy Stones weren't exhausted.
"Zhang Yi, collect all the monster corpses."
"Yes."
Zhang Yi, who had been holding back his excitement, immediately opened the refrigerator and stuffed all the monster corpses inside. This refrigerator was great. Among the things on the Stellar Train, it was one of his two favorites.
The first was the refrigerator, and the second was the Roujiamo.
"Continue forward."
In the following journey, they didn't encounter any more monsters. All the monsters that had been in the corridor had already charged at them earlier.
After advancing for about 10 minutes.
The scenery finally changed. Up until now, it had been nothing but corridors, as if a large maze had been built deep underground.
Ahead, there was a huge square.
Around the square were many cylindrical containers filled with an unknown green liquid. Each container had a monkey soaked inside, and there were also many shattered containers.
Clearly, the monkeys they had encountered earlier had escaped from those shattered containers.
"Is this some kind of biological experiment?"
Biao Zi glanced around, then looked toward the center of the square. In the center was a glass laboratory filled with screens and experimental equipment.
The laboratory was empty of living people.
No living people, but there were dead ones.
There were seven human corpses in white robes, the bloodstains long since dried. On the ground lay a dropped pistol—likely used for suicide.
「Take everything from the laboratory.」
Following the order, Biao Zi walked up to the glass laboratory, raised his giant axe, and struck with full force!
However.
This time, there was no crisp sound of glass shattering.
Instead, there was a dull thud. The axe handle vibrated rapidly in his hand, but the glass of the laboratory showed no signs of cracking. After several attempts, he finally gave up.
This glass was too hard to break.
But he noticed a card reader at the entrance of the laboratory. Opening his palm, as the "First Layer Palm" fragmented and retracted into his arm, a card appeared in his hand. This card had been given to him by Lord Mang.
He held the card and placed it on the reader.
"Beep."
A faint sound was heard, and soon the glass walls of the laboratory lowered.
"Start loading!"
Outside the military base.
Inside the Stellar Train, Chen Mang looked at the lines of text flashing on the control panel. Biao Zi and the others had returned safely, bringing back a blueprint, a large amount of experimental equipment, a chip, and a large machine resembling a printer but much larger from the core laboratory.
It was too big to fit into the refrigerator.
Zhang Yi had carried it on his back to bring it back.
This large machine was their biggest haul this time.
The chip contained all the experimental data from the laboratory, the last words of the researchers before their deaths, and the laboratory's logs. After Xiao Ai absorbed all the information from the chip, a summary appeared on the screen.
Ten minutes later.
The screen stopped displaying new information.
"..."
Chen Mang remained silent for a long time before finally picking up the blueprint in his hand.
「Stimulant Production Line.」
A yellow-tier Accessory Blueprint.
When injured, injecting oneself with this stimulant would numb the pain, boost mental activity for a period, heal some injuries, and restore a lot of strength—with no side effects.
It wasn't useful inside the Train, as there were better alternatives.
But it was invaluable for missions outside the Train.
Although not feeling pain wasn't always a good thing—it often meant a quicker death—this item could significantly reduce the casualty rate of Guardians on missions.
As for this military base.
Its sole purpose was to research and manufacture this「Blueprint.」
Yes.
Blueprints could be manufactured, and that large machine was the instrument for creating this Blueprint. Through extensive experimental data, they first researched how to produce the stimulant, then how to create a production line for it, and finally, after a lot of calculations.
This machine produced the「Stimulant Production Line」Blueprint.
And now that the machine was inside the Train, it meant...
After a long while.
Chen Mang turned to Xiao Ai, "Now that we have the machine inside the Train, can we manufacture Blueprints?"
"Yes."
Xiao Ai nodded, "The machine still has seventeen「Blank Blueprints.」All the data for manufacturing the「Stimulant Production Line」has been input into the machine. Once connected to the Circuit System and powered by the Generator, it can produce seventeen more「Stimulant Production Line」Blueprints."
"I mean, can we manufacture other Blueprints? For example, something I just thought of... like a「Lighter Production Line Blueprint」?"
"No. It requires extensive experimental data and a large number of researchers conducting various experiments. Maybe in the future. Besides, researching a simple「Lighter」accessory would be much easier than a「Lighter Production Line Blueprint.」"
"Hmm."
Chen Mang didn't say anything more. For example, a Level 1 Train could produce a white-tier「Single Bed」accessory, but just a single piece, not a「Single Bed Production Line.」After a moment, he suddenly laughed.
This haul was really good.
The card given to him by the「Ten Steps to Kill One Person」Train was truly useful. Without it, Biao Zi and the others wouldn't have been able to enter the laboratory.
The「Secondary Dimension」Train had also led him to a good place.
Both were good people. If he got the chance, he would offer incense to both of them.
Oh wait, the former wasn't dead yet. He'd do it after they died.
Although the machine couldn't be used for now, once he collected enough experimental data and found a large number of researchers, he would someday be able to design and create the accessories he wanted.
As for the story of this laboratory, it was quite simple.
A long time ago.
Or perhaps not that long ago, Biao Zi was searching among the residents for a forensic doctor to perform autopsies on the human corpses to determine the approximate time of death.
This laboratory had been tasked with researching the「Stimulant Production Line」Blueprint.
But because it involved biological experiments.
During the experiments, it was easy to create some extremely terrifying monsters. This had happened many times before. To prevent such incidents, the military base was built underground, and heavy firepower weapons were placed on the surface to deal with any monsters that might escape from the laboratory.
Inside the experimental base.
The glass laboratory at the core of the square had an extremely high defense level. In case of any problems, the bombs embedded in the walls of the laboratory corridors would detonate, burying all the created monsters deep underground.
The researchers and experimental data, however, would survive inside the laboratory, waiting for rescue.
Later.
Later, something did go wrong, but it wasn't a problem within the laboratory. The city was hit by a devastating attack from countless monsters, turning the entire city into a monster's playground. All living beings were slaughtered.
This underground laboratory managed to escape unscathed.
But after losing contact with the outside world for a long time, the monkeys used in the experiments began to mutate, killing the assistants and staff outside the laboratory. Trapped and with no hope of rescue, the researchers chose to end their lives in despair.
But the experimental data and equipment were preserved.
That.
Was the entire story of this underground secret laboratory. Hidden in the machine's AI was a "Research AI," according to Xiao Ai. This AI had no human emotions and was solely responsible for calculating data. Once the machine was restarted, the "Research AI" would awaken again.
"Whew."
Chen Mang exhaled softly, then stretched his body and continued piloting the Stellar Train through the air toward the next anomaly on the map.
This was the first time he had seen humans in the ruins of a mechanical civilization.
He had thought that mechanical civilizations were full of robots, but it seemed there were humans too. He just didn't know whether humans or robots were dominant in this civilization.
It didn't seem like humans were in charge.
At least, if humans had built this city, they probably wouldn't have designed it this way.
All the office buildings looked almost identical, from the streets to the high-rises, all in a deep black color. The roads were perfectly straight and standard, with no greenery or parks.
It was extremely dull and monotonous.
This didn't align with human aesthetics.
Even if it had been designed as a refuge city, they couldn't have completely ignored the livability aspect, right?
The Train continued forward.
Soon, it arrived at the second anomaly, located in the city center.
It was a deep pit.
The pit was about a hundred meters in diameter.
Chen Mang piloted the Stellar Train through the air, slowly descending into the pit. The walls of the pit were lined with Incandescent Lamps. It wasn't very deep, only about a hundred meters.
At the bottom of the pit, he saw a missile standing upright on the ground.
Seven meters long, three meters wide.
It didn't seem to have a very large yield. Next to the missile was a line of text displayed on a light screen.
-
「Nuclear Warhead capable of destroying the entire city.」
「Press the red button to initiate a 10-second countdown to detonation.」
「Detonation will occur after 10 seconds.」
-
Found it. This was the mission objective of the map.
But Chen Mang's face showed no joy. Instead, he expressionlessly looked around. The pit was empty, with nothing but the missile and a button on a nearby pillar.
Escape?
Where to?
There was no escape route indicated, and 10 seconds wasn't enough time to get anywhere.
After a moment.
Chen Mang silently ordered a team to stay behind and guard the square while he went to check the third anomaly for any possible escape route. He was now very glad he had cleared the map earlier.
Otherwise, such a deadly weapon would be sitting here, exposed.
Anyone who pressed the button would take him down with them.
How unjust would that be?
At least they could have put a cover over the button. He was worried that if some monster appeared and accidentally hit the button, how unlucky would that be? He left a team here to guard it, making sure nothing could press the button.
He went to check the escape route.
The third anomaly was very far from the second, about thirty thousand meters in a straight line.
The Stellar Train slowly stopped in front of a tunnel.
The tunnel was entirely made of glass, starting from the ground and descending at a thirty-degree angle straight into the ceiling of the underground space.
This tunnel was the escape route.
From high above, it was located in a patch of rubble at the back of the city, quite noticeable.
-
「High-Speed Train Tunnel.」
「After inserting a Level 3 Energy Stone, the Train will hover in the center of the tunnel using magnetic levitation and escape the city at high speed, breaking through to the surface.」
「In a damaged state, only one Train can pass through.」
-
This was the escape route in this Fortuitous Encounter map, a route that had been prepared when the city was first built.
In other words.
Whether he had chosen to clear the map or not, only one Train could pass through this map in the end. The other four Trains were destined to perish here.
In the future, he would have to avoid going on Fortuitous Encounter maps with Er Dan.
He didn't want to fight with friends. Er Dan probably hadn't experienced this kind of Fortuitous Encounter map before, otherwise he wouldn't have so carelessly joined him on this map.
And also—
This「High-Speed Train Tunnel」was located at the edge of the city, far from the nuclear detonation point.
A straight distance of thirty thousand meters.
It was impossible for the Train to appear at the tunnel entrance ready to depart just 10 seconds after the nuclear detonation.
There was only one solution.
Choose a sacrifice. Let the sacrifice press the nuclear button, and at the moment the countdown begins, the Train enters the tunnel and starts escaping.
Of course.
If he wanted to be extra cautious, he could choose two sacrifices. That would be more auspicious.
"It's huge."
Chen Mang, who had stepped out of the Train, stood on the open ground, gazing at the underground city in the distance. He couldn't help but marvel, although he didn't know how deep underground this was, to dig out such a vast space and build a city inside it.
The infrastructure capabilities of this mechanical civilization were impressive.
"Shan Mao Zi, what do you think you're doing?"
Biao Zi, sitting inside his mech, glared down at Shan Mao Zi with a dark expression. "It's not your turn to play the hero. What the hell are you trying to prove by acting like a big shot here? Put the gun down!"
"I said put the gun down, did you hear me?"
Shan Mao Zi was standing in the square, pointing the gun barrel at his own head, his eyes red and his voice hoarse.
"Biao Ge."
"We both know what's going on here."

chapters.title: Chapter 172 - 172: The Stellar Train Will One Day Soar Through the Starry Seas!
chapters.content:
"Once this button is pressed, the nuclear bomb will detonate within 10 seconds. The power of this bomb is enough to flatten the entire city!"
"How can we escape in 10 seconds?"
"Where can we run?"
Shan Mao Zi's eyes were red, his voice hoarse as he spoke word by word: "The only escape route is the glass tunnel outside the city where the Train was flying earlier. It can only be there."
"The Iris Chip has been disconnected, which means Lord Mang has also gone there to investigate the situation."
"That place is at least 30,000 meters away from here. At such a distance, the Train won't be able to make it in time after activating the bomb."
"The teleportation range of the Train Ticket is only 10,000 meters!"
"The only solution is to leave one person here to press the bomb button while the rest of us head to the tunnel to prepare for escape!"
He took a deep breath, his body trembling slightly as he spoke.
"I once made a promise to Lord Mang."
"He saved my woman's life. I told Lord Mang that if the Stellar Train ever needed someone to carry out a suicide mission in the future, I, Shan Mao Zi, would be the first to step forward!"
"I'm not joking!"
"I never joke!"
"Now it's my turn to step forward. Biao Ge, please take care of Mei Jia for me in the future."
"Don't be crazy."
Biao Zi, with a grim expression, jumped out of his mech and walked up to Shan Mao Zi, staring directly at him: "Since when did you have the authority to make decisions for the Stellar Train?"
"Huh?"
"Lord Mang hasn't even spoken. What gives you the right to make decisions? Where's the discipline?"
"Besides, even if someone needs to sacrifice themselves, couldn't we just pick one of the 1,900+ Survivors? Why do you have to play the hero here?"
"That won't work." Shan Mao Zi shook his head with a bitter smile: "This is a suicide mission. You want those Survivors to do it? Since it's certain death, do you think they might harbor resentment, detonate the bomb early, and take the Stellar Train with them?"
"Biao Ge, tell me, who on the Stellar Train is more suited to stand in this position than me?"
"..."
Biao Zi was about to retort, but his lips moved without saying anything. It seemed like Shan Mao Zi was indeed the only one on the Train suited for this position, but...
After a moment, he shook his head.
"You haven't even had your honeymoon yet. Put the gun down first."
"Lord Mang might have another solution."
"If it really comes to it, let me... or Lao Zhu do it."
Shan Mao Zi couldn't help but laugh: "Biao Ge, Train Conductor Zhu is terrified of death. He would never volunteer for a suicide mission."
Just then—
Biao Zi quickly lunged forward, tackling Shan Mao Zi to the ground and snatching the "Tidal Gatling Gun" from his hands. He wiped the cold sweat from his forehead and couldn't help but kick him, cursing: "Are you fucking insane? At least wait for Lord Mang to speak before you play the hero, alright?"
"Biao Ge."
Shan Mao Zi, lying on the ground, stared at Biao Zi with red eyes, speaking word by word: "Everyone on the Train knows that Lord Mang saved my woman's life, and they also know that I promised him. If someone else dies instead of me in the end..."
"I won't be able to hold my head up high on the Train anymore, and neither will Mei Jia."
"It would be humiliating."
"Face, face, face—is it really that important?" Biao Zi said irritably: "We're in the apocalypse now. How much is face worth anymore?"
"For me, it's very important."
"Get up first. If it comes to it, let Zhang Yi die."
"Huh?"
Zhang Yi, who had just jumped out of his mech and was standing nearby munching on a bun, was momentarily confused: "Where's the candied sweet potato?"
The next moment—
The Stellar Train appeared above the pit without warning, slowly landing in the square. Chen Mang, leaning on his cane, stepped out of the Train and looked at Shan Mao Zi lying on the ground. He calmly waved at Biao Zi.
"Bring Mei Jia down. Let her and Shan Mao Zi press the bomb together here."
"Even in death, they can be a pair of doomed lovers."
"Make it a double blessing."
"Yes."
Biao Zi nodded solemnly and immediately strode toward the Train.
"Huh?" Shan Mao Zi was momentarily stunned: "Can't just one of us die?"
"Come back!"
Chen Mang shouted at Biao Zi's retreating figure in annoyance: "Are you really going to do it?"
Then he pulled Shan Mao Zi up from the ground, dusted him off, and sighed lightly, looking somewhat exhausted: "I just went for a smoke, thinking I'd enjoy the scenery for a bit, and you guys were here putting on a melodrama?"
"Do you need to die?"
"Haven't I told you before? The Stellar Train will never be reduced to a point where someone needs to voluntarily sacrifice themselves."
"You're more valuable to me alive. Stop thinking about dying. Are you constantly imagining in your head how heartbroken I'll be after you die? Do you have some kind of illness?"
"Get up now."
"I'm getting a headache just looking at you. I'm afraid that one day we'll encounter some monster, and you'll charge forward shouting something about dying for Lord Mang."
"Huh?"
Shan Mao Zi muttered awkwardly: "I'm mainly worried that everyone will complain about the resources the Train has spent on my wife. I thought if I died... no one would complain about her anymore."
"But the bomb button is so far from the escape route. How are we going to solve that?"
"Don't worry about it. Biao Zi, take everyone back to the car."
"Yes."
Chen Mang then looked at Doba and Mundo, who had just stepped off the Train. While he was smoking earlier, he had already conducted an experiment—the "Goblin Ticket" could be used normally within this map; there was no spatial blockade.
The "Train Ticket" has a range limit of only 10,000 meters.
But the "Goblin Ticket" has no distance restriction.
The solution is simple.
Just leave one Goblin here to press the bomb button and then return to the Train using the "Goblin Ticket." Everyone can leave alive.
"Doba."
Chen Mang looked at Mundo with a serious and solemn expression: "This member of your tribe hasn't fully regained his intelligence. I've explained the plan to you in detail. You must clearly and firmly relay it to him!"
"Once I'm ready on my end, I'll launch a Level 1 missile that will explode above the pit."
"The moment he sees the missile explode above the pit, he must press the button. Understand?"
The "Super High-Speed Train Tunnel" is currently unusable. Only after the bomb button is pressed will the gate in the tunnel retract, allowing the Train to escape from underground.
"Understood, Lord Mang!"
Doba solemnly accepted the task and pulled Mundo aside: "By the authority of the Goblin King, I command you to remain here until a missile explodes above the pit. Only then can you..."
Soon.
The Stellar Train had left with everyone on board.
Only Mundo remained in place, looking up at the pit above. Even though his neck was sore, he didn't move an inch.
This was the Goblin King's command, a grand plan related to the revival of the Goblins!
He had to carry it out seriously!
"Are we leaving now?"
The Stellar Train, having confirmed that there was nothing left worth exploring in the city, flew over the city and headed straight for the "Super High-Speed Train Tunnel" behind the city, preparing to leave this Fortuitous Encounter map.
In Guard Car No. 7.
Shan Mao Zi stared out the window at the city below, lost in thought. After a while, he awkwardly whispered to Biao Zi: "Biao Ge, did Lord Mang think I was just acting earlier? Trying to show off? I really didn't mean it, I..."
"Enough."
Biao Zi shook his head, interrupting Shan Mao Zi: "Lord Mang just doesn't want you to always approach things with a mindset of seeking death. If someone is always looking for an opportunity to die, they'll eventually die—even when they shouldn't."
"And stop overthinking. No one has complained about the resources the Train has spent on your woman."
"There's no such thing. Stop imagining things."
Shan Mao Zi nodded softly: "I understand."
Biao Zi was silent for a moment before speaking softly.
"Generally speaking, if someone is too concerned about what others think, even to the point of privately speculating, they often ruminate excessively, constantly recalling past painful events and tormenting themselves."
"That's you."
"I'll give you a solution. If you can't stop thinking about those painful things, don't think about the ones close to you. Instead, think about the ones that are very distant. Keep doing this."
"This way, even though you'll still frequently recall those painful memories, because so much time has passed, the pain they cause you will be much smaller."
"Over time, the mental damage you suffer will be minimal. Stop tormenting yourself."
Shan Mao Zi was momentarily stunned before he instinctively began to think. After a while, he looked up at Biao Zi in confusion: "Biao Ge, didn't you used to be a contractor? How do you know this stuff?"
"Hmph."
Biao Zi snorted coldly, somewhat arrogantly: "Don't look down on people. I was still in charge of a team. Keeping an eye on the psychological state of my subordinates was part of my job, you know."
"Biao Ge, what if there were no Goblins on the Train?"
"Then you'd be screwed."
"..."
The Stellar Train had already pulled up beside the "Super High-Speed Train Tunnel" and was slowly entering the glass tunnel. A Level 3 Energy Stone was inserted into the control panel nearby.
Everything was ready.
The lights on the tunnel walls were glowing red, and deep within the tunnel, a gate blocked the way.
The Train wasn't hovering in mid-air but had landed at the bottom of the tunnel.
The next moment—
A missile from Car No. 14, the second-to-last car, slowly rose into position.
"Boom!"
Orange flames instantly engulfed the entire car, and with a deafening roar, the missile shot toward the pit above the city's second anomaly point, exploding with precision.
Almost simultaneously.
The red lights on the tunnel walls turned green, and the Train instantly levitated in the tunnel. A powerful thrust surged forward!
The Train shot through the tunnel at incredible speed!
The gate ahead retracted at the same time.
With all the "nitrogen thrusters" activated, the Train's speed increased further. The intense thrust pressed Chen Mang tightly against his seat. It was the first time he had experienced such speed.
The Train's speed on the screen had reached.
"2120 km/h."
Nearly Mach 2!
"Roar!"
Chen Mang couldn't help but roar with excitement, gripping the control stick tightly, as if trying to vent all the frustrations he had experienced since coming to this world.
He slapped the control panel, and deafening, rhythmically intense music instantly filled every car of the Train.
The rapid speed.
Made the green lights in the tunnel blur into a continuous line.
It felt like traveling through time.
All he could see was the endless tunnel ahead and the green lines on the walls.
He didn't know where the tunnel led. He only wanted to experience this moment of speed and thrill!
Mundo wasn't on the Train.
Instead, he stayed at the entrance of the "Super High-Speed Train Tunnel." Just before departure, he had been ordered to jump off, holding a camera with a Mechanical Eye at its core, aimed at the city above.
When the bomb button was pressed.
The city's hidden backup power seemed to activate, and all the lights turned on. The once pitch-black steel city was instantly bathed in neon lights, resembling a modern city at dusk, stunningly beautiful.
All the searchlights on the rooftops of the skyscrapers shot beams of light into the sky.
Converging into a massive, ever-changing number.
-
"9."
"8."
"7."
-
At the same time, shrill alarms echoed across the steel city. The city's hidden power began to overload, causing the neon tubes in the billboards to burst.
Countless fireworks, hidden who knows where, exploded in the sky.
The scene was so beautiful it didn't look like a nuclear countdown but more like a New Year's countdown.
When the countdown reached zero.
A deafening explosion rang out, and endless flames erupted from the center of the steel city, surging outward like a wall of glass.
Countless skyscrapers collapsed.
Mundo, still in place, recorded the scene with his camera. Just as the shockwave was about to reach him, he tore his "Goblin Ticket."
The scene was breathtaking.
Originally, no one would have witnessed this moment—like a performer putting on a show for an empty audience. But Mundo brought this scene back to the Stellar Train.
If Chen Mang had seen this.
He might have retracted his earlier criticism of this civilization's lack of aesthetic sense. Their sense of beauty was fully displayed in their final, dazzling moment.
Inside the "Super High-Speed Train Tunnel."
The Stellar Train was speeding through the tunnel at incredible velocity. The tunnel behind them was collapsing. As the 10-second countdown ended, Xiao Ai's voice came through.
"The Targeting Radar has detected Zombies on the surface."
"They're still in the Zombie Basin, at the center."
"There are dozens of Trains parked outside, like a gathering."
Xiao Ai's voice was quick, but the Train's speed was even faster. In the blink of an eye, the Stellar Train charged toward the pale yellow light at the tunnel's exit, crashing through it.
Propelled by its speed.
Like a cannonball, the Train shot out of the ground and into the sky!
"Soar high!"
Chen Mang, thoroughly exhilarated, sat in the control chair, pushing the control stick to the limit. The Train switched to Bunny Cloud wheels as it soared into the sky. Chen Mang looked up at the long-missed starry sky and shouted with excitement.
At this moment.
All he wanted was to charge forward.
To reach the starry skies and tell everyone that the Stellar Train would one day soar through the starry seas!
He, Chen Mang, would be the greatest Train Conductor in the history of the starry seas!
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 173 - 173: "Am I Really That Important?"
chapters.content:
"Was that an earthquake?"
"I don't know, but it's not impossible. I remember learning in school that basin areas are prone to earthquakes. So, even if it was an earthquake, it would make sense, right?"
"Are you sure basin areas are prone to earthquakes?"
"Not entirely sure. Let me think."
In the center of the yellow zone, known as the "Zombie Basin," under a sky full of stars, dozens of trains were parked nearby. Several Train Conductors, accompanied by their trusted aides, had gathered together for a small, self-organized meeting.
The tradition of holding meetings had persisted even in the yellow zone.
It wasn't just about exchanging supplies; it was also about sharing information. Face-to-face meetings allowed for the exchange of more valuable information.
In the white zone, meetings were usually held during the day for safety reasons. Although monsters were active both day and night, their activity was generally less intense during the day, making daytime meetings safer.
But in the yellow zone, meetings were typically held at night.
This way, they didn't waste time.
The Slaves rested in the train cars while the Train Conductors attended the meeting. They could return to mining the next day after the meeting.
At this moment—
Many Train Conductors felt a slight tremor in the ground and instinctively looked toward the slope of a small hill in front of them.
On the slope of that hill, there was a seemingly endless passage with a glass tunnel inside. Many people knew about this, but at the entrance of the tunnel, there was a faint yellow membrane.
Next to it was a light screen.
"Prohibited Area Ahead."
It wasn't that no one had tried to explore it, but no one had ever managed to enter. Over time, people stopped paying attention to it, except for some newcomers to the Zombie Basin who, out of sheer disbelief, would approach it, imagining themselves to be the chosen ones. Of course, they all ended up returning disappointed.
At this moment, the ground was shaking slightly.
It felt as if something had exploded underground, like an earthquake, but not quite.
Just then!
A piercing sonic boom erupted in everyone's ears, followed by the sight of a train bursting out of the tunnel at the slope of the hill at an incredible speed, shattering the membrane and soaring into the sky.
Like a meteor from the heavens, it disappeared from sight in an instant.
The last impression it left was the numerous thrust nozzles on both sides of the train, with faint blue exhaust flames lighting up the night, making the train appear incredibly dazzling.
"..."
Almost all the Train Conductors stood frozen in place, stopping whatever they were doing, and looked up at the train that had vanished into the horizon. It took them a while to react, and they exchanged glances.
"Was that a train?"
"Obviously, with so many carriages, it was clearly a train. I wonder where they got the Bunny Cloud. I'm already at Level 8, and I still haven't gotten that accessory."
"If you spend all your time mining, of course you won't get it. Rare accessories like that can only be obtained from Fortuitous Encounter maps or by killing rare bosses."
"I don't remember anyone in the Zombie Basin being that powerful. Who could catch up with that speed?"
"Could it be the Stellar Train?"
"You mean the train that just arrived in the Zombie Basin, ranked first in Supermodel Effect count?"
"Possibly."
"..."
Inside the Stellar Train, Chen Mang switched to the "Bunny Cloud" wheels, which allowed the train to fly high in the air. He was looking for a place to rest. As he burst out of the ground, he noticed the ongoing meeting below.
But he had no intention of joining for now.
He had gained a lot this time.
He needed to find a place to regroup.
Soon—
He landed on a flat area with no high-level Zombies nearby. He didn't activate the "Train Zombie Jammer" because it consumed energy. There was no need to use it for lower-level Zombies; it was better to let the people below practice their skills.
Chen Mang looked at the resource column on the Train Panel.
First, the resources.
"3.49 million units of Iron Ore, 365,000 units of Copper Ore, 500,000 units of Wood, 200,000 units of Crimson Heartstone."
The Iron Ore obtained from the trains that were swallowed in the Geocentric Nuclear Bomb Fortuitous Encounter map had already been included in the inventory.
This map had replenished a lot of resources for him.
There was also a white-grade Accessory Blueprint and 4 Murphy Stones. He now had 16 Murphy Stones.
The blueprint was for... a "Fleshlight Production Line."
A Fleshlight, a tool used for stress relief and relaxation, was somewhat useful. Aside from the hassle of cleaning and the soreness from overuse, it didn't have many major drawbacks.
This blueprint was found in the "Anime Train."
Actually.
Even if you destroyed a train, it was rare to obtain blueprints from it. Most people used the blueprints they got immediately. Who would keep them unless they were planning to sell them?
This thing.
"Hmm."
Chen Mang pondered for a while and then decided to spend 4,500 units of Iron Ore to produce it, upgrading it to Level 10. Although it wasn't useful to him, he could produce a few and place them in the "Resident Store." Not only would it diversify the product range, but it would also provide the residents who couldn't afford meat with an alternative way to relieve stress.
-
"Fleshlight Production Line Level 5 Supermodel Effect": Softer and more elastic.
"Fleshlight Production Line Level 10 Supermodel Effect": Half the consumption.
-
Not bad. Originally, it took 10 units of Iron Ore to produce one. After halving the consumption, it only took 5 units.
It really was a rather useless accessory.
No wonder the "Anime Train" kept it for sale. Whether it could be sold was another matter, though. Unless the price was low enough, even the most garbage blueprint could be sold as long as it was cheap.
Chen Mang leaned back in his chair and looked at the vacuum-packed dried ducks in the refrigerator next to him. There were hundreds of bags, all spicy. This was a good find. When he got tired of the food on the train, he could switch things up with this.
He casually opened a bag, tore off a duck leg, and popped it into his mouth.
Hmm?
Not bad. Chen Mang's eyes lit up slightly. Perhaps it was because he hadn't eaten it in a while. The meat was dry and flavorful, chewy in his mouth. Although it was a bit spicy, it was addictive.
He wondered where the guy had gotten it. Was there a dried duck factory in the Zombie Basin?
But after eating a dozen bites—
Chen Mang's cheeks turned slightly red. He threw the dried duck aside and quickly grabbed a bottle of chilled Mineral Water from the refrigerator, downing it in one go. But it was no use. Why the hell was that duck so spicy?!
His mouth was now burning with intense pain!
At first, it was just flavorful and a bit spicy, still tolerable. But after a dozen bites, the full force of the spiciness hit him. He even felt like his tongue was losing sensation.
"Hiss—"
Chen Mang inhaled sharply several times, but the pain didn't subside at all. He glanced at the packaging on the ground. The flavor was indeed labeled as "spicy," not "extra spicy."
"Damn it!"
Without further delay, he quickly made his way to the "Medical Pod" in Carriage 2. No, this spiciness was killing him. He needed a reboot!
After the reboot, Chen Mang returned to the train compartment, completely back to normal. He gave the half-eaten bag of dried duck to Xiao Fang, who was standing at the door, before turning his attention to the other loot.
He definitely couldn't enjoy these dried ducks himself, but they would make a great interrogation tool.
Feed them the duck, but don't give them water!
Of course, that was just a joke. He decided to put a dozen packs in the resident car and let the guards try the rest.
The confiscated cigarettes were all placed in the Resident Store, along with various supplies stored in the train's refrigerators. There were enough refrigerators to hold everything, including the two to three hundred figurines.
"These are quite nice."
Chen Mang thoughtfully picked up a figurine about the size of a phone, examining it for a moment before tossing it back into the pile. Although these things were useless, it would be a waste to throw them away. He decided to put them in the Resident Store to see if anyone wanted them.
It was worth noting—
According to the information from Biao Zi, there were no females in the Anime Train, only males.
And based on the information from the Slaves of the Anime Train, some time ago, the "Internal Fire Control System" of the Anime Train had suddenly activated in the middle of the night without warning, killing all the female members.
Not even the sows were spared.
Although every train had an "Internal Fire Control System," hardly anyone ever used it. Most of the time, it served as a deterrent. Once activated, it wasn't just about killing one or two people. In such a dense crowd, it was impossible to target individuals accurately.
During the chaos in the Anime Train, many males also ended up as collateral damage.
The only ones who had truly witnessed the power of the "Internal Fire Control System" were the Slaves of the Anime Train. As a result, the Slaves from that train were the most obedient. Especially after seeing the 10 Heavy Machine Guns in the carriage, they obediently entered the refrigerator without any resistance.
In contrast, the Slaves from the other carriages were a bit more unruly. Of course, under the suppression of the third team, these troublemakers were dealt with.
"Added over 1,900 Survivors."
There were hardly any troublemakers; they were all quite obedient, or rather, quite numb.
"..."
Chen Mang frowned slightly. With these 1,900+ Survivors, the total population of the train had now reached over 3,300. The daily consumption of various accessories, along with food, water, and other expenses, had already reached nearly 6,000 units of Iron Ore.
Blink, and 6,000 units of Iron Ore were gone just like that.
And this was during normal rest or mining operations.
If they encountered battles or emergencies, the consumption would skyrocket, and it wouldn't just be Iron Ore; Copper Ore and other resources would also be consumed.
"Well."
He shook his head in resignation but soon smiled again. Although daily expenses had increased, mining efficiency had also improved. It wasn't a matter of pros and cons; it was just that the scale had grown.
With a larger scale, the gains were greater.
But if there was a dry spell with no Iron Ore income for a while, the entire operation could collapse.
He didn't dwell on it further. Instead, he spent 190,000 units of Iron Ore to create Iris Chips for these 1,900+ Survivors, assigning Xiao Ai to implant them one by one. He also spent over 1,900 units of Wood to create a set of clothes for each person.
Of course.
They were orange-red.
This was the standard uniform of the Stellar Train. In the foggy environment of the apocalypse, wearing bright colors could lift one's spirits.
"Am I really that important?"
In the "Space Gate" within Carriage 2, which had been designated as the Mecha Research and Development Center, Xiao Ai was tinkering with the experimental equipment brought back from the Geocentric Nuclear Bomb Fortuitous Encounter map when he heard Lord Mang's order.
He was to implant the Iris Chips.
Only he could do it because his hands were steady enough.
Xiao Ai looked expectantly at the simple robot fixed in the middle of the frame. He was in the process of building himself a new body so that he could be in multiple places at once in the future.
Without delay.
He immediately left the Space Gate, packed the produced Iris Chips and clothes into a refrigerator, and then carried the refrigerator to the resident carriages at the back.
Carriages 10 and 11, originally Goblin Cars, housed over 100 Goblins.
But Doba had taken all the Goblins into the "Space Gate" installed in Carriage 11. The Goblins lived in a refrigerator, so these two carriages had been empty for some time.
However, the Resident Store was placed in the refrigerator in Carriage 11.
Lao Zhu had arranged 10 refrigerators in Carriage 10. These 10 refrigerators would serve as the dormitories for the 1,900+ Survivors for the time being, with 200 people per refrigerator.
Starting with Level 3 Resident treatment.
Xiao Ai stood at the refrigerator door, implanting the "Iris Chips" one by one. Each person who received a chip would follow the example of those before them and take their assigned clothes from the side. Everyone queuing to enter the refrigerator, regardless of gender, was completely naked, with no clothes on their bodies.
But no one paid any attention.
Firstly, they were all a bit dirty. Secondly... in this situation, who cared about such things?
The difference between humans and dogs is that humans still care about atmosphere. When doing certain things, there needs to be some ambiance—a private space, soft music, and for the more luxurious, even the requirement that the other person is someone they like.
"None?"
Biao Zi frowned as he stood with his team, both to maintain order and to scout for potential candidates, such as those with high Physical Fitness Indexes and mental strength, who could be trained as backup Guardians.
With so many Train Residents, the Guardians also needed to expand. Otherwise, if too many died during a mission, there would be no one to replace them. At the very least, they needed to train a batch of backup Guardians.
"None."
Xiao Ai, like an emotionless robot on an assembly line, continued implanting one Iris Chip after another.
"Due to frequent mining, their overall physical fitness is decent, but compared to the current Train Residents, they still fall short."
