chapters.title: Chapter 178 - 178: "In a state of flow, people can unleash immense potential."
chapters.content:
"You're saying..."
Li Shiji looked thoughtfully at Biao Zi in front of him: "After failing the 'Dragon Fortress' on normal difficulty eight times in a row, you accidentally selected the 'Dragon Fortress' on Extreme Difficulty in a daze, and entered an extremely calm state, almost like a third-person perspective, and managed to clear it?"
"Mm-hmm." Biao Zi nodded seriously. "It's like what you taught me—tricking your brain to unlock your potential."
"I didn't teach you that."
Li Shiji pondered for a while before speaking: "I do know a bit about the state you're describing. Many people call it 'flow.' When you're fully immersed in something, your brain devotes itself entirely to that task."
"In this process, self-awareness diminishes."
"And you lose track of time."
"When flow reaches its peak, it can lead to a detachment of perspective, allowing you to control yourself almost as if in a third-person view. This is common among writers and in competitive fields."
"Like gaming."
"If you played games before the apocalypse, under the right conditions, you might have entered a state akin to 'oneness with the universe.' Your body would instinctively perform precise actions, and you'd feel incredibly confident, as if you could take on ten opponents at once."
"However, this state is extremely difficult to enter and even harder to control manually. It requires the right combination of factors."
"Although you failed eight times in a row, based on your description, you were actually very close to succeeding each time. The issue was that the monsters made noise before dying, which led to you being overwhelmed."
"Monsters in Extreme Difficulty are stronger."
"But for you, they're still killable. The challenge lies in delivering a quick, fatal blow and ensuring the monster doesn't make noise before dying. Also, in Extreme Difficulty, death in 'Dragon Fortress' is permanent."
"When you entered the flow state, you were completely focused, forgetting everything—even the fact that death in Extreme Difficulty is final. You immersed yourself entirely, and that's why you had a chance to clear it."
"In a state of flow, people can unleash immense potential."
"You're quite something."
Li Shiji looked at Biao Zi with a mix of admiration and concern: "If you hadn't entered the flow state back then, or if you had made even a single mistake while in it, I'd probably be attending your funeral right now."
"Speaking of which..."
"The Stellar has hosted weddings, but never a funeral. If you keep playing like this, I think it won't be long before I attend yours."
"My hands are still shaking."
Biao Zi sat nearby, trembling as he lit a cigarette and brought it to his lips: "I almost died. Thankfully, it turned out well. But I think I'll have no problem clearing the normal difficulty 'Dragon Fortress' map later."
"That's true."
Perhaps that wasn't Biao Zi's original intention.
But in the end, the result was this:
All members of Guardian Team One cleared the 'Biohazard' map on Extreme Difficulty, making them the only team on the entire Stellar to achieve this.
In reality, Extreme Difficulty isn't that much harder than normal difficulty.
As long as one can clear the normal difficulty, with a bit more focus and caution, they can conquer the extreme difficulty.
However, extreme difficulty comes with the risk of actual death, which brings immense psychological pressure.
Once this psychological pressure is overcome, clearing maps on extreme difficulty becomes as easy as pie.
The results are excellent.
Of course.
While Biao Zi and the others are now at ease, the second and third squads are starting to feel the heat.
"..."
The Third Squad Leader, who was on patrol, glanced at the message on his Iris Chip, his lips twitching slightly.
"Congratulations to Biao Zi for becoming the first member of the Stellar Train to clear the 'Dragon Fortress' map on extreme difficulty."
"Congratulations to all members of the Guardian First Squad for clearing the 'Biohazard' map on extreme difficulty."
This was the message Director Ai sent to all the guardians and management personnel via their Iris Chips.
It was equivalent to a reward.
It was almost as if he had directly written "Lord Mang is very pleased" on it.
"Is the competition pressure really this intense?"
The Third Squad Leader looked somewhat helplessly at his squad members who were on patrol and alert nearby. His team wasn't ready yet; they had only just cleared the normal difficulty of the 'Biohazard' map.
Even if they were a bit late, it didn't matter. He didn't want his team members to perish in the map.
That would be too unjust.
"It's fine."
"Phew..."
Inside the Wild Bull Train, the man looked at the private message from the Stellar Train and finally breathed a sigh of relief. The other party had finally seen the message he posted on the Train Radio, and this dispute should be settled for now.
He would stop selling cigarettes for the time being.
The other party wouldn't stay in the yellow zone for too long anyway. He would resume selling once the Stellar Train left this area.
He had no intention of heading to the blue zone; he planned to stay in the yellow zone for the rest of his life.
Although going to the blue zone would grant access to higher-level mines, more resources, and rarer parts, what did that have to do with him?
He didn't care about becoming stronger.
As long as he could survive in this apocalypse, staying in the yellow zone and developing peacefully was fine. Hadn't he seen that Level 9 train? Since he entered this zone, that train had been Level 9, and it showed no signs of leaving, as if it intended to retire in the 'Zombie Basin.'
Although not being able to sell cigarettes was a bit of a loss for him.
But it didn't matter; he still had the Cigar Production Line.
The man smiled and typed another line into the Train Radio.
"Temporarily not selling cigarettes. Selling cigars instead. Pre-order if interested, face-to-face delivery at the next gathering."
The next moment—
The Train Radio once again displayed a pinned message from the Stellar Train.
"Stellar Train": "Selling cigars, cigarettes, pork trotter rice, rice noodle rolls, and other daily necessities. Remote transactions available. DM if interested."
"..."
The man silently opened the private chat window with the Stellar Train again.
"Bro, I won't sell cigars either. You can sell them."
"Hmm..."
Chen Mang's expression turned slightly odd as he looked at the message from the 'Wild Bull' in the chat window. Did this guy misunderstand something? He never said only one person could sell and others couldn't.
Wasn't it you who monopolized first, then he stepped in, and you provoked him?
He wasn't planning to monopolize.
Fair competition, right?
As for the 'Train Radio,' he only occasionally tweaked some of the text. The rest was handled by Xiao Ai, who would automatically complete transactions and occasionally pin a message.
This "Cigar Production Line" is a yellow-tier accessory.
Consuming 46,000 units of Iron Ore, it was successfully upgraded to level 10.
And two corresponding Supermodel Effects were obtained.
-
"Cigar Production Line Level 5 Supermodel Effect": Cigar quality is significantly improved.
"Cigar Production Line Level 10 Supermodel Effect": Can refresh and invigorate the mind.
-
His cigars are of better quality than others, so it seems they should be priced higher, just like his cigarettes. The cigarettes produced by his "Cigarette Production Line" also have pain-relieving effects and are sold at a slightly higher price.
But not by much, after all, this is just an additional feature, not the main selling point.
Just like a beautifully designed milk tea packaging bag—it's an extra, and no one would buy a cup of milk tea just for the bag. Well, actually, some people might.
Two days later.
This level 3 Iron Ore Mine has been completely depleted, and the yield was quite good, bringing the Train's current Iron Ore stock to 1.1 million units.
Inside the Train.
Chen Mang glanced at the "Token of Civilization" in his hand. In just over ten days, he would be able to enter the Goblin Tomb space again to mine. Mining there is much more enjoyable than mining outside.
"."
Looking at the 1.1 million units of Iron Ore in the Train, he decided to upgrade some of the basic white and green-tier accessories inside the Train. Meanwhile, Xiao Ai continued to pilot the Train through the night in search of other Mines.
First, the "Resource Detection Radar" was upgraded to level 20.
Its detection range increased to 20,000 meters.
The "Targeting Radar" was also upgraded from level 15 to level 20, with its radar detection range now reaching 20,000 meters.
-
"Resource Detection Radar Level 20 Supermodel Effect": Consumption halved.
"Targeting Radar Level 20 Supermodel Effect": All firepower weapons can lock onto enemies within the radar range via the "Train Auxiliary AI."
-
Halving the consumption of this versatile tool is a good way to save costs.
The Targeting Radar's level 20 Supermodel Effect is quite useful. Upgrading these two accessories consumed a total of 180,000 units of Iron Ore.
In addition, there were others.
The "Moldy Bread Slice Production Line," "Steamed Bun Production Line," "Generator," "Circuit System," "Purified Water Filter," "Clothing Customization Production Line," "Cola Production Line," and "Train Auxiliary AI."
All nine of these accessories were upgraded to level 20, directly granting nine Supermodel Effects.
And it only consumed 188,000 units of Iron Ore. Most of these were white-tier accessories, so the resource consumption was minimal.
-
"Moldy Bread Slice Production Line Level 20 Supermodel Effect": Option to add 'smoked sausage,' price remains unchanged.
"Steamed Bun Production Line Level 20 Supermodel Effect": Option to add 'donkey meat,' price remains unchanged.
"Generator Level 20 Supermodel Effect": None.
"Circuit System Level 20 Supermodel Effect": None.
"Purified Water Filter Level 20 Supermodel Effect": None.
"Clothing Customization Production Line Level 20 Supermodel Effect": Clothes produced will have a small pocket space.
"Cola Production Line Level 20 Supermodel Effect": Long-term consumption can slightly improve physical fitness.
"Train Auxiliary AI": None.
-
Although this round of upgrades didn't consume many resources.
However, most of the life modules on the entire Train received a comprehensive enhancement. Among them, the "Generator" increased its power output with each upgrade, which was more than sufficient for the numerous modules on the Train. Similarly, the "Circuit System" could handle stronger energy flows with each upgrade.
The "Train Auxiliary AI" also saw improvements in its computational power with each upgrade.
As for the "Clothing Customization Production Line"...
Chen Mang walked to Carriage 4 and looked at the clothes produced. No matter how many pockets the garments had, only one pocket possessed an internal spatial effect, and the position of this pocket could be chosen freely.
The space wasn't particularly large.
It could only hold items like a briefcase, a pickaxe, or a Tidal Gatling Gun, which was far less than what the Refrigerator could accommodate.
But...
It was more than enough.
Whether it was storing a mech's briefcase, a Tidal Gatling Gun with Energy Stones, or residents carrying a pickaxe in their pockets, it was highly practical.
After some thought, he spent over 6,000 units of wood to craft two new sets of clothes for everyone on the Train. These would be used for rotation and washing, while the original clothes were kept as backups. If the residents wanted to switch between them, they could do so without any issues.
Afterward, Chen Mang walked through the subsequent carriages, something he rarely did—moving from the front to the rear of the Train to inspect his creation.
First was Carriage 5, the carriage for high-level female talents.
As soon as he pushed the door open, he saw Ji Chuchu and Yan Yao sitting by the window in their strappy nightgowns, chatting while gazing at the scenery outside. When they noticed him entering, they quickly stood up: "Lord Mang."
"Mm."
Chen Mang looked at the two of them.
He swore his original intention was simply to tour his Train and admire the masterpiece he had built in this apocalyptic world. But when Ji Chuchu, in her red strappy nightgown, inadvertently revealed a glimpse of her fair skin...
And Yan Yao, in her form-fitting white silk nightgown, her figure fully on display...
Under the moonlight, they looked utterly captivating.
He glanced at the moonlight outside the window—it was indeed beautiful.
Then he slowly walked over to Yan Yao, pulled her into his arms, and gently inhaled the scent of shampoo lingering in her hair.
He sat down on the chair.
Perhaps Chen Mang had also entered the moment. He forgot about the passage of time, only feeling that the moonlight was beautiful and that the fatigue of the past few days had finally eased.
An hour later.
Chen Mang stood up and looked at Ji Chuchu and Yan Yao, who were kneeling side by side on the bed. He smiled and gave each of them a light pat.
Casually picking up a bottle of Mineral Water by the window, he drank half of it.
Then he sat by the window, lit a cigarette, and lazily tilted his head to gaze outside.
Ji Chuchu climbed out of bed, picked up the half-empty bottle of Mineral Water, and took a sip.
Ten minutes later.
Chen Mang extinguished his cigarette in the water bottle, feeling refreshed, and continued on to Carriage 6, the carriage for high-level male talents.
Pushing the door open, he found Li Shiji and others still awake. They quickly got up: "Lord Mang."
"Mm."
Chen Mang casually waved his hand. "Go back to sleep."
The moonlight in this carriage wasn't particularly noteworthy, so there wasn't much to inspect.
He continued on to Carriage 7, the Guard car.
The second team of Guardians was already asleep, while the first team was patrolling the rear carriages to maintain order. The third team was training in the "Combat Training Space" inside the Refrigerator. He didn't disturb anyone.
After taking another stroll through the four Resident cars at the back, Chen Mang retraced his steps once more.
When he returned to Car No. 5 again,
Ji Chuchu and Yan Yao were whispering to each other, their faces slightly flushed. Whether it was the moonlight or the silk nightgowns they were wearing, Chen Mang couldn't help but feel that Ji Chuchu and Yan Yao were particularly alluring tonight.
Especially beautiful.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 179 - 179: "Your Train Has Been Upgraded to Level 7."
chapters.content:
"..."
Chen Mang walked over under the gazes of the two, reached out to lift Ji Chuchu's chin, and softly said, "You are quite beautiful."
"Such beauty is truly remarkable."
"..."
Under the moonlight.
Raising a cup to invite the moon, their shadows formed a trio.
An hour later.
Chen Mang returned to the train compartment, leaned back in his chair, let out a long sigh, propped his feet on the table, and lazily lit a cigarette, gazing absentmindedly at the starry sky through the skylight.
As the Train Conductor.
He couldn't stay in the train compartment all the time; he had to visit the grassroots level occasionally.
This inspection of his train gave him a clearer understanding of it. Although he could see the three-dimensional model of the train on the control screen, it wasn't as intuitive as seeing it directly.
He looked at the conditions for upgrading the train to Level 7.
-
「Upgrade Conditions」: All 3 essential vehicle components must be crafted, consume 50,000 units of Level 2 Iron Ore, all accessory levels in the train must exceed Level 140, and clear a Fortuitous Encounter map.
-
These conditions had already been fully met.
The train still had 732,000 units of Iron Ore, which was more than enough for the upgrade. The conditions were immediately satisfied.
Without waiting any longer.
He directly chose to upgrade.
After consuming 500,000 units of Iron Ore.
The next moment—
A panel appeared on the control screen.
-
「Your Train Has Been Upgraded to Level 7.」
「More Craftable Components Will Be Unlocked.」
-
As long as the train met the upgrade conditions, he would usually upgrade it immediately without waiting. Others would wait because they were worried about the train's level being inflated, wasting resources, since upgrading the train required consuming 500,000 units of Iron Ore.
After the upgrade, the train basically didn't improve at all.
But those 500,000 units of Iron Ore invested in any component would result in a solid improvement. Therefore, many trains would choose to prioritize upgrading components, and only upgrade the train level after the components were almost fully upgraded.
He didn't have this concern.
His foundation was extremely solid, and his speed of acquiring Iron Ore far surpassed others. This depended on many factors, such as his train being fast enough, his Resource Detection Radar having a wide enough range, his residents being numerous, and him having many Fortuitous Encounters to obtain Iron Ore, like the Goblin Tomb.
Most importantly, his strength was sufficient.
The Iron Ore he occupied was not dared to be taken by anyone. Even if a Corpse Tide came, he didn't need to run; he could just slaughter the Corpse Tide directly, unlike others who had to flee when they saw a Corpse Tide while mining.
All these factors led to his train being unstoppable among those of the same level.
He didn't need to waste resources on "transitional components."
Of course.
There were also gamblers, like the Level 7 train he destroyed in the "Geocentric Nuclear Bomb" Fortuitous Encounter map. Because they didn't want to waste resources on transitional components, even though the train was Level 7, the defensive component "Energy Shield" was only Level 5.
Pure gamblers.
Such trains basically had no combat power and would be immediately destroyed at the slightest crisis. Therefore, he was surprised that this train dared to attack him in the Fortuitous Encounter map.
Not everyone had the means to detect other trains' components; this was the Level 10 Supermodel Effect of the "Targeting Radar."
This led many people to not realize that they were actually hitting a rock with an egg.
Chen Mang looked at the control panel and let out a helpless sigh. "No way."
When the train reached level 6, a "?" button appeared on the control panel. Now that the train had reached level 7, the "?" button remained unchanged, as if it were permanently fixed.
Normally, after the train reached level 6, the additional button should have been "Squad Voice," not a "?" But it didn't matter much to him. He wasn't lacking the Squad Voice function, and even if it were missing, it wouldn't be a big deal. He refused to believe that the button would remain a question mark forever.
After the train reached level 7, no new functions or buttons were added.
These days, he had been paying attention to the messages exchanged by other trains on the "Train Radio."
The reason he responded to the Wild Bull was entirely because that train kept sending pleas for mercy in the group chat all day long, severely affecting his efficiency in gathering information. He wanted to see what other trains were discussing, but all he found were the Wild Bull's incessant, neurotic apologies and pleas for forgiveness.
He was forced to reply just to stop the Wild Bull from spamming the chat.
It was like dealing with a lunatic—someone who would keep spamming unless he responded.
After the train reached levels 7, 8, and 9, no new functions or buttons were added.
Level 10 was a major hurdle.
Once the train reached level 10, there would be earth-shattering changes.
That's what the Train Radio said.
As for what those changes would be, he didn't know. All he knew was that several level 9 trains in the Zombie Basin hadn't ventured into the blue zone to upgrade to level 10, and this was the reason.
"..."
Chen Mang didn't dwell on it too much. Instead, he turned his attention to the new craftable parts that appeared after the train reached level 7.
This time, there was even fewer—only one part.
-
"Space Stillness": A purple-tier part. Requires 10,000 units of Iron Ore to craft.
-
This was the first purple-tier part he had ever seen. Purple-tier parts could be upgraded up to level 10, meaning anyone who crafted this part could gain two Supermodel Effects.
However, he wasn't entirely sure what this part was for.
At level 1.
Activating this part would freeze all living beings and AI inside the train, except for him, for 30 minutes.
Time itself wasn't frozen; it continued to flow.
But everyone's thoughts would be suspended at that moment, and their bodies would remain motionless, completely maintaining the state they were in before "Space Stillness" was activated. After the effect wore off, they would have no memory of the elapsed time, only feeling as if 30 minutes had suddenly jumped forward.
"..."
Chen Mang furrowed his brow slightly as he sat in his chair, pondering the effect of this part. It couldn't be a useless part—this was a must-craft part for the "Train," so it couldn't be without purpose.
So far, every must-craft part for the train had proven useful in some way.
But...
Even the AI would be frozen during this period, while time outside continued to flow. It was as if it gave the Train Conductor 30 minutes of uninterrupted thinking time?
And it was a purple-tier part.
The only use he could imagine for this part was for an A-tier Mechanical Train. It could instantly freeze the thoughts of everyone, including the AI, and during that time, the "Train Auxiliary AI" part could be dismantled and recrafted.
Breaking free from the relationship with the AI.
It was like forcing a divorce.
At other times, if one wanted to force a divorce, it was easy to end up in a tragic love-suicide with their AI.
But for other trains, this component seemed completely useless. If the goal was to enhance control over the train, the regulations and the "Internal Fire Control System" were already more than sufficient.
He shook his head and didn't dwell on it further.
Instead, he got up and headed toward the "Combat Training Virtual Space." When the time came to use it, he would naturally know how. For now, he wanted to practice more in the "Biohazard" map.
He had already cleared the Biohazard map on normal difficulty five times.
He was familiar with all the key points, and his route was fairly standard—the same points Biao Zi had initially figured out.
He planned to clear it a few more times before attempting the Biohazard map on Extreme Difficulty. If the entire Guardian team could pass it, there was no reason he couldn't. But just to be safe, he wanted to familiarize himself with the route a bit more.
After all,
though he hadn't been in action for a long time, when he first established himself in this world, it wasn't through mere talk.
Surely, no one really thought of him as a powerless Train Conductor, did they?
"Lord Mang is so fierce," Ji Chuchu murmured, lying sideways on the bed, exhausted. She tucked the blanket between her legs and couldn't help but laugh as she watched Yan Yao across the room, busy folding the bedsheet. "You're so old-fashioned. I've only ever seen girls in movies collect bedsheets stained with their first blood."
Yan Yao didn't respond, only bit her red lip lightly as she continued her task.
"You remind me of a friend I used to have. She was an escort."
"Once, she found a sugar daddy and wanted to secure him, so she used her period blood to fake her virginity. But she was caught on the spot and got slapped a few times."
"When she told me about it, I almost died laughing."
"But in the end, whether it was because of superstition or something else, that sugar daddy's career actually started to decline."
Ji Chuchu didn't seem to mind that Yan Yao wasn't responding. She just kept talking to herself, her expression distant, as if lost in thought.
Before she knew it,
she had fallen asleep.
Leaving Yan Yao alone, sitting on the edge of the bed, her head tilted as she gazed out the window, lost in her own thoughts.
Dawn broke.
The train had stopped beside a Level 3 Iron Ore deposit, ready to continue its mining journey for the day.
"Is this really necessary?" Chen Mang glanced at Xiao Ai standing beside him, his tone annoyed. "Such a trivial matter, and you had to announce it to everyone?"
Earlier that morning, when he went out for a stroll, he noticed that all the Guardians were treating him with even more respect than usual, their admiration practically overflowing. At first, he didn't know what had happened, but after asking around, he found out.
Xiao Ai had sent out an announcement to all the Guardians and management through their Iris Chips that morning.
-
"Lord Mang has successfully cleared the Biohazard map on Extreme Difficulty."
-
"Train Conductor,"
Xiao Ai's mechanical voice echoed from the corner of the train compartment. "This is the instruction you set. Whenever a member of the train crew performs a commendable act, it must be announced to the entire train as an encouragement."
"As the Train Conductor, you took the risk to clear the Biohazard map on Extreme Difficulty."
"This is a completely commendable act."
"Train Conductor, why don't you reset the settings so that announcements about you aren't necessary in the future?"
"Hmm."
Chen Mang paused for a moment before clearing his throat lightly. "Well, that's not really necessary. Although it's just a small matter, I didn't pay much attention to it. But since it's been mentioned, let it be. It boosts everyone's morale."
Last night, after passing the "Biohazard" map twice on normal difficulty, he dove straight into the Extreme Difficulty. It went well; he managed to clear it without resorting to any brain-tricking methods. He was just cautious enough to minimize injuries, maintaining his position through spatial manipulation.
He had tried these spots many times in several normal difficulty runs.
Apart from the increased psychological pressure, there wasn't much difficulty.
The psychological pressure was much greater than when he first arrived in this world. Back then, he had nothing and was willing to fight recklessly, ready to die if necessary. But now, he was the conductor of a Level 7 train. The negligible boost to his Physical Fitness Index didn't enhance him at all, and he didn't need to enter the map.
But—
He always felt that whether it was the Train Conductor or the Guardians, they had to keep that fighting spirit alive.
When the Train Conductor becomes timid and avoids facing crises, the development speed of the train would inevitably slow down.
However, this was only limited to the "Biohazard" map. He had no plans to tackle the Extreme Difficulty of Dragon Fortress anytime soon. After watching Biao Zi's entire run, it was clear that it was like walking on a knife's edge, with several near-death experiences—it was just too dangerous.
"Achoo!"
In Guard Car No. 7, Biao Zi sneezed, rubbed his nose, and muttered, "Am I getting sick, or is someone thinking about me?"
Then he downed the cup of dark liquid in his hand in one gulp.
This was his newly concocted drink, which he named "Man's Drink."
He mixed cola with mineral water, then brewed tea, and finally ended up with this drink.
It was a last resort.
Long-term consumption of mineral water could increase Physical Fitness Index.
Long-term consumption of tea could increase Mental Strength.
Long-term consumption of cola could increase Physical Fitness Index.
Since everyone's daily water intake was limited, how could he possibly drink so much water every day? So, the solution he found was to mix all these things together and gulp it down in one go.
Although the taste was a bit strange.
But... the effect was great.
Speaking of which, he was truly envious of Zhang Yi and Zhang Er. Long-term consumption of "steamed buns" could also increase Physical Fitness Index, but a person's stomach capacity was limited. Even if they ate themselves to death, how many could they consume in a day?
And those two guys, Zhang Yi and Zhang Er, were almost always seen eating steamed buns whenever he saw them.
At this rate, the Physical Fitness Index they gained from "dietary supplements" would far surpass everyone else, leaving them far ahead.
There was one phrase he had always disliked.
"To those who have, more will be given, and they will have an abundance. From those who have not, even what they have will be taken away."
But what was infuriating was that this was the way the world worked.
Even Zhang Da Mei had a big appetite, but her two brothers' appetites were much larger than hers.
In the train compartment of the Stellar, Chen Mang leaned back in his chair, pondering the purpose of the newly crafted purple accessory. Perhaps it was meant for someone like the Black Market Merchant—lure them onto the train, immobilize them, and then start looting.
Alternatively, it could directly initiate a 30-minute fixed-point concentrated fire using the "Internal Fire Control System."
Moreover, this component refers to all living beings inside the Train, not necessarily the Train Crew. Therefore, it is most likely not intended for use on the Train Crew, but rather for something that might infiltrate the Train in the future.

chapters.title: Chapter 180 - 180: "Fools Outsmart Masters."
chapters.content:
Chen Mang raised an eyebrow slightly, feeling that he had already figured out the correct way to use this accessory. He truly was a genius.
Just then—
Xiao Ai's voice came from beside him: "Train Conductor, it seems the residents have dug up something strange while mining. Would you like to take a look?"
"Let's go."
Chen Mang replied without hesitation. He immediately put on the Individual Exoskeleton Armor under his sweater and walked out of the train compartment, heading toward the iron ore mine next to the train.
By now, the train guards had already cordoned off a specific area.
The other residents were still working.
Only that one spot, like Lao Zhu's former Mediterranean hairstyle, was left empty.
"Lord Mang."
The guards stood straight, their expressions respectful as they looked at Chen Mang and spoke in a deep voice.
Chen Mang walked into the crowd and saw a bronze door lying flat on the ground. On the door was an electronic lock.
The combination of the electronic lock and the bronze door looked extremely incongruous.
"Lord Mang."
Zhang Da Mei stepped forward to report: "One of the residents dug this up while mining. It seems like there's an air wall around this door. The pickaxe didn't have any effect when it struck."
Chen Mang leaned on his cane and remotely activated the Resource Detection Radar and Targeting Radar inside the train. They didn't detect anything beneath the bronze door. It was exactly the same as the ordinary ground—no red dots, nothing special.
He took the pickaxe from a guard nearby, walked to the side of the bronze door, and swung the pickaxe at the ground.
Clang.
It was as if he had struck metal. No dirt flew into the air. Although his eyes clearly saw the pickaxe hitting the soil, the sensation upon impact was completely different from striking dirt.
His arm tingled slightly.
He returned the pickaxe to the guard and crouched down, examining the bronze door, whose surface had already been cleaned. Experience told him that this was a fortuitous encounter map, similar to the one he had encountered in the Kunlun Mountains region, which was exclusive to the Flesh Train.
But...
He frowned slightly and looked at the "password lock" on the bronze door.
There were 10 digits, from 0 to 9.
Next to the password lock was a "Confirm to Open" button. Clearly, only by entering the correct password could the bronze door be opened. But what the password was, no one knew. There were no hints around.
"..."
After pondering for a while, Chen Mang said: "Zhang Da Mei, have all the residents stop mining and return to the train."
"Yes."
Today was the first day of mining for the 1,900 new survivors who had just joined the train. These people had already fully understood the train's promotion mechanism and were ready to work hard to improve their status and earn the right to obtain Stellar Coupons. However, they had barely started mining when they were abruptly called to stop.
Chen Mang controlled the train to drill into the ground, heading toward the area beneath the bronze door.
Sure enough.
Upon reaching the area below the bronze door, the drill bit seemed to hit an air wall. Although the front displayed what appeared to be ordinary soil, the Level 50 drill bit sparked without leaving even a trace of damage.
After circling around, he found that this fortuitous encounter, wrapped in an air wall, wasn't very large—about the size of four refrigerators.
Not the internal space.
It was about the size of four refrigerators stacked together, roughly the size of a burial pit. If this was a map of a fortuitous encounter, then it was the smallest one he had ever encountered. Forget about the Train not being able to drive in, even people could only fit two or three inside.
And that was if they went in sideways.
Since taking a shortcut wasn't an option, the only way left was to crack the password.
"Lao Zhu, from those 1,900 survivors, find someone brave enough to input the password I gave you. Whether it opens or not, they'll immediately be granted Level 1 resident privileges."
Chen Mang parked the Train about a kilometer away from the bronze door before giving the order.
He had a hunch in his heart.
With no password hints, the coordinates of the bronze door might be the password.
After all, there were no other numerical clues, and the bronze door had no patterns or anything that seemed like a decryption mechanism.
Having more people was indeed helpful.
Out of 1,900 people, there was bound to be someone fearless.
Soon, a burly man jumped off the Train, a Mechanical Eye pinned to his chest, and strode toward the bronze door a kilometer away.
Chen Mang, meanwhile, sat in the Train's control room, watching the first-person perspective of the burly man on the screen.
The moment the coordinates were input and the confirm button was pressed.
The burly man turned and ran without hesitation, but... there was no explosion, no movement at all. Only after receiving the command did he muster the courage to approach the bronze door again.
A line of text appeared on the bronze door.
「Incorrect password. Two attempts remaining.」
"..."
"Meeting!"
Chen Mang furrowed his brows and immediately called Li Shiji, Lao Zhu, Biao Zi, and others into the Train's control room to discuss cracking the password. Although he didn't know what lay beneath, it was undoubtedly an opportunity. Since he had seen it, it was his.
Missing it would be a great pity.
Once everyone had gathered.
Chen Mang scanned each face in the room, the screen displaying a detailed image of the bronze door: "This bronze door has two password attempts left. Share your thoughts directly."
His gaze lingered on Li Shiji for an extra second.
He had high hopes for Li Shiji. Perhaps Li Shiji could figure something out.
Feeling Lord Mang's intense gaze, Li Shiji's back gradually broke into a cold sweat. His eyes were fixed on the bronze door on the screen, but the more he looked, the more clueless he became.
Think faster, think faster!
He was just a game designer, passionate about mazes and with a better sense of space than most, but that was it.
He wasn't God.
How could he possibly look at a completely clue-less password lock and immediately guess the password?
The biggest problem was that he didn't even know how many digits the password was. Even if it were six digits, there were a million possible combinations.
And without knowing the number of digits, it was like searching for a needle in a haystack.
Just then—
Li Shiji's eyes suddenly lit up: "Maybe it's the coordinates of the bronze door?"
"Already tried."
Chen Mang shook his head: "The first attempt was with the coordinates. It didn't work."
The light in Li Shiji's eyes dimmed, and he began to fidget nervously, staring intently at the bronze door on the screen.
"I think..."
Biao Zi hesitated for a moment before sharing his thoughts: "Take a look at this bronze door. It likely represents history, while the combination lock represents modern technology. These two are clearly polar opposites."
"And since the combination lock is placed above the bronze door, could the password be the two-digit number '09'?"
"Just like the two extremes."
"That makes sense." Lao Zhu glanced at Biao Zi with a hint of surprise before offering his own speculation.
"Lord Mang, I think Biao Zi's theory has some merit. From my perspective, there are no clues on the bronze door itself. The only clue lies right in the center of the Level 3 Iron Ore deposit."
"The regional tiers, from low to high, are white, green, and yellow."
"The 'Zombie Basin' happens to be a yellow zone, which corresponds to the number 3."
"And it's located in the middle of the Level 3 Iron Ore deposit."
"So the password might be '3' or '33'."
"..."
Chen Mang pondered for a while, finding both arguments reasonable. Finally, he turned his gaze to Xiao Ai, who was sitting in the corner. "What do you think?"
Xiao Ai's voice echoed through the train compartment.
"Both Lao Zhu and Biao Zi make good points, but I might offer a different perspective. This Level 3 Iron Ore deposit isn't freshly spawned; it has been respawned several times."
"That means during the previous respawns of this Level 3 Iron Ore deposit, many trains have already mined it, and they must have discovered this bronze door as well."
"They must have tried to open it too."
"But so far..."
"Not a single train has shared this information over the Train Radio. Setting aside the possibility that they simply didn't want to share, there's only one other explanation: entering the wrong password three times in a row might trigger something terrible."
"It could even lead to the destruction of the entire train."
"Of course, this is a rather pessimistic assumption. My guess is that the password might be the specific year and month when this apocalypse began."
"..."
After listening to everyone's opinions, Chen Mang remained silent for a long time before picking up the walkie-talkie. "Enter the password 33."
From the first-person perspective.
It was clear that the burly man's hand was trembling slightly, but he carefully pressed the number 3 twice before hitting the "Confirm to Open" button.
Soon.
Another line of text appeared on the bronze door.
-
"Password incorrect. 1 attempt remaining."
-
The password 33 was also wrong.
Chen Mang didn't speak, only furrowing his brows as he stared intently at the image of the bronze door on the screen. After a long while, he finally spoke again. "Don't enter any password. Just press the 'Confirm to Open' button directly."
On the other side of the screen.
It was obvious that the burly man was now shaking like a leaf, but he forced himself to stay calm and pressed the "Confirm to Open" button directly.
In the next moment—
A faint white light suddenly emanated from the bronze door, and the indicator light on the combination lock turned green. The bronze door slowly began to open.
The password was correct. It had opened.
Chen Mang laughed, immediately steering the train toward the bronze door. He had gambled correctly. Without any clues or hints, it was impossible for anyone to guess the password.
Since it was impossible for anyone to guess the password, the appearance of this bronze door would have been meaningless.
He had always believed one thing.
That is, everything that has appeared after the apocalypse in this world cannot be meaningless. It's impossible for an unopenable bronze door to exist in this world, so there's only one answer.
The purpose of the password lock is solely to mislead.
To open this bronze door is simple—just press the "Confirm Open" button.
"Huh?"
"Huh?"
"Huh?"
The moment the bronze door opened, several voices of disbelief echoed in the train compartment, including Xiao Ai's mechanical electronic voice. They never expected that the password for this bronze door was actually no password at all?
What were they guessing for so long just now?
"Fools outsmart the masters," Biao Zi said with a complicated expression. "If we had sent Zhang Er over, he wouldn't even need three chances. He would have opened it in one try. Who the hell would have thought that you don't need to input any password, just press 'Confirm Open,' and it would actually open?"
"Ahem."
Lao Zhu cleared his throat before reminding, "Uh, I'd like to remind you that it was Lord Mang who opened the password lock."
Only then did Biao Zi realize his mistake, and his expression changed as he hurriedly explained, "Lord Mang, that's not what I meant. What I meant was—"
Li Shiji took over, his face filled with admiration.
"The first realm: seeing a mountain as a mountain, seeing water as water."
"The second realm: seeing a mountain not as a mountain, seeing water not as water."
"The third realm: seeing a mountain still as a mountain, seeing water still as water."
"Although both are seeing a mountain as a mountain and water as water, Zhang Er is in the first realm, while Lord Mang, you are in the third realm!"
"Lord Mang, impressive!"
"Exactly!" Biao Zi let out a long sigh of relief and quickly added, "That's what I meant, Lord Mang."
Chen Mang didn't pay much attention to the minor incident. He simply parked the train next to the iron ore, jumped off, and strode toward the bronze door. As he passed by the burly man, he smiled with satisfaction.
"Not bad, Lao Zhu. You're in charge of handling his promotion in treatment."
"No problem."
Lao Zhu quickly nodded, then waved his hand to signal the burly man to return to the carriage. He remembered this man.
His resident number was probably 1998, one of the 1,900 survivors. He used to be a leader in funeral services, a tough guy. Back then, to demonstrate his ruthlessness, he smashed his head against a steel table, leaving himself bloodied.
Now, it seemed he really was tough.
He had already risen to first-class resident treatment, the fastest promotion among the 1,900 survivors.
Then Chen Mang looked down below the bronze door.
The interior space wasn't large, roughly the size of a tomb, and it wasn't filled with any explosives. This meant that even if you entered the wrong password three times in a row, it probably wouldn't explode.
At most, you'd lose the chance to try again, and the train wouldn't be allowed to make further attempts.
As for why no one mentioned it on the train radio.
It was simply because opportunities like this were never discussed on the train radio. Even if you couldn't get it yourself, you wouldn't talk about it. What if someone else got it?
Not getting it yourself is disappointing.
But seeing someone else get it is even more disappointing.
Inside, two items lay flat.
A blueprint and a voucher.
"Lord Mang, I'll go." Biao Zi, who was standing nearby, immediately jumped into the deep pit. He stuffed the two items into his chest, then took a running start and scaled the wall in three steps, climbing out of the burial pit.
The entire process was incredibly smooth.
And those three steps up the wall were executed with remarkable fluidity.
"..."
Seeing this, Lao Zhu curled his lips. The pit was over two meters deep, and if he had jumped in, it would have been quite difficult to get out. Biao Zi had once again shown off his skills. When he had some free time, Lao Zhu decided he would also go to the Combat Training Virtual Space to practice.
Although he was in a clerical position, there was no harm in improving his physical fitness.
"Lord Mang, here you go."
Biao Zi climbed out of the burial pit with ease and handed the two items from his pocket to Lord Mang.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 181 - 181: You Have Been Locked by Stellar's Level 8 Missile. Please Prepare to Die!
chapters.content:
"..."
Chen Mang looked at the two items Biao Zi handed him. The tomb chamber was now completely empty, and about thirty seconds after the items were taken, the bronze door began to slowly close.
It didn't disappear.
He tentatively entered a random string of numbers.
The screen displayed another line of text.
-
「Incorrect password. 2 attempts remaining.」
-
After pressing the "Confirm to Open" button again, the bronze door slowly reopened. This meant the space wouldn't disappear. He had already tested it—this space was extremely sturdy.
If he were ever stranded alone in the wilderness, surrounded by a Corpse Tide with no way to escape, he could hide inside, wait for a minute, and the bronze door would automatically close. Inside, it was absolutely safe. Barring any unforeseen circumstances, it could withstand a Level 8 missile without issue.
Of course, the bronze door couldn't be opened from the inside. Without food or an Oxygen Generator, it would be equivalent to burying himself alive.
But if someone outside could assist in opening the bronze door, he could come out again.
It was like a little Easter egg.
The items inside were gone and wouldn't regenerate. Even if someone opened the bronze door later, it would be useless.
Then he turned his attention to the two items in his hand.
They were—
A blue-grade Mecha Blueprint, "Thunder," and a Level 4 Crimson Heartstone refresh voucher.
"Not bad."
Chen Mang smiled as he looked at the items in his hand. This was a great Fortuitous Encounter. He liked this kind of opportunity—the more, the better.
So far, Stellar only had two mechas.
A yellow-grade mecha, "Leech," specializing in long-range fire support.
A green-grade mecha, "Executioner," specializing in close combat.
Now, there was a higher-level blue-grade mecha, "Thunder," with impressive stats and a more brutal design—a pure close-combat mecha.
-
「Thunder.」
「Brutal close-combat mecha.」
「All long-range firepower configurations removed, maximizing the mecha's close-combat capabilities.」
「External Armor and built-in Thunder Hammer are Level 7. Maximum speed reaches 280 km/h. Embedded with a Level 4 Energy Stone, it can fight at full capacity for 100 hours. Detailed mecha attributes as follows.」
「The Thunder Hammer can be thrown to deliver devastating blows to distant enemies.」
「Requires the operator's Physical Fitness Index to be above 19.0. At 19.5 or higher, it can unleash its full power.」
「No Mental Strength requirement.」
「Construction cost: 280,000 units of Crimson Heartstone.」
-
Level 7 defensive Armor, Level 7 Thunder Hammer!
These were incredibly exaggerated stats!
The numbers alone felt insufficient.
To put it plainly, during the "Geocentric Nuclear Bomb" Fortuitous Encounter map, when those Level 8 Trains attacked Stellar, Zhang Yi, with this mecha, could almost single-handedly take on four Trains!
Almost, of course.
After all, it was Level 7, not Level 8, but it was still extremely impressive.
Because "Mechas" weren't the Trains' primary means of attack. They were more like extensions, similar to tentacles, used to extend the Trains' attack range—just one of their attack methods.
Zhang Yi, piloting this mecha, could single-handedly take on all the Trains in the "Shahe Plain" without any issues.
This is the significance of advanced regions.
They offer higher-level resources, more fortuitous encounters, and stronger components.
Even if you spent a lifetime mining in the Shahe Plain, you would never come across a blue-tier mecha blueprint.
Chen Mang laughed, and he laughed heartily. Although the crafting cost was steep—a "Thunder" mecha required a whopping 280,000 units of Crimson Heartstone, and the train currently didn't have that much—it came with a "Level 4 Crimson Heartstone Refresh Voucher."
This item had only one effect.
It allowed the creation of a Level 4 Crimson Heartstone mine anywhere.
This was the second time he had obtained a similar item. The first time was in the Iron Ridge Wasteland, where he got a Level 2 Copper Mine Refresh Voucher.
What a win!
Chen Mang was overjoyed.
But he didn't notice that Biao Zi beside him was almost on the verge of tears. To pilot this mecha, one needed a Physical Fitness Index of over 19.0. The mecha was practically reserved, with only Zhang Yi and Zhang Er's names left to be engraved on it.
He had been working so hard these days, eating supplements and training like crazy.
Yet his Physical Fitness Index had only just reached 15.5, still a long way from 19.0. This mecha had nothing to do with him for the time being.
He had tried his best.
When he first emerged from the Tower of Heaven fortuitous encounter map in the Shahe Plain, his Physical Fitness Index was only 12.1. In such a short time, he had already reached 15.5.
"Phew."
Biao Zi took a deep breath, suppressing the jealousy in his heart. He still had three normal difficulty Dragon Fortress and two extreme difficulty Dragon Fortress map rewards to claim.
Keep pushing!
One day, he too would pilot this blue-tier "Thunder" mecha!
After this little episode, the train resumed mining, but now, beside the Level 3 Iron Ore mine, there was also a Level 4 Crimson Heartstone mine.
According to the Resource Detection Radar, once this Level 4 Crimson Heartstone mine was fully exploited, it would yield approximately 5 million units of Crimson Heartstone, enough to craft 17 "Thunder" mechas.
For Crimson Heartstone, this Level 4 mine had an exceptionally high yield.
Generally, rare resource mines don't yield much.
For example, the Level 3 Crimson Heartstone mine encountered in the Iron Ridge Wasteland only yielded 180,000 units after being fully exploited.
Finally, they could start mining again.
All the residents were highly motivated. The sight of over 3,000 people swinging their pickaxes was incredibly spectacular. This was likely the train with the most survivors in the entire Zombie Basin.
The main reason was that he didn't have to worry about being unable to support them.
While other trains followed a cycle of mining, fleeing, mining, fleeing.
His process was mining, mining, mining, Corpse Tide arrives, defeat the Corpse Tide, and continue mining.
There was hardly ever a situation where they couldn't mine for too long and risked being consumed by poverty.
Each resident wore orange clothing. From a distance or a high vantage point, although it was the apocalypse, with no trace of modernity in the surroundings and the air filled with desolation and silence, these residents and the train parked beside them.
They gave off a vibrant sense of life.
Like saplings sprouting from the soil after a wildfire.
A glimmer of hope amidst the disaster.
Soon—
On the Train Panel, the quantity of "Crimson Heartstone" reached 300,000 units. Chen Mang immediately spent 280,000 units of Crimson Heartstone to craft the first "Thunder" mecha for the Stellar. It was still noon, and the residents hadn't finished their work.
However, eager to see the Thunder mecha as soon as possible, he instructed his subordinates to deliver the Crimson Heartstone as soon as they mined it.
He then turned his gaze out the window, where Zhang Yi was familiarizing himself with the Thunder mecha. Leaning back in his chair, Chen Mang smiled with satisfaction.
Level 7 armor, Level 7 Thunder Warhammer.
It could be further upgraded at the "Mecha Research and Development Center," directly boosting the armor to Level 8.
This was the foundation of his Stellar.
Anyone who stepped out of it would possess the strength to single-handedly take on a Level 8 Train.
The Thunder mecha.
A close-combat mecha designed for brute force.
Standing 8 meters tall.
It was the tallest mecha on the Stellar, and in its deactivated state, it was the size of a briefcase.
The mecha's armor was entirely jet black, with a deep blue lightning bolt running from its head to its abdomen, resembling a thunderstruck tree. Just standing there, it exuded an overwhelmingly terrifying aura.
At this moment, Zhang Yi, seated in the cockpit, was learning and mastering the operation of this mecha.
"Buzz..."
The Thunder mecha leaped into the air, and several nozzles on its back and palms simultaneously emitted blue flames. Then, two steel wings suddenly unfolded from its back, each embedded with four tail thrusters beneath them.
With the eight tail thrusters beneath the steel wings, the mecha had a total of fourteen thrusters.
The mecha flew at an incredible speed through the air, disappearing over the mountain in the blink of an eye.
"It can fly! It can fly! This damn mecha can actually fly!!!"
Standing beside the Train, Biao Zi watched the scene unfold, feeling as if his heart was being squeezed and he couldn't breathe. Staring at the Thunder mecha disappearing over the mountain, his eyes reddened, almost on the verge of tears.
Damn it all!
This mecha could fly!
Flight has always been one of humanity's greatest dreams. Although the Train could also fly, sitting inside it was completely different from piloting a mecha soaring through the sky!
He couldn't even imagine how ecstatic he would be if he were the one piloting this mecha!
Even in the Extreme Difficulty of "Dragon Fortress," he had never felt as painfully breathless as he did now!
Meanwhile, Zhang Yi, piloting the Thunder mecha high in the sky, was filled with excitement and awe as he experimented with various tactical maneuvers.
He selectively ignored the flashing messages on his Iris Chip.
"Warning, warning, you are about to leave the Stellar's communication range."
"Warning, warning, please turn back immediately."
"Warning, warning... Damn it, if you keep flying, I won't be able to reach you anymore! What the hell are you doing? Trying to defect?!"
"If you don't come back now, I'll hit you with a Level 8 missile, you hear me?"
The next moment—
A line of crimson text flashed across the Iris Chip.
"You have been locked onto by the Stellar's Level 8 missile. Please prepare to die, please prepare to die!"
Finally snapping back to reality, Zhang Yi, hearing the familiar voice of Director Ai through the cockpit's sound system, hurriedly apologized before turning the mecha around and heading back toward the green dot on the map representing the Stellar.
Wait, wasn't Director Ai supposed to be an AI?
Since when did it learn to curse?
"Phew..."
Inside the "Armor Research Center" of Carriage No. 2, Xiao Ai sat on the ground, puffing out his cheeks as he took deep breaths to calm his emotions. He wasn't sure if it was because the Train Conductor had leveled him up to 20, but he found that he could now sense human emotions—especially anger.
In the past, he had emotions too, but they were composed of strings of code, a stiff imitation of human behavior. Now, however, he naturally experienced human anger. No wonder human civilization had curses. In many situations, curses were truly irreplaceable. Repeated warnings were far less effective and direct than a single "f*** you," which carried a much stronger sense of warning.
He could only contact the Train Crew through the Iris Chip within the range of the Targeting Radar. Beyond that range, he couldn't reach them. It wasn't so much that he was worried about Zhang Yi defecting, but rather that he might get lost and not find his way back. If this happened to someone else, it might be hard to say, but with Zhang Yi, it was practically a 100% probability.
As for the warning about being locked onto by an 8th-level missile and being told to prepare for death—that was just a bluff. Without Lord Mang's orders, he didn't have the authority to manufacture an 8th-level missile, let alone lock onto the "Thunder" mech and fire it. But even if he couldn't do it, he could still scare people.
"Pissed off!" Xiao Ai took a deep breath. He had installed a small blower in his throat to simulate the sound of deep breathing, making him seem more human. Then he continued sitting on the ground, focusing on his experiments.
At the same time, he was also responsible for monitoring the Iris Chips of all residents, the detection of the Targeting Radar, the transactions on the Train Radio, the operations of the Resident Store, and a series of other tasks. After leveling up, his computational power had increased, allowing him to multitask more efficiently.
He was currently brainstorming how to create a custom-made amplifier that could accurately express his emotions. Otherwise, his robotic body always spoke in a cold, mechanical voice, completely failing to convey his feelings. Perhaps, like all infants, the moment he realized he seemed to possess human emotions, he desperately wanted others to perceive them—whether it was joy, sorrow, or, most importantly, anger!
Meanwhile, Zhang Yi, piloting the "Thunder" mech, flew back to the Stellar and landed on a carriage with Level 3 Armor that Lord Mang had specially built for testing. Raising the Thunder Warhammer with both hands, he roared and slammed the hammer into the carriage.
"Boom!" The deafening sound of impact echoed as the section of the carriage with Level 3 Armor was flattened by the blow.
Getting into the rhythm, Zhang Yi swung the massive hammer repeatedly. In just a few strikes, the carriage was reduced to a flat sheet of metal, neatly compressed.
Then, with another roar, he hurled the Thunder Warhammer into the distance, smashing it into a boulder a hundred meters away, instantly shattering it. The hammer was quickly reeled back into the mech's hand via the steel wire attached to its end.
"I can't watch this... I can't watch this..." Outside the train, Biao Zi staggered, clutching his chest, his expression dazed as he made his way to the No. 7 Guard Car. He needed to continue training—train until he dropped dead!
He had been quite happy these past few days.
Finally, he had piloted the "Executioner" mech, and he was the first member on the Train to conquer the "Biohazard" and "Dragon Fortress" maps on Extreme Difficulty. His Physical Fitness Index was rising at an exceptionally fast rate.
He felt like he had already stood up.
But upon seeing this "Thunder" mech, he felt as if he had been knocked back down.
When he compared his "Executioner" mech to the "Thunder" mech.
It was like...
It was like the difference between the Azure Dragon and the Stellar—there was simply no comparison!
