chapters.title: Chapter 186 - 186: "Eden Memory Bank."
chapters.content:
"Bang, bang!!"
Two clean and swift punches landed, earning Chen Mang another 20,000 points.
A uniform "15," far exceeding the standard.
The standard was 7.
He had already doubled it.
After Zhang Yi stepped down, Zhang Er, who had been eager for his turn, stepped up. With three crisp punches, he scored a uniform "14," earning another 30,000 points.
At that moment—
Biao Zi hesitated and said, "Lord Mang, how about letting me give it a try?"
"You?"
Chen Mang turned to Biao Zi with a skeptical look. "What's your Physical Fitness Index right now?"
"15.5."
"Alright, give it a shot."
Biao Zi took a deep breath, steadied his stance in front of the punching machine, and with veins bulging on his forehead, he roared as he threw the most powerful punch of his life. The air seemed to ignite with the force of his strike.
At that moment.
Countless images flashed through Biao Zi's mind like a kaleidoscope. He lost himself in a state of absolute focus.
He thought of nothing else. At that moment, all he wanted was to smash the damn punching machine in front of him!
A sharp sonic boom suddenly echoed throughout the hall!
The next moment!
"Boom!"
A deafening crash resounded in the hall, and then the number "8" slowly appeared on the punching machine.
"Not bad."
Chen Mang looked at Biao Zi with a hint of surprise. "Come on, you've got two more chances. Give it two more punches."
"No, no, I can't."
Biao Zi, his legs feeling weak, quickly waved his hands, his face bitter as he shook his arm. "Lord Mang, that one punch drained me. My legs feel like jelly now."
"Keep practicing after this."
"Yes."
Chen Mang, satisfied, led Biao Zi and the others away from the stall and headed to the next one. This stall had earned him a total of 70,000 points. Not bad. He was pleased.
His balance now stood at 149,940.
Nearly 150,000.
He was more than ready to go on a shopping spree at the "Mechanical Train Parts Store."
The game at the fourth stall was—
"Sing and Guess."
Chen Mang glanced at it and immediately moved on. The songs were all from the mechanical civilization, and none of them had heard them before. There was no way they could guess.
After wandering around.
None of the games at the remaining stalls seemed suitable for them, so they left that floor and headed to the fourth floor of the "Entertainment City."
Entertainment City, Fourth Floor.
Here, there were still plenty of beautiful women, but the quality on this floor was even higher. These women were all in the flesh trade, and a quick inquiry revealed that prices started at 300,000.
However, he also saw the "Mom" who was priced at 1 million.
"You seem quite intelligent?"
Chen Mang raised an eyebrow as he looked at the madam who had approached him to make a pitch. This was the first time he had encountered someone with their own logical thinking, rather than a robot that responded based on programming.
"I'm equipped with a Level 3 intelligent chip, darling."
The woman in the evening gown placed her finger on Chen Mang's chest, gently tracing it with a seductive smile. "I possess intelligence close to that of a human. There are 3,280 girls here. Do you see anyone who catches your eye?"
"There used to be over ten thousand, including many human and other species girls. But this place has been abandoned for a long time, and those girls had short lifespans. They're all dead now."
"I've been in hibernation for a long time."
"After you arrived, the energy of this city was reactivated."
"See which one you like?"
"I heard you're worth a million?"
"Mhm, do you like me?" The woman's eyes glistened as she took a step closer, looking up at Chen Mang. Her hair inadvertently brushed against his chin as she whispered softly, "You can ask me anything. This floor is managed by my sister."
"Hmm."
Chen Mang pondered for a moment before firing off a series of questions in rapid succession: "Have you heard of Blue Star and Aqua Star? What about the Nai-1 Star System?"
"Has the mechanical civilization been destroyed?"
"How long have you been in hibernation?"
"Who brought about the apocalypse?"
"How much do you know about the Mechanical Train?"
"What does the Five-Year Pact mean?"
"Where can I get more Iron Ore?"
"Where are the Energy Stones in this city? Are there any Fortuitous Encounter spots, or any ways to make money quickly?"
The woman, who had been alluring just moments ago, suddenly showed a hint of confusion in her eyes. She instinctively took a few steps back before stiffly replying, "I haven't heard of Blue Star, Aqua Star, or the Nai-1 Star System. There's no information about them in my database, and I haven't received any such data."
"I also don't know if the mechanical civilization has been destroyed."
"It's been 49.29 million hours since the last awakening."
"I don't know what the apocalypse is, and there's no information about the Mechanical Train in my database. I only know from conversations with guests that everyone has a Mechanical Train, though the levels vary."
"I also don't know about Iron Ore or the Five-Year Pact, and I don't know where the Energy Stones are."
"But if you want to make money quickly, you can try your luck in the lobby on the first floor. If you're lucky, you can earn a lot fast."
"Um..."
"Don't you want to play with women?"
Chen Mang shook his head without saying much. He simply turned and led Biao Zi and the others downstairs, preparing to leave this entertainment city. The upper floors were all hotels, and there was no need to explore further.
Although this woman was the only robot he had encountered who could hold a conversation, her level of intelligence still seemed inferior to Xiao Ai's.
Her database was practically empty, with nothing of value.
Blue Star was the name of the planet from his previous world, Aqua Star was the name of this planet, and the Nai-1 Star System was the galaxy this planet belonged to.
49.29 million hours was roughly 5,000 years.
Since the mechanical civilization had built this "Eden" for indulgence and hadn't reactivated it in 5,000 years, it was likely that the civilization had either been destroyed or simply didn't have the resources to manage this place anymore.
However, based on what he had seen in the "Tower of Heaven," he thought the probability of destruction was higher.
After leaving the "Sun Entertainment City," Chen Mang, now carrying nearly 150,000 in wealth, headed toward the next entertainment city. Once he had exhausted the money-making opportunities in these three entertainment cities, he could try his luck elsewhere.
He was actually quite satisfied with this amount.
It was enough to buy several Map Chips.
On the deserted streets, only 11 motorcycles were speeding along.
Chen Mang gently squeezed the brakes, bringing his motorcycle to a stop in front of a shop. It was the "Eden Memory Bank," and next to it was the "Mechanical Train Confession Room." He had seen both of these shops marked on the map.
Both were highlighted in crimson.
He was also very curious about what these two shops were for, as they might both be opportunities.
He first walked into the "Eden Memory Bank."
As he pushed the door open, accompanied by the sound of wind chimes, a hoarse male voice greeted him.
"Welcome."
A man dressed in a waiter's uniform stood at the entrance, holding a tablet and offering a professional smile to Chen Mang and his companions: "This is the Eden Memory Bank."
"We offer the following services."
"1: Purchase memories."
"2: Implant memories."
"3: Delete memories."
"4: Print memories."
"5: Memory banking."
"May I know which services you are interested in?"
"Purchase memories?" Chen Mang raised an eyebrow, sizing up the waiter with curiosity. "What do these services mean? Could you explain them?"
It was not easy.
This was the first male waiter he had seen in this city.
"Certainly."
The man smiled and invited Chen Mang and his group to take a seat before bringing over 11 bottles of chilled Mineral Water.
"Everyone's most valuable asset is their memories. Many memories are almost unique and scarce."
"For example—"
"If a peerless beauty has only slept with you, and when this peerless beauty dies, no one else can experience her. You only need to sell us the memory of sleeping with her, and we will sell this memory to others, allowing them to experience the peerless beauty as well."
"This is uniqueness."
"Because the dead cannot be brought back to life."
"Or, for instance, if you were lucky enough to fall from the 20th floor and survive, this memory is very scarce. After we replicate and sell this memory, many people can also enjoy this rare experience of yours, as not everyone is as fortunate as you."
"But not every memory has value."
"Our shop uses instruments to mark all the important memories in your life, and the system will automatically assign a fair price to them. Once you agree to sell and sign the 'Memory Authorization Agreement,' the transaction is complete, and you will receive a substantial reward."
"The entire process is painless and without any discomfort. Of course, the only cost is that this memory will be completely erased from your mind."
"However, only those with a Mental Strength of 16.0 or higher can undergo memory extraction surgery."
As he spoke.
The man swiped a few times on the screen: "Judging by your attire and demeanor, you don't seem to be short on money, and you probably aren't here to sell memories. The price for purchasing memories is much lower, as memories can be replicated multiple times."
"The more unique the memory, the higher the price."
"You can take a look and see if there are any memories you'd like to purchase."
"There are no Mental Strength requirements for purchasing memories, but if your Mental Strength is below 16.0, it is not recommended to purchase more than 20 units of memory, as it may pose a risk of mental fragmentation."
Chen Mang narrowed his eyes slightly, thoughtfully gazing at the list of products on the screen.
"1: A fragment of a frontline worker's hard labor, capacity of 380 units, price 2 million points."
"2: Beginner's memory of piloting the 'Stellar Generation One' mecha, capacity of 90 units, price 180,000 points."
"3: All memories of sharing a room with Zhang Meiqi, capacity of 980 units, price 700,000 points."
"4:"
"."
After browsing for a while, he finally spoke up: "Fragments of memories from frontline workers' jobs are this expensive?"
"Mm-hmm."
The man, gentle and scholarly, smiled and explained: "Because the memory extraction surgery requires a Mental Strength of at least 16.0, very few frontline workers have a Mental Strength that reaches this number. Scarcity drives up the price, so naturally, it's expensive. Generally speaking, these memories are bought by politicians."
"It ensures they can deliver speeches to workers with more genuine emotion, making the workers empathize more."
"Can knowledge-based memories like piloting mechs also be sold?"
"Mm-hmm, but they are usually beginner-level memories, used to assist in quickly learning something previously unfamiliar. Since most people who pilot mechs have a Mental Strength above 16.0, the price is relatively cheaper."
"Is that Zhang Meiqi some kind of celebrity?"
"No, she's just an ordinary man's wife."
"An ordinary man's wife, selling for 700,000 points?"
"There aren't many sellers, and clients who buy this part often inspect the goods first to ensure there's genuine emotional connection. These clients enjoy the immersive experience of real-life scenarios, and... they have plenty of money."
"Of course, this woman is somewhat good-looking, so the price is a bit higher."
At that moment—
"Let me give it a try."
Biao Zi looked at the man in confusion: "Where's the device? Let's see which of my memories can be sold."
"Alright, hold on, extend your arm and roll up your sleeve."
The man immediately took out something resembling a "blood pressure monitor" from under the table, attached a part to Biao Zi's arm, and explained: "This device will quickly search all the memories deep in your mind and identify the valuable ones."
"To respect the customer's privacy."
"The displayed memory names are all garbled codes with corresponding prices. Only when the customer clicks on the screen will the name of that memory appear."
"Shall we begin?"
"Mm, let's start."
One minute later.
Ten memory fragments with garbled names appeared on the screen, the only ones with commercial value.
"Huh?"
"So my life has been this eventful?"
Biao Zi looked at the memory fragment with the highest price tag, a hint of surprise flashing in his eyes. He eagerly clicked on the garbled code of this memory fragment, wanting to see which part of his life it was, worth 380,000 points.
Equivalent to 6 Map Chips.
When his finger touched the screen.
Soon, the name of this memory fragment appeared.
"Memory of sharing a room with a Goblin."
"."
The smile on Biao Zi's face slowly froze, his expression quickly turning gloomy, as if dripping with discomfort. But soon, he spoke in a hoarse, pained voice: "What happens if my Mental Strength isn't 16.0 and I force the memory extraction surgery?"
"You'll die."
The next moment—
The device on the table suddenly began to disassemble itself. The man, with practiced ease, swept the fragments into a nearby trash bin: "All devices for testing memory prices are disposable. After testing the price, they automatically disassemble to absolutely ensure the customer's memories are not leaked."
"Rest assured, esteemed customers, since our opening, there hasn't been a single case of leakage."
"Is this free of charge?"
"The test is complimentary, and the shop covers the equipment wear and tear."
"Let me give it a try."
Li Shiji took a deep breath, extended his arm, and said with a serious expression, "My Mental Strength is sufficient. Let's see which of my valuable memories can be sold."
His Mental Strength was 26.9.
Originally, it was 26.8, but after continuously working on maps these past days, his mental exertion had caused it to increase slightly.
It seemed like he was about to make a significant contribution this time.
Soon—
Just a minute later, the test results were out.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 187 - 187: "Don’t You Need to Restock?"
chapters.content:
"What does 'zero' mean?"
Li Shiji looked up in confusion at the man sitting across from him: "Does this mean that none of my life experiences have any commercial value?"
"Even Biao Ge has ten. How can I have zero?"
"The instrument doesn't make mistakes. It's accurate."
"Can I see what the remaining nine memories of Biao Ge are?"
"The instrument has already been destroyed. It's impossible to check."
"What about testing again?"
"Each person can only test for free once. If you want to pay, it's 100,000 points per test."
"Huh?"
Hearing Li Shiji's words, Biao Zi also became curious. He had glanced at his remaining nine memory fragments earlier, and the most expensive one was only worth 10,000 points, so he didn't bother to check further.
He thought everyone should have something.
He never expected that Li Shiji wouldn't have a single memory fragment of value.
"..."
Chen Mang had been leaning back in his chair, silently observing everything. In truth, both Biao Zi and Li Shiji should have one most valuable memory in their minds—the memory of struggling to survive during the apocalypse.
But since Li Shiji's memories with commercial value were zero, it proved that this memory wasn't worth anything.
In other words.
This kind of thing had happened countless times, making memories of surviving the apocalypse so common that they were worthless.
Although the woman on the fourth floor of the entertainment city said that the term "apocalypse" didn't exist in her database, the information here easily led to one conclusion: it wasn't just their planet that had suffered an apocalypse.
But
countless planets.
"Try mine."
After a long while, he stretched out his arm and said calmly, "See if I have any memories worth selling."
"Alright."
The man skillfully threw the discarded instrument on the table into the trash can, then took out a new one and connected it to Chen Mang's arm.
A minute later.
Thirty-seven memory fragments with garbled names appeared on the screen, and the most expensive one was priced at
「73,900,000,000.」
「Far exceeds the store's balance. Unable to complete the purchase.」
"..."
"..."
Everyone sitting at the table was stunned. Biao Zi stared at the string of numbers in disbelief, starting to count them one by one: "One, ten, hundred, thousand, ten thousand, hundred thousand, million..."
"Don't bother counting. It's 7.39 billion."
Li Shiji looked up at Chen Mang with wide eyes, his voice trembling in disbelief: "Lord Mang... have you met the King of Hell?"
The number was simply too exaggerated, so much so that everyone present was completely dumbfounded.
The man sitting across from them, however, didn't seem too fazed. He just smiled and said, "Since your Mental Strength isn't sufficient for memory extraction surgery, would you like to purchase some memories?"
This man was just a robot. Although he appeared more intelligent, he was still just following his programming and didn't have much emotion.
Unless certain keywords were programmed to trigger specific emotions.
"7.39 billion divided by 380,000..."
Biao Zi was still dazedly bending over, trying to calculate how many Goblins Lord Mang's memory was equivalent to sleeping with, but the number was too large for him to figure out.
"..."
Chen Mang didn't react much, just quietly gazed at the instrument that had self-destructed. Although he hadn't opened the garbled code, he knew what that memory fragment was—it should be the memory of him just crossing over to this world, the memory of living two lives.
This was a bit troublesome.
The rarer the memory, the more expensive it was. Such a costly memory indicated that the probability of this happening in the vast universe was extremely small.
In other words.
He probably had no hope of returning to his previous world in this lifetime. Fortunately, he had no attachment to going back to that world, otherwise, he might have felt a little disappointed.
However, upon seeing the looks in Biao Zi and the others' eyes, he decided to explain.
After a moment of silence, he smiled and said.
"Some small matter, how should I put it... let me think."
"I saw a dragon before the apocalypse."
"I believe it!"
Biao Zi nodded with extreme determination: "And it must have been the Dragon King of the Universe, otherwise, it wouldn't be worth this price."
"Just seeing it isn't enough," Li Shiji shook his head: "At least you have to do something, then it might be worth this price."
At this moment.
The man continued to explain with a smile: "The remaining deleted memory mainly helps customers erase some painful memories, thus leading a more sunny and cheerful life."
"The surgery is also a memory stripping surgery, just like acquiring memories."
"However, this surgery requires the customer to pay, and the stripped memories are not retained but permanently destroyed."
"Printing memory is about printing certain memories into capsule pills. When the pill is taken, the memory will clearly reappear in the mind without erasing the original memory, usually used to print important memories."
"For example, elderly people with dementia often forget their families from time to time."
"The memory bank strips some important memories from customers and keeps them with us, ensuring that no matter what severe interrogation they face, they won't speak, guaranteeing absolute safety of the memories."
"Of course."
"Currently, all memory surgeries require the full cooperation of the customer; forced stripping is impossible. Moreover, whether it's forced stripping or memory implantation, a person cannot undergo it too many times, even after complete repair through the 'Medical Pod'."
"Too many times might lead to sinking into the consciousness space, commonly known as a vegetative state."
Chen Mang led Biao Zi and the others away from the store.
Standing on the street.
Chen Mang lit a cigarette, looking up at the skyscrapers filled with neon lights, the city sky was blue with white clouds. He didn't know where this city was located, but he clearly understood one thing: in the 'Mechanical Train Parts Store', there was something he must buy.
-
'Special Item': Neon City Free Admission Ticket, priced at 100,000 points.
'Item Effect': Admission ticket to the Fortuitous Encounter map 'Neon City'. Anytime this ticket is crushed, you can directly enter this Fortuitous Encounter map. The Train Conductor must go, and can bring up to 10 Train Crew members.
-
He must buy this item.
This city is completely worth a second visit, and before the second visit, he would make all necessary preparations, such as having Biao Zi quickly increase his Mental Strength to 16.0, or asking Li Shiji if he likes green skins.
This city is not just a "Mechanical Train Parts Store."
There are also many shops with special functions, and one day, these shops will play a decisive role.
The special item that brought him into this Fortuitous Encounter map was the "Neon City Ticket," a freely sold admission ticket in the shops.
The difference between the two is that the former requires a certain number of people to enter together, while the latter allows entry at any time as long as it is crushed.
Most importantly...
Chen Mang exhaled a faint blue cloud of smoke in silence, gazing at the distant skyscrapers, and softly said, "Biao Zi, that woman from Sun City just said they've been asleep for nearly 5,000 years, right?"
"She said over 40 million hours, which should be about 5,000 years."
Biao Zi continued to count on his fingers, still stuck on the last arithmetic problem he hadn't finished. Now he had to calculate this one too. Why were the numbers always so big?
"So, this city should be ownerless."
Chen Mang narrowed his eyes and murmured.
"Even though it's a Fortuitous Encounter map, it is indeed an ownerless city. Unlike the 'Tower of Heaven' or the 'Geocentric Nuclear Bomb,' this is a map that can be entered repeatedly."
"All the robots in the map operate according to pre-set programs."
"They might have had owners once."
"But now, they definitely don't."
"Do you think... there's a place that could be the heart of this city? If we control that heart, we could completely own this city?"
"That makes sense!"
Biao Zi's eyes suddenly lit up, but then he scratched the back of his head in confusion. "Lord Mang, even if we control this city, we can't restock it. Many items in the 'Mechanical Train' store are out of stock."
"And the currency system is different too."
"We don't have the Energy Stones to sustain the entire city's operations, and we don't have any customers. It seems like the city can't function properly."
"No rush."
Chen Mang smiled as he tossed the cigarette butt into a nearby trash bin, then strode toward the "Mechanical Train Confession Room" shop next door. "As long as we know this city is temporarily ownerless, that's enough."
"Next time, I'll bring Xiao Ai and see if we can figure out how to change the permissions on these robots' chips."
"For now, this city is out of reach."
"But I've claimed it."
"I'll make sure the city's future currency system is Stellar Coupons. This city will become the backyard of the Stellar Train. The situation is clear now."
"No problem."
Although Biao Zi didn't fully understand, he nodded seriously, then sighed, "Before the apocalypse, the Federation had never detected any alien intelligent life."
"But when the apocalypse came..."
"We realized that our planet is just a tiny corner in the vast sea of stars."
"If we strive to reach the highest point of our planet, we'll naturally see further."
Chen Mang didn't share these sentiments. After all, when he first crossed over, his first thought was, "So many aliens speak Mandarin, huh?"
"Mechanical Train Confession Room."
The shop was decorated in black and white, with no staff in sight. There was only a meditation cushion, and a screen next to it introducing the shop's information.
"When you feel guilty about something you've done, you can come here to confess."
"Confession is divided into three levels."
"1. Ordinary Confession: Costs 100 points per minute."
"2. Advanced Confession: Costs 1,000 points per minute."
"3. Extreme Confession: Costs 10,000 points per minute."
"The higher the level of confession you choose, the more sincere your heart is, and the more likely the God of Machinery will forgive your wrongdoings."
Biao Zi remained silent for a while before he couldn't help but speak up: "Lord Mang, isn't this just a scam? It must be a scam, right? What's the difference between this and selling indulgences?"
"Not quite."
"Indulgences at least have some practical use. This has none at all. It's just preying on the willing."
"Isn't this too simple for a startup in the mechanical civilization?"
"..."
Chen Mang frowned slightly. He was tempted to try it because he felt that this "Mechanical Train Confession Room" couldn't possibly be so crude. Such a simple scam wouldn't fool anyone. Perhaps there would be some reward after the confession.
He immediately turned to the others.
"Do any of you have something to confess? Go try the ordinary confession. I'll pay for it."
"Me."
Li Shiji raised his hand and stepped forward.
Soon—
Li Shiji knelt on the prayer cushion, clasped his hands together, and his lips kept moving. To show sincerity, he specifically confessed things that truly made him feel guilty before the apocalypse. He confessed for a full five minutes.
"Lord Mang."
Li Shiji stood up again and said softly, "I finished confessing, but I don't feel any peace inside. Instead, because I went through it in detail again, I feel even more pain."
"..."
Chen Mang didn't speak. He just stood there patiently, waiting. After a full minute passed and nothing happened, except for the deduction of 500 points from his wristband balance, he turned around expressionlessly and left this so-called confession room.
There was really nothing.
It was truly a pure scam!
Chen Mang, who had walked out of the "Mechanical Train Confession Room," stood by the roadside, looking at the empty street. He took a few deep breaths to calm himself down as much as possible. He had never imagined that he would be scammed in his lifetime.
The main thing was...
He simply didn't believe it was a scam. It was too crude. If it really was a scam, who would fall for such a crude trick?
Wait, he wasn't scammed.
This was called trial and error.
If he ever found out who opened this shop, he would definitely catch them and make them kneel there for 24 hours a day, confessing until they received Lord Mang's forgiveness!
Then Chen Mang got back on his "Off-Road Motorcycle," twisted the throttle, and drove down the street toward another entertainment city, occasionally glancing at the shops on both sides of the street.
To see if there was any shop worth stopping by.
Biao Zi, who was following Chen Mang, was already starting to look forward to the return trip. After experiencing so many things, he had to brag to Lao Zhu when he got back.
Especially about the Memory Bank.
Over 70 billion, that's just insane!
What kind of memory could possibly be worth that much?
Just seeing the dragon isn't enough; you have to eat the dragon.
Soon—
Chen Mang stopped in front of a convenience store that was open for business. There wouldn't be any opportunities inside the store, but the place had a strong sense of everyday life. Through the products sold there, he could learn a lot of information about the mechanical civilization.
"Welcome!"
As soon as he stepped into the store, a girl wearing a short-sleeved shirt and jeans behind the cash register greeted him with a bright smile.
Chen Mang glanced at her and then continued walking deeper into the store. She was the most fully dressed girl he had seen in this city, which was quite an achievement.
This city might as well have been named "Decadence" outright.
"Redheart Nuts?"
He narrowed his eyes slightly, noticing a box of nuts on the shelf. The packaging was quite attractive, priced at 200 points per box.
"Redheart Nuts" are a specialty of the Goblins, right?
They have them here too.
But he soon thought of something and turned his head to look at the girl at the cash register: "Do you need a new supplier? For example, someone to provide you with Redheart Nuts."
"No, we don't."
"Don't you need to restock?"
"No one buys them. You're the first customer to step into this store in such a long time. No need to restock."

chapters.title: Chapter 188 - 188: "Using Steel Pipes to Fight Mechs?"
chapters.content:
"That makes sense."
Chen Mang silently withdrew his gaze from the shop assistant. Since no one was buying, there was no need to restock. However, he soon realized something and turned back to the assistant: "It's been so long, is this stuff still edible?"
"It's all perfectly fine to eat."
"Really?"
"Yes, it is."
"Why do you add a 'ha' at the end of every sentence?"
"It's the boss's setting, it makes it seem more friendly, ha." The shop assistant behind the counter smiled as she answered Chen Mang and his group.
Seeing this, Biao Zi instinctively shivered, hugging his arms and rubbing the goosebumps that had risen on his skin. Honestly, during the day, with all the hustle and bustle, these robots seemed quite interesting, dressed in bikinis with lifelike human bodies.
It could even stir some feelings.
Really impressive.
But at night, if you were alone in this city, it would truly turn into a horror movie. The way they talked always gave off a creepy vibe.
Wait.
Biao Zi suddenly thought of something. After hesitating for a while, he walked up to the shop assistant and tentatively placed his hand on her shoulder.
In the casino, those women in red bikinis were all flirtatious and provocative. With any physical contact, they would say, "Sir, want to? 100,000 points."
Although in the casino environment, it didn't seem out of place.
But this shop assistant was dressed in a short-sleeved shirt and jeans, a very normal outfit, looking just like the girl next door. Surely she wouldn't be like those flirtatious women in the casino, right?
The next moment—
Feeling the physical contact, the shop assistant turned to Biao Zi with a smile.
"Sir, want to? 30,000 points."
"Damn it, I knew it!"
Biao Zi cursed in frustration and quickly withdrew his arm. He had discovered that it wasn't just the casino environment—it was the entire city. In this city, anyone could do whatever they wanted as long as they had the money.
But
Only 30,000 points? That's two-thirds cheaper than in the casino. The value for money is pretty good.
Although he still thought it would be better to just go to a brothel. Aren't brothels even cheaper?
Wait, he was getting sidetracked. Why go to a brothel? What's the fun in a bunch of robots? Why play with robots when you can have real people?
Just then—
The wind chime at the door suddenly rang. A burly man strode into the store, shouting angrily, "Where is everyone?"
He completely ignored Chen Mang and the others, directly placing his wristwatch on the counter device. As the sound of 30,000 points being deducted echoed, the burly man walked behind the counter, stood behind the shop assistant, and pressed her onto the table.
"Wait..."
Biao Zi looked bewildered, glancing at his reflection on the refrigerator: "Lord Mang, we're not invisible, are we?"
"How could he just ignore us like that?"
"..."
Chen Mang narrowed his eyes, carefully observing the scene. The burly man was putting in a lot of effort, and the shop assistant was cooperating fully. The previously normal situation had instantly taken a bizarre turn. The burly man was, of course, also a robot.
A plant for this city.
Around this convenience store, aside from their group, there was no one else. Others couldn't reach this area for now.
This setup couldn't have appeared here for no reason. The scene of the clerk being pinned down seemed more like a program set by the original owner of this city, deliberately creating this absurd sense of depravity to gradually lure customers into sinking deeper.
"Let's get out of here."
Chen Mang put down the Redheart Nut in his hand and led Biao Zi and the others straight out of the convenience store. After lingering at the entrance for thirty seconds, he suddenly strode back in.
"Hey, are you still at it?"
"Never mind, sorry to interrupt. Carry on."
He had initially thought these two robots were just putting on a show for them. Since they were gone, the act would naturally stop. But to his surprise, they were still going at it. It seemed the program was set to finish what it started.
However—
Chen Mang suddenly laughed. He had thought of a way to earn points faster. These robots were all loaded with cash, spending so generously. Perhaps he could try asking each robot individually to see if he could trigger any money-making tasks.
Like the one at the casino.
Without hesitation, he strode back into the convenience store and looked at the burly man busy behind the clerk, speaking earnestly, "Hello, brother."
"Is there anything I can help you with?"
"Of course there is!"
The burly man grumbled while exerting force, "I'm pissed off! A batch of goods I just received this morning was stolen by those damn 'Viper Gang' from the next street. If you can help me get them back, I'll reward you handsomely!"
"Huh?"
Biao Zi, standing behind Chen Mang, looked at the scene in disbelief, his voice rising uncontrollably, "What the hell? This works?!"
"Fighting is our specialty."
Chen Mang laughed, genuinely pleased. It seemed this city had indeed set up some triggerable story missions for certain robots, providing guests with a more immersive experience.
It allowed those who weren't particularly wealthy to participate in the city's activities.
At the same time, it added more playability.
So this "convenience store" must be the trigger point for such missions.
When a guest enters the convenience store and stays for a certain period, this burly man would walk in, appearing furious, and pin the clerk, who earlier seemed like a girl-next-door, under the table.
If you leave at this point, there's no follow-up.
But if you ask a question, the hidden mission is triggered.
"So…"
"When do we set off? When can you finish here?"
"At least half an hour."
Outside the convenience store.
Chen Mang leaned against the off-road motorcycle, lit a cigarette, and waited patiently. Half an hour it is. Even if it were an hour, he'd wait. Those robots that seemed to act unusually often had hidden missions.
"Lord Mang."
Biao Zi squatted stiffly by the roadside, his face looking as if he'd eaten something foul, "What the hell can a robot shoot? Code?"
"Check if Dad's code has no excessive complexity or redundancy."
"Are the comments on each line concise and clear?"
"Be patient."
Chen Mang said casually, "Haste makes waste."
"I'm not impatient, just curious," Biao Zi said as he stood up and strode towards the store. "Wait for me, Lord Mang. I'll go take a look and see if they really have that thing."
At that moment—
A burly man walked out of the store, fastening his belt while cursing under his breath.
"That felt great!"
"But I'm still pissed off."
"Hey, weren't you guys just saying you'd help me get my goods back? Come with me. The 'Viper Gang' next door is tough. I wonder if you can handle them."
With that, he turned and headed into a nearby alley.
"Hey, this guy talks tough, huh?"
Biao Zi chuckled in anger, then turned back to the store and looked at the clerk behind the counter, who was pulling up his jeans.
"Welcome!"
"Thanks for your hard work," Biao Zi said sarcastically, rolling his eyes before quickly jogging to catch up with Lord Mang, following him into the alley.
Behind them, the clerk's cheerful voice rang out.
"Come again next time!"
"Definitely will when I have the money!"
Soon—
Led by the burly man, the group twisted and turned through the alley until they arrived at the underground parking lot of an office building.
Chen Mang surveyed the underground parking lot.
Not a single support column in sight.
The view was incredibly open, and each parking space was unusually large, almost as if it were designed for trains.
It almost resembled a train station.
However, there were no trains in sight at the moment. Instead, there were about twenty to thirty men in floral shirts, looking sloppy, covered in tattoos, smoking cigarettes, and holding bottles of alcohol, gathered together and laughing loudly.
"This is great! After this job, we won't have to work for months!"
"Hahaha, after all, we're the Viper Gang!"
"..."
Biao Zi looked at the scene before him and muttered expressionlessly, "Such a stereotypical and flat portrayal of villains."
It seems the two civilizations still have some similarities, at least in their stereotypes of gangsters.
The next moment—
"Bang!"
The burly man who had led them there angrily pulled a bottle from his coat and smashed it on the ground. The sound of the shattering bottle echoed throughout the basement as he pointed at the group with a sinister grin.
"You dared to steal my goods! I've found help now. Let's see if you can handle them!"
"Let's go!"
"Where did you even pull that bottle from, old man?"
"Huh?" The burly man in front turned back, confused, and glanced at Biao Zi. "I bought it at the convenience store earlier. What's the problem?"
"Nothing, go ahead. Are you done with your lines?"
"Yeah, didn't I just say 'let's go'?"
"So, are we going, Lord Mang?"
Chen Mang tilted his head and looked at Zhang Yi. "Go easy on them. Don't kill anyone, just seriously injure them."
Normally, attacking others isn't allowed in this city. Earlier, at the entrance of the "Mechanical Train Parts Store," a Train Conductor tried to rob the store and was immediately kicked out of this Fortuitous Encounter map.
But now the situation is different. He's been invited by a local gang to join the fight. They can't just kick him out, right? This should count as one of those "Fortuitous Encounters" mentioned in the map's information.
Still, to be safe, it's better not to go for the kill.
"Got it."
Zhang Yi nodded with a serious expression, then tossed the refrigerator to Zhang Er. He reached into his coat pocket and pulled out a briefcase, throwing it into the air. The all-black briefcase disassembled mid-flight and, in the blink of an eye, transformed into an incredibly imposing mech.
The blue mech, Thunderbolt!
In the next moment—
Zhang Yi immediately piloted the mech and charged forward. Seeing this, the members of the "Viper Gang" pulled out steel pipes and machetes from a nearby bag, roaring as they rushed to meet him.
"Steel pipes?!"
Biao Zi shouted in disbelief, "You guys don't even have a single gun?!"
"Are you seriously fighting a mech with steel pipes?"
Three minutes later.
The battle was over.
Victory was secured. All the members of the "Viper Gang" lay on the ground, battered and groaning in pain. However, there was no blood—instead, numerous mechanical parts had been knocked loose and scattered around.
The reason it took so long was mainly due to the requirement of not dealing fatal blows, which made the fight unnecessarily difficult.
"Hahahaha!"
"This is what happens when you mess with our 'Battle Damage Gang'!"
The burly man who had just been fighting ran over excitedly, picked up a briefcase, and hurled it toward Chen Mang with force: "Brother, thanks! This is the batch of goods that was stolen. Consider it your reward!"
"You're giving it all away?!" Biao Zi couldn't help but raise his voice in disbelief again.
What's the difference between this and Lord Mang robbing you?
You might as well have let the Viper Gang take it.
"Hahahaha!"
Immediately after, the burly man walked away laughing, looking rather carefree, while the battered members of the "Viper Gang" muttered curses under their breath as they prepared to leave.
"I can understand you."
Li Shiji patted Biao Zi's shoulder, sighing with emotion: "As a game designer, this plot has way too many flaws. It's clear that the original creator of this city wasn't very skilled in this area. If I were to design it, I could make it much more interesting."
Just then—
"Wait."
Chen Mang looked at the battered members of the "Viper Gang" and suddenly called out to stop them, speaking in a serious and loud voice: "Brothers, is there anything I can do to help you?"
The group paused, and soon a leader stepped forward, his face filled with anger as he shouted:
"I'm furious! A batch of goods that just arrived this morning was completely stolen by those damn 'Battle Damage Gang' from the next street over. If you can help me get those goods back, I'll reward you handsomely!"
"Huh?" Biao Zi's mouth hung open as he couldn't help but speak up again: "Did he seriously not change his lines? Are they reading from the same script?"
In the next moment.
The burly man who had just been laughing and walking away so carefree was caught by Zhang Yi and dragged back, held in the air like a chick.
"We've accepted the 'Viper Gang's' commission. Hand over the goods you stole from them."
Chen Mang looked seriously at the burly man being held in the air.
"Didn't I already give you that batch of goods?"
"What if I give it back to you?"
Chen Mang tentatively handed the bag of goods to the burly man.
"Then... I'll hand it over."
The burly man, somewhat confused, handed the bag back to Chen Mang, who then passed it to the leader of the Viper Gang.
The leader of the Viper Gang, his face flushed with excitement, threw his head back and laughed heartily. He then tossed the bag of goods back in front of Chen Mang.
"Brother, thank you. This is the batch of goods that was stolen. As a reward, it's all yours!"
"Hmm."
Chen Mang tilted his head and glanced at the burly man being held by Zhang Yi. "Don't you have anything to say? Any new requests?"
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 189 - 189: "Fuck! I fucking knew it!"
chapters.content:
The burly man being held midair by Zhang Yi froze for several seconds before suddenly roaring in anger.
"My temper's fucking raging right now! A fresh batch of goods I just got this morning was stolen by those damn Viper Gang bastards from the next street over. If you can help me get them back, I'll reward you handsomely!"
"Got it."
Chen Mang waved his hand, signaling Zhang Yi to toss the man aside, then picked up the bag of goods and walked out of the parking lot.
No matter how they took on this job or whose side they chose, it seemed the mission reward would only be this single bag of goods.
On the street.
Chen Mang opened the bag to inspect its contents—over a hundred chips, all memory chips. A faint smile curled at the corners of his mouth.
This haul was a jackpot.
Who would've thought? Initially, he just wanted to understand the products sold in this convenience store to gain deeper insight into this mechanical civilization. Yet now, he'd stumbled upon such a massive windfall.
Just as described in the Serendipity Map's holographic display, this city wasn't just for relaxation—it was full of Fortuitous Encounters.
"Let's see what chips we've got." Biao Zi squatted down eagerly, picking up one chip and reading the fine print on its packaging: "'A Satisfying Poop' memory fragment, capacity 0.2 units."
"'A Wank' memory fragment, capacity 0.4 units."
"'Arguing with a Stranger and Overwhelming Them' memory fragment, capacity 1.4 units."
"'A Hearty Feast' memory fragment, capacity 1.2 units."
"Hmm..."
The smile gradually faded from Biao Zi's face. "Lord Mang, are these things even valuable?"
"If this city's gangs are dealing in crap like this, no wonder they're all carrying steel pipes. How could they afford guns?"
"Let's check at the Memory Bank."
Chen Mang didn't elaborate, simply tossing the bag to Zhang Yi before mounting the off-road motorcycle to retrace their path back to the Memory Bank. He wanted to see how much this batch was worth.
Soon.
They arrived at the Memory Bank. After inventory, the male attendant smiled and quoted a price.
"Total for the full batch is exactly 240,000."
"Confirm sale?"
"Confirmed."
Chen Mang grinned, extending his wristwatch to receive the attendant's transfer. His balance immediately updated to—
389,440.
Nearly 400,000!
This windfall was massive—far more than what he'd earned at the entertainment district. Clearly, through his exploration, he'd discovered that the fastest way to make money in this city wasn't playing those mini-games, but seeking out robots with unusual behavior to trigger quests.
"That much...?"
Biao Zi's jaw dropped slightly at the number. They'd worked so hard in Sun City to earn less than 150,000, yet this single effortless job just netted them 240,000.
Now...
His Zombie Siege map chip was practically guaranteed. Plus, they could buy plenty of other things too.
The Train had grown stronger again.
All thanks to Lord Mang.
Outside the Memory Bank.
Li Shiji sighed with emotion, "Lord Mang, if nothing unexpected happens, the wealth gap in this mechanical civilization is probably enormous. Before the apocalypse, the capitalists in the federation would exploit the working class, but at most, they only took away mental and physical labor—just making you work a bit harder."
"But in this mechanical civilization..."
"The people at the bottom can't even keep their memories."
"If they finally have a memory worth cherishing, they might have to sell it off on some day when they're short on money, just to survive."
"Not the bottom-tier people," Chen Mang shook his head casually. "Memory extraction surgery requires a Mental Strength of at least 16.0. According to that shop assistant, the lower class in their civilization probably can't reach that level."
"But... I've definitely... you know..."
"Why didn't the first scan detect my commercially valuable memories?"
"Simple," Chen Mang swung his leg over the off-road motorcycle and glanced at his wristwatch before speaking. "The memory products we saw in the Memory Bank were all large, coherent memories. The memory chips seized from that gang were fragmented—definitely not obtained through legal channels."
"Most likely, they completely dissected some poor kid's memories and kept the leftovers."
"Let's go."
His next target was still another "entertainment district."
Of course.
He planned to stop by any shops that looked unusual, just to see if there were any quests to trigger.
He couldn't stop at every shop—there wasn't enough time.
If he missed an opportunity, so be it. He couldn't hog all the good things.
"Ahhh... refreshing!"
Customized Brothel.
The King of Electronic Music Train's conductor, the Dwarf Man, descended the stairs with a spring in his step, stretching his limbs. There was no denying it—a three-meter-tall woman really hit the spot.
He loved it.
Next time he got the chance, he'd try a five-meter one. Maybe he could crawl inside entirely.
Like sleeping in a camping bag.
Just then, he thought he heard faint sobbing. Pausing, he pushed open a small side door and found a cramped space where a girl was curled up, crying.
She looked about 18.
Utterly pitiful.
When the door opened, the girl hurriedly wiped her tears and forced a smile at the Dwarf Man. "How may I serve you?"
"Uh..."
The Dwarf Man stared at the girl huddled in the corner, hesitating before tentatively asking, "Is there... anything I can do to help?"
"Did this brothel force you into this?"
"Wait, no—you're a robot, aren't you? I—"
"Really?"
The girl's eyes suddenly lit up, and she trembled with emotion. "Seven is missing. I'm so sad. If you can help me find her, I'll reward you handsomely."
"Seven is my cat."
"..."
The Dwarf Man expressionlessly closed the door again, rolling his eyes in annoyance. Crying so miserably in a brothel—he'd almost felt guilty, thinking something truly awful had happened. Turns out it was just her damn cat.
At that moment—
A cat strutted past the shop door with leisurely steps, almost as if taunting them.
Coincidentally, his thugs had just come downstairs.
"Go catch that damn cat for me."
"Fuck."
"I'm too kind-hearted."
Half an hour later.
The Dwarf Man twisted the cat's tail expressionlessly. As expected, it was a mechanical cat—the wind-up kind. But he didn't comment, simply returning to the Customized Brothel and opening the hidden compartment under the counter. Inside, a girl was still curled up, sniffling.
"Here, your Seven is back."
"Thank you."
The girl immediately brightened, wiping away her tears. "I don't have much to repay you with, so here's a Free Pass for Neon City. With this, you can have anyone in the city serve you however you like—but only once."
"..."
The Dwarf Man took the Free Pass from her, remaining silent.
She could've given this earlier. Now that he'd already had his fun, what was the point?
Not that he could use it now anyway. Middle age was different from his youth. Back then, seven or eight times a night wasn't an exaggeration—effortless, never knowing exhaustion.
Hell, he'd even sneak off to the bathroom beforehand to take the edge off, just to last longer when it counted.
Now? After one round, he felt like a monk sworn to celibacy.
A second round was out of the question.
Might as well save it. He'd cash it in right before leaving this Serendipity Map.
"Fine."
The Dwarf Man tucked the pass into his pocket, satisfied enough, then led his men outside to wander around. His pockets were nearly empty—only 129 points left.
Time to hit a convenience store for food and water.
Staying here for 48 hours on an empty stomach wasn't an option.
Most Train Conductors who entered this Serendipity Map were high-level, driven by ambition.
Sure, some were more curious about the brothels.
But most were scouring every shop, every corner, hoping for a Fortuitous Encounter or a quick buck. And so—
A flood of Train Conductors swept through the city, searching building by building, even the offices in skyscrapers. Most doors were locked tight, but a few stood open.
This was a Serendipity Map with near-total freedom.
Anywhere was accessible—as long as the door wasn't locked.
Meanwhile—
Chen Mang stood before a factory gate, surrounded by towering walls topped with electric fences, heavy machine guns, and anti-aircraft artillery—the first heavy firepower he'd seen in the city.
Beside the entrance was an iris scanner.
They couldn't bypass it. Couldn't get in.
But...
Chen Mang narrowed his eyes at the scanner. Since leaving the Memory Bank, he'd spent over three hours exploring the city without encountering a single interactive robot. Instead, he'd stumbled upon this mysterious factory.
No name. No clues.
But he discovered one thing—all the cash registers, entertainment centers, and robots in this city were connected via the internet. This was the first place he had encountered since the apocalypse that still had a functioning network.
The Train had no internet.
None of the previous Serendipity Maps he had visited had networks either.
Only this city had one.
This meant that the long-dormant "Supermodel Effect" of the "Train Auxiliary AI" could finally be put to use.
-
"Train Auxiliary AI Level 10 Supermodel Effect": Capable of network intrusion, decryption, and breaching most network firewalls.
-
As long as he brought Xiao Ai into this Serendipity Map next time, he could unlock more areas that were otherwise inaccessible to him.
There had to be good stuff inside.
Only two problems needed solving.
First, Xiao Ai wasn't a member of the Train Crew and couldn't be brought here.
Second, Xiao Ai's core was just the Train AI. It could only control robots by manipulating their components, and once a robot moved beyond a certain distance from the Train, Xiao Ai would lose connection with it.
But he believed both problems had solutions.
After all, when Er Dan's consciousness had descended into a robot and entered his Train, the AI had also remotely taken control of the robot and followed along. This meant there was a way—he just hadn't figured it out yet.
Once these two issues were resolved and Xiao Ai was brought into this city, the place would practically become his private playground.
Free for him to explore.
He just hoped the city's backup power reserves were sufficient. The energy consumption of an entire city had to be astronomical—far beyond what he could sustain. And couldn't they at least turn off the lights in the unused areas? What a waste of energy.
No sense of frugality at all.
Turning around, Chen Mang led Biao Zi and the others as they mounted their off-road motorcycles and continued exploring the city.
The duration of the "Neon City" Serendipity Map was 48 hours.
Only 4 hours remained.
During this time, they had only encountered one interactive robot with a quest—a bounty notice issued by the law enforcement bureau, offering a reward for locating a stolen aircraft. They earned 120,000 credits.
How bizarre.
This city even had a law enforcement bureau.
They found the stolen police aircraft, taken by a gang, and collected the 120,000-credit reward.
After that, they hadn't run into any other robots with interactive quests.
Now, they stood at the entrance of the law enforcement bureau.
"Thank you."
A mature, intellectual-looking middle-aged woman in uniform stepped out of the bureau, her expression earnest and sincere as she addressed Chen Mang and his group. "Eden has become a better place because of you."
"One day—"
"I will eradicate all crime in this city!"
"Good work."
Chen Mang smiled at the woman. Though 120,000 wasn't much, it was still something. He didn't mind offering a smile, though he felt a slight regret—with only 4 hours left on the map, it seemed they'd only make it to 500,000 credits.
Not bad, though.
500,000 could buy quite a few things at the "Mechanical Train Parts Store."
"."
Biao Zi glanced at the prim and proper mature woman, curling his lips in silent exasperation. If all the illegal activities in this city were truly eradicated, what would even be left of it? Wouldn't it just become a ghost town?
This woman was the director of the law enforcement bureau.
She looked so serious and upright.
But—
Suddenly remembering something, he tentatively poked her again with his finger.
The next moment—
"Sir, would you like to? One million points."
The woman turned her head toward Biao Zi with a deadpan expression.
"Damn it!"
"I fucking knew it!"
Biao Zi took a deep breath and immediately turned to follow Lord Mang as they walked away. He already knew—no matter what someone's status was in this city, as long as there was physical contact, this interaction was inevitable!
Goddammit!
He shouldn't have dared to hope for anything different. He'd tried countless times—every single person was like this, without exception!
