chapters.title: Chapter 244: Calling It a Behemoth Is No Exaggeration!
chapters.content:
Soon—
By the time all residents had exited the train, the thirty-minute countdown was nearing its end.
The moment the timer reached zero—
"Click!"
A crisp yet muffled sound emanated from the locomotive, followed by countless white light particles drifting out from Carriage No. 2 and seeping into the train. Before the eyes of all residents, the Stellar Train suddenly began to... transform?
Or perhaps mutate?
The steel seemed to gain life and soul, growing wildly and uncontrollably. The usually thick armor now flowed like viscous liquid, stretching and crawling through the void.
The entire Stellar Train visibly expanded at a rapid pace.
A complete, overall enlargement.
Wider, longer, taller!
Even the Wind-Fire Wheels rapidly spread outward, increasing in size.
The entire process lasted a full three minutes.
Three minutes later.
Under the awestruck gazes of all residents, the Stellar Train had completely transformed, growing several times larger. Each carriage now measured 10 meters wide, 30 meters long, and 10 meters tall!
The locomotive reached 10 meters in width and 21 meters in length.
The Stellar Train now consisted of 14 carriages plus 1 locomotive, with a total length of 441 meters!
The connections between carriages weren't rigidly welded but had slight gaps, ensuring greater flexibility, so the actual length slightly exceeded this figure.
Most strikingly—
Its height!
Each carriage stood 10 meters tall, equivalent to a three-story building.
At a glance—
This was a true mechanical dragon, a colossal beast coiled across the wasteland. The previously menacing ten Level 20 Doomsday Cannons now looked like miniature toys on the train, lacking their former intimidation.
"..."
Chen Mang observed the scene with a satisfied smile, his sense of fulfillment peaking. This—this was the Doomsday Train he had built within months of crossing into this world!
This was his foundation in this world.
He immediately gripped his cane and manipulated it remotely. Through the Custom Carriage options, he spent 60,000 units of Iron Ore to emblazon three massive characters across the pitch-black train:
「Stellar」!
The character "Stel" spanned Carriage No. 3, "lar" covered Carriage No. 6, and the suffix symbol occupied Carriage No. 9.
Each character was enormous.
Even from a distance, the name "Stellar" was unmistakable.
Both sides of the train bore the name. The price was steep—60,000 units of Iron Ore just for a paint job. No wonder he'd rarely seen anyone use this feature. But now, he wanted it. He wanted to spend 60,000 units of Iron Ore to truly christen his train with its name!
He wanted the name "Stellar" to one day resound across the heavens!
For everyone to know the name of his Stellar.
This was his dream.
And the goal he aspired to achieve.
The residents behind him finally snapped out of their daze, their faces alight with excitement as they roared in exhilaration, their eyes filled with awe as they gazed at the Train before them—now completely transformed into a true steel behemoth.
In the apocalypse, who wouldn't want to follow someone strong enough?
Especially the group of children standing behind Teacher Qiu. They kept tiptoeing, straining to catch a glimpse of Lord Mang sitting on a chair at the front of the crowd. But their short stature and the many obstacles in front made it impossible, leaving them scratching their heads in frustration.
Though they had seen Lord Mang many times on screen, they had never laid eyes on him in person.
"Board the Train."
Chen Mang stood up, cradling Xiao Lu in his arms, and strode toward the Train's control room. He wanted to experience the changes brought by the Train Expansion firsthand.
Following his command through their Iris Chips, the residents lined up in an orderly manner and returned to the Train.
The most immediate impression upon entering the control room was—
Spacious!
Far more spacious than before.
His Single Bed, tucked into a corner, now looked as small and cozy as a dog's nest.
The once-cramped control room now held only a central console, two Refrigerators beside it, and a portal on the carriage wall. The Heavy Machine Guns that had once densely covered the ceiling were now spaced farther apart, creating a more aesthetically pleasing arrangement.
Yet, it felt somewhat empty.
"I need to find something to fill up the control room," Chen Mang muttered, frowning as he surveyed the surroundings. The old control room had been crowded, but it gave him a sense of security—he liked small, cozy spaces. Every time he stayed inside, he felt safe.
But now, the control room felt… hollow.
He rolled Xiao Lu onto the floor. Once Xiao Lu woke up, there'd be plenty of space for her to play around in.
Another issue—
The control room was now over ten meters above the ground. Previously, a simple retractable folding ladder had provided access, but now it was just a climbing ladder. Chen Mang wasn't afraid of heights, but scaling a ten-meter ladder every time he needed to enter or exit the Train was undeniably inconvenient.
"Hmm…"
The Train needed further upgrades.
Chen Mang silently made a mental note: an elevator for easier access, and a few slides or retractable large staircases for the Resident Carriages to help passengers board and disembark quickly.
Though there were drawbacks, the benefits far outweighed them!
Not bad.
But the Train still needed more upgrades. Each upgrade unlocked a new function. At Level 10, the two unlocked functions were "Train Expansion" and "Mechanical Fortress."
The effect of Mechanical Fortress was this:
Pressing the button on the console would cause the Train to encircle itself from end to end, anchoring to the ground for 24 hours. During this time, all "Defensive Components" would automatically upgrade by one level, and all "Firepower Components" would have Halved Consumption.
The trade-off? The Train couldn't move during those 24 hours, remaining rooted in place.
If he activated this effect, his "Armor" would jump to Level 14!
But so far, there hadn't been a situation where this function was necessary. Back then, even Shen Ye hadn't had the chance to use it—not that it would've mattered, given how the Level 13 artillery had crushed everything.
After this Train Expansion—
The Iron Ore reserves in the Train were once again depleted!
Nearly empty.
Only 150,000 units of Iron Ore left—practically back to poverty.
He distinctly remembered earning a substantial amount of Iron Ore recently, so how had it suddenly dwindled to nothing?
"."
Inside the Train's cabin.
Chen Mang frowned slightly. He couldn't keep taking the conventional path. Last night, he had scoured the wasteland all night but failed to find a Level 4 Iron Ore deposit. Another night of searching would likely yield the same result.
Once a Level 4 Iron Ore deposit was discovered by other Trains, it was almost always mined immediately—no chance of leaving it for latecomers.
Finding one that had just spawned or newly appeared was far too difficult.
Though the "Pickaxe Production Line" was only a green-tier accessory, capped at Level 3, this was still the Blue Zone. The Trains here were considered high-tier in this apocalyptic world, and obtaining a few Murphy Stones wasn't entirely impossible.
He had to take an unconventional route.
Tonight, he would head to the Mechanical City Ruins in the Red Zone via the "Train Tunnel." He needed to try something different!
Only after all residents had climbed up the ladders into the Resident Car did the Stellar Train slowly start moving.
Chen Mang didn't activate the Drill Bit immediately.
Instead, he gradually pushed the control lever, sitting in the cockpit and looking down at the ground ahead. Feeling the Train beneath him gradually accelerate and the intense g-force pressing him into his seat, his excitement grew.
The Stellar Train now handled completely differently from before!
The bird's-eye view!
The incredibly spacious cabin, the Train like a steel dragon!
It made him feel as though he were piloting a colossal steel beast, racing across the wasteland. He slowly pushed the lever all the way, steering toward the Corpse Tide marked on the Targeting Radar—30,000 meters ahead!
Thirty thousand meters—covered in an instant!
Seated in the cabin, Chen Mang looked at the Corpse Tide, whose highest-level Zombies were Level 9, and drove the Train straight into them without slowing down.
"Boom! Boom! Boom!"
Countless Zombies were sent flying, shattered into pieces. The Stellar Train mercilessly crushed the apocalyptic horde beneath it.
A few months ago, he had nearly died at the hands of the Corpse Tide.
Now, the Corpse Tide was nearly wiped out by him.
"Damn, that felt good!"
After ramming through them four or five times, the horde was almost entirely pulverized. The Wind-Fire Wheels were now taller than a person. The Carriage stood 10 meters high, with nearly two meters of clearance beneath it.
There was no way the Zombies could jam the wheels and immobilize the Train like before.
Now, he could just drive right over their heads.
The current Stellar Train—
Calling it a behemoth wasn't an exaggeration at all!
After a while, Chen Mang, still unsatisfied, finally stopped wasting time. He extended the Drill Bit, and as it spun at high speed, the "Spider Legs" also emerged, lifting the Carriage and lowering the front of the Train. The Drill Bit pressed against the ground and began boring into it.
The Drill Bit was enormous—
As wide as the Carriage, if not slightly wider.
After the Train Expansion, he noticed many accessories had also scaled up, including the "Spider Legs." Originally large, they had grown even more massive post-expansion.
Looking out the window—
The mechanical, sci-fi-inspired Spider Legs were a sight to behold, exuding sheer intimidation and dominance.
Honestly.
If he had possessed such a train when the apocalypse first descended, his train would have looked more like the apocalypse itself than those Zombies. The source of the apocalypse would have been him.
"Bzzzzz..."
Accompanied by the rapid spinning of the Drill Bit.
The Train soon plunged deep underground again, heading straight for the hole he had drilled in the Train Tunnel last time. That hole was definitely too small now, but it didn't matter—he could just drill it bigger.
Perhaps because the Train's size had increased.
He noticed that the Train now consumed more energy while moving, and its speed—whether underground or aboveground—had slowed by about a third. The reduction wasn't insignificant.
Clearly.
This was the crossroads where he had to choose between speed and size.
He chose size. As for speed...
A reduction was just a reduction. It didn't matter. Who cared about a little slowdown? As long as he gathered enough Iron Ore for a full upgrade of the Wind-Fire Wheel and other speed-boosting components, the speed would skyrocket again!
Numerical reductions didn't bother him much. As long as upgrading the parts could boost the stats back up, it was as if there had been no reduction at all.
But a mechanical weakening? That would be the real disaster.
Worth mentioning—
The Car Blade component was now completely useless against ordinary Zombies. With the Train nearly three meters off the ground, shorter monsters would only feel a chilly breeze above their heads, completely unaffected.
Soon!
The Train reached the entrance of the Train Tunnel and located the hole he had drilled earlier. Without hesitation, the massive Drill Bit plunged into the tunnel again, spinning rapidly.
The Stellar Train smoothly entered the Train Tunnel once more, switching to Bunny Cloud Wheels to float midair.
"Seems like it's about to collapse..."
Inside the Train.
Chen Mang glanced back at the torrent of dirt cascading down like a waterfall. The ground had already accumulated plenty of dirt from the drilling days prior, but the hole back then wasn't as large, and it had quickly been clogged by the falling debris.
But now...
The hole seemed a bit bigger. And it didn't seem like it would clog itself this time.
The dirt poured down like diarrhea.
After a few minutes, a small mountain of dirt had piled up inside the Train Tunnel, but the hole was blocked again, and the cascade stopped.
It wasn't the dirt that had clogged it—the Stellar had fixed it. The solution was simple.
He crafted seven or eight oversized band-aids and sent Zhang Yi, Zhang Er out in mechs to plaster them over the hole.
Not bad.
These band-aids were surprisingly sturdy. No wonder—they were made of Iron Ore. Durability guaranteed!
Of course, the band-aids couldn't withstand the sheer weight of all that falling dirt, but as long as they provided enough resistance, the dirt would eventually clog the hole itself. Who knew how long it would last, but it would do for now.
"See that?"
After the Train Expansion.
Every Carriage now had windows—floor-to-ceiling ones, stretching from bottom to top.
Immersive as hell.
The train was gradually transforming into something resembling a cosmic train. At the very least, a normal train shouldn't have floor-to-ceiling windows.
But then again, let's not talk about normal trains.
If we're being truly realistic, a normal train shouldn't have any of the components found on the Stellar Train.
"The train has changed so much," murmured the young man who had been following Uncle Li as he gazed at the scene before him. "It's only been a short while, yet the train has transformed from its initial state to what we see now. Uncle Li, do you remember when the Stellar was just a bare train engine?"
"Though the immersion is stronger now..."
"It does feel a bit dangerous."
"Don't worry," Uncle Li reassured him. "Lord Mang said these windows have the same defensive rating as the armor—they're practically black technology."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 245: Compounding Interest Upon Interest – The Doomsday Capitalist!
chapters.content:
"I'm not talking about that. I mean, if the Stellar Train were to face an extremely dire crisis, Uncle Li, which carriage do you think it would prioritize abandoning?"
"It's really hard to guess."
"It definitely can't be Carriage No. 15, the Breeding Carriage, right, Uncle Li?"
"..."
Uncle Li suddenly fell silent, his lips twitching slightly before he finally spoke. "If it ever comes to that, are you stupid? Don't you know to run to the front carriages?"
The expanded Stellar Train had now become a colossal behemoth.
But...
Inside the nearly 100-meter-high train tunnel, it still looked like a tiny toy, not particularly eye-catching. This time, the Stellar Train wasn't heading south—it was speeding north!
Its destination? The Mechanical City Ruins!
Though the ruins had been scavenged by many trains countless times, leaving almost nothing behind, Chen Mang was certain the Mechanical City accessible through the train tunnel still held treasures. No one had been here before.
It was worth noting.
So far.
The Stellar Train was the most expanded train he had ever seen. Other trains had expanded too, but none as extensively as his. Though he also struggled with iron ore shortages, at least he didn't face the same overwhelming pressure as other trains when it came to upgrading defensive components.
Billions of units of iron ore...
Just thinking about it gave him a headache.
The train raced through the tunnel, the incandescent lamps along the walls glowing steadily as always. He had passed through this tunnel many times—it was all too familiar.
After about an hour or so.
The incandescent lights on both sides of the tunnel began flickering, replaced by flashing red warning lights.
This meant... he had arrived.
Sure enough, soon enough, a massive train elevator appeared on the left side of the tunnel, large enough to accommodate his entire train. Surprisingly, this wasn't the end of the tunnel.
"..."
Chen Mang narrowed his eyes slightly but didn't dwell on it. Instead, he took out a Level 2 Energy Stone and dropped it into the funnel extended by the train elevator. As the elevator doors slowly opened, the Stellar Train rolled inside.
He could only hope the journey ahead wouldn't require any iron ore.
There was none left.
Absolutely none—the train was completely empty.
If he really needed iron ore, he'd have to urgently sell something over the Train Radio or ask the Traveling Frog for a loan. Without at least a few million units of iron ore stocked in the train, exploration just felt unsettling.
The elevator began ascending rapidly.
It was massive.
Even a 400-meter-long train fit inside with plenty of room to spare.
Meanwhile, the Targeting Radar showed that the area above ground was the "Red Zone"—the Mechanical City Ruins—where three or four other trains were currently scavenging.
The elevator continued rising.
"Ding."
With a chime, the train elevator came to a stop. The walls of the elevator slowly retracted into the ground, revealing the train in a vast, flat indoor plaza buried a thousand meters beneath the Mechanical City.
Was this... a laboratory?
Flickering incandescent lamps on the walls, dried bloodstains on the floor, shattered glass containers in the distance, and toppled monitors—everything suggested this place wasn't exactly safe!
"Roar!"
At that moment, a hoarse roar erupted as hundreds of zombies suddenly charged out from the rooms surrounding the square, sprinting wildly toward the train!
However...
The train was too high.
Only a few zombies managed to climb up using the Wind-Fire Wheels, gripping the uneven surfaces of the carriage exteriors. The majority could only vent their frustration by jumping up and down helplessly on the ground.
"Level 4 zombies?"
Chen Mang frowned slightly. It had been a long time since he'd seen zombies of such low level. But just as he was about to press a red button on the control panel to eliminate them, Xiao Ai's voice suddenly echoed through the train compartment.
"Train Conductor, Uncle Li wants these zombies for research. He says since this is an almost sealed environment, these zombies must have survived here for a long time. There must be something unusual about them."
After a pause, Xiao Ai added,
"I thought this was urgent enough to bypass the flashing light alert."
"Understood."
Chen Mang withdrew his hand and instead picked up the walkie-talkie. "Biao Zi, get down there and capture them alive."
"Copy that!"
Biao Zi's response came swiftly through the walkie-talkie.
Though transmitting orders via the Iris Chip was faster and more convenient, Chen Mang still preferred using the walkie-talkie sometimes.
The battle ended quickly.
Biao Zi and his team, clad in mechanized armor, efficiently broke the zombies' arms and legs before bundling them up like crabs and tossing them into the Breeding Carriage.
They then proceeded to explore the surrounding rooms as ordered.
One of the zombies was brought to the train compartment.
"..."
Chen Mang stood up and walked over to examine the zombie, its eyes milky white and lips tinged with blue. If not for Uncle Li's reminder, he wouldn't have noticed that these zombies had clearly been here for a long time—there wasn't a trace of fresh blood around their mouths, meaning they hadn't fed in ages.
How did they survive without eating?
Pure starvation?
Do zombies not starve to death?
They didn't look emaciated either.
"Don't move!"
Suddenly, Xiao Ai's excited voice blared through the compartment.
"Are you fucking trying to get yourself killed?!"
Startled, Chen Mang turned and glared at the Train Auxiliary AI on the control panel before cursing. He tossed the gun he'd just pulled out onto the table—he'd nearly shot the zombie out of reflex.
For safety, he always carried a Tidal Gatling Gun in his pocket.
"Train Conductor," Xiao Ai continued, voice trembling with excitement, "Biao Zi and the others found a warehouse full of materials. They were about to start rummaging through them, but I told them to stop."
"The materials in that warehouse are all 'Fiber Copper Mold Sheets'!"
"What are they for?" Chen Mang frowned, studying the footage transmitted by the Mechanical Eye on the control screen. The warehouse wasn't large—about the size of a basement beneath a residential building. He'd never heard of this material before and had no idea what it was used for.
"The receiving end of the Cosmic Receiver is made from this material!"
"Got it."
Chen Mang calmly pulled out his walkie-talkie. "Leave the cargo untouched for now. Wait until we've secured the entire area before returning. Teams Two and Three, disembark immediately. Team Two will guard the cargo. Team Three, explore the other sectors."
With that, the orders were given.
He couldn't help but smile as he looked at the images on the screen. With this batch of materials, he could manufacture more "Cosmic Receivers"—far superior to "Solar Energy Panels."
After consuming millions of units of iron ore to upgrade the "Solar Energy Panel" to level 100, he discovered it could yield 180,000 units of iron ore daily.
His first thought was simple:
Scale up.
Anyone in business knows the process is straightforward. First, create a viable business model—one where an initial investment of 100 units can break even and then generate steady profits. The next step is simply to amplify that model.
Business may sound complicated, but it's essentially about expanding from 0 to 1, then from 1 to 100.
The problem is, 70% of people fail at the 0-to-1 stage, and even those who succeed often struggle through setbacks.
So his immediate instinct was to stockpile iron ore and manufacture 100 "Solar Energy Panels." In the short term, the Train's progress would stall, but once completed, the daily income would skyrocket to 18 million units of iron ore!
Compound interest upon compound interest—a post-apocalyptic capitalist's dream!
Unfortunately, most components in the Train could be replicated, but this particular one was limited to a single unit.
His newborn plan was strangled in its cradle.
Yet, just as despair set in, an unexpected opportunity arose. While duplicating Solar Energy Panels was impossible, replicating Cosmic Receivers—an idea he'd never even considered—had somehow become feasible.
"Not bad."
Chen Mang grinned as he surveyed the warehouse full of materials. He wasn't sure how many receivers they could produce, but his expression soon darkened with anger.
The outermost materials had been gnawed to scraps!
No doubt the work of those damned Zombies.
"It's fine, Train Conductor. These materials don't need to be intact. Even if parts are chewed up, the remaining portions are still usable. No major impact."
"That's good."
After a pause, he added, "Can you... hear my thoughts?"
"Of course not. But I can infer them from your expression."
"Don't do that next time."
"Understood."
Chen Mang sat in the Train's control room, watching the footage of Biao Zi and the others exploring the area. The space wasn't large—just an underground Laboratory, though its exact purpose remained unclear.
By now, the area had been fully cleared.
Only one elevator led upward—the sole entrance and exit. The Train couldn't fit inside; the elevator could hold at most twenty humans. It wasn't a "Train Elevator."
Every last Zombie had been eliminated.
The horde that had rushed out earlier comprised nearly all of them. Any stragglers hiding in dark corners had since been wiped out by Biao Zi's team.
"All clear!"
Biao Zi, who had sprinted to the base of the control room, looked up and shouted.
Soon—
The control room door slid open.
Chen Mang stepped out calmly, leaning on his cane with one hand and cradling Xiao Lu in the other. He walked through the air as if descending an invisible staircase, his feet never faltering. Without turning his head, he murmured softly:
"Let's check that warehouse."
"."
Biao Zi stood rooted to the spot, his eyes wide with shock. It took him a good while to snap out of it before he hurriedly responded and rushed to catch up. The rest of the team members behind him rubbed their eyes in disbelief, wondering if they were sleep-deprived and seeing things.
Lord Mang...
Did he just walk in mid-air?
Without any armor, flying through the air?
Lord Mang really is a Cultivator.
Inside the underground laboratory.
Chen Mang leaned calmly on his cane as he walked across the plaza toward the warehouse, his face expressionless and his eyes indifferent. But inwardly, he couldn't help but chuckle.
A ladder?
Him, a Train Conductor, Lord Mang, turning his backside to his subordinates and climbing down a ten-meter ladder?
Far too undignified.
He hadn't even planned to come down at first. But then, he thought of a brilliant solution.
Using the Mechanical Heart, he forged two pieces of steel and stuffed them into his shoes, then made a few more to tuck into his belt. By remotely controlling the Powerful Magnet through his cane and coordinating his movements, he successfully created the visual effect of walking in mid-air.
Perfect.
If he hadn't stuffed some steel into his belt, he might've lost his balance.
The level 100 "Powerful Magnet" attachment was truly excellent—highly recommended. Every Train Conductor should have one!
By now—
They had reached the warehouse entrance. Biao Zi strode ahead, overtaking Lord Mang, and pulled the door open first before announcing, "Lord Mang, this is the warehouse."
"..."
Chen Mang surveyed the vast stockpile of materials before him and nodded in satisfaction before waving his hand with a smile. "Move everything to the Armor Research Center in Carriage No. 2. Be careful—don't damage anything."
"Yes, sir!"
Then he proceeded to another warehouse, much larger than the first. This one was filled with piles of Iron Ore—all level 3!
Each piece of Iron Ore was equivalent to 100 units.
The warehouse held a massive stockpile, though none of it was stored in Storage Boxes—just left scattered across the floor.
"..."
Chen Mang stared impassively at the Iron Ore as Zhang Yi and Zhang Er swiftly loaded it up. Finding a warehouse full of Iron Ore should've been a cause for celebration, but he couldn't quite bring himself to feel happy.
Because over half of it had been eaten.
Yes—eaten by those damned Zombies!
Damn it!
They should've just stayed dead like proper Zombies. What business did they have eating Iron Ore? That's not even on their menu! Aren't Zombies supposed to feast on flesh? Why the hell are they eating Iron Ore?!
If not for those Zombies, all the Iron Ore in this warehouse would've been his.
Soon, the inventory was complete.
[Train Conductor, this warehouse contains 3.4 million units of Iron Ore.]
[The Zombies consumed roughly 12 million.]
"...Hah."
Chen Mang took a deep breath, trying his best to suppress his fury. Damn it all... 12 million units of Iron Ore, gone. He hated Zombies!
With that, he turned and strode back toward the train.
As he approached, he effortlessly floated through the air and landed smoothly inside the train cabin.
Not bad.
He'd secured a batch of materials and 3.4 million units of Iron Ore. With over 3 million units as a safety net, he could venture forth with much greater peace of mind. Still, he could've had so much more if not for those cursed Zombies!
As for that single-person elevator—no need to bother with it now.
According to the Targeting Radar, that single-person elevator leads directly to the outskirts of the Mechanical City Ruins. There probably isn't much left to explore in the Mechanical City anyway—it's been thoroughly picked over by so many people.
Next, I'll check out the Train Tunnel to see what lies ahead.
Only by taking the road less traveled can one reap uncommon rewards.
When others take the water route, you take the land route.
When others take the land route, you take the water route.
Following the crowd may keep you fed,
But going against the grain is how you strike it rich.
Of course, there's also a good chance you might starve.

chapters.title: Chapter 246 - 246 Not Even Jesus Can Stop Me, I Said So!
chapters.content:
When Biao Zi and the others had transported large quantities of iron ore and materials back to Carriages No. 2 and No. 3.
Chen Mang tossed a Level 2 Energy Stone into the funnel beside the Train Elevator.
The Train Elevator started up again.
Descending slowly.
Once more, it arrived at the Train Tunnel, bypassed the Mechanical City, and headed straight north!
What lay ahead, he didn't know.
But he knew he had the Train and the cannons.
No matter what was ahead.
It would be his.
After roughly half an hour of travel, they finally saw the end of the Train Tunnel. However, the path ahead suddenly lost all traces of mechanical craftsmanship, revealing instead a massive natural cavern, pitch-black without a single ray of light.
Chen Mang glanced at the control panel screen.
Both the Targeting Radar and Resource Detection Radar showed no activity ahead.
Yet for some reason, he felt uneasy. The screen indicated they were no longer in the "Peril Rail Valley" area but had entered an unknown region.
The moment the train's front entered the cavern, a shrill alarm blared inside the train cabin!
Flashing red incessantly!
The Targeting Radar screen also displayed a monster lurking in the cavern—Level 15.
Chen Mang's expression shifted slightly. His Train Armor was only Level 13.
At the same time—
The Resource Detection Radar began flashing wildly, showing mines scattered all around the cavern. Dozens of them densely covered the area, with at least three Level 4 Iron Ore mines visible at a glance!
The headlights instantly illuminated the cavern's interior.
A massive Two-Headed Giant charged out of the darkness, roaring as it swung its Spiked Club down hard onto the train!
"Boom!"
The Stellar Train, unable to dodge in time, took the full brunt of the blow. The cabin flashed red violently, and Carriage No. 5, where the impact landed, was nearly flattened—on the verge of total destruction!
Quickly pushing the control lever, Chen Mang maneuvered the train away from the monster into a corner, swiftly scanning the information on the screen.
「Carriage No. 5 Armor Integrity: 34% | No. 5 Doomsday Cannon Integrity: 0%.」
「Mechanical Nanite Spiders are rapidly being produced and dispatched for repairs.」
The monster didn't act recklessly again. Instead, it stood still, its eyes fixed intently on the Stellar Train, filled with bloodlust and savagery. Its body leaned slightly forward, ready to charge at any moment!
Standing over twenty meters tall, its body was bloated and entirely blue.
With two heads.
The sheer pressure it exuded was overwhelming.
"Damn it..."
Sitting in the train cabin, Chen Mang looked at the screen displaying the Doomsday Cannon's 0% integrity and muttered, "Crafting a Level 20 Doomsday Cannon is expensive as hell, you balls-on-the-neck freak!"
Zero integrity meant it was beyond repair—completely scrapped.
It would have to be rebuilt from scratch.
Despite the monster's enormous size, its explosive sprinting speed was terrifyingly fast—far surpassing the train's speed!
Just then—
"ROAR!!!"
The Two-Headed Giant roared again, leaning forward and raising its massive Spiked Club high, launching another death charge at the Stellar Train!
A faint Sonic Boom could even be heard in the air.
The well-prepared Stellar Train immediately switched to its Spider Leg configuration, nimbly scaling the wall behind it and climbing onto the ceiling, where the entire train hung upside down, successfully dodging the attack.
As the Stellar Train moved swiftly across the ceiling, the remaining nine Doomsday Cannons locked onto the two-headed monster, their barrels spinning rapidly!
"Boom! Boom! Boom!"
Flaming shells erupted one after another, instantly enveloping the monster in a storm of projectiles!
The upgrades to the Doomsday Cannons didn't increase their power—only their range and rate of fire.
But rate of fire was power!
The faster the firing speed, the greater the damage!
With all nine Doomsday Cannons firing at full capacity, Level 17 shells were churned out without restraint, raining down on the two-headed monster like a metallic tempest!
But then—
"..."
Chen Mang's pupils constricted sharply. The two-headed monster was swinging its Spiked Club with terrifying speed, deflecting every single shell. After a full volley, it had only suffered minor injuries?
"How is this possible?!"
He didn't have time to dwell on it, immediately launching another barrage.
Then, still hanging upside down from the ceiling, he maneuvered the Stellar Train behind the monster and fired another volley—targeting its weak spots!
Yet...
Despite its massive size, the monster reacted with startling speed, spinning around to block the shells aimed at its back.
Chen Mang had even targeted multiple areas simultaneously—feet, legs, head, torso—yet the monster blocked them all.
So far, the two-headed monster had only sustained superficial damage from the explosions, with no critical injuries!
Fortunately, the cavern was tall—nearly a hundred meters high. As long as he stayed upside down on the ceiling, he could slowly whittle the boss down.
But the next moment—
He suddenly noticed the monster bending its legs. A sense of foreboding flashed through him. The Doomsday Cannons roared again, but the monster, already coiled to leap, had no time to react further. Its Spiked Club spun furiously, knocking shell after shell out of the air.
This damn thing was clearly about to jump up and attack him!
If it was preparing to leap, it could definitely reach him.
Should he retreat?
A shadow crossed Chen Mang's eyes. If he wanted to escape, he could use the Drill Bit to quickly flee the cavern. But... the abundance of Mines here was too tempting. He desperately needed that Iron Ore!
If he ran now, he could always come back later when the Train was stronger.
But that thought left him unsatisfied.
By the time the Train reached Level 15 or 16, the Iron Ore here wouldn't be as enticing.
He firmly believed that so-called "delayed gratification" was just an excuse for unfulfilled desires.
Would a toy you craved as a child bring you any joy if you finally got it at 30?
But if he stayed and fought, that damn Spiked Club was making it impossible to break through.
The moment he stopped firing, the monster would leap up and attack!
His Copper Ore reserves couldn't sustain this much Level 17 shell production!
Still...
Chen Mang's expression gradually turned peculiar. He tentatively fired a level-14 shell, which couldn't penetrate the defense at all. Yet, the opponent remained squatting in a horse stance, knees bent, brandishing the spiked club with formidable force, blocking every single shell.
Level 12.
Level 9.
Level 6.
All the way down to level 1. Now, every shell fired by the Doomsday Cannon was level 1!
Completely ineffective!
But that two-headed monster showed no intention of ignoring them. Its bloodthirsty and savage eyes remained fixed on the Stellar Train, while it continued spinning the spiked club in its hands, deflecting every shell.
Clearly.
This monster's unique mechanism allowed it to block every shell with the spiked club—unless the shell's level was high enough, say level 22 or 25, where even the shockwave would be unbearable for the monster. Otherwise, this creature was nearly invincible!
But...
Even a level-1 shell would trigger the monster's forced blocking mechanism.
There was no need to rush now.
"..."
Chen Mang glanced at the control panel screen and suddenly laughed.
The train originally had 4.62 million units of copper ore!
The cost of a level-14 shell was 3,000 units of copper ore.
Level 15: 3,500 units.
Level 16: 4,000 units.
Level 17: 4,500 units—two shots could deplete a level-1 copper ore deposit.
After three consecutive Halved Consumption reductions, the price dropped to 562.5 units.
He had already fired over 3,000 shells, consuming 1.813 million units of iron ore, yet the two-headed monster remained unfazed. Including the low-level shells used for testing, he still had 2.71 million units of copper ore left.
This amount would only cover around 4,000 level-17 shells.
That many level-17 shells clearly wouldn't be enough to kill this monster—that near-absolute blocking mechanic was too infuriating!
But—
A single level-1 shell cost only 5 units of copper ore.
After three Halved Consumption reductions...
0.625 units per shell.
His remaining 2.71 million units of copper ore could produce over 3 million level-1 shells!
From now on, he wouldn't do anything else. He'd just slowly fire level-1 shells.
He refused to believe it!
No matter how much of a boss you are, even a level-15 boss should get tired, right?
If this thing had to spin its spiked club in a horse stance all day, he refused to believe it wouldn't wear out.
If, after firing all 3 million level-1 shells, the boss still showed no signs of fatigue—fine, he'd admit defeat. He'd leave, develop a bit more, and come back next time.
In the blink of an eye, three hours passed.
If not for the constant explosions echoing through the cavern, the scene would have seemed like a frozen frame.
The Stellar Train hung upside down from the cavern ceiling, its nine Doomsday Cannons firing relentlessly, shells pouring out like they were free!
The massive two-headed monster had long since collapsed to its knees, unable to hold its stance. Yet, its spiked club still spun rapidly—though noticeably slower and less forceful than before.
"Already giving up?"
Leaning back in his chair with his feet propped up on the control panel, he took his eyes off the movie playing beside him. Holding a cigar between his fingers, he glanced indifferently at the struggling two-headed monster below and remarked lazily, "I thought you were supposed to be 100% adept at disarming bare-handed? Go on, take your time."
"Let's see just how far your forced blocking can go."
He had all the time in the world.
Three hours?
He could even spare thirty if needed—this mine was his for the taking!
Not even Jesus could stop him—that was his word!
"How should I record this..."
Seated in a private room within Guard Carriage No. 7, Lao Zhu frowned as he stared at the scene below, his pen hovering hesitantly over the paper.
"Today, Lord Mang piloted the Stellar Train northward through the underground train tunnel, accidentally entering an unknown cavern. There, it was ambushed by a Level 15 boss, resulting in damage to Carriage No. 5."
"Lord Mang... ultimately achieved an instant kill!"
The main dilemma was whether to include the words "instant kill."
Theoretically speaking,
even though it had taken three hours, if the Stellar Train ever ventured into space in the future, three hours there might as well be a blink of an eye. But after some thought, he decided to rephrase it.
"A fierce battle ensued, with Lord Mang gaining the upper hand!"
After all, this was a Level 15 monster, while the train was only Level 10. Defeating a boss above their level, even if it took some time, was still an impressive feat. Moreover, this version better highlighted Lord Mang's decisive choices in the face of danger, his unyielding will, and his brilliant tactics.
It would make for excellent teaching material.
Yes, this would do.
"...That was way too close."
In Carriage No. 5, now fully repaired thanks to the Mechanical Nanite Spiders, Ji Chuchu and Yan Yao sat by the window, still shaken by the ordeal. The moment the attack had struck, the carriage had nearly been flattened!
Thankfully, after the Train Expansion, its size had increased significantly—
now standing at a full ten meters tall.
Even after being smashed down to just three meters, the two of them had suffered only minor injuries, protected by the effects of the "Permanent Shock Absorption" component.
Had the train not been expanded, that single blow would have crushed Carriage No. 5 into a sheet of metal.
They would've died on the spot.
And—
if Carriage No. 5 had been instantly flattened, it would have lost its connecting function, severing the link to the following carriages. Everyone in the rear sections would have been left stranded, waiting for death.
Too close.
Ji Chuchu patted her chest lightly as she gazed out the window at the two-headed monster below, murmuring, "Survived another day. Feels good."
Though she was seated by the window, her head was tilted downward.
Gravity seemed to have no effect inside this carriage.
This was the result of the "Internal Space Stabilizer" component. While it didn't cause any physical discomfort, the perspective was admittedly strange. Still, she had mostly gotten used to it by now.
Another four hours passed.
Chen Mang checked the remaining Copper Ore reserves—120,000 units left, with over 1.5 million already consumed.
Four hours ago, the two-headed monster below had already looked like it was on its last legs, yet it had stubbornly held on until now.
Its stamina and endurance were truly top-tier.
But it seemed to have finally reached its limit.
The remaining 120,000 units of Copper Ore would be more than enough.
He'd wear it down if he had to!
Damn it!
Still, the earlier attack on Carriage No. 5 had reminded him of something.
"Xiao Ai, if the carriage containing the Space Gate is destroyed, what would happen to the Space Gate?"
"It would shatter."
Xiao Ai's voice echoed through the train compartment: "Theoretically speaking, this is the most powerful attack, nearly impossible to defend against. The shattered space fragments would instantly slice the entire Space Gate into countless pieces."
"..."
Chen Mang nodded thoughtfully, as if realizing the potential uses for "Space Stasis"—that purple accessory he had never used before.
This accessory wasn't useless after all.
On the contrary, at critical moments, it could deliver the decisive blow!
Seven hours had passed since the Stellar Train entered the cavern. Apart from an initial encounter, the ensuing seven-hour battle could be described as stop-motion animation!
After seven hours of relentless combat,
the emotions in the eyes of that two-headed monster had shifted many times.
From initial savagery and bloodlust, to later exhaustion and fury.
Then to confusion and helplessness.
Until now—despair, resentment, and complete breakdown.
And just then—
Finally drained of all energy, with both physical strength and mental fortitude at their limits, the spiked club slipped from its grasp and was flung away!

chapters.title: Chapter 247: Time for the Harvest!
chapters.content:
When the spiked club in the hands of this two-headed monster, after spinning continuously for seven hours, was finally flung away—
The monster, which had been filled with despair moments ago, suddenly regained a trace of clarity in its eyes. It frantically tried to rise and lunge toward its spiked club.
However...
After kneeling for seven hours, its legs gave out the moment it stood, causing it to stumble and collapse onto the ground.
At the final moment, the monster turned its head to see the countless artillery shells already descending upon it. It let out a desperate roar.
But—
The outcome was already decided!
The instant the spiked club was flung away, Chen Mang swiftly switched from Level 1 artillery shells to Level 17 shells. With a single volley, the monster, now defenseless, was riddled with thigh-thick projectiles that exploded inside its body.
In an instant!
Countless bursts of blood erupted across the monster's body, and chunks of flesh scattered through the air.
The scene was both tragic and eerily beautiful.
The two-headed monster, its eyes brimming with despair, couldn't even withstand a single volley before its massive body crashed to the ground like a collapsing mountain. Even in death, its gaze remained fixed on the enormous spiked club lying nearby.
The battle—was over!
The Stellar Train, which had been suspended from the cavern ceiling, finally descended. As soon as it landed, hundreds of residents, directed by Biao Zi, rushed out armed with Train Blade Fragments, ready to dismember and carve up this Level 15 boss.
This was standard procedure.
The flesh of high-level monsters had to be carefully sectioned and stored in refrigerators for future use.
"Exhausting..."
Inside the train, Chen Mang glanced at the control panel's clock and shook his head helplessly. It was already 6 a.m., nearly dawn—he had been at it all night.
The last time he'd endured such a prolonged battle was back in the Iron Ridge Wasteland.
But there was no denying it—
This was what a duel between experts felt like. After slaying this Level 15 boss, he couldn't help but feel a sense of accomplishment. It was deeply satisfying.
This was a Level 15 boss! The strongest creatures in the Blue Zone capped at Level 12. Even in the Purple Zone, a Level 15 monster would be a dominant force!
Yet he had soloed it with ease!
Thankfully, Shen Ye had supplied him with plenty of copper ore. Without it, he wouldn't have been able to pull this off today and would've had to return another time.
Now—it was time for the harvest!
A large number of residents had already disembarked, pickaxes in hand, heading toward the nearby mines. Their eyes gleamed with excitement!
It had been ages since they'd seen so many mines in one place!
Just how many Stellar Coupons could they earn from this?!
Though the entire battle had been broadcast live inside the train last night, leaving many sleepless, who cared? A couple of colas later, and they were ready to work!
Chen Mang promptly activated the purple-tier accessory, Vitality Aroma, to help the residents quickly recover their stamina.
There were dozens of mines here.
-
[Four Level 4 Iron Ore Mines, One Level 4 Copper Ore Mine, One Level 4 Titanium Crystal Mine.]
[Nine Level 3 Iron Ore Mines, Two Level 3 Copper Ore Mines.]
[Fourteen Level 2 Iron Ore Mines, Eleven Level 2 Copper Ore Mines.]
-
This was the most densely packed resource area he had ever seen, bar none!
What more was there to say?
Until these mines were exhausted, he wasn't going anywhere. For the next stretch of time, he would stay right here, going into full seclusion. By the time he emerged, his Train would have reached level 12!
The three Oxygen Generators began working furiously, transforming the cavern into a high-oxygen environment, making labor more energetic.
The Headlights were turned on at full power, illuminating the entire cavern brightly.
The once brutal battlefield.
Almost instantly and seamlessly transitioned into a scene of production, vibrant and thriving!
Though it was exhausting.
Seeing this, Chen Mang couldn't help but laugh—it was all worth it!
After wandering all night in Crisis Valley the previous evening without finding a single level 4 Iron Ore, here he had discovered four!
Only then did Chen Mang turn his attention to the three items in his hand.
This was the highest-level boss he had ever killed.
Naturally, the rewards were substantial.
-
1: Red-grade Accessory Blueprint, "Magnetic Levitation."
2: Special Item, "Hell Hat."
3: Purple-grade Mecha Blueprint, "Pope."
-
The rewards were absurdly generous, perhaps due to the challenge of fighting above his level, or maybe because this was a hidden boss in an unexplored region. But the rewards were so lavish that he almost felt unworthy.
First reward: Magnetic Levitation.
A type of wheel.
Similar to an accessory, there was the red-grade "Inferno Wheels," which could be crafted once the Train reached level 10. Both were red-grade wheels, but in terms of speed, the "Inferno Wheels" were slightly faster.
The advantage of "Magnetic Levitation" was that it eliminated the need for wheels altogether—the Train would hover directly above the ground, ignoring certain obstacles.
Whether hills or swamps, it didn't matter.
In theory, it could even partially replace "Rabbit Wheels," though it could only hover up to three meters above the ground, unable to fly too high. It seemed to have its own merits compared to the red-grade wheel accessory "Inferno Wheels!"
But—
The red-grade Accessory Blueprint for "Magnetic Levitation" explicitly stated that if paired with a level 100 "Powerful Magnet" accessory, the combination would yield unexpected special effects.
What more was there to say?
"Good stuff."
Chen Mang nodded in satisfaction. Next was the second item, the "Hell Hat," a bowler hat. When worn, within a 10,000-meter radius of the Train, the wearer's body would gain a defensive rating equivalent to the Train Armor.
Even better stuff.
In his mind, this Special Item could almost tie for first place with the "Hell Staff" as the most incredible item.
He had previously obtained another item called "Hell Sunglasses," which slightly increased the wearer's Physical Fitness Index. The three items had such similar names—could they be part of a set?
He thought renaming them to "Heaven" might be more auspicious.
The last item went without saying—the purple-grade Mecha Blueprint, "Pope"!
Biao Zi hadn't even gotten to pilot the blue-grade mecha "Thunder" yet, and now the purple-grade mecha "Pope" had appeared.
To be fair, Biao Zi's growth rate was already impressive.
And he was working incredibly hard.
But sadly, in the rapid development of the Train, individual progress seemed somewhat insignificant.
And that.
Was the entirety of this haul.
Chen Mang chuckled as he cradled Xiao Lu in his arms, leaning on his cane while stepping through the air one foot at a time until he landed on the ground. In high spirits, he strolled through the cavern, observing the scene—residents on the left butchering the boss's flesh while those on the right mined.
A harmonious and thriving atmosphere.
Everything was being rebuilt.
Excellent.
The oxygen levels in this cavern had originally been extremely low. It was unclear how long that monster had stayed here, surviving without needing oxygen. There were no other exits either, suggesting the creature had simply been dormant here all along.
No traces of excretion were found.
Did it sustain itself solely on these iron ores?
Just like those Zombies?
"Lord Mang!"
Not far away, Biao Zi ran over excitedly to report: "We've finished cutting everything up."
"Well done." Chen Mang nodded with a smile.
"Lord Mang, there's something else. Over these past few days, I've completed the normal difficulty of the remaining five maps, including Dragon Fortress. I've also cleared the Extreme Difficulty of Dragon Fortress twice. My Physical Fitness Index has reached 19.9 now."
"I was wondering..."
Biao Zi scratched his head, both excited and a little embarrassed. "I'd like to request a 'Thunder' mech."
The blue-tier mech, Thunder.
「Requires the operator's Physical Fitness Index to exceed 19.0. Full power can be unleashed when above 19.5.」
He had been pushing himself relentlessly for this goal, even neglecting sleep and meals!
Every day, he chugged down his self-brewed "Man's Drink" like crazy.
With the dual support of technology and sheer effort, his progress had been nothing short of revolutionary.
Finally, he had caught up to Zhang Yi and Zhang Er.
"..."
Chen Mang fell silent for a moment before patting Biao Zi's shoulder and speaking softly, "You've been training Zhang Yi and Zhang Er all this time. Have you noticed what their Physical Fitness Index is now?"
"N-no..."
"Your request is approved. But I also have some news for you—the Train now has a purple-tier mech called 'Pope,' which is even more powerful than 'Thunder.' So far, only those two can operate it in the entire Train."
"Tell them to go see Xiao Ai later to collect their new mechs."
"You can pick whichever one of their old ones you prefer."
"Go on."
With that, Chen Mang didn't linger any longer and continued walking into the distance, surveying the cavern. The dark round-top hat on his head filled him with an immense sense of security. It had been so long since he arrived in this world.
This was the first time he had ever felt so at ease leaving the Train to wander around.
He had actually been itching to conduct an experiment.
If the hat could grant him the same defense as the Train Armor, what would happen if he jumped from 100 meters in the air and landed on the ground...?
After some thought, he figured he'd probably end up dead.
After all, his body didn't have components like "Permanent Shock Absorption."
Against larger monsters, he'd still have to flee. But when it came to attacks like firearms—if their level wasn't higher than his Train Armor—he could probably ignore them. He'd test it out later.
"..."
Chen Mang left, leaving Biao Zi standing rigidly in place, his expression frozen in bewilderment. The smile on his face slowly faded. After a long while, he finally snapped out of it, lowering his head to stare at his hands, his face twisted in despair.
Why?!
He had given it his all!
After finally catching up, he thought he could have the Thunder mech just like Zhang Yi and Zhang Er, only to find out the train now had a new purple mech called the Pope.
He was still one step behind.
Just then—
Zhang Yi and Zhang Er walked past him side by side, munching on stuffed buns and muttering.
"Boss, Director Ai wants us to pick up the new mech—something called the Pope. I don't really feel like taking it, though. I've gotten used to the Thunder mech, and I'm kinda reluctant to switch."
"Same, but we have to. Director Ai said our Thunder mechs need to be handed down to Biao Ge. If we don't switch, he won't get one."
"Alright then. But why doesn't Biao Ge want the Pope mech?"
"Probably just doesn't like it."
"Hah—"
Biao Zi took a deep breath, hands pressed to his chest, forcing a smile as he watched the two walk away. "It's fine, it's fine. Biao Zi, don't worry about what others have. Didn't you originally just want the Thunder mech?"
"Your dream has already come true, and you've done it perfectly. What others have doesn't concern you."
"Doesn't con—"
In the end, he couldn't hold back and slammed a fist into the ground, his face twisted in anger as he stormed toward Carriage No. 2. After claiming the Thunder mech, he was heading straight for the Extreme Difficulty maps!
He had a new goal now!
He wanted the Pope too!
He was the captain—how could he keep getting overshadowed by his own subordinates? If he didn't vent this frustration, his resolve would waver!
"..."
Inside the cavern, Chen Mang watched Biao Zi's furious retreating figure and shook his head with a helpless chuckle. It was just too hard for Biao Zi to catch up to those two freaks of talent. But in a way, that was a good thing.
Without those two ahead of him,
Biao Zi wouldn't have improved this fast.
A few months ago, Biao Zi was just a former contractor before the apocalypse, with only slightly more combat experience than others—nothing special. But now...
In such a short time,
he had already become someone who could hold his own.
His growth speed was actually insane. The problem was, Biao Zi couldn't see his own progress, too fixated on chasing those two freaks. He had no idea how much pressure his rapid improvement was putting on the rest of the first team!
Which, in turn, forced the first team to keep up at an equally breakneck pace.
And the first team didn't realize their own growth was putting immense pressure on the other two teams!
So—
Under this kind of competition, everyone was being pushed to improve at an extreme speed... except for those two idiots.
Natural talent—nothing you could do about it.
Especially under Biao Zi's leadership, where they had both talent and relentless training intensity. How could Biao Zi possibly keep up with that kind of growth rate...
"Hey."
Chen Mang, sitting back in the train compartment, suddenly sighed and smiled wryly.
"Make a new Thunder mech for Biao Zi. The ones Zhang Yi and Zhang Er are handing down can go to the others. A few in the first team are almost ready for them anyway."
"That guy's been looking forward to the Thunder mech for so long."
"Let him have a new one to play with."
"Understood." Xiao Ai's voice echoed from within the compartment.
Then Chen Mang looked up at the distant, shimmering mine—a special one, structured similarly to iron ore, with jagged resource deposits jutting sharply from the ground.
However, it wasn't pitch black, nor was it brass-colored.
Instead,
it was transparent, shimmering brilliantly under the light, quite beautiful to behold.
This was a level 4 Titanium Crystal Mine.
He had never seen this ore before, nor did he know what it was used for, but he understood it was rare and might prove useful in the future.
Just like when he first mined the Crimson Heart Rock Mine, he hadn't known its purpose either—only later did he learn it was used to construct mechas.
"Not bad."
Chen Mang sat inside the Train's cabin. After washing up, he headed to his bed to sleep, feeling drowsy after staying up all night.
The remaining tasks no longer required his involvement.
His part was done.
Once they left this mine, the Train would reach level 11, and most likely even jump straight to level 12.
